dd_procedures.title: SPN 3251 FMI 18 - DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3251 FMI 18 – DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Fault (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3251 FMI 18 indicates a fault with the DPF differential pressure sensor, which is the component the ECM relies on to measure the pressure difference across the Diesel Particulate Filter and calculate soot load levels. When this sensor fails on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines the ECM cannot accurately monitor DPF condition, which can affect regeneration scheduling and lead to derate conditions.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regeneration cycles may become erratic or not initiate 
Engine derate possible 
DPF soot load readings may be inaccurate 
May appear alongside DPF soot load codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects the DPF differential pressure sensor is reading outside the acceptable range. Common causes include:
Failed or degraded differential pressure sensor 
Clogged or blocked pressure sensor lines or ports 
Damaged sensor wiring or connector 
Water intrusion at the sensor connector 
Cracked or disconnected pressure sensing tubes 
Carbon buildup blocking the sensor ports 
Faulty sensor giving implausible pressure readings
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without accurate differential pressure data the ECM cannot properly manage DPF regeneration. This can result in either premature or missed regeneration cycles, potentially leading to a soot overload condition and derate. Address this fault promptly.
Recommended Action
Inspect the differential pressure sensor lines and ports for carbon buildup or blockages — clogged sensor ports are a very common cause of this fault and are often overlooked. Check the sensor wiring and connector for damage or water intrusion. If the lines and wiring are clear and intact replace the differential pressure sensor as sensor failure is the next most likely cause.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3251 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DPF differential pressure sensor is reading outside the acceptable range and the ECM cannot accurately measure the pressure difference across the DPF to determine soot load levels.
 
 
What causes SPN 3251 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are clogged sensor ports or lines, a failed differential pressure sensor, damaged sensor wiring, or water intrusion at the connector.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3251 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but without accurate DPF pressure data the ECM cannot properly manage regeneration cycles and a soot overload condition or derate may follow.
 
 
Will SPN 3251 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
It can if the inaccurate pressure readings cause the ECM to miss regeneration cycles and allow soot to accumulate beyond acceptable levels.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3251 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and clean the sensor ports and lines first. If ports are clear check the wiring and connector. Replace the differential pressure sensor if it is faulty. The code should clear once the sensor is providing accurate readings within the expected range.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is a high delta-P always a dirty filter, or can the sensor be wrong?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Both are possible. Clogged sensor tubes are a known cause of false high readings and should be inspected before condemning the filter. However, if the tubes are clear and Insite confirms a consistently elevated delta-P across multiple exhaust flow rates, the filter itself is the more likely cause.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can a parked regen clear this code?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: A successful parked regen can reduce soot load and lower the delta-P reading enough to clear the fault. It will not remove ash �?ash requires physical cleaning. If a forced regen doesn't bring the delta-P back within range, ash loading or a sensor issue is worth investigating.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How often should DPF cleaning be performed as preventive maintenance?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Cleaning intervals vary by application and duty cycle. Cummins QuickServe and the engine's maintenance manual provide guidance based on operating conditions. Vocational and urban-cycle trucks typically need cleaning earlier than long-haul applications.

Soot accumulation from insufficient passive regen - common in city, construction, or vocational duty cycles Failed active regen attempts: incomplete regen due to low exhaust temperature, DEF issues, or operator interruption Ash loading past the point where regeneration removes the blockage (high-mileage filters) DPF differential pressure sensor tube clogged with soot or moisture, giving a falsely elevated reading Leaking sensor tube fitting creating a false pressure differential
steps: Kablo bağlantılarını kontrol edin ve NOx sensörünün çalışmasını test edin.
Arızalı sensörleri değiştirin ve SCR sisteminin düzgün çalıştığını doğrulayın.
Öncelikle DEF (AdBlue) kalitesini ve seviyesini kontrol ederek başlayın; kalitesiz DEF, katalizör çıkışındaki yüksek NOx değerlerinin yaygın bir nedenidir.
DEF kalitesi uygunsa, katalizör çıkışındaki NOx sensörünü ve kablo tesisatını hasar veya kirlenme açısından kontrol edin.
DEF dozajlama sisteminin yeterli püskürtme debisine sahip olduğunu kontrol ettirin.

Tüm bileşenler testten başarıyla geçerse SCR katalizörünü verim kaybı açısından değerlendirin; aşınmış veya zehirlenmiş bir katalizör, sürekli yüksek çıkan çıkış NOx değerlerinin sık görülen bir nedenidir.
Fark basınç sensörü hatlarını ve portlarını kurum birikmesi veya tıkanıklık açısından inceleyin; tıkalı sensör portları bu arızanın çok yaygın ve sıklıkla gözden kaçan bir nedenidir.
Sensör kablo tesisatını ve konnektörünü hasar veya su girişi açısından kontrol edin.

Cummins Insite'ı bağlayın ve çeşitli motor yüklerinde güncel fark basınç (delta-P) değerini kontrol edin; bu egzoz debisinde beklenen değerlerle karşılaştırın. Aktif bir rejenerasyonun sürüp sürmediğini, beklemede olup olmadığını veya yakın zamanda başarısız olup olmadığını kontrol edin.

Insite rejenerasyon geçmişini gösterecektir. Fark basınç sensörü borularını (sensörü DPF giriş ve çıkışına bağlayan küçük çaplı kauçuk veya metal hatlar) çatlak, bükülme veya kurum tıkanıklığı açısından inceleyin. Motor yağı tüketimini gözden geçirin.

Aşırı yağ tüketimi, DPF'ye normalden daha hızlı kül girmesine neden olabilir. Filtre yüksek kilometredeyse (son bakımdan bu yana 400.000+ km), DPF temizliği veya değişimi en doğru çözüm adımı olacaktır…
[FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_3251.pgn_description: The purpose of this PG is to group the aftertreatment intermediate gas temperature and pressure messages. Note: The 5 bits of SPN 3253 are positioned into the data field in the following manner. The 2 most significant bits are placed in bits 2-1 of byte 8 such that the most significant bit of SPN 3253 located at byte 8 bit 2, and the 3 least significant bits are placed in bits 8-6 of byte 7 such that the least significant bit of SPN 3253 located at byte 7 bit 6.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 0 means Cummins DPF exhaust restriction is above limit. Check soot load, run regen for high soot, or clean DPF for high ash restriction. DPF differential pressure measures exhaust flow restriction across the particulate filter. When pressure exceeds calibrated thresholds, Cummins sets SPN 3251 and regen or service is required.
causes: High soot load from incomplete regen cycles
Short trips and excessive idle prevent soot burn-off, raising delta-P.
Ash accumulation causing permanent restriction
Ash cannot be burned — only professional cleaning or replacement resolves restriction.
Plugged or failed DPF pressure sensor lines
Carbon-blocked impulse tubes report falsely high restriction to the ECM.
steps: Read soot load % and DPF delta-P in Cummins INSITE — soot above 80% warrants forced regen; ash high with low soot means cleaning.
Inspect DPF pressure sensor tubes for carbon plugging — blow out with regulated shop air below 30 PSI.
Run forced parked regen and monitor delta-P — should drop below 3 PSI at idle if soot was the cause.
Check for failed regen history from short trip cycles or stuck EGR causing excess soot.
If delta-P stays high after regen with low soot, plan DPF ash cleaning or replacement.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 0 means DPF differential pressure has climbed high enough to indicate a genuinely restricted filter on a Mercedes-Benz Actros or Arocs. It's a High severity fault that can lead to a real power derate if left unaddressed. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always checks soot load percentage first on a code like this - it tells you immediately whether you're dealing with a normal regen candidate or an ash-loaded filter that needs to come out.
causes: Heavily soot-loaded DPF from missed regen opportunities
A mechanical/aftertreatment restriction, not an electrical fault - the filter simply hasn't had the highway running time needed to burn off accumulated soot.
Ash-loaded DPF at or near its service interval
A genuine physical restriction that regen cycles cannot clear, since ash is a non-combustible byproduct that requires physical removal.
Failed or incomplete regen cycles
A control strategy or sensor issue that prevents the regen process from fully completing, leaving soot behind that should have burned off.
Blocked differential pressure sense tube
A sensor/plumbing fault that can produce a false high reading even when the filter itself isn't as restricted as reported.
steps: Check the DPF soot load percentage in live data using Jaltest or Xentry - a reading well above 100% confirms a genuinely restricted filter.
Verify the vehicle has had the opportunity to complete highway-speed passive or active regen cycles recently, since excessive short-trip or stop-and-go driving prevents proper soot burn-off.
Perform a stationary forced regen if soot load is confirmed high and the vehicle qualifies for it based on exhaust temperature and safety conditions.
If differential pressure stays high after a complete regen, the filter is likely ash-loaded rather than soot-loaded and needs physical removal for cleaning or replacement.
Inspect both pressure sense tubes for carbon blockage, since a plugged tube can occasionally mimic a true restriction reading.
symptoms: Noticeable loss of power under load or while climbing grades
Check engine light with a DPF warning message on the dash
Excessive idle time or false regeneration cycles that don't seem to complete
Possible burnt smell during or after a regen attempt

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 0 means Detroit Diesel DPF exhaust restriction is above limit. Check soot load, run regen for high soot, or clean DPF for high ash restriction. DPF differential pressure measures exhaust flow restriction across the particulate filter. When pressure exceeds calibrated thresholds, Detroit Diesel sets SPN 3251 and regen or service is required.
causes: High soot load from incomplete regen cycles
Short trips and excessive idle prevent soot burn-off, raising delta-P.
Ash accumulation causing permanent restriction
Ash cannot be burned — only professional cleaning or replacement resolves restriction.
Plugged or failed DPF pressure sensor lines
Carbon-blocked impulse tubes report falsely high restriction to the ECM.
steps: Read soot load % and DPF delta-P in Detroit DDDL8 — soot above 80% warrants forced regen; ash high with low soot means cleaning.
Inspect DPF pressure sensor tubes for carbon plugging — blow out with regulated shop air below 30 PSI.
Run forced parked regen and monitor delta-P — should drop below 3 PSI at idle if soot was the cause.
Check for failed regen history from short trip cycles or stuck EGR causing excess soot.
If delta-P stays high after regen with low soot, plan DPF ash cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Amber MIL with DPF restriction or exhaust message
Frequent automatic regen requests
Reduced power and turbo lag under load
DPF delta-P above 8 PSI at idle after regen in live data
High exhaust temperature during passive regen attempts

procedures_full.overview: The ECM continuously compares DPF inlet pressure to outlet pressure under specific speed, load, and temperature windows. When the measured differential exceeds the most severe calibrated limit, FMI 0 is set. This is a protection-level fault — the ECM may derate power or inhibit further operation to prevent DPF substrate damage. Common misdiagnosis: replacing the DPF when plugged hoses or an ash-loaded filter are the actual cause. Always verify hose integrity and regen history before condemning the filter.
causes: Loaded DPF — soot accumulation from incomplete regens or short-trip duty cycle
Ash interval exceeded — DPF requires cleaning or replacement
Plugged delta-P hoses or ports — most common misdiagnosis cause
Damaged or cracked DPF substrate
Failed delta-P sensor — stuck voltage, no change with restriction
Upstream soot overproduction — underboost, EGR faults, fueling issues
Repeated aborted parked regens — operator or inhibit-related
steps: Single Action Gate — Code & Freeze Frame
Capture all active codes and freeze frame data. Record soot load %, delta-P live value, and regen history before clearing anything.
Binary Decision Gate — Soot vs Delta-P Agreement
Compare soot load % to delta-P reading. If soot is low but delta-P is high, suspect plugged hoses or sensor. If both are high, restriction is real.
Override Manager — Hose & Port Inspection
Physically inspect both delta-P hose ports at the DPF inlet and outlet. Clean any soot/ash blockage. Inspect hoses for kinks, cracks, or contamination.
Safety Interceptor — Sensor Electrical Verification
Verify 5V reference, ground, and signal circuit. KOEO baseline should be near atmospheric. Stuck voltage or no response to restriction indicates sensor failure.
Resume Point — Regen Abort History Review
Review regen abort history. Identify whether regens are being inhibited by operator, temperature, or system faults. Correct inhibit causes before forcing another regen.
Verification Loop — Upstream Soot Contributors
Check boost levels, EGR operation, and fueling for abnormal soot production. Underboost and EGR faults accelerate DPF loading.
Repair Ledger Output — DPF Service Decision
Service DPF (clean or replace) only after hoses, sensor, regen history, and upstream causes are proven. Document all findings in the repair ledger.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean and inspect both delta-P hose ports and hoses — remove any soot or ash blockage.
2 . Replace delta-P sensor if electrical testing confirms failure ($150–$450).
3 . Correct any regen inhibit conditions — operator settings, inhibit switches, or system faults.
4 . Address upstream soot contributors: repair boost leaks, EGR faults, or fueling abnormalities.
5 . Perform a successful parked regen after upstream corrections.
6 . If soot load remains high after successful regen, perform DPF cleaning ($400–$1,200).
7 . Replace DPF only if cleaning fails or substrate is physically damaged ($2,500–$7,000+).
Verification Steps
Confirm delta-P reading drops to normal range after repair.
Verify soot load % decreases after a successful parked regen.
Confirm no regen abort codes return during a test drive under load.
Check that delta-P hoses are clear and properly routed.
Clear codes and confirm no return of SPN 3251 FMI 0 after 50+ miles of operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Follow OEM-recommended DPF cleaning intervals (typically every 200,000–300,000 miles).
✓ Avoid excessive idle time and short-trip duty cycles that prevent regen completion.
✓ Inspect and clean delta-P hoses and ports at every major service.
✓ Address boost and EGR faults promptly to prevent accelerated soot loading.
✓ Train operators not to abort parked regens unless safety requires it.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity

High severity. Limit driving with this fault active. Severe DPF restriction can cause significant power loss, aftertreatment damage, and potential engine protection shutdown. Do not continue forcing regens without identifying and correcting the root cause.
symptoms: High DPF differential pressure reading on scan tool
Failed or aborted active regen cycle
Black smoke under load
Frequent regen requests
Restricted exhaust / high backpressure
Power loss on grade or under load
Derate or engine protection active

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 2 indicates DPF delta-P signal unstable or implausible. Failing sensor, moisture or soot in hoses, intermittent 5V or ground, cracked sense lines, and connector fretting are the primary causes. Water in sense lines causing cold-start spikes and heat-damaged hoses are documented patterns. Replacing the DP sensor without inspecting the hoses and ports first is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Failing sensor — failing DP sensor producing unstable signal
Moisture or soot in hoses — moisture or soot in sense hoses producing unstable readings
Intermittent 5V or ground — intermittent reference voltage or ground producing unstable sensor signal
Cracked sense lines — cracked sense lines producing air intrusion and unstable readings
Connector fretting — connector fretting producing intermittent sensor signal
steps: Step 1 — Inspect and Clean Hoses and Ports

Inspect and clean the DP sense hoses and ports. Water in sense lines causing cold-start spikes is a documented pattern. Inspect the hoses for moisture, soot, and damage. Inspect the ports on the DPF for plugging and debris. Clean or replace hoses and clear ports if moisture, soot, or plugging is found.
Step 2 — Electrical Reference and Ground Checks

Check the electrical reference voltage and ground at the DP sensor connector. An intermittent 5V or ground producing unstable sensor signal requires circuit repair. Verify reference voltage stability and ground integrity.
Step 3 — Graph Delta-P

Graph the delta-P signal. A KOEO baseline should be stable near zero. A loaded response should be smooth, not spiking randomly. Spikes at cold start suggest moisture in sense lines. Random spikes at operating temperature suggest sensor or circuit integrity faults.
Step 4 — Replace Sensor After Proof

Replace the sensor after proof of sensor failure. Confirm hoses, ports, and circuit integrity before sensor replacement. A sensor replaced without proof may be replaced into a hose or circuit fault that will produce the same erratic readings.
Step 5 — Verify After Repair
Verify delta-P readings are stable after repair. Confirm SPN 3251 FMI 2 does not return. Monitor for return of erratic delta-P events over extended operation.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean or replace DP sense hoses if moisture, soot, or damage is found.
2 . Clear DP ports if plugging is found.
3 . Repair circuit if reference voltage or ground fault is confirmed.
4 . Replace DP sensor after proof of sensor failure.
Verification Steps
Confirm delta-P readings are stable after repair.
Verify SPN 3251 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm regen strategy is stable after repair.
Monitor for return of erratic delta-P events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect DP sense hoses for moisture and damage at every major service.
✓ Inspect DP ports for plugging at every major service.
✓ Inspect DP sensor connector for fretting at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High if regen strategy becomes incorrect Severity
Medium to High if regen strategy becomes incorrect. Erratic delta-P is almost always hoses, moisture, or sensor circuit integrity.
symptoms: DPF pressure sensor intermittent
Delta-P jumping
Erratic backpressure reading
Regen based on bad DP
Cold-start delta-P spikes
procedures_full.source_title: SPN 3251 FMI 2 — DPF Differential Pressure Data Erratic

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 2 means the DPF differential pressure signal is jumping around inconsistently. It's a Medium severity fault usually traced to a loose or corroded connector rather than a real pressure problem. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com finds that a five-minute wiggle test with live data running solves most of these calls before a single part gets ordered.
causes: Loose or corroded sensor electrical connector
An electrical/wiring fault, not a real pressure fluctuation - a poor connection produces the erratic signal the ECM is flagging.
Moisture intrusion at the connector
Another wiring-side issue, common on trucks that see frequent wash bay exposure near the exhaust area.
Loose sense tube fitting
A mechanical connection issue that lets the reading drift intermittently rather than staying stable.
Internal sensor component drift
A genuine sensor hardware fault, confirmed only after ruling out the connector and tube connections.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and watch the differential pressure reading over several minutes at a steady idle - erratic jumps with the engine steady confirm a signal issue rather than a real pressure change.
Inspect both sense tube connections at the sensor and at the exhaust pipe for looseness that could cause an intermittent signal.
Wiggle-test the sensor's electrical connector while watching live data for a signal that drops out or spikes with movement.
Check for moisture intrusion at the connector, which is a common cause of erratic readings on trucks that see a lot of wash bay time.
If the connector and tubes check out solid, replace the sensor itself since internal component drift can also cause this symptom.
symptoms: Check engine light with no consistent power loss
DPF soot load percentage that jumps erratically in live data
Possible unnecessary or missed regen cycles from confused sensor data
No steady performance change most of the time
procedures_full.source_title: Kenworth SPN 3251 FMI 2: DPF Differential Pressure Erratic

procedures_full.overview: The ECM sees an implausible or erratic reading from the diesel particulate filter (DPF) differential-pressure sensor. The truck can't trust soot-load data, so it may block regens and stage an engine derate to protect the aftertreatment system.
procedures_full.severity_action: Power derate likely — plan to stop soon
causes: Plugged, kinked, or soot-fouled DPF pressure sensor lines/tubes
Failed or drifting DPF differential-pressure sensor
An actually overloaded/plugged DPF skewing pressure readings
Wiring/connector corrosion or chafe to the pressure sensor
first_moves: Read full freeze-frame data — note soot load %, miles since last regen, and any companion SCR/DEF codes.
Inspect the two pressure-sensor hoses for soot packing, kinks, or melt near the exhaust.
If soot load is high and a parked regen is allowed, attempt a forced/parked regen in a safe spot.
Check the sensor connector for corrosion or a backed-out pin before condemning the sensor.
common_misdiagnoses: Replacing the DPF when only the pressure tubes were plugged with soot.
Condemning the sensor when the real issue is a fully loaded DPF that needs a shop bake/clean.
Clearing the code without a regen — it returns within a few miles.

procedures_full.overview: DPF differential pressure — voltage high.
procedures_full.severity_action: Power derate likely — plan to stop soon
causes: Signal wire shorted to 5V
Failed sensor

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 3 means the DPF differential pressure sensor circuit is shorted high or open. It's Medium severity - regeneration scheduling can be disrupted, but there's no immediate derate risk. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com checks the two pressure sensing tubes first on this fault, since a pinched or disconnected tube causes the same reading as a failed sensor.
causes: Failed DPF differential pressure sensor
Electrical fault - internal sensor failure produces an out-of-range high signal.
Pinched, cracked, or disconnected pressure sensing tube
Mechanical fault - damage to either sensing tube produces an implausible pressure reading that mimics an electrical circuit fault.
Corroded sensor connector
Electrical fault - exposure to road spray near the frame rail can corrode the connector over time.
Chafed harness wire shorted to power
Electrical fault - a wire contacting a powered circuit injects voltage onto the signal line.
steps: Connect Volvo PTT and check the reported differential pressure value - a reading pegged at maximum scale confirms an open or shorted-high circuit.
Locate the DPF differential pressure sensor, typically mounted on the frame rail with two pressure tubes running to the DPF inlet and outlet.
Unplug the sensor connector and check for a short to power on the signal wire, and measure the sensor's baseline voltage output at key-on with no exhaust flow.
Inspect both pressure sensing tubes for pinches, cracks, or disconnection - a blocked or damaged tube can also produce an implausible pressure reading.
Check the sensor connector for corrosion, especially on trucks that see heavy road spray or wash-down exposure near the frame rail.
symptoms: Amber check engine light
Possible unnecessary or missed regeneration cycles
No immediate power loss
Dash message referencing aftertreatment system fault in some configurations

Short trips and excessive idle prevent soot burn-off, raising delta-P.
Ash accumulation causing permanent restriction
Ash cannot be burned — only professional cleaning or replacement resolves restriction.
Plugged or failed DPF pressure sensor lines
Carbon-blocked impulse tubes report falsely high restriction to the ECM.
steps: Read soot load % and DPF delta-P in Cummins INSITE — soot above 80% warrants forced regen; ash high with low soot means cleaning.
Inspect DPF pressure sensor tubes for carbon plugging — blow out with regulated shop air below 30 PSI.
Run forced parked regen and monitor delta-P — should drop below 3 PSI at idle if soot was the cause.

If delta-P stays high after regen with low soot, plan DPF ash cleaning or replacement.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 16 means the DPF differential pressure is higher than expected from soot buildup, usually because regen cycles aren't completing on a truck's typical driving pattern. This is your early warning before a soot-load derate. In many cases the fix is procedural - complete a full parked regeneration - rather than replacing hardware.
causes: Regen cycles interrupted before completion
Short trips or driver-cancelled regens never let soot fully burn off, so load accumulates over time.
Predominantly low-speed/idle duty cycle
Trucks that rarely reach highway exhaust temps rely more heavily on active regen, which can fall behind.
Cracked or clogged differential pressure sensor hoses
Gives a falsely elevated reading that doesn't reflect actual filter condition.
Upstream EGR or turbo issue increasing soot production
A fault elsewhere in the air/EGR system can push more soot into the DPF than normal.
steps: Check the DPF soot load percentage on a scan tool - values climbing steadily rather than resetting after regen point to a regen system that isn't completing successfully.
Review recent driving history - trucks running mostly short trips or heavy idle time don't reach the exhaust temperatures needed for passive/active regen and load up faster.
Inspect the differential pressure sensor's hoses for cracks, disconnection, or soot clogging, which can give a false high reading.
Verify a parked regeneration completes successfully when commanded, rather than aborting partway through.
Check for any recent EGR or turbo faults that could be increasing soot production upstream.
symptoms: Dash may show a DPF status warning lamp or increasing soot load percentage
Slightly reduced fuel economy as the engine works around the restriction
No performance loss yet, but a countdown toward derate if uncorrected
procedures_full.source_title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3251 FMI 16: High DPF Differential Pressure

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 16 means the ECM has confirmed genuinely elevated DPF backpressure from real soot loading. It's Medium severity - usually resolved with a forced regeneration rather than a filter replacement. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always checks the truck's recent duty cycle first, since short-trip or heavy-idle operation is the leading cause of this exact condition.
causes: Soot accumulation from a duty cycle that prevents natural regeneration
Not a component failure - short trips or excessive idle time keep exhaust temperatures too low for passive regeneration to occur.
Interrupted or incomplete regeneration cycles
Operational issue rather than a mechanical fault - a regen that keeps getting interrupted by stop-and-go driving allows soot to keep accumulating.
Blocked or moisture-contaminated pressure sensing tubes
Mechanical fault - contaminated tubes can produce an inaccurate but still elevated pressure reading.
Genuine DPF ash loading requiring physical cleaning
A real mechanical restriction from accumulated ash (from oil consumption) that regeneration alone cannot clear.
steps: Connect Scania SDP3 and check the actual soot load percentage and differential pressure reading to confirm this is a genuine restriction rather than a sensor glitch.
Verify the truck's recent duty cycle - extended idle time or short-trip city driving prevents the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature naturally and commonly causes this exact condition.
Check both pressure sensing tubes for soot blockage or moisture, which can produce an inaccurate reading even during a genuine restriction.
Perform a parked/stationary forced regeneration through SDP3 if the truck's duty cycle hasn't allowed a passive or active regen to complete recently.
If forced regeneration doesn't reduce the differential pressure reading, inspect the DPF for ash loading requiring a physical cleaning or professional service.
symptoms: Amber check engine light with a DPF-related dash message
Reduced fuel economy from increased backpressure
Possible mild power loss under heavy load
Frequent automatic regeneration cycles as the ECM tries to manage soot load
procedures_full.source_title: Scania SPN 3251 FMI 16: DPF Differential Pressure Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3251 FMI 18 means the DPF differential pressure reading is lower than expected, usually from a clogged sense tube rather than a real restriction. It's a Medium severity fault that's inexpensive to fix once you find the blocked line. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this one resolved with a can of brake cleaner and a length of stiff wire more often than with a new sensor - always clear the tubes first.
causes: Carbon-clogged differential pressure sense tube
A mechanical restriction inside the small sense line itself, not the sensor - soot packs the narrow tube and produces a falsely low reading.
Disconnected or damaged sense tube
A physical plumbing fault where the tube has come loose or cracked, letting exhaust pressure escape before reaching the sensor.
Corroded sensor electrical connector
An electrical/wiring fault that produces an inaccurate reading despite the pressure tubes being clear.
Failed differential pressure sensor
A genuine sensor component failure, confirmed only after ruling out both sense tubes and the connector.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and check both DPF differential pressure sense tubes for physical damage, disconnection, or a pinched line.
Inspect both sense ports at the exhaust pipe for carbon blockage, since a partially clogged tube reads lower pressure than actually exists.
Check the sensor's electrical connector for corrosion or a loose pin that could cause an artificially low reading.

Compare differential pressure readings at idle versus under load - a sensor or tube issue typically shows an inconsistent or flat reading regardless of load, while a real restriction climbs with exhaust flow.
If both tubes and the connector check out, test the sensor itself against a known specification using a calibrated pressure source.
symptoms: Check engine light with no immediate power loss
DPF soot load percentage reading that seems inconsistent with actual driving pattern
No noticeable performance change in most cases
Possible failed or skipped automatic regen cycles due to inconsistent pressure data

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 – DPF Soot Level High Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 – DPF Soot Level High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) has reached a high soot load level and requires regeneration. This code commonly appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines when regeneration cycles are incomplete.
Symptoms
Regen light illuminated
Check engine light on
Reduced engine power
Possible engine derate
Cause
This fault code is triggered when excessive soot accumulates inside the DPF due to frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed active regeneration, or malfunctioning aftertreatment components.
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible, but continued operation without regeneration can lead to severe engine derate or shutdown.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. If regeneration fails or the code returns, seek professional diagnostics to inspect the DPF system and related sensors.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 mean?
 
It indicates the DPF soot load is high and regeneration is required to prevent engine power reduction.
 
 
What causes SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
It indicates the DPF soot load is high and regeneration is required to prevent engine power reduction.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
Short-distance driving may be possible, but ignoring the fault can trigger engine derate or shutdown.
 
 
Will SPN 3719 cause a derate?
 
Complete a successful regeneration and repair any underlying DPF issues.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
The fault will clear after a successful regeneration and once the soot level returns to normal. If the code remains active, further diagnostics of the DPF system may be required.

SPN 1569 FMI 31
SPN 5246 FMI 0
SPN 3364 FMI 2

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 – DPF Soot Level High Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 – DPF Soot Level High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) has reached a high soot load level and requires regeneration. This code commonly appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines when regeneration cycles are incomplete.
Symptoms
Regen light illuminated
Check engine light on
Reduced engine power
Possible engine derate
Cause
This fault code is triggered when excessive soot accumulates inside the DPF due to frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed active regeneration, or malfunctioning aftertreatment components.
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible, but continued operation without regeneration can lead to severe engine derate or shutdown.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. If regeneration fails or the code returns, seek professional diagnostics to inspect the DPF system and related sensors.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3719 FMI 0 mean?
 
It indicates the DPF soot load is high and regeneration is required to prevent engine power reduction.
 
 
What causes SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
It indicates the DPF soot load is high and regeneration is required to prevent engine power reduction.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
Short-distance driving may be possible, but ignoring the fault can trigger engine derate or shutdown.
 
 
Will SPN 3719 cause a derate?
 
Complete a successful regeneration and repair any underlying DPF issues.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3719 FMI 0?
 
The fault will clear after a successful regeneration and once the soot level returns to normal. If the code remains active, further diagnostics of the DPF system may be required.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can I perform a parked regen without DiagnosticLink?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: On many Detroit-equipped trucks, a dash-initiated parked regen can be triggered through a button or menu without a service tool, provided no inhibits are active. If the regen button is grayed out or unavailable, DiagnosticLink may be needed to clear an inhibit condition before the regen can proceed.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will highway driving clear SPN 3719 FMI 31 on its own?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: If the soot load is not yet at the maximum, sustained highway driving at load can sometimes allow passive regen to reduce soot loading enough to clear the code. However, once the fault is active at FMI 31, the ECM has already determined passive regen is insufficient. A parked regen is the more reliable path.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does this code affect emissions compliance?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: A properly functioning DPF regen cycle is part of the certified emission control system. Running with excessive soot loading and avoiding regen can affect particulate emissions. Beyond compliance, a filter that is not maintained can sustain heat damage during eventual regeneration.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on DPF status indicates the highest severity class, commonly associated with severe restriction or ash accumulation requiring service. Ash accumulation at high mileage, repeated incomplete cleaning regens, damaged substrate, and ignored maintenance intervals are the primary causes. Ash service intervals missed on high-idle vocational trucks are a documented pattern. Sensing validation is required before condemning DPF hardware — a delta-P sensor or hose fault can produce a false severe status without any actual restriction. The service decision is DPF cleaning or replacement based on measured restriction and ash strategy after sensing is confirmed.
causes: Ash accumulation at high mileage — ash load requiring DPF cleaning or replacement
Repeated incomplete cleaning regens — soot accumulation from incomplete regens
Damaged substrate — physical DPF damage
Ignored maintenance intervals — ash service intervals missed
False status from sensing fault — delta-P sensor or hose fault producing false severe status
steps: Single Action Gate — Validate Delta-P Sensor and Hoses

Validate the delta-P sensor and hoses before any DPF hardware decision. A delta-P sensor or hose fault can produce a false severe status without any actual restriction. Inspect hoses for contamination and blockage. Verify sensor baseline at KOEO is near zero differential pressure.
Binary Decision Gate — Review Mileage and Service History

Review mileage and service history. Ash accumulation at high mileage is the most common cause of highest-severity DPF status. Confirm whether ash service intervals have been followed. High-idle vocational trucks accumulate ash faster than highway trucks.
Override Manager — Perform OEM Service Routine

Perform the OEM service routine for highest-severity DPF status. Some platforms require specific service procedures before DPF removal. Follow OEM procedures for the specific platform and DPF configuration.
Safety Interceptor — Remove and Inspect DPF

Remove and inspect the DPF for physical damage and ash accumulation. A DPF with confirmed ash accumulation requires professional cleaning or replacement. A DPF with physical substrate damage requires replacement — cleaning cannot restore a damaged substrate.
Resume Point — Professional DPF Cleaning Assessment

Assess whether professional DPF cleaning can restore the filter. A DPF with ash accumulation but no substrate damage can often be restored by professional cleaning. A DPF with substrate damage or severe soot accumulation beyond cleaning limits requires replacement.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Status Confirmation

After DPF service, verify status returns to normal. Perform a successful regen after DPF service to confirm the filter is functioning. Monitor for return of highest-severity status over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Clean or Replace Decision

Professional DPF cleaning if ash accumulation is confirmed and substrate is intact. DPF replacement if substrate damage is confirmed or cleaning limits are exceeded. Address upstream soot contributors before returning to service.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair delta-P sensor or hoses if sensing fault is confirmed.
2 . Professional DPF cleaning if ash accumulation is confirmed and substrate is intact.
3 . DPF replacement if substrate damage is confirmed or cleaning limits are exceeded.
4 . Address upstream soot contributors before returning to service.
5 . Perform required service resets after DPF service.
Verification Steps
Confirm DPF status returns to normal after service.
Verify successful regen after DPF service.
Confirm SPN 3719 FMI 0 does not return after service.
Monitor for return of highest-severity status over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Follow OEM ash service intervals — do not extend beyond recommended mileage.
✓ Monitor regen completion rates — frequent incomplete regens accelerate ash accumulation.
✓ Inspect delta-P sensor hoses at every major aftertreatment service.
✓ Plan DPF cleaning at OEM-recommended ash load intervals for vocational trucks.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High. Severe status usually requires service before continued dispatch. Sensing validation takes minutes and prevents unnecessary DPF replacement for a sensor fault.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3719 FMI 0 means Cummins ash load model shows the DPF is ash-packed. Forced regen removes soot only — plan professional DPF cleaning or replacement. Ash is non-combustible residue from burned oil and fuel additives that remains after soot oxidizes during regen. When ash load crosses the Cummins calibrated threshold, SPN 3719 sets and exhaust restriction climbs regardless of regen attempts.
causes: Normal ash accumulation at high engine hours
Ash builds in the DPF substrate over hundreds of thousands of miles and cannot be burned away.
Excessive oil consumption
Burned crankcase oil leaves metallic ash deposits faster than the ash model predicts.
Faulty DPF pressure sensor skewing ash model
Plugged impulse lines can cause incorrect ash load calculation and false high-ash faults.
steps: Read ash load % and soot load % with Cummins INSITE — ash above service threshold confirms ash packing.
Measure DPF differential pressure before and after forced regen; pressure above 8–12 PSI at idle after regen points to ash restriction.
Inspect DPF pressure sensor impulse lines for soot plugging that can corrupt ash model calculations.
Check oil consumption — burning 1 qt per 1,000 miles accelerates ash loading significantly.
Schedule DPF thermal cleaning or replacement; do not rely on parked regen to clear ash faults.
symptoms: Amber MIL with DPF or exhaust system message
Regen cycles complete but restriction remains high
Sluggish acceleration and reduced fuel economy
Ash load percentage high in scan tool data
Soot load low while ash load climbs on high-mileage units

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3719 FMI 1 means Detroit Diesel ash load model reads lower than expected. Perform ash load reset after DPF service and verify pressure sensor inputs. The ash load model estimates non-combustible material in the DPF based on operating history and pressure data. After DPF service, Detroit Diesel may set SPN 3719 FMI 1 until the model is reset and relearned.
causes: Ash load model not reset after DPF cleaning or replacement
ECM retains old ash data against a new or cleaned filter substrate.
Faulty DPF pressure sensor inputs
Implausible pressure data drives ash model below expected range.
Incorrect DPF part installed
Wrong filter specifications change pressure characteristics and confuse ash model.
steps: After DPF replacement or cleaning, perform ash load reset in Detroit DDDL8 per OEM procedure.
Verify DPF pressure sensor readings are plausible — inlet and outlet pressures should differ during loaded driving.
Drive 200+ highway miles after reset to allow ash model to relearn.
Confirm correct DPF part number was installed — wrong substrate type skews ash model.
If ash load stays at zero, check for pressure sensor circuit faults feeding the ash estimation algorithm.
symptoms: Ash load reads 0% or unusually low after DPF service
Amber MIL after DPF cleaning or replacement
Ash load does not increase over driving miles as expected
Possible stacked DPF pressure sensor codes
Regen behavior may be abnormal until ash model stabilizes

Ash builds in the DPF substrate over hundreds of thousands of miles and cannot be burned away.
Excessive oil consumption
Burned crankcase oil leaves metallic ash deposits faster than the ash model predicts.
Faulty DPF pressure sensor skewing ash model
Plugged impulse lines can cause incorrect ash load calculation and false high-ash faults.
steps: Read ash load % and soot load % with Jaltest — ash above service threshold confirms ash packing.
Measure DPF differential pressure before and after forced regen; pressure above 8–12 PSI at idle after regen points to ash restriction.
Inspect DPF pressure sensor impulse lines for soot plugging that can corrupt ash model calculations.
Check oil consumption — burning 1 qt per 1,000 miles accelerates ash loading significantly.
Schedule DPF thermal cleaning or replacement; do not rely on parked regen to clear ash faults.

procedures_full.overview: The diesel particulate filter (DPF) soot load has climbed into the high range. The ECM is asking for a regeneration. Caught early this is just a regen; ignored, soot keeps building toward a forced derate (often SPN 3719 FMI 0) and eventually a plugged DPF.
procedures_full.severity_action: Limp to the next safe stop
causes: Lots of idling or short, low-load trips that prevent passive regen
Repeatedly canceled/interrupted regens
A fault blocking regen (DPF pressure sensor, EGR, or dosing issue)
Genuinely loaded DPF approaching its limit
first_moves: If conditions allow, perform a parked/forced regen in a safe spot, or run a steady highway load to trigger an active regen.
Check for companion codes that could be blocking regen (DPF pressure, EGR, DEF).
Don't keep canceling regens — each cancel pushes soot load higher.
Note the soot-load % from the dash/scan tool to track whether the regen actually worked.
common_misdiagnoses: Clearing the code without running a regen — soot load is still high and it returns fast.
Replacing the DPF when a forced regen would have recovered it.
Treating a high-soot warning as 'nothing' until it escalates into a derate.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 4364 FMI 18 – EGR Flow Fault Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4364 FMI 18 – EGR Flow Fault (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4364 FMI 18 indicates an issue with Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) flow. This code appears when the EGR system is not operating within expected parameters and can contribute to emissions system faults.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Rough idle
Reduced fuel efficiency
Increased exhaust smoke
Possible aftertreatment warnings
Cause
This fault is commonly triggered by a stuck EGR valve, clogged EGR cooler, faulty EGR differential pressure sensor, or restricted exhaust passages.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR flow issues can lead to additional emissions faults and eventual engine derate.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve and cooler for blockage or failure. Verify proper sensor readings and clean or replace faulty components as needed.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4364 FMI 18 mean?
 
SPN 4364 FMI 18 indicates that Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) flow is outside the expected operating range.
 
 
What causes SPN 4364 FMI 18?
 
Common causes include a stuck EGR valve, clogged EGR cooler, faulty differential pressure sensor, or restricted exhaust passages.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4364 FMI 18?
 
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR faults can contribute to emissions issues and engine derate.
 
 
Will SPN 4364 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If EGR flow remains incorrect, the engine control module may reduce power to protect emissions components.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 4364 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and clean the EGR valve and cooler, test related sensors, and verify proper exhaust flow before clearing the code.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Cummins SPN 4364 FMI 18 �?SCR NOx Conversion Efficiency Below Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is SPN 4364 FMI 18 likely to require SCR catalyst replacement?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Not necessarily �?and in the field, DEF quality, dosing faults, and NOx sensor issues are frequently the root cause rather than a failed catalyst. Before replacing an SCR catalyst, confirm the DEF is correct concentration, the dosing system is injecting the right amount, and both NOx sensors are reading plausibly. Replacing a catalyst when the actual issue is a clogged dosing injector or a skewed sensor is expensive and leaves the real cause in place.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can this code clear without a shop visit if the DEF issue is corrected?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: If DEF quality was the root cause, refilling with properly concentrated, uncontaminated DEF and driving enough miles for the ECM to recalculate efficiency may allow the code to go inactive. However, if the inducement counter has accumulated significant distance, Cummins Insite may be required to reset the inducement counter after confirming the aftertreatment system is operating within limits.

troubleshooting_faq.question: What is the difference between SPN 4364 FMI 18 and SPN 3364 FMI 1 on a Cummins?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: SPN 3364 FMI 1 is a direct DEF concentration measurement �?the DEF quality sensor reads the fluid and finds it below specification. SPN 4364 FMI 18 is a system performance calculation �?the ECM measures how much NOx the catalyst removed and finds it insufficient. SPN 3364 points directly at fluid quality; SPN 4364 can result from fluid quality, dosing volume, sensor accuracy, or catalyst condition.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 4364 FMI 18 �?SCR Conversion Efficiency Below Threshold | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is SPN 4364 FMI 18 a sign the catalyst needs replacement?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Not automatically. A thorough diagnostic should rule out DEF quality problems, dosing issues, and NOx sensor drift first �?all of which can cause this code without actual catalyst failure. However, if those checks come back normal and the truck has high mileage, the catalyst is a strong suspect.

troubleshooting_faq.question: What is the difference between SPN 4364 and SPN 3226 on a Detroit DD15?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: SPN 3226 is the raw downstream NOx sensor reading �?it tells you how much NOx is coming out of the SCR brick. SPN 4364 is a calculated efficiency value �?the ECM's judgment of how well the catalyst is performing based on both sensors and the dosing model. A fault on 3226 may be a sensor issue; a fault on 4364 points to the overall SCR system not meeting its NOx reduction target.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does SPN 4364 FMI 18 affect emissions compliance?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: By definition, a system not meeting its conversion efficiency target is not keeping NOx within the certified emission standard. While this is primarily a vehicle performance and regulatory concern rather than an immediate roadside enforcement trigger, addressing it is important for both environmental compliance and avoiding escalating derate conditions.

causes: This fault is commonly triggered by a stuck EGR valve, clogged EGR cooler, faulty EGR differential pressure sensor, or restricted exhaust passages.

DEF quality below specification: diluted fluid, wrong fluid, or fluid degraded from age or heat cycling DEF dosing system fault: injector clogged, pump pressure low, or incorrect DEF quantity being delivered relative to exhaust conditions SCR catalyst degraded from thermal aging, sulfur poisoning, or hydrocarbon fouling from repeated failed or incomplete DPF regen events Upstream NOx sensor reading lower than actual NOx, making the catalyst appear less efficient than it is Downstream NOx sensor reading higher than actual NOx, artificially deflating the efficiency calculation Exhaust leak between the DEF dosing injector and the SCR catalyst, reducing the DEF concentration available for the catalytic reaction

SCR catalyst aged beyond effective conversion capability - common after 300,000 - 00,000+ miles depending on DEF quality history Poor DEF quality reducing the amount of effective reductant available to the catalyst DEF dosing rate below target - worn dosing pump, clogged injector, or air ingestion in the DEF supply line Upstream or downstream NOx sensor drifting, producing a false efficiency calculation Exhaust system leak between the dosing injector and SCR brick, diluting the reductant before it reaches the catalyst
common problems affect how the engine runs and its environmental impact.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 1 means Cummins SCR is not converting enough NOx. Check DEF quality, doser operation, and NOx sensor plausibility before replacing the catalyst. The SCR system reduces NOx by injecting DEF into hot exhaust. When conversion efficiency drops below calibrated limits, Cummins sets SPN 4364 and inducement timers may begin counting down toward derate.
causes: Contaminated or diluted DEF fluid
DEF below 32.5% urea concentration reduces NOx conversion and sets efficiency faults.
Failed DEF doser or low DEF pressure
Insufficient DEF delivery at the SCR inlet prevents adequate NOx reduction.
Degraded or poisoned SCR catalyst
Coolant leaks, oil ash, or thermal damage reduce catalyst conversion efficiency permanently.
steps: Connect Cummins INSITE and monitor upstream/downstream NOx ppm during steady 1,500 RPM — efficiency below 70% confirms SCR underperformance.
Test DEF concentration with refractometer — target 32.5% urea; readings below 30% cause efficiency faults.
Inspect DEF doser injector for crystallization and verify DEF pressure at 130–145 PSI during dosing.
Check exhaust for coolant smell indicating head gasket leak poisoning the SCR catalyst.
Verify NOx sensor readings are plausible — intake reading above 800 ppm at idle may indicate bad upstream sensor.
symptoms: Amber or red MIL with emissions warning
Visible white DEF crystallization at doser or exhaust
SCR inducement timer counting down
Low DEF consumption relative to miles driven
High upstream NOx with low downstream reduction in live data

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 3 on Peterbilt means the SCR NOx conversion efficiency monitor circuit voltage is above the ECM maximum. Test NOx sensor wiring and 5V reference before assuming low SCR efficiency. SPN 4364 tracks how effectively the SCR catalyst converts NOx using upstream and downstream sensor data. FMI 3 specifically flags an electrical voltage-high condition in the efficiency calculation circuit — not confirmed poor SCR performance. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees Peterbilt operators confuse FMI 3 with FMI 18 and order unnecessary OneBox assemblies. Work the NOx sensor harness and ACM inputs first.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 or Noregon JPRO and confirm SPN 4364 FMI 3. Record upstream and downstream NOx sensor voltages — typical good sensors output 0.5V-4.5V proportional to NOx ppm on a 5V reference.

Key on, engine off: measure 5V reference at the ACM NOx efficiency input connector. Supply should read 4.75V-5.25V. Signal voltage above 4.8V with sensors disconnected indicates harness short to power.
Inspect upstream (SPN 3216) and downstream (SPN 3226) NOx sensor connectors for coolant or DEF contamination. Resistance between signal and ground below 1 kΩ at the harness confirms a short.

Perform a DEF quality test with a refractometer (32.5% target) and verify DEF tank level — electrical FMI 3 does not require DEF checks, but companion efficiency faults often follow ignored DEF issues.
After wiring repair, run a stationary SCR efficiency test in Davie4. Conversion efficiency should calculate 70%-95% at 1800 RPM loaded idle once both NOx sensors report valid data.
symptoms: Amber check engine or aftertreatment warning lamp
NOx conversion efficiency parameter pegged at maximum or showing implausible values on Davie4
Possible loss of SCR monitor readiness until fault is cleared
Companion NOx sensor voltage codes (SPN 3226 or SPN 3217) may appear with shared harness damage
No immediate derate on most calibrations, but inducement may follow if efficiency data stays invalid

procedures_full.overview: Volvo SPN 4364 FMI 3 means the SCR NOx conversion efficiency sensor circuit voltage is above normal, indicating an open or high-resistance sensor circuit rather than a catalyst failure. This CRITICAL fault triggers SCR derate and inducement shutdown countdown on Volvo D13/D11 engines. Diagnose with Texa or Jaltest to confirm the circuit fault before any catalyst or DEF components are replaced.
causes: Heat-damaged NOx efficiency sensor wiring harness

The harness routing along the SCR catalyst body is exposed to extreme heat during regen cycles. Insulation degrades and wires chafe on mounting brackets, causing an open circuit that the ECM reads as FMI 3 high voltage.
Failed NOx efficiency sensor (open internal element)

The NOx sensing element inside the catalyst assembly ages and eventually fails open, removing the signal load and causing the ECM to read above 4.75 V. Sensor removal and resistance testing confirms this failure mode.
Corroded or loose sensor connector at the SCR outlet

Moisture and exhaust condensate corrode the NOx sensor connector pins. A corroded pin with high contact resistance creates the same open-circuit voltage signature as FMI 3, even when the sensor itself is functional.
steps: Connect Texa Navigator TXTs or Jaltest to the J1939 data link. Navigate to Aftertreatment > SCR and read SPN 4364 live data. FMI 3 (voltage above normal) typically indicates the NOx efficiency sensor signal wire has gone open or high-resistance, reading above 4.75 V on the ECM input.

Locate the SCR NOx efficiency sensor (mounted on the SCR catalyst outlet or integrated into the NOx sensor assembly on the Volvo D13 aftertreatment module). Inspect the connector for corrosion, backed-out pins, or heat damage from proximity to the SCR catalyst body.

Unplug the NOx efficiency sensor connector and measure signal-wire voltage at the harness side to chassis ground. At key-on engine-off with the sensor disconnected: if voltage reads 4.9-5.0 V (near reference rail), the signal wire is open between the sensor and ECM. A healthy circuit should read near 0 V with the sensor unplugged.

Measure continuity on the signal wire from the harness connector back to the ECM connector. Any open confirms wiring damage. Inspect the harness routing along the SCR canister - heat from the SCR body degrades insulation over time, and the harness frequently chafes on the canister mounting brackets.

After repairing wiring or replacing the NOx sensor, clear faults with Texa or Jaltest, perform a drive cycle at operating temperature, and confirm SPN 4364 reads within the expected efficiency range (typically 70-95% at steady highway load). Verify the inducement countdown has reset.
symptoms: Amber SCR warning lamp followed by red inducement lamp within hours or days if fault persists.
Engine enters SCR-related derate, reducing power progressively as the inducement countdown advances.
DEF gauge and system appear normal because the fault is in the NOx efficiency sensor circuit, not the DEF supply.
Possible yellow or red Stop Engine light if inducement countdown reaches the final phase.
No perceptible exhaust odor change because the DEF dosing and catalyst may still be functioning while the sensor circuit has failed.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 15 means SCR NOx conversion efficiency is trending below target at the least-severe warning level. It's a medium-severity code with no derate yet - check DEF quality and doser spray pattern before it escalates. This is the earliest stage of an SCR efficiency warning, giving you the best chance to fix a cheap DEF quality issue before it develops into a derate-triggering fault. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always starts with a refractometer check on DEF quality, since it's the fastest and cheapest thing to rule out.
causes: Diluted or contaminated DEF fluid
DEF that doesn't meet the 32.5% urea concentration specification reduces NOx conversion effectiveness even with a perfectly functioning doser.
Partially clogged or worn doser injector
An inconsistent spray pattern from the doser reduces even DEF distribution across the catalyst, lowering measured conversion efficiency.
Aging or degraded NOx sensors
Inlet or outlet NOx sensors drifting out of calibration can report an efficiency reading that doesn't reflect the catalyst's true performance.
steps: Pull the fault on Navistar diagnostic software or Jaltest and check inlet versus outlet NOx sensor readings side by side.
Test DEF quality with a refractometer to confirm it meets the 32.5% urea concentration specification.
Inspect the DEF doser injector spray pattern for partial clogging or an inconsistent spray cone.
Check for any DEF crystallization buildup in the SCR mixing chamber, which can reduce effective dosing even with a healthy doser.
Run a parked regeneration if soot loading upstream may be affecting SCR inlet temperature and dosing enable conditions.
Clear the code and monitor NOx conversion efficiency trend data over the following drive cycles to confirm improvement.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp, no derate at this stage
No noticeable drivability complaint
Possible slightly increased DEF consumption

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 17 means the Mercedes-Benz SCR catalyst is converting NOx below normal at the least severe warning level. It is Medium severity, an early warning stage, and worth addressing promptly to avoid progressing toward a full operator inducement derate. SCR conversion efficiency codes track how effectively the catalyst is turning NOx into harmless nitrogen and water using DEF, and SPN 4364 FMI 17 represents the earliest, least severe warning level in that tracking system. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always recommends treating this fault as an opportunity to catch a developing problem early, since DEF quality issues and doser spray pattern problems are both inexpensive to check and fix at this stage, well before the fault escalates into the far more disruptive inducement derate that comes with higher severity levels.
causes: Diluted, contaminated, or expired DEF fluid
DEF that doesn't meet the required 32.5% urea concentration reduces the SCR system's ability to effectively convert NOx, even with everything else working correctly.
Weak or partially clogged DEF doser spray pattern
A doser injector with a degraded spray pattern doesn't atomize DEF properly, reducing the effective dosing reaching the catalyst even if the commanded quantity is correct.
Drifted or inaccurate NOx sensor readings
Intake or outlet NOx sensors that have drifted out of calibration can make the ECM believe conversion efficiency is lower than it actually is.
Early catalyst aging or ash accumulation
Over very high mileage, the catalyst substrate itself can begin losing conversion capability, though this is less common than fluid quality or dosing issues at this early severity level.
steps: Connect a Mercedes-Benz compatible diagnostic tool and confirm SPN 4364 FMI 17, then review recent DEF quality and dosing rate history.
Check DEF quality with a refractometer to confirm it meets the required concentration specification, since diluted or contaminated DEF is a common cause of reduced conversion efficiency.
Inspect the DEF injector/doser for a weak spray pattern or partial clogging, which can reduce effective dosing even with good quality fluid.
Verify the intake and outlet NOx sensors are reading accurately and haven't drifted out of calibration, since inaccurate sensor data can mimic a real efficiency problem.
Address any confirmed DEF quality, dosing, or sensor issue, clear codes, and monitor conversion efficiency trend over the next several drive cycles.
symptoms: MIL illuminated
No immediate drivability change at this severity level
Possible slightly elevated NOx readings on emissions testing
Risk of progressing to a more severe inducement fault if left unaddressed

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 18 indicates low SCR catalyst conversion efficiency in Detroit Diesel engines. It can lead to engine derate, affecting power and speed. Immediate diagnosis is essential to prevent downtimes. In the shop, nothing halts productivity quite like an SCR-related code. When a Detroit Diesel engine throws SPN 4364 FMI 18, you're dealing with an SCR catalyst conversion efficiency problem. This isn't just a warning light; it can lead to a dreaded engine derate, limiting your truck's speed and power. Drivers usually notice a drop in performance before the check engine light blinks on. The code tells you the SCR catalyst isn't doing its job—converting NOx effectively. This page will help you understand the root causes, what to look for, and whether it's time to call a tow truck. Before you start swapping parts, we’ll guide you through the most likely culprits and common pitfalls in diagnosing this fault. From DEF fluid contamination to injector issues, understanding these systems' intricacies can save you a lot of time and frustration. With an engine derate looming, time is of the essence to get this resolved efficiently.
causes: DEF Fluid Contamination
Contaminated DEF fluid can drastically affect SCR efficiency. Poor storage conditions or using non-compliant DEF can lead to crystallization and clogging of the SCR system.
DEF Injector Malfunction
A DEF injector not spraying correctly can cause uneven distribution of DEF, leading to poor NOx conversion and triggering the fault code.
SCR Catalyst Blockage
Blockage within the SCR catalyst can occur due to particulate accumulation or physical damage, impeding exhaust flow and reducing conversion efficiency.
NOx Sensor Failure
Faulty NOx sensors can report incorrect data to the ECM, causing it to misjudge the SCR system's performance and set off the code.
steps: Inspect DEF Fluid: Use a refractometer to check DEF quality. Ensure it's within the correct urea concentration (32.5%). Contaminated DEF needs immediate replacement.
Check DEF Injector: Remove and visually inspect the DEF injector for crystallization or blockage. Clean with warm water if clogged.
Examine SCR Catalyst: With the vehicle on a lift, inspect the SCR catalyst for any visible physical damage or blockage.
Scan for Additional Codes: Use a diagnostic tool to check for related codes that may indicate underlying issues.
Measure Catalyst Inlet Temperature: Use an infrared thermometer to measure the temperature at the SCR catalyst inlet. It should be consistent with OEM specifications.
Assess NOx Sensors: Verify the operation of upstream and downstream NOx sensors with live data. Replace if readings are erratic.
symptoms: Noticeable loss of engine power and performance, often leading to a 5 mph speed limit.
Check Engine Light illuminated, often accompanied by other SCR-related codes.
Increased fuel consumption as the engine compensates for inefficient NOx conversion.
Unusual exhaust smoke or odor indicating improper NOx breakdown.
Frequent regeneration cycles as the system attempts to clear faults.
Driver reports of DEF tank levels dropping more rapidly than usual.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 18 means International SCR is not converting enough NOx. Check DEF quality, doser operation, and NOx sensor plausibility before replacing the catalyst. The SCR system reduces NOx by injecting DEF into hot exhaust. When conversion efficiency drops below calibrated limits, International sets SPN 4364 and inducement timers may begin counting down toward derate.
causes: Contaminated or diluted DEF fluid
DEF below 32.5% urea concentration reduces NOx conversion and sets efficiency faults.
Failed DEF doser or low DEF pressure
Insufficient DEF delivery at the SCR inlet prevents adequate NOx reduction.
Degraded or poisoned SCR catalyst
Coolant leaks, oil ash, or thermal damage reduce catalyst conversion efficiency permanently.
steps: Connect ServiceMaxx and monitor upstream/downstream NOx ppm during steady 1,500 RPM — efficiency below 70% confirms SCR underperformance.
Test DEF concentration with refractometer — target 32.5% urea; readings below 30% cause efficiency faults.
Inspect DEF doser injector for crystallization and verify DEF pressure at 130–145 PSI during dosing.
Check exhaust for coolant smell indicating head gasket leak poisoning the SCR catalyst.
Verify NOx sensor readings are plausible — intake reading above 800 ppm at idle may indicate bad upstream sensor.
symptoms: Amber or red MIL with emissions warning
Visible white DEF crystallization at doser or exhaust
SCR inducement timer counting down
Low DEF consumption relative to miles driven
High upstream NOx with low downstream reduction in live data

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4364 FMI 18 on Cummins means the SCR catalyst is not converting enough NOx — efficiency is below the moderately severe threshold. The truck will derate. Check DEF quality with a refractometer and verify dosing system function before spending money on a new catalyst. When the SCR system efficiency drops below threshold on a Cummins, the natural assumption is a dead catalyst. That assumption costs fleets thousands of dollars every year. The real culprit is DEF quality the majority of the time, followed by dosing system issues, and only then actual catalyst degradation. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com diagnoses SPN 4364 FMI 18 from the cheapest cause to the most expensive — every time.
causes: Off-spec or degraded DEF (aftertreatment)

DEF with incorrect urea concentration (below 30% or above 36%) reduces ammonia generation in the SCR catalyst, directly lowering conversion efficiency. Contaminated, diluted, or stored-too-long DEF is the most frequent cause of this fault on Cummins platforms.
Failed or fouled DEF dosing injector (aftertreatment)

The DEF dosing injector nozzle can crystallize with urea deposits, partially or fully blocking the spray pattern. Reduced DEF delivery into the exhaust stream directly reduces available ammonia for NOx reduction across the SCR catalyst.
Degraded SCR catalyst (aftertreatment)
Moderate

Over time and high mileage, the SCR catalyst active sites are reduced by thermal aging, sulfur poisoning, or hydrocarbon fouling from oil consumption. When conversion efficiency falls below the ECM's threshold even with proper dosing, catalyst replacement is the end result.
Failed or contaminated NOx sensor (electrical)
Moderate

A contaminated upstream NOx sensor reading falsely low will make the calculated efficiency appear lower than actual. A failed downstream sensor reading falsely high also produces a false-low efficiency calculation. Both sensor locations must be verified before condemning the catalyst.
steps: 1. Connect Cummins INSITE and check the live SCR NOx conversion efficiency percentage. Also read upstream NOx sensor (before SCR) and downstream NOx sensor (after SCR) simultaneously. At steady highway cruise, a healthy system should show upstream NOx 150-400 ppm at load and downstream NOx below 50 ppm.

2. Check DEF quality with a refractometer — spec is 32.5% urea concentration, corresponding to a refractive index of 1.3814-1.3818 at 20°C. Contaminated, diluted, or water-only DEF is the single most common cause of SCR efficiency faults on Cummins platforms.

3. Run the DEF dosing system diagnostic in INSITE. Verify DEF pump pressure is within spec (typically 600-1,000 kPa / 87-145 psi on Cummins ISX). Test the DEF dosing injector on/off function and check for injector nozzle fouling — a clogged nozzle delivers partial or no spray.

4. With both NOx sensors visible in INSITE live data during a steady-load highway test, compare upstream to downstream readings. If upstream NOx is normal but downstream is nearly as high as upstream (low differential), the catalyst is not converting. If upstream NOx reads implausibly low at load, suspect a contaminated or failed upstream sensor masking the true efficiency.

5. If DEF quality and dosing are confirmed good, attempt a forced SCR desulfurization cycle in INSITE (where available for your calibration). Sulfur deposits temporarily inhibit SCR catalyst activity and respond to a high-temperature desulfurization event.
symptoms: NOx/aftertreatment warning lamp illuminated
Staged power derate, typically starting at 25% reduction
INSITE showing SCR efficiency percentage below 70-80%
Exhaust may smell of ammonia if over-dosing is occurring
Possible active regen activity as ECM attempts to restore catalyst function
