procedures_full.overview: SPN 653 FMI 5 on a Cummins engine means the cylinder 3 injector solenoid drive circuit has an open circuit — the ECM fired the injector command but detected no current. Measure solenoid resistance at the connector before removing the injector. Cummins SPN 653 FMI 5 flags an open circuit in the cylinder 3 injector driver on ISX15 and X15 engines. The ECM expects to see a current return of 15 to 25 amps during the peak-and-hold injection event; FMI 5 means that current never flows. The result is a cylinder that does not fire, contributing to rough idle, white smoke, and a power reduction proportional to the lost cylinder. At ProfessionalDieselRepair.com, the first step is always to measure solenoid resistance (0.4 to 0.6 Ohm at room temperature) at the injector connector before pulling the injector — because valve cover harness failures cause the same code and are less expensive to repair.
causes: Failed injector solenoid coil (open winding)
The solenoid winding inside the injector body breaks, usually due to thermal fatigue from repeated high-current pulses over millions of injection events. Resistance measures above 5 Ohm or OL.
Open circuit in the valve cover harness wiring
The harness routing over the cylinder head is subject to extreme heat cycling. The conductor breaks inside the insulation, creating an open that the ECM sees as a missing solenoid.
Corroded or damaged injector connector pins

Oil contamination and heat cycling degrade the small-gauge pins in the 2-pin injector connector. A high-resistance connection (above 1 Ohm) can generate enough voltage drop to prevent the ECM from detecting adequate current return.
ECM injector driver output failure (rare)

The ECM output driver for cylinder 3 can fail open, preventing any current from reaching the injector. This is confirmed by comparing injector resistance (in spec) against a known-good driver output voltage during a commanded injection event.
steps: Connect Cummins INSITE to the J1939 diagnostic connector on the truck. Read active fault codes, confirm SPN 653 FMI 5, then run the Cylinder Contribution Test under special tests. A cylinder 3 contribution reading near zero while all others are normal confirms the injector or its circuit is the fault source. Diesel Laptops with NEXIQ USB-Link 2 can also perform this test.

Access the cylinder 3 injector connector (Cummins ISX15: top-mounted injector under the valve cover, routed through the valve cover harness). With the key off and engine off for at least 2 minutes to discharge the rail, disconnect the 2-pin injector connector. Set a DVOM to ohms and measure resistance between the two solenoid pins. Expected resistance at room temperature: 0.4 to 0.6 Ohm for ISX15 and X15 solenoid injectors. A reading above 5 Ohm or open (OL) indicates an internal injector solenoid failure.

If the injector solenoid resistance is in specification, check the harness for continuity from each injector connector pin back to the ECM connector. Set the DVOM to continuity or low-ohm mode. Each wire should show less than 0.5 Ohm end-to-end resistance. An open reading on either wire indicates a broken conductor in the valve cover harness, commonly caused by heat cycling near the injector cup.

Inspect the injector connector pins for corrosion, pushed-back terminals, or oil contamination. Oil wicking into the connector creates resistive paths that can mimic an open circuit. Clean with electrical contact cleaner and re-test resistance before condemning the injector.

If the solenoid is open or the harness is confirmed damaged, replace the injector or repair the harness section. After replacement, connect Cummins INSITE and run the cylinder contribution test again. All cylinders should show similar contribution values within 10 percent of each other.
symptoms: Rough idle and visible engine misfire on cylinder 3 bank.
White or grey exhaust smoke from unburned fuel passing through the unfired cylinder.
Power loss of approximately 15 to 20 percent compared to rated output.
Fuel economy reduction and increased cylinder head temperature on adjacent cylinders.
Cummins INSITE cylinder contribution test shows near-zero contribution from cylinder 3.
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 653 FMI 5: Open-Circuit Fault on Cylinder 3 Injector

procedures_full.overview: SPN 653 FMI 6 on Freightliner means the cylinder 3 injector circuit is shorted — current above normal. Disconnect the injector, test resistance, and inspect the valve cover harness before replacing parts. SPN 653 monitors the cylinder 3 injector circuit on Freightliner trucks across Detroit, Cummins, and Mercedes powertrains. FMI 6 flags excess current draw from a shorted injector or harness. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com emphasizes immediate injector disconnection on FMI 6 to protect the ECM — a lesson learned from too many Cascadia ECM driver failures.
causes: Injector 3 solenoid internal short to ground
Very Common
Thermal cycling and fuel pressure stress degrade coil insulation, dropping resistance below 0.3 ohms and drawing current that can damage the ECM driver.
Valve cover harness chafe shorting injector circuit to ground
Freightliner Cascadia DD15 harnesses rub against the rocker pedestal through the valve cover grommet, wearing through insulation.
Corroded injector connector creating conductive path between terminals
Moderate
Fuel vapor and heat at the valve cover connector form a conductive film that bridges injector terminals to ground.
steps: Connect Detroit DDDL8 (DD13/DD15), Cummins INSITE (X15), or Noregon JPRO and confirm SPN 653 FMI 6. Run cylinder cutout — cylinder 3 should show zero or erratic RPM contribution.

Shut engine off, disconnect injector 3 connector at the valve cover. Measure solenoid resistance across both terminals — Detroit DD15 injectors read 0.5-2.5 ohms; Cummins X15 reads 0.5-3.0 ohms. Below 0.3 ohms confirms internal short.

With injector unplugged, measure harness resistance to ground and battery positive at the connector. Any reading below 5 kΩ indicates a harness short that must be repaired before reconnecting any injector.
Inspect the valve cover harness grommet on the exhaust side — Freightliner Cascadia DD15 harnesses chafe against the rocker pedestal bracket. Look for exposed copper and heat-discolored loom.

After repair, clear codes and run cutout test. Cylinder 3 RPM drop should match cylinders 1, 2, and 4-6 within 15%. Monitor injector driver current in DDDL8 or INSITE — normal peak is 15-25A per firing event.
symptoms: Rough idle with single-cylinder miss felt at 800-1000 RPM
Amber check engine lamp on Freightliner dash display
Cylinder 3 shows abnormal contribution on DDDL8 or INSITE cutout test
Possible fuel smell from cylinder washing if injector is partially stuck
Driver display may show fuel economy reduction of 5%-10%
procedures_full.source_title: Freightliner SPN 653 FMI 6: Injector Cylinder 3 Current Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 653 FMI 7 means Peterbilt ECM commanded cylinder 3 injector electrically but detected no mechanical fuel delivery response. Severe misfire, cylinder disable, and possible engine protection shutdown can follow until the injector or internal obstruction is corrected.
causes: Stuck or seized injector needle
Carbon or corrosion binds the needle despite normal solenoid pull, so no fuel sprays.
Internal injector spill valve failure
Mechanical spill valve stuck open dumps rail pressure at the injector without metering fuel to the cylinder.
Debris from failing injector upstream
Metal particles from another failing unit can jam cylinder 3 injector passages.
steps: Perform active cylinder cutout in Noregon JPRO; cylinder 3 should change RPM noticeably — no change confirms dead mechanical response.
Verify electrical side first: injector resistance 0.5-2.0 ohms and driver current above 10A peak on cylinder 3 during crank.
Remove cylinder 3 injector and inspect tip for carbon bridging or stuck needle; compare spray pattern on a bench tester if available.
Check for metallic debris in fuel filter indicating internal injector failure contaminating the rail.
Install known-good test injector on cylinder 3 bore; if engine smooths immediately, mechanical injector failure is confirmed.
symptoms: Hard misfire on cylinder 3 with SPN 653 FMI 7 in JPRO or Davie4
Loud knock or uneven idle that worsens under load
Black or white smoke from single-bank imbalance
ECM may disable cylinder 3 injection entirely
Fault persists after clearing codes and may return immediately at start

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
steps: Open Circuit, Short to Ground or Short to Power Check
Check for multiple codes.
If fault code 168/1 is active in addition to other codes, service 168/1 first. Refer to "32.2 SPN 168/FMI 1".
If fault 651/14 and 652/14 are active in addition to 653/14, go to step 2.
If only fault code 653/14 is active, go to step 10.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 5.
Measure the resistance between pins 10 and 1 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #3 pins 1 and 2.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness.Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 10 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. See Figure "120–pin MCM Connector".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 8.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 10 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the negative battery cable.
Measure the resistance between the positive battery post and pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to power between battery positive and pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector"
. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. 120–pin MCM Connector
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 and pin 5 on the valve cover side of the injector harness.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 18.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #3.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 and pin 1 on the valve cover side of the injector harness and pin 1 of the injector #3 harness connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the injector harness and pin 2 of the injector #3 harness connector.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 17.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the injector harness and ground.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #3. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the injector harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #3 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 19.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 22.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect the injector #3 connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the injector harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #3 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #3. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the MCM.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the MCM side of the injector harness connector and pin 24 of the 120–pin MCM connector.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open circuit between pin 1 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 24 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".

If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 5 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 24 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "61.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 654 FMI 5 means Cummins ECM detected below-normal or open-circuit current on cylinder 4 injector. Expect misfire, rough idle, and possible cylinder-disable derate until continuity and injector resistance meet OEM specifications. Open-circuit injector faults spike after valve-cover work on Cummins engines, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always ohms the cylinder 4 branch from ECM to injector before approving injector replacement on SPN 654 FMI 5.
causes: Broken wire in valve-cover harness
Flex fatigue opens the injector circuit while the solenoid itself remains good.
Open injector solenoid winding
Thermal cycles crack coil wire and produce infinite resistance at the connector.
Corroded ECM or injector connector pin
Pin fretting creates intermittent or permanent open circuit on cylinder 4 branch.
steps: Run injector diagnostic test in INSITE for cylinder 4; open circuit flags instantly if harness continuity is lost.
Measure resistance at cylinder 4 injector connector — target 0.5-1.5 ohms on many X15 solenoids; OL reading confirms open coil or wire.
Wiggle-test valve-cover harness while monitoring resistance; intermittent OL indicates broken wire inside cover.
Inspect ECM injector harness pin for cylinder 4 at the ECM connector — look for pushed-back pins or green corrosion.
Repair open circuit or replace injector, then verify peak actuator current above 10A on cylinder 4 during cranking in INSITE.
symptoms: Cylinder 4 misfire with SPN 654 FMI 5 in Cummins INSITE
Rough idle and vibration at low RPM
Balance rate shows cylinder 4 not contributing fuel
Fault may set immediately after valve-cover removal or injector service
Check engine lamp with possible white exhaust at idle

procedures_full.overview: SPN 654 FMI 5 means the Mack ECM sees an open circuit in the cylinder #4 injector driver and cannot fire that injector. It's a High severity fault causing a rough idle and power loss, but it does not shut the engine down. Mack MP7, MP8, and MP10 engines use the same J1939 injector cylinder numbering as other heavy-duty platforms, with SPN 654 flagging cylinder #4 specifically. FMI 5 points to current below normal, the classic signature of an open circuit rather than a short. As ProfessionalDieselRepair.com covers in its injector diagnostic content, most of these codes trace back to harness damage rather than an actual dead injector, making a thorough electrical check well worth the extra fifteen minutes before ordering parts.
causes: Chafed valve cover harness wire
The harness routing near rocker arm hardware wears through insulation over time from engine vibration, eventually breaking the conductor.
Corroded or loose injector connector
Moisture intrusion or an improperly seated locking tab creates a high-resistance or open contact point the ECM reads as a dead circuit.
Failed injector solenoid winding
Internal solenoid coil failure from heat and vibration fatigue can open the circuit after extended service.
ECM injector driver stage failure
An internal ECM fault on that driver channel would show the same code, but only after the injector and harness both test clean.
steps: Connect Mack Premium Tech Tool (PTT) and confirm SPN 654 FMI 5, then run a cylinder cutout test to verify cylinder #4 shows zero contribution.
Shut down and unplug the cylinder #4 injector connector, checking for corrosion, bent pins, or a loose locking tab.
Measure resistance across the injector solenoid terminals with a multimeter and compare to Mack MP engine spec.
If the injector reads good, trace the harness back toward the ECM for chafing near the valve cover or rocker assembly.
Repair or replace the faulty component, clear the code with PTT, and re-run the cutout test to confirm cylinder #4 is firing correctly.
symptoms: Rough idle with a miss traceable to cylinder #4
Amber warning lamp illuminated
Reduced power and fuel economy
Possible white smoke from unburned fuel at the affected cylinder

procedures_full.overview: FMI 6 on the cylinder 4 injector indicates the ECM driver detected above-normal current during injection events. True causes include internal injector short, harness short to power, oil-bridged terminals, and pinched loom after service. Repeated actuation into a shorted circuit can damage the ECM driver — minimizing run time with an active FMI 6 is important. Oil-filled connectors creating intermittent high-current faults are a documented pattern. Replacing the injector without isolating the short source produces repeat FMI 6 if the harness short remains.
causes: Internal injector short — failed injector coil or piezo producing low resistance
Harness short to power — insulation rub-through on sharp bracket edges
Oil-bridged terminals — oil contamination bridging connector terminals
Pinched loom after service — loom pinched at valve cover or bracket after service
Valve-cover corner chafe — insulation worn at valve-cover corners

Disconnect the cylinder 4 injector connector. With the injector disconnected, check if the short condition clears. If the short clears with the injector disconnected, the injector is internally shorted. If the short remains with the injector disconnected, the harness is shorted.
Binary Decision Gate — Resistance Check

Measure injector resistance with the injector disconnected. Resistance below the OEM minimum specification supports an internal short. Compare to adjacent cylinder injector resistance for reference. A reading within specification with the injector disconnected confirms the harness is the short source.
Override Manager — Short-to-Battery and Short-to-Ground Checks

Check for short-to-battery and short-to-ground on the cylinder 4 harness with the injector disconnected. Look for insulation rub-through on sharp bracket edges and valve-cover corners. Inspect for pinched loom after recent service.
Safety Interceptor — Oil-Bridged Terminal Inspection

Inspect the cylinder 4 connector for oil contamination bridging terminals. Oil-filled connectors create intermittent high-current faults that can appear as intermittent FMI 6. Clean or replace oil-contaminated connectors before any injector replacement.
Resume Point — Harness Repair Before New Injector
Repair the harness short before installing a new injector. Installing a new injector into a shorted harness exposes the new injector and ECM driver to the same high-current condition.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Current Confirmation
After repair, verify cylinder 4 current is within normal range. Confirm misfire does not persist. Monitor for return of FMI 6 over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Harness or Injector Decision

Repair harness short if short is found in the circuit. Replace injector only after internal short is proven by resistance test with injector disconnected and harness integrity is confirmed. Code or trim replacement injector per OEM procedure where required.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 654 FMI 6 on a Detroit Diesel means the cylinder 4 injector solenoid drive circuit has a short to ground. Measure solenoid resistance at the connector (spec: 0.3 to 0.5 Ohm) before replacing the injector. When a Detroit Diesel DD13 or DD15 logs SPN 654 FMI 6, the ECM has detected a current-above-normal condition on the cylinder 4 injector driver — the J1939 definition of a short-to-ground fault. Unlike FMI 5 (open circuit), FMI 6 means current is flowing where it should not be, pulling the driver line to ground. At ProfessionalDieselRepair.com we see this code split roughly evenly between a failed injector solenoid (shorted winding) and a chafed harness wire inside the valve cover. The solenoid resistance test (0.3 to 0.5 Ohm on a good DD15 injector) takes under two minutes with a DVOM and immediately separates these two failure modes before any parts are purchased.
causes: Injector solenoid winding shorted to injector body or ground
The solenoid coil insulation breaks down from thermal fatigue or fuel contamination, creating a direct path from the winding to the injector barrel. Resistance drops below 0.1 Ohm.
Chafed or pinched drive harness wire in the valve cover

The injector drive harness routing inside the valve cover is subject to pinch points near the rocker arms. A chafed wire can contact the valve cover or cylinder head, creating a ground fault that mimics an internal solenoid short.
Moisture or oil contamination in the injector connector
Oil wicking into the 2-pin connector cavity creates a conductive path between the driver pins and the grounded connector shell, generating a partial short that sets FMI 6 intermittently.
Faulty ECM injector driver output for cylinder 4

A failed ECM output driver stage can generate a false short condition even when the injector and harness are good. Confirm by testing the harness and injector first before considering ECM replacement.
steps: Connect DDDL (Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link) to the 9-pin J1939 port on the Freightliner or other Detroit-powered vehicle. Confirm SPN 654 FMI 6 is active. Run the DDDL injector disable test to command cylinder 4 off — if the code becomes inactive when cylinder 4 is disabled, the fault follows the injector circuit rather than being an ECM internal fault.

With the key off and engine off for 3 minutes to allow rail pressure to drop, access the cylinder 4 injector connector under the valve cover (DD15: right-side valve cover, cylinder 4 is the fourth from the front). Unplug the 2-pin connector. Measure solenoid resistance between the two injector pins: expected value for DD13/DD15 is 0.3 to 0.5 Ohm at room temperature. A reading below 0.1 Ohm or direct continuity to ground from either pin indicates an internal short in the solenoid.

With the injector connector unplugged, measure each solenoid pin to chassis ground using the DVOM in ohms mode. Both pins should read above 10 MOhm to chassis. A reading below 100 Ohm on either pin to chassis indicates the injector solenoid has shorted internally to the injector body or the drive harness has a ground fault.

If the injector solenoid resistance is in spec (0.3 to 0.5 Ohm) and neither pin shows a ground path, the fault is in the harness. Inspect the valve cover harness run for chafing, heat damage near the rocker assembly, or moisture ingress in the connector. Use a NEXIQ USB-Link 2 adapter with DDDL to perform a live current waveform capture if available to confirm the short location.

Replace the injector if the solenoid is confirmed shorted. Replace or repair the harness segment if the solenoid is good and the fault is wiring. After repair, reconnect DDDL and run the injector disable test again to confirm the fault is resolved and all six cylinders contribute normally.
symptoms: Engine misfire on cylinder 4 with rough idle and vibration felt throughout the cab.
Possible protection shutdown by the ECM if the short draws enough current to trigger a driver fault.
White or grey smoke from unburned fuel in the cylinder 4 exhaust stream.
Power and torque reduction proportional to the loss of one cylinder.
DDDL displays SPN 654 FMI 6 as active with an injector current fault for cylinder 4.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 5 on the cylinder 5 injector indicates the ECM driver found an open-circuit condition during injection events. Open connector, broken conductor, failed injector coil or piezo path, and pass-through terminal exit are the primary causes. Service-induced opens from incomplete latch of injector connectors after valve-cover service are a documented pattern. Inline-six and V-configuration engines with cylinder 5 electronic injection control are all affected. The circuit-to-component sequence keeps the diagnosis cylinder-local and evidence-based.
causes: Open connector — incomplete latch after valve-cover service
Broken conductor — harness break at flex point
Failed injector coil or piezo path — internal open
Pass-through terminal exit — open at valve-cover pass-through connector
Harness chafe — insulation worn at clamp or bracket
steps: Single Action Gate — Connector Seat and Lock Confirmation

Confirm the cylinder 5 injector connector is fully seated and latched. Service-induced opens from incomplete connector latch after valve-cover service are a documented cause of FMI 5. Press the connector firmly and confirm the latch clicks before any electrical measurements.
Binary Decision Gate — Resistance Test

Measure injector circuit resistance versus OEM specification. Infinite resistance or OL indicates an open circuit. A reading within specification after connector reseating confirms the connector was the fault. Compare to adjacent cylinder injector resistance for reference.
Override Manager — Continuity to ECM

Confirm continuity from the ECM connector to the injector connector. An open between the ECM and the injector connector confirms a harness fault. An open only at the injector connector confirms a connector or injector fault.
Safety Interceptor — Insulation Integrity Check

Verify insulation integrity on the cylinder 5 circuit. No short is required for FMI 5, but a circuit with compromised insulation can develop a short after harness repair. Confirm insulation integrity before closing the repair.
Resume Point — Injector Internal Open Proof

If circuit integrity from ECM to injector connector is confirmed and resistance at the injector connector is OL, the injector itself is internally open. This is the only condition that justifies injector replacement for FMI 5.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Contribution Confirmation
After repair, verify cylinder 5 contribution returns to normal. Confirm rough idle and misfire do not persist. Monitor for return of FMI 5 over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Connector, Harness, or Injector Decision

Repair connector or harness if open is found in the circuit. Replace injector only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation. Code or trim replacement injector per OEM procedure where required.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Reseat and latch cylinder 5 injector connector if found incompletely latched.
2 . Repair harness break at flex point or clamp.
3 . Replace injector only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation.
4 . Code or trim replacement injector per OEM procedure where required.
Verification Steps
Confirm cylinder 5 contribution returns to normal after repair.
Verify rough idle and misfire do not persist after repair.
Confirm SPN 655 FMI 5 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of contribution imbalance under load after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify injector connector latch after every valve-cover service.
✓ Inspect cylinder 5 harness for chafe at clamps and brackets at every major service.
✓ Inspect pass-through connectors for backed-out pins at every major service.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 655 FMI 5 means the International ECM sees an open circuit in the cylinder #5 injector driver and cannot fire that injector. It's a High severity fault causing a rough idle and power loss, but it does not shut the engine down. International's A26 and N13 engines follow the same J1939 injector cylinder numbering convention as other heavy-duty platforms, with SPN 655 flagging cylinder #5 specifically. FMI 5 points to current below normal, the classic electrical signature of an open circuit rather than a short. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com covers this fault frequently since valve cover harness chafing is such a consistent root cause across nearly every OEM platform that uses individual cylinder injector fault codes.
causes: Chafed valve cover harness wire
Vibration wears through insulation where the harness routes near rocker arm hardware, eventually breaking the conductor completely.
Corroded or loose injector connector
Moisture intrusion or an improperly seated locking tab creates a high-resistance or open contact the ECM reads as a dead circuit.
Failed injector solenoid winding
Internal solenoid coil failure from heat and vibration fatigue can open the circuit after extended service life.
ECM injector driver stage failure
An internal ECM fault on that specific driver channel would show the same code, but only after the injector and harness both test clean.
steps: Connect a compatible International diagnostic tool and confirm SPN 655 FMI 5, then run a cylinder cutout test to verify cylinder #5 contributes nothing.
Shut down and unplug the cylinder #5 injector connector, checking for corrosion, bent pins, or a loose locking tab.
Measure resistance across the injector solenoid terminals with a multimeter and compare to the engine manufacturer's spec.
If the injector reads good, trace the harness back toward the ECM for chafing near the valve cover or rocker assembly.
Repair or replace the faulty component, clear the code, and re-run the cutout test to confirm cylinder #5 is firing correctly before road testing.
symptoms: Rough idle with a miss traceable to cylinder #5
Amber MIL illuminated
Reduced power and fuel economy
Possible white smoke from unburned fuel at the affected cylinder

procedures_full.overview: SPN 655 FMI 6 means Detroit ECM measured below-normal actuator current on cylinder 5 injector circuit. Misfire, rough idle, and possible cylinder-disable derate can follow until injector resistance and harness integrity meet factory specifications. Cylinder 5 low-current faults on DD platforms often start as oil leaks into the valve-cover harness, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com resolves many Detroit SPN 655 cases with gasket and connector service instead of a full injector replacement.
causes: Degraded cylinder 5 injector solenoid
Coil resistance rises with heat and age, pulling actuation current below ECM thresholds.
Oil-contaminated valve-cover harness
Oil increases connector resistance and drops current without fully opening the circuit.
Weak ECM injector driver on bank 2
Driver output loss mimics injector failure until swap testing proves otherwise.
steps: Run cylinder balance test in DDDL8; cylinder 5 contribution should match bank average within 5 percent at idle.
Measure injector resistance on cylinder 5 connector — expect roughly 0.8-1.2 ohms on many Detroit solenoids at 70°F; readings above 2.5 ohms fail spec.
Inspect cylinder 5 branch of valve-cover harness for oil saturation and green pin corrosion at the 2-pin injector connector.
Compare peak actuation current on cylinder 5 versus cylinder 6 during crank — below 8-10A peak indicates circuit loss.
Swap cylinder 5 and 6 injector connectors temporarily; if FMI 6 follows the connector, repair harness — if it stays on cyl 5, replace injector.
symptoms: Cylinder 5 misfire logged as SPN 655 FMI 6 in Detroit DDDL8
Rough idle with noticeable cab vibration at 600-800 RPM
Exhaust imbalance or faint white haze at idle
Cylinder 5 balance rate low in comparative cylinder data
Code may follow valve-cover gasket leak or harness disturbance

Measure the resistance between pin 5 and pin 6 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pins 1 and 2.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 12.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 and ground on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pins 1 and ground.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 5 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector on the valve cover side and pin 19 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "63.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #5.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 (injector #5 pin 1 if using J-48671–10 ) on the valve cover side of the injector harness and pin 1 of the injector #5 harness connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "63.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.
Measure the resistance between pin 6 (injector #5 pin 2 if using J-48671–10 ) on the valve cover side of the injector harness and pin 2 of the injector #5 harness connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "63.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace injector #5. Refer to "63.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 5 on the cylinder 6 injector indicates the ECM driver found an open-circuit condition during injection events. The cylinder 6 connector family is the same as other open injector circuits — connector, harness, and injector internal open are the primary causes. Rear-bank connectors on inline-six engines are harder to access and are often disturbed during aftertreatment or turbo work on some packages. An overlooked rear connector not fully locked after in-frame service is a documented cause. Single-circuit isolation prevents replacing all injectors on a one-circuit fault.
causes: Open connector — rear connector not fully locked after in-frame service
Broken conductor — harness break at flex point near rear of engine
Failed injector coil or piezo path — internal open
Harness disturbed during AT or turbo work — connector backout from adjacent service
Pass-through terminal exit — open at valve-cover pass-through connector
steps: Single Action Gate — Rear Connector Access and Inspection

Access and inspect the cylinder 6 injector connector. Rear-bank connectors are harder to access and are often disturbed during aftertreatment or turbo work. Confirm the connector is fully seated and latched. An overlooked rear connector not fully locked after in-frame service is a documented cause of FMI 5.
Binary Decision Gate — Resistance Test

Measure injector circuit resistance versus OEM specification. Infinite resistance or OL indicates an open circuit. Compare to adjacent cylinder injector resistance for reference. A reading within specification after connector reseating confirms the connector was the fault.
Override Manager — Continuity to ECM

Confirm continuity from the ECM connector to the injector connector. An open between the ECM and the injector connector confirms a harness fault. An open only at the injector connector confirms a connector or injector fault.
Safety Interceptor — Safe Comparison to Adjacent Cylinders

Compare cylinder 6 resistance and continuity to adjacent cylinders. A single cylinder with an open circuit while adjacent cylinders are normal confirms the fault is localized to cylinder 6. Multiple cylinders with open circuits suggests a shared harness or pass-through fault.
Resume Point — Injector Internal Open Proof

If circuit integrity from ECM to injector connector is confirmed and resistance at the injector connector is OL, the injector itself is internally open. This is the only condition that justifies injector replacement for FMI 5.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Contribution Confirmation
After repair, verify cylinder 6 contribution returns to normal. Confirm rough idle and misfire do not persist. Monitor for return of FMI 5 over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Connector, Harness, or Injector Decision

Repair connector or harness if open is found in the circuit. Replace injector only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation. Code or trim replacement injector per OEM procedure where required.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Reseat and latch cylinder 6 injector connector if found incompletely latched.
2 . Repair harness break at flex point near rear of engine.
3 . Replace injector only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation.
4 . Code or trim replacement injector per OEM procedure where required.
Verification Steps
Confirm cylinder 6 contribution returns to normal after repair.
Verify rough idle and misfire do not persist after repair.
Confirm SPN 656 FMI 5 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of contribution imbalance under load after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify cylinder 6 injector connector latch after every in-frame, AT, or turbo service.
✓ Inspect rear-bank harness for chafe at clamps and brackets at every major service.
✓ Inspect pass-through connectors for backed-out pins at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High. Rail pressure control with multiple failed injectors can compound. Address before extended high-load operation.
symptoms: Cylinder 6 injector open fault active
No contribution cylinder 6
Rough idle from rear cylinder misfire
Power loss from cylinder 6 contribution loss
Smoke under load from cylinder 6

procedures_full.overview: SPN 656 FMI 5 means the cylinder #6 injector solenoid circuit is open, causing a misfire on that cylinder. This is a high-severity code with noticeable power loss and rough running - check the harness connector before replacing the injector. A dead cylinder on the back end of an inline-six is easy to feel but sometimes harder to access. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always checks the engine harness connector pins first, since corrosion there mimics an actually failed injector solenoid perfectly.
causes: Corroded or bent pin in the engine harness connector
Moisture intrusion or a bent pin at the injector connector interrupts the circuit without the injector itself being defective.
Failed injector solenoid
Internal solenoid winding failure directly opens the circuit and requires injector replacement.
Chafed harness wire near the valve cover
Heat and vibration exposure over time can wear through insulation, breaking the injector circuit conductor.
steps: Pull the fault and freeze-frame data on Scania SDP3 to confirm cylinder #6 is the affected injector.
Inspect the injector #6 connector for corrosion, looseness, or heat damage near the valve cover.
Back-probe the injector solenoid circuit with a multimeter, key on engine off, to check for continuity through the driver circuit.
Measure injector solenoid resistance at the connector and compare against Scania's specification.
Trace the wiring from the injector connector back to the engine harness connector for chafing or a broken conductor.
Replace the injector only after confirming the solenoid itself is open, since a harness break produces the identical fault code.
symptoms: Amber or red warning lamp with active misfire on cylinder #6
Rough idle and noticeable engine shake at low RPM
Noticeable power loss under load
Possible white smoke from unburned fuel at the affected cylinder

procedures_full.overview: SPN 656 FMI 6 means the cylinder #6 injector driver circuit on a PACCAR MX engine is shorted to ground or drawing excessive current. It is High severity, does not shut the engine down, but should be repaired quickly to avoid damaging the ECM injector driver stage. PACCAR MX-11 and MX-13 engines use individual injector cylinder codes similar to other J1939 platforms, with SPN 656 covering cylinder #6 specifically. FMI 6 means current above normal, the electrical opposite of an open circuit - this is a genuine short, not a break. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com stresses that a shorted injector circuit deserves faster attention than an open one, since repeated key cycles with an active short can overheat and damage the injector driver transistor built into the ECM.
causes: Chafed injector harness shorting to the cylinder head or valve cover
Tight harness routing against metal surfaces on MX platforms makes this the most frequent cause of a shorted injector circuit.
Water intrusion at the injector connector
A failed connector seal lets moisture into the injector plug, creating a conductive path to ground.
Internally shorted injector solenoid
Heat and vibration fatigue can break down the internal winding insulation of the solenoid, shorting it to the injector body.
Damaged ECM injector driver stage
If the short has been present for an extended period, the ECM's own driver circuit for that cylinder can be damaged and require repair or replacement.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 656 FMI 6 is active, then check for any accompanying injector or harness fault codes.
Shut down and unplug the cylinder #6 injector connector, inspecting for melted plastic, burnt pins, or visible arcing confirming a hard short.
Measure resistance from each injector terminal to chassis ground with a multimeter - any reading other than infinite (OL) confirms a short to ground in the injector or harness.
If the injector itself reads shorted internally, replace it; if it reads clean, trace the harness from the connector back toward the ECM for a chafe point against the valve cover.
After repair, clear codes with Davie4 and verify no injector driver damage occurred by checking injector balance rates in live data before returning to service.
symptoms: Rough idle with a miss traceable to cylinder #6
MIL illuminated
Possible burnt smell or visible connector damage
Reduced power and fuel economy

causes: Faulty Float Sender: Resistive fuel level sender unit has degraded wiper contact, producing rapid voltage fluctuations that exceed ECM-accepted rate-of-change thresholds
Damaged Signal Wiring: Chafed or intermittently open-circuit wiring between the fuel sender and ECM introduces signal spikes interpreted as abnormal fuel level transitions
Tank Baffle Damage: Broken internal tank baffles allow excessive fuel surge, causing float arm mechanical oscillation beyond the sensor's designed damping capability
ECM Software Fault: Corrupted ECM calibration data or outdated firmware alters rate-of-change filter parameters, triggering false FMI 10
Technicians may see erratic fuel gauge behavior without a clear electrical fault
Float arm stuck: Mechanical binding of the float arm at the top of its travel due to debris or tank deformation
Sender short to Vref: Internal short circuit in the fuel level sensor connecting the signal wire to the 5V reference
Open ground circuit: Loss of sensor ground forces signal voltage high, mimicking a full tank condition

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on fuel level indicates the sensor reports below the minimum calibrated threshold. True low fuel, failed sender, harness issues, and tank aeration or starvation near empty are the primary causes. Air ingestion and hard start after running near empty on some supply systems are documented patterns. Distinguishing true low fuel events from sender faults before pump diagnosis prevents replacing the fuel pump for a low fuel or sender fault.
causes: True low fuel — fuel tank genuinely low from consumption
Failed sender — fuel level sender failure producing false low reading
Harness issues — wiring fault producing false low reading
Tank aeration or starvation near empty — air ingestion from running near empty
steps: Single Action Gate — Confirm Actual Fuel Volume

Confirm the actual fuel volume by direct inspection or fuel fill. Physical fuel proof distinguishes true low fuel events from sender faults. A tank that is confirmed empty confirms a true low fuel condition. A tank that is confirmed full with a low fuel reading confirms a sender or wiring fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Evaluate Sender If Gauge Disagrees

Evaluate the fuel sender if the gauge or PID disagrees with the confirmed physical level. Inspect the sender connector and ground integrity. Perform sender resistance sweep where applicable. A sender resistance that does not match the physical level confirms sender failure.
Override Manager — Inspect for Supply Aeration History

Inspect for supply aeration history if the truck ran near empty. Air ingestion and hard start after running near empty on some supply systems are documented patterns. Inspect the fuel supply system for air ingestion and perform priming procedure if required.
Safety Interceptor — Refuel and Prime Before Restart

Refuel and prime the fuel system before restart if the truck ran out of fuel. Running a diesel engine out of fuel can introduce air into the high-pressure fuel system. Follow OEM priming procedure for the specific platform before restart.
Resume Point — Sender Replacement After Circuit Proof

Replace the fuel sender only after circuit integrity is confirmed and sender failure is proven by resistance sweep. A sender that does not match the physical level with confirmed circuit integrity confirms sender failure.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Level Confirmation
After repair, verify fuel level reads correctly at known fuel volumes. Confirm SPN 96 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of false low level readings over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Refuel, Sender, or Harness Decision
Refuel if true low fuel is confirmed. Repair harness fault if confirmed. Replace sender if failure is confirmed after circuit proof. Do not replace fuel pump for a low fuel or sender fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Refuel and prime fuel system if true low fuel is confirmed.
2 . Repair harness fault if confirmed.
3 . Replace fuel sender if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm fuel level reads correctly at known fuel volumes after repair.
Verify SPN 96 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Confirm no hard start or aeration complaints after repair.
Monitor for return of false low level readings over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Monitor fuel level before every dispatch.
✓ Avoid running diesel tanks near empty to prevent air ingestion.
✓ Inspect fuel sender connector and ground at every major service.
✓ Follow OEM priming procedure after any fuel system work.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High if near empty under load. Refuel and purge or prime strategy as needed. Physical fuel proof distinguishes true low fuel events from sender faults before pump diagnosis.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 97 FMI 4 means the water-in-fuel sensor circuit voltage is below normal. Drain and inspect the filter bowl first, then test the 5 V supply and signal before replacing the sensor. Scania operators often see SPN 97 FMI 4 after a sloppy filter change or a night parked in heavy rain. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com recommends separating real water contamination from a shorted harness before buying parts, because the warning can look identical on the dash.
causes: Actual water accumulation in the primary filter bowl
Contaminated fuel trips the sensor legitimately until the bowl is drained and the system is primed.
Short to ground in the WIF sensor harness
Chafed wiring near the frame rail pulls signal voltage low and sets FMI 4 even with dry fuel.
Failed water-in-fuel probe sensor
Internal sensor failure pulls the signal line low while supply and ground remain intact.
steps: Drain the primary fuel filter bowl into a clear container and inspect for visible water separation; do not restart if a large water layer is present.
With key on engine off, measure sensor supply at the WIF connector: expect 5.0 V ±0.5 V on supply and less than 0.1 V offset on ground.
Back-probe the signal wire; a healthy sensor typically shows 0.5-4.5 V depending on water presence—0 V with supply present indicates a short to ground.
Inspect the harness between the filter head and chassis loom for chafing near the steer axle, repairing any exposed conductors with heat-shrink and proper gauge wire.
After repair, refill with clean diesel, prime the system to 30 psi supply pressure if equipped with a hand primer, clear codes, and road test 10 miles monitoring SPN 97.
symptoms: Water-in-fuel warning lamp or text message on the instrument cluster
SPN 97 active in scan data with FMI 4 voltage-below-normal status
Intermittent warning that appears after rain, car wash, or filter service
Possible low-idle torque reduction when the ECM assumes contaminated fuel
Sensor reading stuck at 0 V or near ground in live data

procedures_full.overview: SPN 97 FMI 15 is an early, least-severe warning that water content in the fuel has exceeded the normal threshold. It's Medium severity and usually resolves by draining the water separator bowl - it's not an active derate. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as a maintenance-interval fix in most cases - the water separator did its job, it just needs to be drained before the water reaches the injectors.
causes: Accumulated condensation in the fuel tank
Not an electrical fault - normal moisture buildup from temperature swings, especially in tanks that sit partially full.
Contaminated fuel from a bad fill-up
Fuel quality issue rather than a component failure - water entered the tank from the pump source itself.
Fouled or algae-coated WIF sensor probe
Electrical/sensor fault - a coated probe can produce a false-positive water reading even with clean fuel.
Damaged fuel cap seal allowing water intrusion
Mechanical fault - a cracked or missing gasket lets rainwater into the tank, especially on flatbed or vocational trucks.
steps: Open the fuel filter/water separator drain valve at the bottom of the housing and drain until only clean fuel comes out, catching the water/fuel mixture in a clear container to visually confirm water presence.
Connect DDDL and clear the fault, then run the engine and monitor whether the code returns - a code that stays clear after draining confirms actual water contamination.
If the code returns quickly, pull the WIF sensor from the filter housing and inspect it for fuel algae buildup or a fouled probe, which can also trigger a false-positive reading.
Check the fuel tank and fill cap seal for a path that could be letting condensation or rainwater into the tank, especially on trucks that sit for extended periods.
Replace the fuel filter element if water contamination is confirmed, since a saturated filter media can continue feeding water downstream even after draining.
symptoms: Amber water-in-fuel warning light on the dash
No immediate drivability change at this severity level
Possible rough running if water content is high enough to affect combustion
Fuel filter housing may show visible water at the drain
procedures_full.source_title: Detroit Diesel SPN 97 FMI 15: Water In Fuel Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: The water-in-fuel sensor in the fuel/water separator has tripped. Water in diesel can damage injectors and the high-pressure pump, so address it before it becomes an expensive fuel-system failure.
procedures_full.severity_action: Limp to the next safe stop
causes: Water collected in the fuel/water separator bowl (needs draining)
Contaminated fuel from a bad fill
Condensation in a low/empty tank
Faulty water-in-fuel sensor (verify after draining)
first_moves: Drain the fuel/water separator bowl — that's the first and usually the fixing step.
If it refills with water quickly, suspect a contaminated tank/bad fuel.
Replace the fuel filter if water has carried through.
If the bowl is dry but the code stays, suspect the sensor.
common_misdiagnoses: Ignoring the warning and running water through the injectors and pump.
Replacing the sensor without first draining the separator.
Missing a contaminated tank that keeps refilling the separator with water.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 98 FMI 1 means the Cummins ECM received a valid but low engine oil level reading. It is a High-severity fault that can trigger derate and shutdown timers. Check the dipstick on level ground before replacing the oil level sensor or float assembly. Low oil level faults are among the most common overnight calls to ProfessionalDieselRepair.com, and SPN 98 FMI 1 sits in the moderately severe tier where the ECM trusts the sensor but does not like what it sees. A real low level is cheap to fix; ignoring it is not.
causes: Low oil level from consumption or missed top-off
The sensor is reporting accurately. Oil consumption, a slow leak, or an incomplete fill after service drops the pan below the calibrated minimum.
Failed oil level sensor or stuck float
A cracked float or worn resistive track sends a valid but falsely low voltage even when the dipstick shows adequate oil.
Corroded harness or poor ground at sensor connector
High resistance on the signal or ground pin pulls voltage low, mimicking a low-level condition without mechanical loss of oil.
steps: Park on level ground, shut down, wait five minutes, then check the dipstick. Oil must sit between the low and high marks on a warm engine.
Connect Cummins INSITE and monitor SPN 98 live data while rocking the truck gently. A stable low reading with correct dipstick level points to sensor or float failure.
Inspect the oil level sensor harness at the block. Backprobe pin 1 (signal) and pin 3 (ground) on the 3-pin Deutsch connector; expect 0.5-4.5V proportional to level with 5V reference on pin 2.
Measure sensor resistance between signal and ground at the connector unplugged. Most Cummins float sensors read 80-220 ohms at mid-level; open circuit reads infinite resistance.
If level is genuinely low, add approved CJ-4 oil to spec, clear codes in INSITE, and road test. Do not restart a shutdown engine until level is verified.
symptoms: Amber check engine or low oil level lamp illuminated on the dash
Oil level gauge or INSITE reading shows below minimum while engine is warm and level
Progressive power derate after extended idle or low-level operation
Audible low-oil alarm on some chassis configurations
Possible shutdown if level drops further while the fault remains active

procedures_full.overview: SPN 98 FMI 17 means the Mack oil level sensor is reading below normal at the least severe warning level. It is Medium severity, serves as an early low-oil warning, and should prompt a manual dipstick check rather than an immediate part replacement. Oil level sensors give drivers and fleets an early heads-up before a low oil condition becomes a serious problem, and SPN 98 FMI 17 sits at the earliest, least severe warning stage Mack's system tracks. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always recommends starting with the simplest possible check: pull the dipstick and see if the truck actually needs oil before assuming anything electrical is wrong. Most of the time this code means exactly what it says, and a quart or two of the correct oil resolves it completely.
causes: Genuinely low oil level from normal consumption or a slow leak
Extended oil change intervals or a minor external leak can gradually drop oil level enough to trigger this early warning threshold.
Oil level sensor float fouled with sludge or debris
Contaminated oil or infrequent oil changes can cause sludge buildup that interferes with the float mechanism's accuracy.
Corroded oil level sensor connector
The sensor connector location in or near the oil pan is exposed to road grime and moisture, which can corrode contacts over time.
Failed oil level sensor
The sensor itself can fail electrically and report an inaccurate low reading despite adequate actual oil level.
steps: Park on level ground, let the engine sit for several minutes, and check the dipstick manually to confirm the actual oil level.
Compare the dipstick reading to the scan tool's reported oil level using Mack Premium Tech Tool (PTT) to see if they agree.
If oil is genuinely low, add the correct grade and amount to bring it back to the full mark, then recheck after a short drive cycle.
If the dipstick shows adequate oil but the code persists, inspect the oil level sensor connector in the oil pan for corrosion or a loose fit.
Clear the code with PTT once the discrepancy is resolved, and monitor for the fault returning on subsequent drive cycles.
symptoms: Amber warning lamp illuminated
Low oil level warning message on the dash display
No immediate change in engine performance at this severity level
Possible oil consumption trend visible on recent PM records
procedures_full.source_title: Mack SPN 98 FMI 17: Low Engine Oil Level Warning

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on intake manifold temperature indicates the sensor reports above the maximum calibrated limit. Heat-soaked sensor, failed CAC efficiency, recirculation of hot air, sensor bias high, and extreme ambient combined with high load are the primary causes. CAC efficiency loss from internal restriction or external debris packing is a documented cause that produces true high intake temperatures. Ignoring high IAT faults as weather-related nuisance codes is a documented pattern that leads to power loss and derate under hot ambient conditions.
causes: Heat-soaked sensor — sensor reading above actual air temperature
Failed CAC efficiency — internal restriction or external debris pack
Recirculation of hot air — missing air seals recirculating engine heat
Sensor bias high — thermistor reading above actual temperature
Extreme ambient plus high load — thermal accumulation in intake system
steps: Single Action Gate — Sensor Correlation Check

Compare IAT scan data to an infrared measurement at the sensor boss. A large disagreement between scan data and infrared measurement supports sensor bias. A reading that correlates with infrared measurement supports true high intake temperature.
Binary Decision Gate — CAC Airflow Package Inspection

Inspect the charge air cooler airflow package for external debris packing and internal restriction. Vocational trucks and trucks operating in debris-heavy environments are prone to packed coolers that reduce CAC efficiency.
Override Manager — Duct and Seal Inspection

Inspect intake ducting for missing or damaged air seals that allow hot engine bay air to recirculate into the intake. Missing seals between the CAC and the intake manifold are a documented cause of elevated intake temperatures.
Safety Interceptor — Sensor Circuit Verification

Verify sensor circuit integrity if sensor correlation check suggests bias. IAT sensors are typically thermistor style — measure resistance and compare to OEM temperature-resistance curve. Inspect connector for heat damage near intake plumbing.
Resume Point — Hard-Pull Condition Retest
If the fault is intermittent, retest under hard-pull conditions. True CAC efficiency loss produces elevated intake temperatures under high load that may not be apparent at idle.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation
After repair, verify intake temperature remains within OEM specification under high ambient and high load conditions. Confirm derate does not activate after repair.
Repair Ledger Output — CAC, Seal, or Sensor Decision
Clean or replace CAC if efficiency loss is confirmed. Repair or replace missing air seals if recirculation is found. Replace sensor if bias is confirmed after CAC and seal integrity are proven.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean external CAC fins if debris packing is found.
2 . Replace CAC if internal restriction or damage is confirmed.
3 . Repair or replace missing air seals between CAC and intake manifold.
4 . Replace IAT sensor if bias is confirmed after CAC and seal integrity are proven.
Verification Steps
Confirm intake temperature remains within OEM specification under high ambient and load after repair.
Verify derate does not activate after repair.
Confirm SPN 105 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of power loss under high ambient conditions.
Preventative Measures
✓ Clean CAC external fins at every major service.
✓ Inspect air seals between CAC and intake manifold at every major service.
✓ Inspect IAT sensor connector for heat damage at every major service.
✓ Address CAC efficiency loss before summer operation in high-ambient environments.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High in protection derate conditions. True CAC efficiency loss reduces power and increases soot production. Do not ignore as a weather nuisance code.
symptoms: Intake air temperature high fault active
Hot CAC outlet indication
Derate from high IAT
Heat-soaked intake indication
Power loss under high ambient and load conditions

procedures_full.overview: Intake-manifold (charge-air) temperature is above the high limit. Hot intake air hurts power and combustion and the ECM will derate. It usually points to a charge-air-cooler (CAC) airflow or EGR-related problem.
procedures_full.severity_action: Power derate likely — plan to stop soon
causes: Plugged/bug-packed CAC or radiator face restricting airflow
CAC leak or restriction reducing cooling
EGR over-flowing hot gas into the intake
Intake-air temp sensor fault reading high (verify first)
first_moves: Inspect the CAC and radiator face for bugs, mud, and debris blocking airflow.
Check for CAC leaks/restriction and loose charge-air piping/boots.
Reduce load on grades to keep intake temps in range until repaired.
Confirm the reading is real before replacing the sensor.
common_misdiagnoses: Replacing the sensor when a packed CAC face was the airflow restriction.
Missing a charge-air leak that drives temps up.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 105 FMI 0 means intake air temperature is genuinely too high, most often from a blocked charge air cooler or a leaking CAC boot letting hot air bypass cooling. This code reflects real airflow and cooling performance, not an electrical fault. The charge air cooler and its boots are the first place to look.
causes: Charge air cooler externally blocked with debris
Bugs, mud, and road grime packed into the CAC fins reduce its ability to cool compressed air.
Leaking CAC boot or clamp
A leak lets hot, uncooled air bypass the cooler and enter the intake manifold directly.
Cooling fan or shroud malfunction
Reduced airflow across the CAC raises charge air temperature even with the cooler itself intact.
Turbo overboost raising charge temperature
Excess boost pressure increases compressed air temperature beyond what the CAC is sized to handle.
steps: Inspect the charge air cooler for external blockage - bugs, debris, or mud packed into the fins restrict cooling airflow.
Check charge air cooler boots and clamps for leaks, which let hot, unregulated air bypass the cooler.
Verify the cooling fan and shroud are functioning correctly, since CAC cooling often shares airflow with the radiator.
Compare the intake air temp sensor reading against a handheld infrared thermometer at the intake manifold to confirm sensor accuracy.
Check for any recent turbo overboost codes, since excess boost pressure also raises charge air temperature.
symptoms: Reduced power, especially noticeable under sustained load or in hot weather
Amber check-engine lamp
Possible correlation with ambient temperature - worse on hot days or after extended idling in traffic
No unusual noise typically associated with this fault alone

procedures_full.overview: SPN 105 FMI 0 means the ECM detected intake manifold air temperature above the most severe high threshold. It's a high-severity code that typically brings a power derate, not a shutdown - check the charge air cooler and boots before condemning the sensor. A hot-running intake charge robs power and, left unchecked, risks detonation-range cylinder temperatures. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this code most often on trucks with a partially blocked charge air cooler or a leaking CAC boot letting hot compressor discharge air skip the cooling process entirely, rather than a failed sensor.
causes: Leaking or collapsed charge air cooler boot/clamp
A leak on the cold side lets hot, uncooled compressor discharge air reach the intake manifold, spiking measured temperature under boost.
Restricted or fouled charge air cooler core
Bent fins, bug/debris packing, or internal oil residue reduce the CAC's ability to shed heat from the compressed intake charge.
Intake manifold temperature sensor drift or corrosion
A sensor with a cracked thermistor or corroded pins can report falsely high readings even with a healthy cooling system.
Radiator/CAC airflow restriction from debris
Packed cooling fins reduce ambient heat rejection across the entire front-end cooling package, raising both coolant and intake charge temps together.
steps: Pull the fault on Cummins INSITE and record freeze-frame intake manifold temperature versus ambient air temperature at the time of the fault.
Inspect the charge air cooler (CAC) core and end tanks for cracked seams, oil residue, or crushed fins restricting airflow.
Check the CAC boots and clamps for leaks with a boost-leak tester; a leaking hot side or cold side boot lets hot compressor discharge air bypass the cooler.
Back-probe the intake manifold temperature sensor connector with a multimeter and compare resistance against the OEM temp/resistance chart at known ambient temp.
Verify the radiator, CAC, and AC condenser fins are not packed with debris that's starving both cooling circuits.
If live data tracks correctly with ambient and load, this is a genuine heat-soak issue, not a sensor fault - address the CAC/cooling package before returning to service.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp with active power derate under load
Noticeable loss of pulling power on grades or when towing
Elevated coolant and EGT readings alongside the intake temp fault
Rough idle or hesitation on hot restarts
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 105 FMI 0: Diagnosing High Intake Manifold Temperature

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on intake manifold temperature indicates the sensor reports below the minimum expected temperature for conditions. Failed sensor, open circuit, connector corrosion, and incorrect sensor installation are the primary causes. A sensor left unplugged after intake service is a documented cause. If the engine heat-soaks and the IAT never rises above ambient, the sensor or circuit is the fault — not the fuel or boost system. Performing fuel system or boost system diagnosis based on a false cold IAT reading is the primary wasted-time pattern on this fault.
causes: Failed sensor — thermistor failure producing cold bias
Open circuit — open signal or ground producing cold bias
Connector corrosion — high-resistance connection producing cold bias
Incorrect sensor installation — wrong sensor or improper seating
Sensor left unplugged after intake service
steps: Single Action Gate — Cold-Soak Ambient Correlation

Compare IAT reading to ambient temperature at cold soak. IAT should be near ambient at cold soak. If IAT reads significantly below ambient at cold soak, the sensor or circuit is biased cold. If IAT reads near ambient at cold soak but never rises during operation, the sensor is stuck.
Binary Decision Gate — Sensor Connection Verification

Verify the sensor is connected and properly seated. A sensor left unplugged after intake service produces a cold bias that triggers FMI 1. Inspect the sensor connector for proper engagement and pin condition.
Override Manager — Harness Continuity Check
Perform continuity test on the IAT sensor circuit. An open signal or ground produces a cold bias reading. Inspect connector for corrosion that creates high resistance mimicking an open circuit.
Safety Interceptor — Sensor Resistance vs Temperature Chart
Measure sensor resistance and compare to OEM temperature-resistance curve if available. A sensor reading outside the expected resistance for current temperature confirms sensor failure.
Resume Point — Operating Temperature Rise Assessment
If cold-soak reading is near ambient but IAT never rises during operation, the sensor is stuck at a cold value. This confirms sensor failure rather than a circuit fault.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation
After repair, verify IAT rises appropriately during operation and correlates with ambient at cold soak. Confirm no smoke or boost control complaints remain after repair.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor or Harness Decision
Replace sensor after circuit integrity is confirmed and sensor failure is proven by resistance test or stuck reading. Repair harness if open circuit or corrosion is found.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Reconnect sensor if found unplugged after intake service.
2 . Repair connector corrosion or open circuit.
3 . Replace IAT sensor after circuit proof confirms sensor failure.
4 . Verify correct sensor installation if incorrect sensor is suspected.
Verification Steps
Confirm IAT reads near ambient at cold soak after repair.
Verify IAT rises appropriately during operation.
Confirm SPN 105 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of smoke or boost control complaints.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify IAT sensor connection after every intake service.
✓ Inspect IAT sensor connector for corrosion at every major service.
✓ Address intake air leaks near IAT sensor that can cause moisture intrusion.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Low to Medium Severity
Low to Medium. Can cause rich smoke and boost control edge cases from false cold IAT. Cold-soak correlation check resolves most cases quickly.
symptoms: Intake temp stuck low fault active
IAT sensor cold indication
Fueling rich smoke from false cold IAT
Boost control edge cases from cold IAT bias

procedures_full.overview: SPN 105 FMI 3 means the intake manifold temperature sensor circuit is reading a voltage above normal, consistent with an open circuit or short to power. It's a medium-severity electrical fault on DD engines with no derate, but it does affect cold-start fueling accuracy. This code shows up regularly on DD13 and DD15 engines with high mileage harnesses. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always starts with a pin test at the connector before assuming the sensor itself has failed, since a chafed wire near the valve cover is the more frequent culprit.
causes: Chafed signal wire near the valve cover or turbo heat shield
Heat cycling and vibration wear through insulation over time, letting the signal wire short against a grounded or powered surface.
Corroded or backed-out connector pin
Moisture intrusion at the connector can corrode pins, creating an intermittent open that the ECM reads as a high-voltage fault.
Internally failed sensor element
A cracked thermistor inside the sensor housing can present as an open circuit, mimicking the same fault signature.
steps: Pull the code and freeze-frame data on Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) to confirm intake manifold temp is pinned at an unrealistic high value.
Locate the sensor at the intake manifold, unplug the connector, and back-probe signal and ground with a multimeter, key on engine off.
A signal reading near 5V with the sensor disconnected confirms the fault is in the harness rather than the sensor itself.
Trace the signal wire for chafing near the valve cover, turbo heat shield, or engine harness routing points.
Test the sensor's resistance at the connector against DDC's published temperature/resistance chart to rule out an internally open sensor.
Repair any damaged wiring or replace the sensor as needed, then clear the code and confirm a plausible reading returns with the engine cold.
symptoms: Check engine lamp illuminated with no drivability complaint
Possible slightly rich or lean cold-start fueling
No power loss under normal operation

procedures_full.overview: SPN 105 FMI 4 on PACCAR MX-13 engines means the intake manifold temperature sensor circuit is reading below normal, consistent with a short to ground. It's a medium-severity fault that pushes the ECM toward conservative default fueling until repaired. Intake manifold temperature works alongside boost pressure to help the ECM fine-tune fueling and EGR strategy, and SPN 105 FMI 4 means that input has dropped out with a shorted-low reading. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com typically finds this comes down to a corroded or contaminated connector at the sensor's mounting point on the manifold itself, since it's directly exposed to engine bay conditions including oil mist and moisture over time.
causes: Corroded or contaminated sensor connector
The sensor's location directly on the intake manifold exposes its connector to oil mist, moisture, and heat cycling that accelerates corrosion.
Chafed wiring shorting the signal to ground
Harness routing near the manifold can wear through insulation over time, creating a short-to-ground path.
Failed sensor element
Internal sensor failure can independently produce a shorted-low reading, though it's less common than connector or wiring issues in this location.
steps: Pull the fault with PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 105 FMI 4 is active; check the reported intake manifold temperature value, which will likely be pegged at an extreme cold reading.
Locate the sensor, typically threaded into the intake manifold itself, and inspect the connector for corrosion or a pinched wire nearby.
Disconnect the sensor and check the signal wire for continuity to ground with the harness isolated from the ECM - any unexpected continuity confirms a short.
Test the sensor's resistance at a known temperature and compare against the manufacturer's resistance-versus-temperature chart to rule the sensor element in or out.
Repair any chafed wiring found, or replace the sensor if it fails the resistance test.
Clear the code and confirm the reported temperature climbs realistically as the engine warms up during a test run before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Slightly reduced performance from conservative default fueling
Amber Check Engine lamp
Reported intake manifold temperature pegged at an unrealistic cold value
No dramatic drivability complaint in most cases

procedures_full.overview: SPN 105 FMI 16 on Mack engines means intake manifold air temperature is above the normal range with valid sensor data. Charge-air cooler leaks, EGR cooler failure, or turbo issues can cause derate. Compare IMT to ambient and CAC outlet temps in ServiceMaxx before replacing the sensor. Intake temperature faults on Mack powerplants usually trace to something heating the air charge, not a bad wire. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com walks through charge-air and EGR checks first because FMI 16 tells you the ECM trusts the temperature reading.
causes: Charge-air cooler leak or clogged CAC
Leaks reduce cooling efficiency and raise manifold air temperature under boost.
EGR cooler internal leak heating intake charge
Coolant entering the EGR path superheats intake air and often pairs with coolant loss.
Failed intake manifold temperature sensor reading high
A drifting NTC can report high temperature when the actual charge air is normal.
steps: Log IMT, ambient air temp, and charge-air cooler outlet temp in ServiceMaxx during a loaded pull.
Inspect charge-air cooler fins, boots, and clamps for leaks; a boost leak raises compressor outlet temperature.
Pressure-test the CAC to 30 psi and listen for leaks at hose ends and tank seams.
Check EGR cooler for white exhaust smoke and coolant loss; a leaking EGR cooler heats intake air with hot coolant vapor.
Test the IMT sensor resistance at room temperature; typical NTC spec is 2.5-4.5k ohms at 77F. Replace only if out of spec and CAC/EGR are healthy.
symptoms: Amber or red check engine lamp with active SPN 105 FMI 16
High intake manifold temperature reading in ServiceMaxx live data
Noticeable power loss or derate climbing grades
Elevated coolant consumption if EGR cooler is leaking internally
Hot air from charge-air plumbing or damaged CAC boots
