dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 111 FMI 1 – Coolant Temperature High Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 111 FMI 1 – Engine Coolant Temperature High (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 111 FMI 1 indicates that engine coolant temperature has exceeded normal operating limits. This fault is commonly triggered by overheating conditions that may lead to engine protection derate.
Symptoms
High temperature gauge reading
Check engine light illuminated
Warning message on dash
Reduced engine power
Cooling fan running constantly
Cause
This code may be caused by low coolant levels, failing thermostat, malfunctioning water pump, clogged radiator, restricted airflow, or heavy load under high ambient temperatures.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving is not recommended. Continued operation while overheating can cause severe engine damage, including head gasket failure or warped components.
Recommended Action
Safely pull over and allow the engine to cool. Check coolant levels and inspect for leaks. Seek professional diagnostics if overheating persists.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 111 FMI 1 mean?
 
SPN 111 FMI 1 indicates that engine coolant temperature is outside the normal operating range, typically reading lower than expected.
 
 
What causes SPN 111 FMI 1?
 
Common causes include a faulty coolant temperature sensor, thermostat malfunction, wiring issues, or cooling system problems.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 111 FMI 1?
 
Driving may be possible temporarily, but incorrect coolant readings can affect fuel management and engine performance.
 
 
Will SPN 111 FMI 1 cause a derate?
 
In some cases, prolonged abnormal temperature readings can contribute to engine protection strategies, including reduced power.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 111 FMI 1?
 
Inspect coolant level, check the thermostat, test the temperature sensor, and verify wiring integrity before replacing components.

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Volvo 780 equipped with the D13 engine may encounter issues related to the SA 0 SPN 111 FMI 1 diagnostic trouble code. This code generally indicates a fault with the coolant temperature sensor. Such problems commonly arise after refilling the coolant reservoir or addressing leaks, leading to engine derate conditions. This issue can stem from air pockets trapped within the cooling system following reservoir refill. These air pockets affect the coolant temperature sensor readings and trigger the fault code. It is important to check the coolant level and carefully bleed the cooling system to remove any trapped air. In addition to bleeding, inspection of the coolant temperature sensor and its wiring is advised. Damage or corrosion to the sensor or wiring can contribute to this trouble

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 1 means coolant level has dropped below the safe minimum on a Scania engine. It's a Critical fault with an active shutdown risk - pull over and check for leaks before the engine forces itself off.
causes: Coolant leak from a hose, radiator, or water pump
A genuine mechanical leak that reduces actual coolant volume, exactly as the sensor is reporting.
Fouled or stuck level sensor float
An electrical/sensor issue where the float mechanism itself is reporting incorrectly despite a physically full tank.
Cracked expansion tank near the sensor mount
A mechanical failure in the tank itself that causes a slow, hard-to-spot leak right at the sensor location.
Air pocket in the cooling system after service
A trapped air issue rather than a true leak, which can cause a temporary false low-level reading until the system is properly bled.
steps: Pull over safely and shut the engine down before the ECU forces a shutdown on its own.
Let the engine cool completely, then visually inspect the expansion tank fluid level against the min/max marks.
Check the water pump, radiator core, and all hose connections for visible leaks or crusty coolant residue.
Connect Scania SDP3 and verify the coolant level sensor's reading matches what you observe physically in the tank.
If the tank is full but the code persists, inspect the level sensor's float mechanism inside the tank for a stuck or fouled float.
symptoms: Red warning lamp paired with an audible low coolant alarm
Coolant level indicator showing empty or critically low on the dash
Rising coolant temperature trend even before a full overheat develops
Possible visible coolant puddling under the truck

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 1 means coolant level has dropped past the critical threshold and the engine will likely shut down automatically to prevent overheating damage. This is Critical - find and fix the leak before restarting.
causes: Coolant hose or clamp failure
Mechanical fault - a failed hose or loose clamp allows coolant to escape, sometimes gradually enough to go unnoticed until a critical level is reached.
Radiator or water pump leak
Mechanical fault - a developing leak from either component can slowly drain the system over time or fail suddenly.
Cracked coolant reservoir tank
Mechanical fault - a hairline crack in the plastic tank, often at a weld seam, causes a slow leak that's easy to miss visually.
Head gasket failure allowing internal coolant loss
Serious mechanical failure - coolant is consumed internally rather than leaking externally, often accompanied by white exhaust smoke or oil contamination.
steps: Pull over safely and shut off the engine immediately if it hasn't already shut down on its own.
Let the engine cool completely before opening any part of the cooling system, then visually inspect the reservoir tank and radiator for coolant level.
Check the bottom of the radiator, water pump, and all hose connections for active leaks or damp residue indicating a slow leak.
Pressure-test the cooling system once safely cooled to identify the leak source before refilling and restarting.
Do not restart the engine until the leak is found and repaired, or you risk repeating the same shutdown event or causing real overheating damage.
symptoms: Red Stop Engine lamp with loud warning buzzer
Automatic engine shutdown sequence
Coolant temperature gauge climbing rapidly before shutdown
Visible coolant loss or empty reservoir tank

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 1 means the Detroit Diesel coolant level sensor has confirmed coolant has dropped to the most severe low level tracked by the ECM. This is Critical severity and will typically force an automatic engine shutdown to prevent overheating damage.
causes: External coolant leak from a hose, clamp, or radiator seam
Age-related hose deterioration or a loosened clamp is the most frequent reason coolant volume drops enough to trigger this critical-level code.
Water pump seal failure
A failing water pump shaft seal allows slow coolant loss that often isn't obvious until the level drops critically low.
Corroded or stuck coolant level sensor float
In rare cases the sensor itself gives a false low reading due to sediment buildup or a stuck float, though the coolant level is actually adequate.
Internal coolant leak such as a head gasket or EGR cooler failure
Internal leaks that consume coolant into the combustion chamber or exhaust system can drop coolant level without any visible external puddle.
steps: Pull to a safe location and shut the engine off immediately before the ECM forces a shutdown mid-drive.
Allow the engine to cool completely before opening the coolant surge tank cap to avoid scalding from pressurized hot coolant.
Visually inspect the coolant level in the surge tank against the low and full marks, and look for obvious external leaks at hoses, the water pump, and radiator seams.
Check the coolant level sensor connector in the surge tank for corrosion or a loose fit if the tank appears adequately full despite the code.
Once the leak is repaired or coolant topped off, bleed air from the system per Detroit Diesel procedure and verify with DDDL that the coolant level reading returns to normal before restarting.
symptoms: Red Stop Engine lamp with audible warning buzzer
Automatic engine shutdown or aggressive derate to protect the engine
Rapidly climbing coolant temperature gauge
Visible coolant leak or unusually low level in the surge tank

procedures_full.overview: The coolant level sensor monitors the surge tank level. FMI 1 is set when the sensor indicates low level beyond the calibrated time threshold. This can be caused by an actual coolant leak, internal consumption, cap failure, or a false sensor reading. Physical level verification must come before any electrical diagnosis.
causes: External coolant leak — hose, clamp, radiator, or fitting
Internal coolant leak — EGR cooler, head gasket, or liner
Pressure cap failure — coolant loss through overflow
Aeration — air in system causing false low level reading
Failed level sensor — open or short circuit
Chronic small hose leak — slow loss over time
steps: Single Action Gate — Visual Level Check
Check surge tank coolant level visually with engine cold. If level is actually low, find the source before any electrical diagnosis.
Binary Decision Gate — Pressure Test
Pressure test the cooling system to identify external leaks. Hold pressure per OEM spec — any drop indicates a leak path.
Override Manager — UV Dye Inspection
If leak source is not obvious, add UV dye and inspect under UV light after a drive cycle. Effective for finding small or intermittent leaks.
Safety Interceptor — Combustion Leak Test
If coolant loss is unexplained and no external leak is found, perform a combustion leak test to rule out internal (head gasket/liner) leak.
Resume Point — Sensor Logic Test
Only after physical level and leak are addressed, test the level sensor circuit. Verify open/closed states with known level. Check connector for corrosion or harness rub.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Level Monitoring
After repair, monitor coolant level over several drive cycles to confirm loss has stopped.
Repair Ledger Output — Internal Leak Decision
Pursue internal leak diagnosis (EGR cooler, head gasket) only with positive combustion test or confirmed unexplained loss after external leak repair.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair any external coolant leaks found (hoses, clamps, radiator, fittings).
2 . Replace pressure cap if failing to hold pressure.
3 . Repair EGR cooler if internal leak is confirmed.
4 . Perform head gasket repair only with positive combustion leak test.
5 . Replace level sensor if circuit fault is confirmed after physical level is verified.
6 . Bleed air from system after any coolant service.
Verification Steps
Confirm coolant level is stable over multiple drive cycles after repair.
Verify no external leaks remain after pressure test.
Confirm combustion leak test is negative after any internal repair.
Monitor for return of SPN 111 FMI 1 over 50+ miles.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect all coolant hoses and clamps at every major service.
✓ Replace pressure cap per OEM service intervals.
✓ Monitor coolant level weekly on high-mileage engines.
✓ Address EGR cooler seepage patterns early before major loss occurs.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High if level is truly low. Do not drive with confirmed low coolant — overheat and engine damage risk is immediate. Identify and repair the leak source before returning to service.

Coolant level fault active
Overheat warning following low coolant
Visible coolant loss under vehicle

procedures_full.overview: Volvo SPN 111 FMI 1 indicates a critical drop in engine coolant level. Immediate action is required to prevent engine damage due to overheating.
steps: Pull over safely and turn off the ignition immediately before the computer forces a shutdown. Ensure the vehicle is on a flat, stable surface and engage the parking brake.
Let the engine cool completely, then visually inspect the plastic coolant reservoir tank fluid level. Use a flashlight to check for any discoloration or sediment that might indicate contamination.
Check the bottom of the water pump, radiator core, and silicone heater hoses for bright green or pink crusty leaks. Pay special attention to connections and joints, as these are common leak points.
Use a coolant pressure tester to identify any leaks in the system. Apply pressure gradually and observe for any drop in pressure that would indicate a leak.
If no leaks are found, inspect the coolant level sensor for proper operation and cleanliness. Use a multimeter to test the sensor's resistance and ensure it matches specifications.
symptoms: Red STOP ENGINE light accompanied by a loud warning buzzer.
Automatic engine shutdown sequence initiated.
Coolant temperature gauge rapidly climbing into the red zone.
Noticeable decrease in engine performance before shutdown.
Steam or coolant odor emanating from the engine bay.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 3 is a coolant level sensor circuit high voltage or open class fault. Open signal, failed level sensor, unplugged header connector, and corroded terminals are the primary causes. False low-coolant warnings with full tanks after connector corrosion are documented patterns. Replacing the level sensor without verifying physical coolant level first is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern — a true low coolant condition produces the same code as a sensor circuit fault.
causes: Open signal — open signal circuit producing high voltage reading
Failed level sensor — failed level sensor producing open circuit
Unplugged header connector — unplugged surge-tank header connector producing open circuit
Corroded terminals — corroded terminals producing open circuit
steps: Step 1 — Physical Level Verification

Verify physical coolant level first. A true low coolant condition produces the same code as a sensor circuit fault. Do not condemn the sensor before visual level proof. Inspect the surge tank and radiator for actual coolant level. A true low coolant condition requires leak diagnosis, not sensor replacement.
Step 2 — Connector Inspection

Inspect the surge-tank sensor connector. False low-coolant warnings with full tanks after connector corrosion are a documented pattern. Inspect the connector for corrosion, coolant contamination of pins, and chafe at the tank bracket. Clean or repair the connector if corrosion or contamination is found.
Step 3 — Circuit Open and High-Voltage Checks

Check for open-circuit conditions and high-voltage conditions in the sensor circuit. Verify reference voltage, ground, and signal circuit integrity at the sensor connector. An open signal circuit produces a high-voltage reading at the ECM input.
Step 4 — Sensor Test and Replacement
Test the sensor per OEM procedure if the circuit is confirmed good. Replace the sensor if the circuit is good and the sensor fails the OEM test. Do not replace the sensor before circuit proof.
Step 5 — Verify After Repair
Verify coolant level sensor operation after repair. Confirm SPN 111 FMI 3 does not return. Confirm the low-coolant warning clears after repair.

Repair Steps
1 . Repair connector or harness if open circuit is confirmed.
2 . Clean or replace connector if corrosion or contamination is confirmed.
3 . Replace level sensor if circuit is good and sensor fails OEM test.
4 . Address true low coolant condition if physical level is confirmed low.
Verification Steps
Confirm coolant level sensor operation is correct after repair.
Verify SPN 111 FMI 3 does not return after repair.
Confirm low-coolant warning clears after repair.
Monitor for return of level sensor faults over extended operation.

✓ Inspect surge-tank sensor connector for corrosion at every major service.
✓ Verify physical coolant level at every major service.
✓ Inspect sensor harness for chafe at every major service.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 3 on PACCAR MX engines means the coolant level sensor circuit voltage is above normal, usually a short to 5V or power. The surge tank may be full while the ECM reads a fault. Verify physical coolant level and test signal voltage with the sensor unplugged. Coolant level warnings on PACCAR trucks should always start with a visual check of the surge tank. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees SPN 111 FMI 3 caused by scaled probes and rubbed harnesses more often than actual coolant loss.
causes: Level sensor signal shorted to 5V or battery positive
Chafed harness between the surge tank and battery box pulls signal voltage high.
Failed coolant level sensor or scaled float probe
Mineral deposits or a shorted internal element send high voltage even with adequate coolant.
Connector moisture bridging supply and signal pins
Glycol seepage into the Deutsch connector creates a conductive path between pins.
steps: Check the surge tank sight glass or dipstick with engine cold; level should be at the COLD FULL mark.
Connect PACCAR Davie4 and monitor SPN 111 voltage; above 4.8V with a full tank confirms FMI 3.
Unplug the level sensor at the surge tank. Key on, measure signal voltage; high reading unplugged means harness short.
Inspect the sensor float and probe for corrosion; MX engines use a resistive or voltage-divider style sensor in the tank neck.
Repair harness or replace sensor; typical resistance at full level is 80-300 ohms depending on sensor type. Clear code and verify level reading matches physical fill.
symptoms: Low coolant level lamp illuminated with full surge tank
SPN 111 FMI 3 active in PACCAR Davie4 or Jaltest
Coolant level gauge pegged high or showing erratic readings
Possible inhibition of idle shutdown or fan strategies with bad level data
Fault present with engine off and key on

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 4 is a coolant level sensor circuit low voltage or short class fault. Signal short to ground, failed sensor, water-bridged connector, and damaged insulation are the primary causes. Wash-bay moisture creating intermittent low-circuit faults is a documented pattern. Assuming a coolant leak from a sensor circuit short without physical level proof is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Signal short to ground — signal circuit shorted to ground producing low voltage reading
Failed sensor — failed sensor producing short circuit
Water-bridged connector — water bridging connector terminals producing short circuit
Damaged insulation — damaged insulation producing short to ground
steps: Step 1 — Physical Level Verification

Verify physical coolant level first. A true low coolant condition requires leak diagnosis, not sensor replacement. Do not assume a coolant leak from a sensor circuit short without physical level proof.
Step 2 — Disconnect and Short-Check Harness

Disconnect the sensor and short-check the harness. A short that remains with the sensor disconnected confirms a harness fault. Wash-bay moisture creating intermittent low-circuit faults is a documented pattern — inspect the connector for moisture and water intrusion.
Step 3 — Inspect for Rubbed Wires and Moisture

Inspect for rubbed wires near tank straps and moisture in the connector body. Rubbed wires near tank straps produce intermittent shorts to ground. Moisture in the connector body produces water-bridged shorts.
Step 4 — Sensor Replacement After Circuit Proof
Replace the sensor only after circuit proof. Confirm the harness is clean before sensor replacement. A sensor replaced into a harness short will fail the new sensor.
Step 5 — Verify After Repair
Verify coolant level sensor operation after repair. Confirm SPN 111 FMI 4 does not return. Confirm the low-coolant warning clears after repair.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair harness short if harness fault is confirmed.
2 . Dry and clean connector if moisture intrusion is confirmed.
3 . Replace sensor if circuit is clean and sensor fails OEM test.
4 . Address true low coolant condition if physical level is confirmed low.
Verification Steps
Confirm coolant level sensor operation is correct after repair.
Verify SPN 111 FMI 4 does not return after repair.
Confirm low-coolant warning clears after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect surge-tank sensor connector for moisture after wash-bay events.
✓ Inspect sensor harness for rubbed wires at every major service.
✓ Verify physical coolant level at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium; treat as High until real coolant volume is confirmed Severity
Medium; treat as High until real coolant volume is confirmed. The FSM enforces short isolation before parts and before overheat assumptions.
symptoms: Coolant level sensor shorted
Level circuit low voltage
False coolant level reading
Low coolant warning from circuit fault

procedures_full.overview: Volvo SPN 111 FMI 7 indicates a critical issue with the engine coolant temperature sensor. Immediate diagnosis and repair are necessary to prevent engine overheating and potential damage.
causes: Faulty Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor

The sensor itself may have failed due to age, wear, or exposure to extreme conditions. This is a common issue and often requires sensor replacement. Regular inspection can help identify early signs of failure.
Wiring Issues

Damaged or corroded wiring can interrupt the signal from the sensor to the ECM, causing false readings. Inspect the wiring harness for breaks or corrosion. Ensuring proper connectivity can prevent misdiagnoses.
Cooling System Blockage

Blockages in the cooling system can lead to localized overheating, affecting sensor readings. This is less common but can occur if debris is present in the system. Regular system flushes can help prevent blockages.
steps: Stop the vehicle and allow the engine to cool down completely before inspection. This prevents burns and allows for accurate diagnosis.
Check the coolant level in the reservoir and top up with the correct coolant mixture if necessary. Ensure the coolant is of the recommended type and mixture to avoid sensor misreadings.
Inspect the engine coolant temperature sensor for any visible damage or disconnection. Look for signs of corrosion or physical damage that might impair its function.
Use an OBD-II scanner to clear the fault code and see if it reappears after testing. This step helps confirm if the issue is resolved or if further diagnostics are needed.
If the issue persists, consult a professional mechanic for a thorough diagnostic and repair. A professional can perform advanced diagnostics to identify underlying issues.
symptoms: Engine overheating warning light illuminates on the dashboard.
Coolant temperature gauge fluctuates erratically or shows incorrect readings.
Steam or coolant fluid leaking visibly from the engine compartment.
Engine performance issues such as reduced power or stalling.
Unusual noises from the cooling system, indicating stress or malfunction.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 111 FMI 17 is the mildest coolant level warning - the level is slightly low but there's no shutdown risk yet. It's Medium severity and usually resolved with a simple top-off, though it's worth checking for a slow leak. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com uses this early warning as a chance to catch a slow reservoir leak before it becomes a roadside shutdown.
causes: Normal coolant level drop from evaporation or minor consumption
Not necessarily a fault - some gradual level drop between service intervals is normal, especially in hot climates.
Hairline crack in the coolant reservoir tank
Mechanical fault - a small crack can slowly lower coolant level without leaving an obvious puddle.
Corroded coolant level sensor connector
Electrical fault - a poor connection can produce a falsely low reading even with adequate coolant level.
Slow leak at a hose clamp or fitting elsewhere in the cooling system
Mechanical fault - a minor external leak reduces coolant volume gradually over time.
steps: Let the engine cool, then visually check the coolant level in the reservoir tank and top off with the correct coolant/water mixture if it's genuinely low.
Connect Mack PTT and confirm the code clears after topping off coolant during the next drive cycle.
If the level was already full, inspect the coolant level sensor connector in the reservoir tank for corrosion.
Check the reservoir tank itself for a small crack or weld seam leak that could be slowly lowering the level without an obvious puddle underneath.
Pressure-test the cooling system if coolant loss is confirmed to find the source before it escalates to a more severe level warning.
symptoms: Coolant level gauge showing slightly below full
Amber warning light in some configurations
No performance impact at this severity level
No shutdown risk in the immediate term

causes: This condition is typically a circuit failed high.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for multiple codes.
If other faults are active in addition to fault 111/3, troubleshoot the other faults first.
If only fault 111/3 is active, go to step 2.
Disconnect the ECL Sensor.
Measure the resistance between pin 1 and 2 of the ECL Sensor.
If the resistance is greater than 600 kΩ (submerged) or open, replace ECL sensor. See Figure
"Engine Coolant Level Sensor Installation for CPC"
. Refer to "30.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. Engine Coolant Level Sensor Installation for CPC
If the resistance is less than 600 kΩ, go to step 4.
Turn the ignition ON (key On, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pins 1 and 2 of the ECL Sensor harness connector.
If the voltage is greater than 2.75 volts, go to step 7.
If the voltage is less than 2.75 volts, go to step 6.
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the ECL Sensor harness connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 2.75 volts, repair the open between pin 2 of the CPC #3 connector and the ECL Sensor harness. Refer to "30.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is less than 2.75 volts, repair the open between pin 11 of the CPC #3 connector and the ECL Sensor harness. Refer to "30.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the CPC #3 connector.
Measure the resistance between pins 1 and 2 of the ECL Sensor harness connector.
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short between the ECL Sensor harness connector pins 1 and 2 and pins 2 and 11 of the CPC #3 connector. Refer to "30.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, review steps 3 through 8
. If the results are the same, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center (313–592–5800).

Turn ignition OFF.

. If the results are the same, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center (313–592–5800).

dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 171 FMI 3 – Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Voltage High (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 171 FMI 3 indicates that the ambient air temperature sensor is reporting a voltage signal above the expected range. This can affect fuel management and emissions performance.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Incorrect temperature readings
Reduced fuel efficiency
Possible aftertreatment warnings
Cause
This fault is commonly caused by wiring issues, short circuits, damaged connectors, or a failed ambient temperature sensor.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving may be possible temporarily, but continued operation with low fuel pressure may cause engine stalling or additional damage.
Recommended Action
Inspect wiring and connectors for damage. Test the ambient air temperature sensor and replace if necessary.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 171 FMI 3 mean?
 
SPN 171 FMI 3 indicates that the ambient air temperature sensor is reporting a voltage higher than the expected range.
 
 
What causes SPN 171 FMI 3?
 
Common causes include a faulty ambient temperature sensor, shorted wiring, damaged connectors, or electrical issues in the sensor circuit.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 171 FMI 3?
 
Driving is typically possible, but inaccurate temperature readings can affect fuel management and emissions performance.
 
 
Will SPN 171 FMI 3 cause a derate?
 
In most cases it does not immediately cause a derate, but unresolved sensor faults can contribute to performance or emissions-related issues.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 171 FMI 3?
 
Inspect wiring and connectors for damage, test the ambient air temperature sensor, and replace it if voltage readings remain outside specification.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 171 FMI 3 on Scania engines means the ambient air temperature sensor circuit is reading voltage above normal, consistent with a short to a high source. It's a low-severity fault, but it can quietly affect cold-start fueling and fan control until fixed. Ambient air temperature might seem like a minor data point, but on Scania engines it feeds directly into cold-start fueling strategy and cooling fan logic. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com flags SPN 171 FMI 3 as one of those faults that's easy to dismiss because there's no derate attached, but a wrong ambient reading can cause winter starting complaints that look unrelated on the surface. The fix is usually quick - check the sensor circuit for a short before replacing the sensor itself.
causes: Corroded or damaged sensor connector
The sensor is mounted in an exposed location on the front of the cab or mirror arm, making it prone to moisture intrusion and connector corrosion over time.
Chafed wiring shorting to a nearby power circuit
Harness routing near the cab exterior can rub against body panels or brackets, wearing through insulation and shorting the signal wire high.
Failed ambient air temperature sensor
The sensor element itself can fail internally, producing an out-of-range voltage reading independent of any wiring issue.
steps: Pull the fault with Scania's SDP3 software or a Texa diagnostic interface and confirm SPN 171 FMI 3 is active, and check the reported ambient temperature value against actual conditions.
Locate the ambient air temperature sensor, typically mounted near the front of the cab or on the mirror arm, and inspect the connector for corrosion or a pinched wire.
Disconnect the sensor and check the signal wire for a short to a nearby power source using a multimeter with the harness isolated from the ECM.
Check the sensor itself with a multimeter for correct resistance at a known ambient temperature, comparing against the manufacturer's resistance-versus-temperature chart.
Repair or replace any damaged wiring, or replace the sensor if it fails the resistance check, then clear the code and confirm the reported temperature tracks a known thermometer reading.
Recheck the fault status after a drive cycle to confirm it doesn't return.
symptoms: No noticeable drivability symptom in most cases
Occasional harder cold starts if the ECM thinks it's warmer outside than it actually is
Cooling fan behaving slightly differently than expected in cold weather
Amber dash lamp with no accompanying performance complaint

Common issues leading to this problem include transmission data errors and faults with the gear sensor. Damage or disconnections in the transmission range sensor and its wiring harness often contribute to communication failures. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 716: Transmission Selected Gear
dd_procedures.overview: The Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) is equipped with solenoids to direct pneumatic flow to actuate the clutch and shift rails and sensors to monitor the clutch and shift rail positions. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) compares the clutch and shift rail commands with the clutch and shift rail positions including speed sensors (ratio calculation) to ensure proper operation.
causes: TCM Software issue Internal failure PTO (If equipped) PTO Confirm Ball Switch Circuit and/or wiring harness shorted to ground Additional Tools None
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 716 FMI 12 is Active or Inactive, and the transmission is equipped with a PTO, Go to Step B If Fault Code 716 FMI 12 is Active or Inactive and the transmission is not equipped with a PTO, Go to Step C

B. Verify TCM Software Key off. Allow TCM to perform a complete power down. Key on with engine off. Connect Service Ranger. Go to “Programming”. dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with position sensors to monitor shift rail positions and speed sensors to monitor shaft speeds. The sensor information is provided to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of making shift decisions, confirming gear engagement, and monitoring shift rail positions. The TCM compares the shift rail commands to the shift rail positions and shaft speeds (ratio calculation) to ensure the transmission is operating properly. troubleshooting_faq.question: What air pressure is required for the Eaton UltraShift range cylinder to shift correctly?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The Eaton UltraShift range cylinder typically requires 90 to 120 psi of regulated air supply for reliable range shifts. If the truck's air system pressure is below this range due to a compressor fault, air dryer issue, or a leak, the range cylinder may not shift fully, resulting in FMI 7 range faults. Confirming adequate air supply pressure is an important first diagnostic step.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can a failed air dryer cause SPN 524 FMI 7 on the Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: An air dryer that allows water or oil contamination into the air system can cause solenoid valves and shift cylinders to malfunction over time. Contaminants can cause solenoid valve spools to stick. If range shift faults are combined with brake system air quality concerns, the air dryer and system filter should be inspected.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does the Eaton UltraShift Plus have the same range shift design as the older Fuller AutoShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The UltraShift Plus and earlier Fuller AutoShift both use a pneumatically actuated range section with similar operating principles. However, the specific range solenoid valve design, position sensor, and diagnostic parameter names may differ between generations. ServiceRanger handles both platforms with model-specific procedures.

procedures_full.overview: The ePTO feature allows the diesel engine to remain off for extended periods of time during PTO usage. The DC/DC Converter is energized only in ePTO mode so it can charge the 12-volt battery system. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) operates the Motor/Generator to power the transmission mounted PTO. Note: To determine which module is controlling the PTO connect ServiceRanger and select “Roadranger Configurations.” Under the “Hybrid Control Module” option is a list for PTO Feedback— Analog Controlled (HCM), or J1939 Controlled (Body Controller). procedures_full.overview: The Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) is equipped with solenoids to direct pneumatic flow to actuate the clutch and shift rails and sensors to monitor the clutch and shift rail positions. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) compares the clutch and shift rail commands with the clutch and shift rail positions including speed sensors (ratio calculation) to ensure proper operation.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Transmission Select Gear command, if the command is invalid, the TCM sets the fault code Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device or Component: Inappropriate selected gear relative to output shaft speed.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 12: Condition no longer exists
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 12: Transmission shifts to Neutral PTO Mode prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 12: Condition no longer exists
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 12: TCM Software issue Internal failure PTO (If equipped) PTO Confirm Ball Switch Circuit and/or wiring harness shorted to ground

steps.A:
A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity report created during the Diagnostic Procedure.

 If Fault Code 716 FMI 12 is Active or Inactive and the transmission is not equipped with a PTO, Go to Step C
steps.B:
B. Verify TCM Software 
 Key off. 
 Allow TCM to perform a complete power down. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect Service Ranger. 
 Go to “Programming”. 
 Under “Software Information”, verify TCM software version. 
 If TCM software is less than 5516036, update the TCM software to latest available version and inspect PTO Confirm Ball Switch and Circuit. Go to Step V 
 If TCM software is 5516036 or greater, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Contact Information . Go to Step V 
 Note: A corroded and/or contaminated PTO Confirm Ball Switch or Circuit intermittently shorted to ground may cause Fault Code 716 FMI 12 to set Active. Refer to OEM and/or Body Builder guidelines for repair or replacement.

 Key off.

 Key on with engine off.

 If TCM software is less than 5516036, update TCM software to latest available version. Go to Step V

steps.V:

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with position sensors to monitor shift rail positions and speed sensors to monitor shaft speeds. The sensor information is provided to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of making shift decisions, confirming gear engagement, and monitoring shift rail positions. The TCM compares the shift rail commands to the shift rail positions and shaft speeds (ratio calculation) to ensure the transmission is operating properly. The sensors and shift rails are located in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the transmission operation. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 206: TCM Program Memory
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs), receives feedback from sensors and actuates solenoids to control transmission performance. The TCM is mounted to the transmission and connected to the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector. The TCM is connected to the transmission sensors and solenoids at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
causes: TCM Software issue Internal failure FMI 2, 14, 31: TCM Incorrect calibration file configured in the TCM or missing Additional Tools Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 206 FMI 11, 12, 13 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B If Fault Code 206 FMI 2, 14 or 31 is Active, contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies at 800-826-4357 for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V If Fault Code 206 FMI 2, 14 or 31 is Inactive, the correct calibration file is installed. Go to Step V

Go to Step V TCM Software

If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 206 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 206 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 200: TCM Operation 1
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs), receives feedback from sensors and actuates solenoids to control transmission operation. The TCM is mounted to the transmission and connected to the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector. The TCM is connected to the transmission sensors and solenoids at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
causes: TCM Software issue Internal failure FMI 14: TCM Incorrect TCM installed on transmission Incorrect MTM Type configured Additional Tools Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950
1. Transmission Control Module (TCM)
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 200 FMI 0, 1, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 18, 19, 20, 21 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B If Fault Code 200 FMI 14 and all the following fault codes are Active: Fault Code 275 FMI 5 Fault Code 295 FMI 8 Fault Code 315 FMI 8 Fault Code 320 FMI 8 Note: Fault Code 596 FMI 5 may also be Active depending on MTM Type configured in TCM. Go to Configure Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) Type . Go to Step V If Fault Code 200 FMI 14 is Active, the TCM installed on the transmission is not correct for the transmission model. Verify the transmission model number and install the correct TCM. Go to Step V If Fault Code 200 FMI 14 is Inactive, the TCM is installed on the correct transmission model. Test complete, Go to Step V

B. Verify TCM software. Key off. Allow TCM to perform a complete power down. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Programming”. Under “Software Information”, record TCM software in table. If a TCM software update is available, update TCM software. Go to Step V If the TCM is at the latest available software, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Contact Information . Go to Step V TCM Software

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 200 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 200 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

TCM, diğer araç Elektronik Kontrol Üniteleri (ECU'lar) ile iletişim kurar, sensörlerden geri besleme alır ve şanzıman çalışmasını kontrol etmek için solenoidleri çalıştırır. TCM şanzımana monte edilmiştir ve 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörü ile 20 Yollu TCM Gövde Kablo Demeti Konnektörüne bağlıdır. TCM, 74 Yollu Şanzıman Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe şanzıman sensörlerine ve solenoidlerine bağlıdır.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with a Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs), receives feedback from sensors and actuates solenoids to control transmission operation. The TCM is mounted to the transmission and connected to the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector. The TCM is connected to the transmission sensors and solenoids through the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM performs a self-check during operation. If a failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 0 – Data Valid But Above Normal (Most Severe): TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 1 – Data Valid But Below Normal (Most Severe): TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 8 – Abnormal Frequency: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 10 – Abnormal Rate of Change: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 11 – Root Cause Unknown: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: The TCM is incorrectly configured as non-Endurant model. FMI 18 – Data Valid But Below Normal (Moderately Severe): TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 19 – Received Network Data in Error: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: The TCM is incorrectly configured for Endurant HD or Procision model.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Amber warning lamp on No degraded modes Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist
procedures_full.possible_causes: All FMIs: TCM Software issue Internal failure

steps.A:

steps.B:

 Key off.

 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger.

 If the TCM was updated to the latest available software during the Diagnostic Procedure, Go to Step V

steps.V:

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates an electrical failure of the relay that allows the engine to start after startup conditions are met. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
procedures_full.detection: Starting at key-on and throughout operation, the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) constantly measures the circuit. A failure mode of short to battery, short to ground or open circuit is detected.
procedures_full.fallback: The start enable relay has no fallback; however, if the failure occurred before the engine was started, it is possible the engine will not start.

steps.A:
A. Verify SER is correctly wired. Check for active or Inactive fault codes, noting FMI. 
 Key on. 
 Note: The SER must be wired according to Eaton GEN III requirements (shown on previous page) for tests to work properly. If wired differently, consult OEM for correct wiring schematic. 
 Retrieve active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-way diagnostic connector. 
 What FMIs are present? 
 If FMI 14 is present, Go to Step B 
 If FMI 3 or 4 are present, Go to Step C
steps.B:
B. Visually inspect SER wiring. 
 Inspect OEM SER breakout connector and inspect for misrouted or defective OEM wiring. Inspect per OEM guidelines. 
 If SER breakout connector is not connected to SER, repair/replace SER per OEM guidelines. Go to Step V 
 If circuit has been bypassed, rewire per OEM guidelines. Go to Step V 
 If harness is defective, repair the Vehicle Harness per OEM guidelines. Go to Step V
steps.C:
C. Measure resistance of SER through the Transmission Harness. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect negative battery cable. 
 Disconnect Vehicle Harness 38-way connector. 
 Measure resistance between Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 32 and Pin 4 and measure resistance between Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 32 and ground. 
 If resistance between Pin 32 and Pin 4 is 40 to 120 ohms (12-volt system) or 140 to 480 ohms (24-volt system) and resistance between 32 and ground is OL, (if fault code is Active) replace the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 
 Go to Step V 
 If resistance is outside of range, Go to Step B
steps.D:
D. Measure resistance of SER at the relay. 
 Remove SER from vehicle dash harness. 
 Measure resistance between SER Pin 85 and Pin 86. 
 If resistance is 40 to 120 ohms (12-volt system) or 140 to 480 ohms (24-volt system), repair/replace OEM wiring from TECU to SER. Go to Step C 
 If resistance is outside of range, replace SER. Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and negative battery cable. 
 Key on. 
 Clear codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the code. 
 Check for codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no codes, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 17 appears, Go to Step A to find error in testing. 
 If fault code other than 17 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with a Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The TECU performs a variety of functions including receiving inputs from sensors, sending outputs to control devices, operating X-Y Shifter motors and actuators and making shift decisions. Fault Code 12 indicates an internal failure of the TECU.
procedures_full.detection: The TECU performs a self-check during power up. If the TECU does not detect valid memory, or if there are missing or corrupt transmission configuration files, this fault sets Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: TECU is unable to determine the proper transmission configuration.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 13: TECU has detected a proper configuration for the transmission.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 13 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Engine may not crank. Transmission may not engage a gear. Transmission may not make up shifts or down shifts. Engine may have to be shut down with transmission still in gear. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 13: TECU has detected a proper configuration for the transmission.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 13 TECU Internal failure Component Identification 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU)

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. 
 If Fault Code 12 is Active or Inactive, replace Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) . Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Clear fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 If no fault codes set Active and vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 12 sets Active during the test drive, refer to Contact Information and contact Eaton for further diagnostics. 
 If a fault code other than 12 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

procedures_full.overview: Fault Code 25 indicates the TECU has determined that all transmission functions are operating normally and the transmission currently has no logged fault codes.

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2010 Series 60 14L engine is known to experience injector failures and communication errors between electronic control modules (ECM) following repairs. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 35 - J1939 Communication Link
dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) failed to communicate with the engine over the J1939 data link. If you have an Active Fault Code 35 with an UltraShift DM transmission and the engine will crank but not start, please check the OEM supplied MEIIR (Momentary Engine Ignition Interrupt Relay) circuit. Ensure that the engine has proper ignition voltage. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"

steps: A. Verify continuity of J1939 Data Link low (-) circuit and test for short to ground. Key off. Disconnect negative battery cable. Disconnect Vehicle Harness 38-way connector. Disconnect engine ECM connector which contains the J1939 Data Link. Measure resistance between: Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and engine ECM pin number (see OEM wiring for (-) J1939). Vehicle harness 38-way Pin 2 and ground. If resistance between Pin 2 and engine ECM pin is 0 to 0.3 ohms and if resistance between Pin 2 and ground is OL , Go to Step B If resistance is outside of range, repair J1939 Data Link Harness between engine ECM and TECU. Go to Step V

B. Verify continuity of J1939 Data Link (+) circuit and test for short to ground. Key off. Go to Step V

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 35: J1939 Communication Link
dd_procedures.overview: The J1939 Data Link is a Controller Area Network (CAN) communication bus. The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the J1939 Data Link to communicate with other ECUs (ABS, Engine, Body Controller, etc.). The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) sends and receives messages from other ECUs on the data link to determine when to initiate a shift, hold shifts, command engine torque to make shifts, as well as other functions. Proper operation of the J1939 Data Link is critical for shift performance. Fault Code 35 indicates an issue with communication across the J1939 Data Link.
causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 35 is Active, Go to Step C If Fault Code 35 is Inactive, and there are other Active fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes first per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . If Fault Code 35 is Inactive, and there are no other Active fault codes, Go to Step B

Neutral Coast may refer to one of several different systems that control various elements of vehicle cruise control logic. The transmission controlled version is an Eaton proprietary logic where the transmission makes the decisions when the driveline should be engaged or disengaged. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 115: Primary Data Link (J1939 A)
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) over the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages called the Primary Data Link and Secondary Data Link. The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to communicate with the Engine, ABS, Body, and other vehicle ECUs during normal operation. The Secondary Data Link is used as a backup in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Primary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 35: J1939 Communication Link
dd_procedures.overview: The J1939 Data Link is a Controller Area Network (CAN) communication bus. The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the J1939 Data Link to communicate with other ECUs (ABS, Engine, Body Controller, etc.). The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) sends and receives messages from other ECUs on the data link to determine when to initiate a shift, hold shifts, command engine torque to make shifts, as well as other functions. Proper operation of the J1939 Data Link is critical for shift performance. Fault Code 35 indicates an issue with communication across the J1939 Data Link.

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) over the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages: the Primary Data Link (J1939A) and the Secondary Data Link (J1939B). The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to send and receive messages to and from the Engine ECU, Anti-Lock Brake ECU and other vehicle ECUs to complete transmission shift operations. The Secondary Data Link is used in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Primary Data Link (J1939A) is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. The Secondary Data Link (J1939B) is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors vehicle and Engine ECU broadcast messages. If messages are not received or are invalid, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Primary Data Link (J1939A) vehicle ECU(s) messages not received for 1 second. FMI 8 – Abnormal Frequency: Primary Data Link (J1939A) Engine ECU messages not received for 1 second while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECU(s). FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: Primary Data Link (J1939A) vehicle messages not received for 5 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Primary Data Link (J1939A) Engine ECU messages not received for 5 seconds while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECU(s). FMI 19 – Received Network Data In Error: Primary Data Link (J1939A) vehicle ECU(s) messages received but in error. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: Primary Data Link (J1939A) receiving a vehicle ECU(s) “Stop Start Broadcast” message.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: Primary Data Link (J1939A) vehicle ECU(s) messages received and valid for 20 seconds. FMI 8: Primary Data Link (J1939A) Engine ECU messages received and valid for 20 seconds. FMI 9: Primary Data Link (J1939A) vehicle ECU(s) messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Primary Data Link (J1939A) Engine ECU messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 19: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist. FMI 31: Fault condition no longer exists.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 2, 8, 19: Amber warning lamp on No degraded modes FMI 9, 14: Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is configured for J1939 Start Enable feature, engine may not crank If vehicle is moving and transmission is in a gear higher than the lowest available start gear: Coast Mode and Neutral Coast prohibited Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Inertia Brake activation prohibited Upshifts prohibited Clutch engagements prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO mode prohibited Hill Start Aid prohibited If vehicle is moving and transmission is in a gear higher than the lowest available start gear and Secondary Data Link (J1939B) is not available: Red stop lamp on Clutch engagements prohibited, vehicle may coast to a stop Transmission downshifts to lowest available start gear FMI 31: Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is configured for J1939 Start Enable feature, engine may not crank Lowest available start gear only Coast Mode and Neutral Coast prohibited Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Inertia Brake activation prohibited Upshifts prohibited Clutch disengagements prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO mode prohibited Hill Start Aid prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive

procedures_full.overview_tr: Şanzıman Kontrol Modülü (TCM), diğer araç Elektronik Kontrol Üniteleri (ECU'lar) ile araç J1939 veri hattı üzerinden iletişim kurar. TCM, mesaj gönderip almak için iki araç J1939 veri hattı kullanır: Birincil Veri Hattı (J1939A) ve İkincil Veri Hattı (J1939B). Birincil Veri Hattı, TCM tarafından şanzıman vites değişimi işlemlerini tamamlamak için Motor ECU'su, Kilitlenme Önleyici Fren ECU'su ve diğer araç ECU'ları ile mesaj gönderip almak üzere kullanılır. İkincil Veri Hattı, Birincil Veri Hattı çalışmadığında kullanılır. Birincil Veri Hattı (J1939A), 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır. procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) over the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages called the Primary Data Link and Secondary Data Link. The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to communicate with the Engine, ABS, Body, and other vehicle ECUs during normal operation. The Secondary Data Link is used as a backup in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Primary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors messages broadcast over the vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A). If vehicle or engine messages are not received or in error, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages not received for 1 second (Service). FMI 8 – Abnormal Frequency: Engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages not received for 1 second while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECUs (Service). FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages not received for 5 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages not received for 5 seconds while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECUs. FMI 19 – Received Network Data In Error: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received but in error. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) receiving a “Stop Start Broadcast” message.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: Valid vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 20 seconds. FMI 8: Valid engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 20 seconds. FMI 9: Valid vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 10 seconds. FMI 19: Key cycle and condition no longer exists. FMI 31: Condition no longer exists.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 2, 8, 19: Amber warning lamp on No degraded modes FMI 9, 14: Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is configured for J1939 Start Enable feature, engine may not crank Lowest available start gear only Urge to Move and Creep prohibited Launch quality may degrade Upshifts prohibited PTO mode prohibited If vehicle is moving and transmission is in a gear higher than the lowest available start gear and Secondary Data Link is not available: Red stop lamp on Clutch engagement prohibited, vehicle may coast to stop Transmission downshifts to lowest available start gear FMI 31: Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is configured for J1939 Start Enable feature, engine may not crank Lowest available start gear only Urge to Move and Creep prohibited Launch quality may degrade Upshifts prohibited PTO mode prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 2: Valid vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 20 seconds. FMI 8: Valid engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 20 seconds. FMI 9: Valid vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid engine Primary Data Link (J1939 A) messages received for 10 secon
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 2, 9: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Bent, spread, or loose terminals Excessive electrical noise Missing or additional terminating resistors Other Vehicle ECU(s) Internal failure FMI 8, 14: Vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939 A) – Between Engine ECU and TCM Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Bent, spread, or loose terminals Excessive electrical noise Missing or additional terminating resistors Engine ECU Not powering up Internal failure FMI 19: Other Vehicle ECU(s) Internal failure FMI 31: Other Vehicle ECU(s) Informational only, indicates a Vehicle ECU experienced a programming event.

steps.A:
A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels.

 If Fault Code 115 FMI 14 is Active, Go to Step N 
 Note: If ServiceRanger connects to the TCM, the vehicle data link is currently functional between the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector and TCM. Refer to OEM guidelines for Engine ECU and vehicle data link diagnostic instructions. 
 If Fault Code 115 FMI 14 is Inactive, an intermittent condition may exist on the Primary Data Link with the following: 
 Power up issue with the Engine ECU 
 Vehicle Primary Data Link to the Engine ECU 
 Fault(s) reported from the Engine ECU 
 Refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939A) or Engine ECU. Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 115 FMI 19 is Active, a condition may exist on the Primary Data Link with the Engine ECU or other Vehicle ECU(s) reporting an issue. Refer to OEM for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V

 If Fault Code 115 FMI 31 is Inactive or Active, informational only, indicates a vehicle ECU experienced a programming event. Test complete.

procedures_full.overview: The J1939 Data Link is a Controller Area Network (CAN) communication bus. The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the J1939 Data Link to communicate with other ECUs (ABS, Engine, Body Controller, etc.). The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) sends and receives messages from other ECUs on the data link to determine when to initiate a shift, hold shifts, command engine torque to make shifts, as well as other functions. Proper operation of the J1939 Data Link is critical for shift performance. Fault Code 35 indicates an issue with communication across the J1939 Data Link.
procedures_full.detection: TECU has either lost communication or received erratic signals over the J1939 Data Link and the TECU has not detected any low battery system fault codes.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: TECU has lost communication or has received erratic signals over the J1939 Data Link for 5 seconds or longer.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: TECU receives messages across the data link for at least 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 2 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). If vehicle is configured for the J1939 Start Enable feature the engine does not crank. If fault occurs during power up, the transmission requires the driver to manually synchronize shifts with the throttle. If fault occurs while driving, transmission remains in its current gear until the vehicle stops. Transmission then requires the driver to manually synchronize shifts with the throttle. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 2: TECU receives messages across the data link for at least 10 seconds.

Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. 9-Way Diagnostic Connector (in cab) 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 3. 9-Way Diagnostic Connector (Black) - OEM Specific CD (in cab) 4. 9-way Diagnostic Connector (Green) - OEM Specific CD (in cab) 5. 9-way Diagnostic Connector (Green) - OEM Specific FG (in cab)

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. 
 If Fault Code 35 is Active, Go to Step C 
 If Fault Code 35 is Inactive, and there are other Active fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes first per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . 
 If Fault Code 35 is Inactive, and there are no other Active fault codes, Go to Step B
steps.B:
B. Use Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode to locate intermittent failures. 
 Set parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Place transmission in PD Mode. See more about Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode . 
 Note: Transmission does not enter PD Mode when Active fault codes exist. 
 Wiggle J1939 Data Link wiring and Vehicle Harness wiring throughout the vehicle. Look for signs of pinched or chafed wiring. Verify all connections are clean and tight. 
 Exit PD Mode by powering down. 
 Note: Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. 
 If Fault Code 35 or Fault Code 36 became Active while wiggling the J1939 Data Link or the Vehicle Harness, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of J1939 Data Link. Go to Step V 
 If no fault codes became Active, Go to Step C

 Key off.

steps.D:

 Key off. 
 If vehicle is equipped with a Bulkhead Connection, inspect Bulkhead Connector for corrosion, loose terminals, and bent or spread pins. 
 Wiggle wiring connections to the Bulkhead Connector to verify the pins are not loose and are secure within the connector. 
 If no Bulkhead Connection is present, Go to Step E 
 If no damage is found and the connector is not loose, Go to Step E 
 If damage or looseness is found, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of Bulkhead Connection. Go to Step V

procedures_full.overview: The J1939 Data Link is a Controller Area Network (CAN) communication bus. The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the J1939 Data Link to communicate with other ECUs (ABS, Engine, Body Controller, etc.). The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) sends and receives messages from other ECUs on the data link to determine when to initiate a shift, hold shifts, command engine torque to make shifts, as well as other functions. Proper operation of the J1939 Data Link is critical for shift performance. Fault Code 36 indicates the TECU can communicate with other ECUs on the J1939 Data Link but has lost communication with the Engine ECU.
procedures_full.detection: TECU has either lost communication or received erratic signals from the Engine ECU over the J1939 Data Link and the TECU has not detected any low or weak battery system fault codes.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 14 – Special Instructions: TECU has either lost communication or has received erratic signals from the Engine ECU over the J1939 Data Link for 5 seconds or longer.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 14: TECU receives messages across the data link for at least 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 14 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). If vehicle is configured for the J1939 Start Enable feature the engine does not crank. If fault occurs during power up, the transmission requires the driver to manually synchronize shifts with the throttle. If fault occurs while driving, transmission remains in its current gear until the vehicle stops. Transmission then requires the driver to manually synchronize shifts with the throttle. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 14: TECU receives messages across the data link for at least 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 14 J1939 Data Link Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Excessive electrical noise Missing or additional terminating resistors Engine ECU Internal failure Vehicle Harness Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Engine Harness Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Component Identification 1. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 2. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. 9-Way Diagnostic Connector (in cab) 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 3. 9-Way Diagnostic Connector (Black) - OEM Specific CD (in cab) 4. 9-way Diagnostic Connector (Green) - OEM Specific CD (in cab) 5. 9-way Diagnostic Connector (Green) - OEM Specific FG (in cab)

procedures_full.overview: When available and enabled, Neutral Coast Mode allows the transmission to disengage the driveline by pulling out of gear on slight downhill grades, where little to no engine power is required, when the vehicle is in cruise control and the transmission is in Drive Mode. Neutral Coast may refer to one of several different systems that control various elements of vehicle cruise control logic. The transmission controlled version is an Eaton proprietary logic where the transmission makes the decisions when the driveline should be engaged or disengaged. Engine/J1939 controlled systems use an engine or another vehicle ECU to determine the appropriate times to engage or disengage the driveline. Engine/J1939 controlled systems have several different variations and brand names based on the manufacturer. Fault Code 76 indicates that either the Transmission ECU or Engine/Vehicle ECU are mis-configured for use with a Neutral Coast system.
procedures_full.detection: Incorrect engine/vehicle or transmission configuration settings can set this fault. When the engine/vehicle and transmission configurations are not matched for use with Neutral Coast systems, this fault will set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 11 – FMI Unknown: Transmission configurations are incorrectly set for use with a Neutral Coast system. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: Engine or vehicle configurations and/or software are incorrectly set for use with a Neutral Coast system.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: This fault is set inactive when the transmission and engine/vehicle Neutral Coast system configurations or software are correctly set.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Neutral Coast systems will not function. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: This fault is set inactive when the transmission and engine/vehicle Neutral Coast system configurations or software are correctly set.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 11 TECU Incorrect Transmission Neutral Coast Mode configuration settings FMI 31 Engine ECM Incorrect engine software settings Component Identification 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU)

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes.

steps.B:
B. Determine which Neutral Coast system the vehicle uses. 
 Determine if the vehicle uses the Eaton Transmission Controlled or Engine/J1939 Controlled Neutral Coast system. 
 Notice
 Some engines can only be configured to use their proprietary Neutral Coast system and do not support the Eaton transmission-based Neutral Coast system. Engine systems are marketed under a variety of brand names. Contact the engine OEM for more information. 
 If the vehicle uses the Eaton Transmission Controlled Neutral Coast system, Go to Step C

steps.C:
C. Configure Neutral Coast Mode for the Eaton transmission based system. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 In ServiceRanger, go to Configuration. 
 Record current value of the Neutral Coast Mode configuration. 
 Change the Neutral Coast Mode configuration to “Transmission Control”. If ServiceRanger permissions do not allow you to change this configuration, contact Eaton at (800) 826-8347 for support. 
 Notice
 Some engines can only be configured to use their proprietary Neutral Coast system and do not support the Eaton transmission-based Neutral Coast system. Engine systems are marketed under a variety of brand names. Contact the engine OEM for more information. 
 If any engine fault codes set, contact the engine manufacturer to properly set engine settings to operate with Neutral Coast Mode. Go to Step V 
 If no engine fault codes set, test complete. Go to Step V
steps.D:

 If any Engine/J1939 fault codes associated to the Neutral Coast system are set Inactive, test complete. Go to Step V
steps.E:
E. Disable Neutral Coast Mode. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 In ServiceRanger, go to Configuration. 
 Record current value of the Neutral Coast Mode configuration. 
 Change the Neutral Coast Mode configuration to “Disabled”. If ServiceRanger permissions do not allow you to change this configuration, contact Eaton at (800) 826-8347 for support. 
 Notice
 Some engine based Neutral Coast systems auto-configure with the transmission, overriding the Neutral Coast Mode configuration setting in the transmission. These systems must be turned on or off in the engine ECM. Contact the engine OEM for more information. 
 Properly set any engine configuration settings required to disable Neutral Coast per manufacturer requirements. 
 Warning
 Contact the engine OEM or reference the Eaton Automated Transmission Engine Configuration Settings Guide (TRIG0910) for more information about engine settings. 
 If any engine fault codes set, contact the engine manufacturer to properly set engine Neutral Coast settings. Go to Step V 
 If no engine fault codes set, test complete. Go to Step V
steps.V:

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) has communicated with another ECU, but is unable to communicate with the engine ECU over the J1939 data link. If you have an Active Fault Code 36 with an UltraShift DM transmission and engine will crank but not start, please check the OEM supplied MEIIR (Momentary Engine Ignition Interrupt Relay) circuit and see that the engine has proper ignition voltage. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
procedures_full.detection: The fault is detected if J1939 communication from the engine is lost for 5 seconds and other devices are present on J1939.
procedures_full.fallback: If the fault occurs during power-up, the transmission will go into AutoSelect mode. If the fault occurs while moving, it causes an in-place fallback and the transmission will remain in the gear that was engaged when the failure occurred. Once the vehicle stops, start and reverse gears can be selected and the transmission will operate in AutoSelect mode.

steps.A:
A. Verify continuity of J1939 Data Link Low (-) circuit and test for short to ground. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect negative battery cable. 
 Disconnect Vehicle Harness 38-way connector. 
 Disconnect engine ECM connector which contains the J1939 Data Link. 
 Measure resistance between: 
 Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for (-) J1939). 
 Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and ground. 
 If resistance between Pin 2 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for (-)J1939) is 0 to 0.3 ohms and if resistance between Pin 2 and ground is OL, Go to Step B 
 If resistance is outside of range , repair J1939 Data Link Harness between engine ECM and TECU. Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Verify continuity of J1939 Data Link High (+) circuit and test for short to ground. 
 Key off. 
 Measure resistance between: 
 Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 3 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for (+)J1939) 
 Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 3 and ground 
 If resistance between Pin 3 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for (+)J1939) is 0 to 0.3 ohms and if resistance between Pin 3 and ground is OL, 
 If equipped with J1939 Lite, Go to Step D 
 If not equipped with J1939 Lite, Go to Step C 
 If resistance is outside of range, repair J1939 Data Link Harness between Engine ECM and TECU. Go to Step V
steps.C:
C. Verify continuity of J1939 Data Link Shield (+) wire (if equipped) and test for short to ground. 
 Key off. 
 Measure resistance between Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 1 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for J1939 shield). 
 If resistance between Pin 1 and engine ECM pin # (see OEM wiring for J1939 shield) is 0 to 0.3 ohms, Go to Step D 
 If resistance is outside of range, repair J1939 Data Link Harness between engine ECM and TECU. Go to Step V
steps.D:
D. Confirm the presence of terminating resistors in the J1939 Data Link. 
 Key off. 
 Measure resistance between Vehicle Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and Pin 3. 
 Note: Make sure the volt/ohm meter is on the proper scale (around 200 ohm scale). 
 If resistance between Pin 2 and Pin 3 is between 50 to 70 ohms, Go to Step V 
 If resistance is more than 70 ohms, 1or more of the terminating resistors on the J1939 data link harness is either missing or out of range. Repair J1939 Data Link Harness. Go to Step V 
 If resistance is less than 50 ohms, repair the J1939 Data Link between the Engine ECM and the TECU. Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. 
 Key on. 
 Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code. 
 Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no codes, test complete.
