procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) failed to communicate with the engine over the J1939 data link. If you have an Active Fault Code 35 with an UltraShift DM transmission and the engine will crank but not start, please check the OEM supplied MEIIR (Momentary Engine Ignition Interrupt Relay) circuit. Ensure that the engine has proper ignition voltage. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
procedures_full.detection: Seventy-five seconds after key-on and throughout the operation, the TECU constantly monitors the communication with the engine ECM. If a communication fault occurs for more than 5 seconds, and no other devices are present, Fault Code 35 is set.
procedures_full.fallback: If the fault occurs during power-up the transmission will go into AutoSelect mode. If the fault occurs while moving, it causes an in-place fallback. The transmission will remain in the gear that was engaged when the failure occurred. Once the vehicle stops, start and reverse gears can be selected and the transmission will operate in AutoSelect mode.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 2 indicates turbo actuator control data or response erratic. Harness intermittents, failing actuator, carbon binding varying with temperature, poor power feed, and connector fretting are the primary causes. Actuator replaced repeatedly while a heat-damaged pigtail remains is a documented pattern. Replacing the turbo for an actuator or harness fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Harness intermittents — harness intermittents at actuator connector in turbo heat zone producing erratic control
Failing actuator — failing actuator electronics producing erratic control response
Carbon binding varying with temperature — carbon binding varying with temperature producing erratic response
Poor power feed — poor power feed producing erratic actuator control
Connector fretting — connector fretting producing intermittent signal
steps: Step 1 — Electrical Integrity Hot

Check electrical integrity while hot. Actuator connector at turbo heat zone with brittle insulation and pin tension is a documented cause. Actuator replaced repeatedly while a heat-damaged pigtail remains is a documented pattern. Inspect the actuator connector and pigtail for heat damage while hot.
Step 2 — Position Graphing

Graph desired and actual actuator position. Watch for dropouts in desired vs actual position. Correlate with boost deviation events. An abrupt dropout in position feedback confirms an electrical fault. A slow deviation that correlates with temperature confirms a mechanical or carbon fault.
Step 3 — Mechanical Freedom Check

Check mechanical freedom of the VGT actuator. Command the actuator through its full range and confirm position feedback matches commanded position. A VGT actuator that does not respond correctly confirms an actuator or mechanical fault.
Step 4 — Boost Leak Test

Perform a boost leak test. A charge-air leak reducing actual boost below desired may produce erratic boost behavior that is misdiagnosed as an actuator fault. Pressurize the charge-air system and inspect for leaks.
Step 5 — Replace Actuator or Turbo Only With Evidence

Replace the actuator or turbo only with evidence. Confirm harness, pigtail, and circuit integrity before any actuator replacement. Replace the turbo only if geometry is seized after all other causes are eliminated.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair harness or pigtail if heat damage is confirmed.
2 . Replace actuator if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
3 . Repair charge-air leak if found.
4 . Replace turbo only if geometry is seized after all other causes are eliminated.
Verification Steps
Confirm turbo actuator control is stable after repair.
Verify SPN 641 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm boost deviation is resolved after repair.
Monitor for return of erratic actuator control events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect actuator connector and pigtail for heat damage at every major service.
✓ Inspect VGT actuator for carbon binding at every major service.
✓ Inspect charge-air boots and pipes at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High for loaded operation Severity
Medium to High for loaded operation. Erratic turbo actuator control needs hot electrical proof and mechanical freedom checks.
symptoms: VGT actuator intermittent
Turbo actuator erratic
Boost swings from actuator fault
Intermittent underboost or overboost
High soot from unstable boost

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 3 on Detroit Diesel means the variable geometry turbo actuator position circuit voltage is above the ECM maximum. Test actuator sweep in DDDL8 and inspect the harness before replacing the turbo. SPN 641 monitors the variable geometry turbocharger actuator that controls vane position for boost regulation on Detroit DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines. FMI 3 flags a voltage-above-normal condition in the position feedback circuit. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com distinguishes FMI 3 (electrical) from FMI 7 (mechanical not responding) — the repair path is completely different.
steps: Connect Detroit DDDL8 or Noregon JPRO and confirm SPN 641 FMI 3. Record VGT actuator commanded vs actual position — DD15 actuators use a 0.5V-4.5V position feedback on a 5V reference circuit.
Key on, engine off: command VGT actuator sweep in DDDL8 through 0%-100% range. Actual position should track commanded within 5%. Voltage above 4.8V at 0% commanded position confirms electrical fault.
Disconnect the actuator connector and measure harness-side signal voltage. Above 4.5V with actuator unplugged indicates a harness short to power; normal open-circuit reading should be near 0V.

Inspect actuator harness from the turbo to the ECM for chafing near the exhaust manifold heat shield. Detroit DD15 harnesses fail at the turbo mounting bracket from vibration — repair with heat-rated wire and loom.

Bench-test a replacement actuator if harness reads clean: apply 12V to motor leads and verify smooth vane travel through full range. Relearn actuator endpoints in DDDL8 after installation (Actuator Calibration routine).
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp illuminated
VGT position reading pegged at 100% or maximum on DDDL8 live data
Reduced boost pressure and sluggish acceleration under load
Possible turbo whistle or flutter if vanes are mechanically stuck while actuator reports high position
Companion SPN 641 FMI 4 (voltage below normal) if harness damage is intermittent

procedures_full.overview: FMI 5 on the turbocharger actuator circuit indicates the ECM driver is seeing below-expected current, which is the open-circuit class. The ECM commands actuator movement and monitors the current feedback from the driver circuit. An open circuit — broken wire, unplugged connector, blown fuse, or failed actuator internal winding — prevents current from flowing and sets FMI 5. Heat-damaged harness near the turbo heat shield is a documented cause on Detroit, PACCAR, and Volvo/Mack platforms. Actuator replacement without repairing a heat-damaged harness produces repeat open-circuit codes.
causes: Open actuator pigtail — broken wire at flex point near turbo bracket
Unplugged connector — locking tab failure or service error
Heat-damaged harness — heat shielding failure near turbo
Failed actuator internal winding — open motor circuit
Blown supply fuse or relay where used on specific platforms
Broken pin at actuator connector — corrosion or heat damage
steps: Single Action Gate — Connector and Harness Visual Inspection

Inspect the actuator connector locking tab, pin tension, and burnt pins. Inspect wire flex points at the turbo bracket. Heat shielding failures are a documented cause of open-circuit faults on multiple platforms — inspect the full harness run from ECM to actuator for heat damage.
Binary Decision Gate — Power and Ground Verification

Verify supply voltage and ground at the actuator connector under key-on. An absent supply or ground confirms a circuit fault upstream of the actuator. Confirm both are present before evaluating the actuator itself.
Override Manager — Resistance and Continuity Test

Measure actuator circuit resistance versus OEM specification. Confirm continuity from ECM or driver module to actuator connector. Infinite or high resistance on the actuator circuit confirms an open wire or failed actuator winding.
Safety Interceptor — Actuator Disconnect Test

Disconnect the actuator and measure resistance across the actuator terminals. An open reading with the actuator disconnected confirms internal actuator failure. A good reading with the actuator disconnected and an open reading in the harness confirms a wiring fault.
Resume Point — Fuse and Relay Check

On platforms with dedicated actuator supply fuses or relays, verify fuse and relay integrity. A blown fuse from a previous short can produce an open-circuit fault that returns after actuator replacement if the fuse is not replaced.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Circuit Confirmation
After repair, verify circuit resistance is within OEM specification. Command actuator movement and confirm response. Verify SPN 641 FMI 5 does not return after a full drive cycle.
Repair Ledger Output — Actuator or Harness Decision

Replace actuator only after circuit is proven good and actuator internal open is confirmed by disconnect test. Repair harness if open wire or heat damage is found. Replace heat shielding to prevent recurrence.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair open wire or heat-damaged harness.
2 . Replace actuator connector if pin damage or heat damage is found.
3 . Replace blown fuse and identify the short that caused it.
4 . Replace actuator after circuit proof confirms internal open.
5 . Replace or reroute heat shielding to prevent recurrence.
Verification Steps
Confirm circuit resistance is within OEM specification after repair.
Verify actuator responds to commanded movement.
Confirm SPN 641 FMI 5 does not return after a full drive cycle.
Monitor boost response returns to normal after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect actuator harness and heat shielding at every major turbo service.
✓ Secure harness away from turbo heat shield flex points.
✓ Inspect actuator connector for heat damage at every major service.
✓ Replace heat shielding when deteriorated to prevent harness damage.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High. Expect power loss and possible derate from fixed turbo geometry. Avoid heavy towing until resolved. Open-circuit proof takes less time than actuator replacement.
symptoms: Turbo actuator circuit open fault active
VGT actuator not working
Underboost with actuator code
Power loss from fixed turbo geometry
Possible derate from boost deficiency

procedures_full.overview: Freightliner SPN 641 FMI 5 on a Detroit DD15 means the VGT actuator circuit has an open circuit or current below normal, so the turbo cannot adjust vane position. This is a CRITICAL fault causing immediate power derate and limp-mode operation. Test actuator winding resistance (8-15 ohms expected) with DDDL and a multimeter before ordering any parts.
causes: Melted or chafed actuator wiring harness near the turbo body

The actuator harness routes close to the hot turbocharger housing on DD15 engines. Extended high-load operation melts insulation, creating an open circuit. Confirmed by tracing wire continuity from the actuator connector back to the ECM.
Failed VGT actuator motor (open winding)

The actuator motor winding fails open from thermal fatigue or mechanical stress. Winding resistance reads infinite ohms instead of the normal 8-15 ohms, confirming zero current flow is possible in this circuit.
Corroded or backed-out actuator connector terminal

A corroded terminal or backed-out pin creates sufficient resistance to drop current below the ECM threshold. Cleaning and re-seating the connector terminals can resolve FMI 5 without replacing the actuator.
steps: Connect Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) software with a Diesel Laptops USB-Link 2 or NEXIQ USB-Link 2 adapter. Navigate to Turbocharger > VGT and read SPN 641 FMI 5. Use the DDDL actuator test function to command VGT open and closed positions and observe current response. Zero current on command confirms open circuit.

Locate the VGT actuator on the turbocharger (the electric actuator motor mounted on the turbo housing, right side of the DD15). Inspect the actuator connector for corrosion, heat damage, or backed-out terminals. FMI 5 means the ECM cannot drive sufficient current through the actuator winding.

Unplug the actuator connector and measure motor winding resistance between the two actuator terminals. A healthy DD15 VGT actuator winding reads approximately 8-15 ohms. Infinite resistance (open winding) confirms a failed actuator motor that requires replacement.

If winding resistance is normal, measure continuity on both actuator wires from the connector back to the ECM. An open in either leg sets FMI 5. Check harness routing near the turbo housing - insulation commonly melts against the turbo body during extended high-load operation.

After repair or actuator replacement, clear faults with DDDL and use the actuator sweep test to confirm VGT moves freely through 0-100% position. Verify SPN 641 does not return under load before releasing the truck.
symptoms: Red or amber lamp with immediate power derate - engine limited to governed limp-home speed.
Noticeably sluggish acceleration and inability to maintain highway speed under load.
Black smoke under acceleration as the engine over-fuels without adequate boost to support combustion.
Turbocharger may emit an unusual pitch because vanes are stuck in a fixed position.
EGR-related fault codes may co-set because VGT vane position directly affects exhaust gas recirculation flow.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 5 means the VGT actuator circuit has current below normal or is open, so the ECM can't control turbo vane position. It's High severity since this directly affects boost and power across the operating range. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com checks the harness near the turbo housing first, since heat damage there is a common and affordable cause compared to actuator replacement.
causes: Chafed or heat-damaged harness wire near the turbocharger
Electrical fault - insulation breakdown from prolonged heat exposure in this area is a well-known failure point.
Corroded actuator connector
Electrical fault - a poor connection can present as an open circuit intermittently or continuously.
Internally failed actuator motor windings
A genuine actuator hardware failure confirmed by an open resistance reading directly at the actuator terminals.
Mechanically seized actuator from soot buildup
Mechanical fault - excessive resistance to movement can cause the actuator to draw abnormal current even if electrically sound.
steps: Connect Scania SDP3 and confirm the fault is active, checking the actuator's commanded versus actual position if available in live data.
Locate the VGT actuator, typically mounted directly on or near the turbocharger housing, and inspect the connector for corrosion or a loose pin.
Measure resistance across the actuator motor windings at the connector - an open reading (infinite resistance) confirms an internally failed actuator motor.
Check the wiring harness between the ECM and actuator for chafing or heat damage, since this run typically passes close to the turbocharger and exhaust manifold.
If the actuator tests good electrically, verify it isn't mechanically seized from soot buildup preventing normal current draw during movement.
symptoms: Noticeable loss of power and turbo lag under acceleration
Boost pressure gauge reading low or erratic
Amber or red warning lamp depending on severity
Possible whistling or unusual turbo noise

procedures_full.overview: FMI 7 is the not-responding or mechanical fault class. The ECM commands actuator movement and monitors the position feedback — if the actual position does not follow the desired position within calibrated time and error limits, FMI 7 sets. Sooted nozzle ring binding the VGT mechanism, failed actuator gear or motor, oil supply issues on oil-controlled designs, harness intermittents, and incorrect installation calibration are the primary causes. Replacing the actuator only, then experiencing repeat failure because the vane pack remains stuck, is the most common misdiagnosis pattern on this fault.
causes: Sooted nozzle ring — carbon binding prevents vane movement
Failed actuator gear or motor — internal mechanical failure
Oil supply issues — oil-controlled actuator designs with restricted oil feed
Harness intermittents — intermittent power or ground mimicking mechanical no-response
Incorrect installation calibration — actuator not calibrated after replacement
Oil-coked mechanism — coking from extended idle or oil quality issues
steps: Single Action Gate — Desired vs Actual Position Graphing

Graph desired versus actual actuator position PIDs. If desired position changes but actual position does not follow, the actuator is not responding. If both desired and actual are stable but boost is low, the fault may be elsewhere. This PID comparison is the mandatory first step.
Binary Decision Gate — Electrical Integrity Check

Verify actuator circuit power, ground, and signal integrity. Intermittent power or ground can mimic mechanical no-response. Wiggle-test the harness at operating temperature to expose intermittent connections.
Override Manager — Mechanical Freedom Inspection

Inspect mechanical freedom of the turbo geometry mechanism where OEM procedure allows. This is the mandatory mechanical gate — replacing the actuator without verifying vane pack freedom produces repeat failures. Some platforms allow shaft freedom check with actuator removed.
Safety Interceptor — Oil Feed Check

On oil-controlled actuator designs, verify oil feed to the actuator. A restricted oil feed prevents actuator movement regardless of electrical integrity. Verify oil pressure and flow to the actuator per OEM procedure.
Resume Point — Boost Leak Test

Perform a charge air system leak test before any final turbo decision. A boost leak can produce underboost symptoms that are misattributed to actuator failure. Confirm the air path is leak-free before turbo replacement.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Position Response
After repair, verify desired versus actual position tracks correctly. Confirm boost meets setpoint under load. Verify actuator calibration if required by OEM procedure after replacement.
Repair Ledger Output — Actuator vs Turbo Assembly Decision

Replace actuator after electrical proof and mechanical freedom confirmation. Replace turbo cartridge or assembly only when geometry is confirmed seized and cannot be freed by approved service procedures.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair harness intermittents found by wiggle testing.
2 . Service or clean turbo geometry mechanism if approved by OEM procedure.
3 . Repair oil feed restriction on oil-controlled actuator designs.
4 . Replace actuator after electrical proof and mechanical freedom confirmation.
5 . Replace turbo assembly when geometry is confirmed seized beyond service limits.
6 . Calibrate replacement actuator per OEM procedure.
Verification Steps
Confirm desired vs actual position tracks correctly after repair.
Verify boost meets setpoint under load after repair.
Confirm SPN 641 FMI 7 does not return after repair.
Monitor regen frequency returns to normal after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Avoid extended idle operation that promotes carbon buildup in VGT mechanism.
✓ Use OEM-specified oil quality to prevent coking.
✓ Inspect actuator harness at every major turbo service.
✓ Perform actuator sweep test at every major service on high-mileage engines.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High. Reduced power and increased regen frequency from underboost soot. Mechanical freedom gate is mandatory before actuator-only closeout — repeat failures are expensive.

Turbo actuator stuck indication
Boost not following command
Actuator sluggish or no movement
Reduced power from fixed turbo geometry
Increased regen frequency from underboost soot

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 7 on Volvo means the VGT turbo vanes are not responding to ECM commands. Check for carbon deposits on the vane mechanism before ordering an actuator or turbo — cleaning fixes a large percentage of these faults. Variable geometry turbos give Volvo D13 engines their broad power band, but the vane mechanism that does that work is vulnerable to carbon deposits from idle time and short-trip operation. SPN 641 FMI 7 is the ECM's way of saying the turbo is not following instructions. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com starts with the vane condition and cleans before it replaces.
causes: Carbon buildup on VGT vanes preventing full range of motion (mechanical)
Very Common

Incomplete combustion byproducts accumulate on the variable-geometry vane actuating ring and individual vane pivots over high-idle and short-trip cycles, progressively reducing the range the actuator can physically move the vanes.
Faulty VGT actuator motor or position sensor (mechanical/electrical)
The electric or pneumatic actuator that moves the vane ring can fail mechanically or lose positional accuracy, causing the commanded vs actual position mismatch that triggers FMI 7.
Turbo bearing wear creating excessive shaft play (mechanical)
Significant bearing wear can cause the turbine wheel to contact the housing at certain vane positions, producing an out-of-adjustment response.
Inadequate oil lubrication accelerating vane mechanism wear (mechanical)
Less Common
Restricted or degraded oil supply to the turbo bearing causes heat and wear on the vane pivot pins, stiffening the mechanism and reducing actuator authority.
steps: 1. Connect Volvo Premium Tech Tool or Diesel Laptops and perform the VGT actuator functional test — command vane position from 0% to 100% and monitor actual position feedback versus commanded.
2. Inspect the VGT actuator rod and vane control ring for carbon buildup or physical damage — on D13 engines, carbon accumulation on the sliding vane mechanism is the primary cause of FMI 7.

3. Check the actuator air supply (pneumatic actuator versions) or the electric actuator harness and connector for voltage, ground, and continuity — a weak air supply or high-resistance connector can reduce actuator authority below the mechanical resistance of carbon-loaded vanes.

4. With Jaltest or Diesel Laptops, monitor boost pressure alongside VGT position during a loaded road test — if commanded position changes but boost does not respond proportionally, the vane mechanism is mechanically binding.
5. Inspect the turbo oil supply line for restrictions and the drain line for sludge — inadequate lubrication accelerates vane carbon buildup on VGT turbos.
6. If the actuator is pneumatic, test air pressure supply at the actuator port — low supply pressure reduces vane range of movement and can produce FMI 7 under load.
symptoms: Low boost pressure or turbo lag under acceleration
Power derate with reduced top-end performance
High exhaust gas temperatures under load as the ECM compensates
Possible black smoke if boost is insufficient and fuel delivery is not proportionally reduced
Overboost symptoms if the vanes are stuck in a low-flow position
VTD or turbo-related warning indicator on the cluster

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 7 on a Freightliner indicates a malfunction in the VGT Actuator. This can lead to poor engine performance and requires immediate attention to avoid further damage. The Freightliner SPN 641 FMI 7 fault code is a critical alert indicating a problem with the Variable Geometry Turbocharger (VGT) Actuator. This component is essential for managing turbo boost pressure by adjusting the angle of the turbo vanes. When the actuator fails to respond, it can lead to significant engine performance issues, including reduced power and efficiency. Understanding this fault code and addressing it promptly is crucial for maintaining your vehicle's performance and preventing further damage. In this guide, we'll explore the symptoms, root causes, and steps to diagnose and repair this issue effectively. The VGT Actuator's role in optimizing turbo performance is vital, as it directly affects the engine's ability to manage air intake and exhaust flow, impacting overall vehicle efficiency.
causes: Soot Buildup

Over time, soot can accumulate within the turbo, causing the actuator linkage to stick. This prevents the actuator from adjusting the turbo vanes properly, leading to performance issues. Regular cleaning of the turbocharger can help mitigate this problem and ensure smooth actuator operation.
Electrical Failure

The actuator relies on electrical signals to function. A failure in the actuator's motor or wiring can prevent it from responding to control inputs, necessitating replacement. Inspecting the wiring harness for damage or corrosion can help identify potential electrical issues early.
Mechanical Wear

The moving parts of the actuator can wear out over time, especially under harsh operating conditions. This wear can lead to mechanical failure, requiring a new actuator. Regular maintenance and inspection can help detect wear before it leads to complete failure.
steps: Turn off the engine and safely remove the passenger-side wheel well shroud to access the turbocharger. Ensure the vehicle is securely supported to prevent accidents.
Locate the mechanical linkage arm connecting the actuator to the turbo housing. Inspect for any visible damage or misalignment.
Check if the linkage arm moves smoothly or if it is obstructed by soot buildup. Clean any visible soot deposits using appropriate cleaning agents.
Use a VGT Calibration Tool to test the actuator's response and recalibrate if necessary. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for calibration procedures.
If the actuator is non-responsive, consider replacing it to restore proper turbo function. Ensure all connections are secure and components are properly aligned before reassembly.
symptoms: Severe lag under acceleration and low boost pressure on your dash gauge.
Loud whistling, fluttering, or puffing noises emanating from the passenger side engine bay.
High exhaust gas temperatures (EGTs) climbing quickly, risking engine damage.
Check engine light illuminated, indicating a fault in the turbo system.
Reduced fuel efficiency, leading to increased operational costs.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 641 FMI 14 on Volvo means the VGT actuator fault requires manufacturer special instructions — usually calibration and mechanical vane checks before replacement. Volvo uses FMI 14 when a fault cannot be resolved by generic FMI definitions alone. SPN 641 points at the variable geometry turbo actuator, and the ECM expects a structured calibration and mechanical verification sequence. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com follows the PTT procedure end to end — skipping calibration is why many actuators get replaced twice.
causes: VGT calibration lost after battery disconnect or ECM flash
Actuator position reference drifts until the OEM calibration routine is completed successfully.
Soot-bound or seized turbo unison ring
Mechanical binding prevents the actuator from reaching commanded positions during sweep tests.
Failed VGT actuator motor or internal position sensor
Genuine actuator failure after high mileage or coolant contamination in electronic units.

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2015 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine can experience a fan solenoid error identified as SPN 647 FMI. This fault code indicates a problem within the fan solenoid circuit, which affects cooling fan operation. In some cases, replacing the fan solenoid alone may not resolve the issue. The root causes of this error often stem from electrical faults such as shorts or open circuits in the wiring harness or connectors. An unusual symptom is that unplugging the fan solenoid causes the fan to run continuously, pointing to possible control or grounding problems in the circuit. Additionally, the fan relay and signals from the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) should be inspected as part of the diagnostic process. procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically a short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically a short to power.‪
steps: Short to Power Check
Disconnect the Constant Throttle Valve connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the Constant Throttle Valve connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11.5 volts, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the Constant Throttle Valve connector and pin 32 of the 120–pin MCM connector. See Figure
"Constant Throttle Valve"
. Refer to "80.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. Constant Throttle Valve
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, go to step 4.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pins 1 and 2 of the Constant Throttle Valve connector.
If the resistance is greater than 5Ω, replace the Constant Throttle Valve solenoid. Refer to "80.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5Ω, repair the short between pins 1 and 2 of the Constant Throttle Valve and pins 32 and 64 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "80.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that the Jake Brake Stage 1 circuit failed low.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that the Jake Brake Stage 1 circuit failed low.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Disconnect the front injector valve cover harness.
Measure resistance between pins 7 and ground on the front injector valve cover harness connector. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure either rear Jake pin and ground.

If the resistance is greater than 15 Ω, repair short to ground between pin 7 of the front injector valve cover harness connector and pin 60 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "82.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, go to step 3.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect the rear Jake Brake harness.
Measure resistance between either terminal on the Jake Brake solenoid and ground.
If the resistance is less than 5 ohms, replace the Jake Brake solenoid. Refer to "82.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pins 7 and 8 of the front injector valve cover harness and the Jake Brake solenoid. Refer to "82.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that the Jake Brake Stage 1 circuit failed open.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that the Jake Brake Stage 1 circuit failed open.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for multiple codes.

If SPN 647/5, SPN 1071/5 and SPN 1072/5 are active repair the open in between pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector and the rear Jake Brake and fan control solenoids. Refer to "82.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If only SPN 1072/5 is active, go to step 2.
Disconnect the front injector valve cover harness.
Measure the resistance between pin 7 and 8 on the front injector valve cover harness connector. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure across the rear Jake pins.
If the resistance is less than 15 Ω, repair the open between pin 7 of the front injector valve cover harness connector and pin 66 of the 120–pin MCM connector.
If the resistance is greater than 15 Ω, go to step 4.
Remove the valve cover.
Measure the resistance across the Jake Brake solenoid.
If the resistance is greater than 15 Ω, replace the Jake Brake solenoid. Refer to "82.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 15 Ω, repair the open between pins 7 and 8 of the front injector valve cover harness connector and the Jake Brake solenoid. Refer to "82.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 21 – DPF Regen Frequency Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 21 – DPF Regeneration Frequency High (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 21 indicates that DPF regeneration is occurring more frequently than expected. This condition often signals excessive soot accumulation or incomplete regeneration cycles.
Symptoms
Frequent regeneration cycles
Increased fuel consumption
DPF or regen warning lights
Reduced engine efficiency
Cause
This fault is commonly caused by excessive idling, short drive cycles, faulty DPF pressure sensors, restricted exhaust flow, or incomplete active regeneration.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving is possible, but frequent regeneration may indicate an underlying issue that could eventually lead to DPF clogging or engine derate.
Recommended Action
Inspect DPF differential pressure sensors, verify proper regeneration operation, and reduce excessive idling where possible. Perform diagnostic checks if regeneration frequency remains high.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 21 mean?
 
SPN 3216 FMI 21 indicates that DPF regeneration is occurring more frequently than expected, often due to excessive soot accumulation.
 
 
What causes SPN 3216 FMI 21?
 
Common causes include excessive idling, short driving cycles, faulty DPF pressure sensors, restricted exhaust flow, or incomplete regeneration.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3216 FMI 21?
 
Driving is possible, but frequent regeneration may signal an underlying issue that can eventually lead to DPF clogging or derate.
 
 
Will SPN 3216 FMI 21 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If regeneration fails or soot levels continue to rise, the engine may enter a power reduction mode.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 3216 FMI 21?
 
Reduce excessive idling, ensure proper regeneration cycles complete, and inspect DPF sensors and exhaust components for faults.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3216 FMI 2 – NOx Sensor Upstream Rationality Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 2 – NOx Sensor Upstream Rationality Fault (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 2 indicates that the upstream NOx sensor, located before the SCR catalyst, is producing readings that do not match what the ECM expects based on current engine conditions. This rationality fault appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and can affect the ECM’s ability to properly control DEF dosing and monitor SCR system performance.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
SCR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Engine derate possible 
DEF dosing may be affected 
Other NOx or SCR related codes may appear alongside
Cause
This code triggers when the upstream NOx sensor reading does not correlate with expected values based on engine load, fuel rate, and other parameters. Common causes include:
Failing or degraded upstream NOx sensor 
Exhaust leaks upstream of the sensor affecting readings 
DEF crystallization contaminating the sensor 
Damaged sensor wiring or connector 
Water intrusion at the sensor connector 
Engine running abnormally rich or lean affecting NOx output
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but the ECM relies on the upstream NOx sensor to control DEF dosing accurately. Without reliable upstream data the entire SCR system performance is compromised and a derate condition is likely to follow.
Recommended Action
Inspect the upstream NOx sensor and its wiring for damage, corrosion, or contamination. Check for exhaust leaks at manifold joints, flex pipes, or fittings upstream of the sensor location. If the sensor wiring is intact and no exhaust leaks are found, replace the upstream NOx sensor as sensor degradation is the most common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 2 mean?
 
It means the upstream NOx sensor is producing readings that do not match what the ECM expects, indicating a rationality fault that affects SCR system monitoring and DEF dosing control.
 
 
What causes SPN 3216 FMI 2?
 
The most common causes are a failing upstream NOx sensor, exhaust leaks near the sensor, contaminated or damaged sensor wiring, or water intrusion at the connector.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3216 FMI 2?
 
Short distances may be possible but without accurate upstream NOx data the ECM cannot properly control DEF dosing and a derate condition is likely.
 
 
Will SPN 3216 FMI 2 cause a derate?
 
Yes. When the ECM cannot trust the upstream NOx sensor data it will typically trigger a derate condition to limit emissions output.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3216 FMI 2?
 
Inspect and replace the upstream NOx sensor if faulty, repair any exhaust leaks, and verify wiring integrity. The code should clear once the ECM receives consistent and rational upstream NOx readings.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3216 FMI 2 – NOx Sensor Upstream Rationality Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 2 – NOx Sensor Upstream Rationality Fault (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3216 FMI 2 indicates that the upstream NOx sensor, located before the SCR catalyst, is producing readings that do not match what the ECM expects based on current engine conditions. This rationality fault appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and can affect the ECM’s ability to properly control DEF dosing and monitor SCR system performance.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
SCR or emissions warning light illuminated 
Engine derate possible 
DEF dosing may be affected 
Other NOx or SCR related codes may appear alongside
Cause
This code triggers when the upstream NOx sensor reading does not correlate with expected values based on engine load, fuel rate, and other parameters. Common causes include:
Failing or degraded upstream NOx sensor 
Exhaust leaks upstream of the sensor affecting readings 
DEF crystallization contaminating the sensor 
Damaged sensor wiring or connector 
Water intrusion at the sensor connector 
Engine running abnormally rich or lean affecting NOx output
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but the ECM relies on the upstream NOx sensor to control DEF dosing accurately. Without reliable upstream data the entire SCR system performance is compromised and a derate condition is likely to follow.
Recommended Action
Inspect the upstream NOx sensor and its wiring for damage, corrosion, or contamination. Check for exhaust leaks at manifold joints, flex pipes, or fittings upstream of the sensor location. If the sensor wiring is intact and no exhaust leaks are found, replace the upstream NOx sensor as sensor degradation is the most common cause of this fault.

Yes. When the ECM cannot trust the upstream NOx sensor data it will typically trigger a derate condition to limit emissions output.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3216 FMI 2?

steps: DPF fark basınç sensörlerini kontrol edin, rejenerasyonun düzgün çalıştığını doğrulayın ve mümkünse aşırı rölantide çalıştırmayı azaltın.
Rejenerasyon sıklığı yüksek kalmaya devam ederse teşhis kontrollerini gerçekleştirin.
Katalizör girişindeki (upstream) NOx sensörünü ve kablo tesisatını hasar, korozyon veya kirlenme açısından kontrol edin.
Sensör konumunun giriş tarafındaki manifold bağlantılarında, spiral borularda veya rakorlarda egzoz kaçağı olup olmadığını kontrol edin.
Sensör kablo tesisatı sağlamsa ve egzoz kaçağı bulunamazsa, giriş NOx sensörünü değiştirin; sensör yaşlanması/bozulması bu arızanın en yaygın nedenidir.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır). Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 19] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3216 FMI 0 means Cummins upstream NOx sensor reads above expected range. Inspect exhaust leaks and sensor heater before replacing the NOx probe. The upstream NOx sensor measures engine-out NOx entering the SCR catalyst. When readings exceed calibrated limits, Cummins sets SPN 3216 FMI 0 and SCR efficiency calculations become unreliable.
causes: Failed upstream NOx sensor element
Thermal degradation causes drift high, corrupting SCR efficiency monitoring.
Exhaust leak upstream of NOx sensor
False air entry alters exhaust gas composition at the sensor tip.
Actual high engine-out NOx from EGR or combustion faults
Real combustion problems produce genuinely high NOx that the sensor reports correctly.
steps: Monitor upstream NOx ppm in Cummins INSITE at idle — readings above 800 ppm at warm idle suggest bad sensor or real combustion issue.
Inspect exhaust piping upstream of NOx sensor for cracks or blown gaskets causing false air dilution.
Check NOx sensor heater circuit — target 12 V supply and 6–8 A draw during warmup.
Perform NOx sensor regeneration or cleaning per OEM procedure if sensor is contaminated with DEF crystals.
Compare upstream NOx to calculated engine-out NOx model — large deviation confirms sensor fault.
symptoms: Amber MIL with NOx or emissions warning
Upstream NOx reading above 1,000 ppm at idle in live data
SCR efficiency calculation shows artificially low
Possible stacked SCR inducement codes
Failed emissions inspection due to high reported NOx

procedures_full.overview: The upstream NOx sensor (SPN 3216) measures exhaust NOx concentration entering the SCR system. FMI 2 (erratic/intermittent) is set when the signal fluctuates beyond plausibility limits or disagrees with the ECM model under stable conditions. This fault affects SCR efficiency calculations and can cascade to SPN 4364 (efficiency) and SPN 5246 (inducement). Thermal-cycle harness failures and probe contamination are the most common causes.
causes: Harness intermittent — thermal-cycle opens at flex points near AT brackets
Probe contamination — soot or oil fouling on sensor tip
Heater circuit failure — sensor heater open causes unstable warmup readings
Water intrusion in module connector — corrosion on signal pins
Exhaust leak upstream of sensor — dilutes sample and creates erratic readings
Shield integrity loss — EMI interference on signal circuit
Sensor failure — internal electronics after electrical and leak causes ruled out
steps: Single Action Gate — Visual Probe Inspection
Inspect the NOx sensor probe tip for soot buildup, oil contamination, or physical damage. A fouled probe produces erratic readings without any electrical fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Power & Ground Stability
Measure battery supply voltage and ground stability at the sensor connector under load. Voltage drop on supply or ground creates false erratic data.
Override Manager — Signal Graphing
Graph the NOx signal live while wiggling the harness at known flex points. Dropouts or spikes during wiggle confirm intermittent harness fault.
Safety Interceptor — Steady-State Comparison
Compare upstream NOx to downstream NOx at steady-state idle. If both sensors track together (same value), one sensor is failed or there is an exhaust leak between them.
Resume Point — Exhaust Leak Check
Inspect for exhaust leaks upstream of the NOx sensor. Even small leaks dilute the exhaust sample and produce erratic or low readings.
Verification Loop — Heater Circuit Test
Measure heater circuit resistance per OEM specification. An open heater circuit causes unstable readings during warmup and can mimic erratic data faults.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor Replacement Decision
Replace sensor only after harness, power/ground, exhaust leak, and heater circuit are proven good. Document all findings.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean sensor probe tip if contamination is found.
2 . Repair any harness opens, chafes, or intermittent connections at flex points.
3 . Repair exhaust leaks upstream of the NOx sensor.
4 . Restore shield integrity on signal circuit if EMI interference is suspected.
5 . Replace sensor if heater circuit is open or internal failure is confirmed ($400–$1,200).
6 . Verify connector seals are intact and moisture-free after any repair.
Verification Steps
Confirm NOx signal is stable at steady-state idle and under load.
Verify upstream and downstream NOx readings correlate correctly.
Confirm no harness dropouts during wiggle test after repair.
Monitor for return of SPN 3216 FMI 2 over 50+ miles.
Confirm SPN 4364 efficiency fault does not return.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect NOx sensor harness routing and flex points at every major service.
✓ Protect sensor connectors from wash-bay moisture and pressure washing.
✓ Inspect exhaust system for leaks at every service.
✓ Replace NOx sensors per OEM recommended intervals on high-mileage engines.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity

Medium severity. Vehicle often drives normally at first, but erratic NOx data will tighten the emissions strategy and can cascade to SCR efficiency faults and inducement. Address promptly to prevent escalation.

Intermittent SCR efficiency codes

procedures_full.overview: Mack SPN 3216 FMI 9 indicates an abnormal update rate in the throttle position sensor circuit, affecting throttle response and drivability. Addressing wiring issues or cleaning the throttle body often resolves the problem. The Mack SPN 3216 FMI 9 fault code signals a problem with the throttle position sensor (TPS) circuit, specifically an abnormal update rate. This issue can lead to inconsistent throttle response, affecting vehicle performance and potentially triggering a limp mode to prevent damage. Understanding the root causes and solutions for this code is crucial for maintaining optimal engine performance. Throttle position sensors play a vital role in ensuring smooth engine operation by providing accurate throttle position data to the engine control module (ECM). When this data is compromised, it can result in poor drivability, increased emissions, and reduced fuel efficiency. Addressing this fault promptly can prevent further complications and costly repairs. Regular maintenance and timely diagnostics are key to avoiding severe engine issues.

When this data is compromised, it can result in poor drivability, increased emissions, and reduced fuel efficiency. steps: Inspect the TPS connector and wiring for visible damage or loose connections. Secure and repair as needed. Ensure the integrity of the wire insulation and the absence of corrosion at the connectors.

Use an OBD-II scanner to access real-time TPS data. Look for irregular patterns or spikes. Verify that the TPS voltage changes smoothly with throttle input, staying within manufacturer-specified ranges.

Clean the throttle body using a throttle body cleaner to remove dirt and debris that may affect sensor readings. Pay special attention to the throttle plate and surrounding areas to ensure full movement and accurate sensor feedback.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How do I know if SPN 3226 FMI 16 is caused by a bad sensor or a bad catalyst?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Compare the upstream and downstream NOx sensor readings simultaneously in DiagnosticLink. If the upstream sensor shows normal inlet NOx and the downstream sensor reads high, and the DEF dosing is confirmed working, the catalyst is suspect. If the upstream sensor also reads abnormally, or if replacing the downstream sensor changes the reading significantly, the sensor was more likely the issue.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 3226 FMI 16 appear without SPN 4364 on the same engine?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. SPN 3226 is a raw sensor reading; SPN 4364 is a calculated ratio. If the downstream reading is elevated but the ECM's efficiency model hasn't crossed its own threshold �?perhaps because dosing commanded rates are artificially holding the ratio in range �?4364 may remain inactive while 3226 is active.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is a NOx sensor replacement something a roadside tech can do?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The physical replacement is straightforward with the correct socket and extension. However, some applications require a sensor reset or learning procedure in DiagnosticLink after replacement for accurate reading. Verify requirements for the specific model year before assuming a bolt-in swap is complete.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3226 FMI 0 means Cummins downstream NOx is higher than expected. Verify DEF quality and dosing before blaming the SCR catalyst or outlet sensor. The downstream NOx sensor confirms SCR conversion efficiency by measuring NOx after the catalyst. When outlet NOx stays high, Cummins sets SPN 3226 FMI 0 and inducement may follow.
causes: Inadequate DEF dosing or contaminated DEF
Low DEF quality or weak dosing leaves NOx unconverted at the SCR outlet.
Failed downstream NOx sensor
Sensor drift high makes a functioning SCR appear failed to the ECM.
Degraded SCR catalyst
Thermal damage or poisoning reduces conversion even with good DEF delivery.
steps: Compare upstream vs downstream NOx in Cummins INSITE at 1,500 RPM — downstream should be 70–90% lower than upstream.
Test DEF concentration with refractometer — must read 32.5% urea for proper SCR conversion.
Verify DEF dosing pressure at 130–145 PSI during active dosing commands.
Inspect outlet NOx sensor for DEF crystal buildup on tip — clean or replace if contaminated.
Check for exhaust leaks between SCR outlet and downstream NOx sensor boss.
symptoms: SCR efficiency below 70% in live data
Amber or red MIL with emissions warning
Downstream NOx near upstream values during steady cruise
SCR inducement timer active or counting down
Visible DEF crystallization at doser injector

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3226 FMI 0 means outlet NOx readings after the SCR catalyst are too high, indicating a real conversion efficiency problem. It's a Critical fault that can escalate quickly into an SCR inducement derate.
causes: Diluted, contaminated, or expired DEF
A fluid quality issue, not a mechanical or sensor fault - bad DEF genuinely can't reduce NOx effectively regardless of how well the rest of the system works.
Partially clogged DEF doser injector
A mechanical restriction that produces an inadequate or uneven spray pattern, reducing actual NOx conversion even with good DEF.
Degraded SCR catalyst
A genuine mechanical/aftertreatment failure where the catalyst itself can no longer convert NOx efficiently, often from age or thermal damage.
Exhaust leak upstream of the outlet sensor
A mechanical exhaust system issue that lets fresh air skew the sensor's reading, mimicking a conversion problem that isn't really there.
steps: Connect Mack Premium Tech Tool (PTT) and confirm DEF quality with a refractometer - contaminated or diluted DEF is the single most common cause of this fault.
Check the DEF doser injector spray pattern and verify it's not partially clogged with urea crystals.
Compare inlet and outlet NOx sensor readings side by side in live data - a large gap that doesn't close confirms a genuine SCR conversion problem rather than a sensor fault.
Inspect for exhaust leaks upstream of the outlet sensor, since fresh air entering the exhaust stream can throw off NOx readings and mimic a conversion efficiency fault.
If DEF quality, doser spray, and exhaust integrity all check out, the SCR catalyst itself may be degraded and require inspection or replacement.
symptoms: Check Engine and Stop Engine lamps illuminated together
SCR system warning message on the dash
Escalating power derate if left unaddressed for multiple drive cycles
Possible strong exhaust odor

procedures_full.overview: Mercedes-Benz SPN 3226 FMI 3 on OM471 means the SCR outlet NOx sensor circuit voltage is above normal, indicating an open or high-resistance circuit - not a failed SCR catalyst. This CRITICAL fault triggers an SCR derate and inducement countdown. Diagnose with Texa or Jaltest to confirm the open circuit before any BlueTec catalyst or sensor replacement is recommended.
causes: Open or abraded outlet NOx sensor wiring harness at the SCR canister bracket

The harness routing along the SCR canister bracket contact surface abrades over time. A severed signal wire produces the FMI 3 open-circuit voltage reading. Tracing the wire from the connector to the ECM with a multimeter isolates the break.
Failed outlet NOx sensor (open internal signal element)

The NOx sensing element in the outlet sensor ages and fails open, removing the signal load from the ECM input and causing it to read above 4.75 V. Confirmed after wiring is verified clean and signal voltage remains high with the sensor plugged in.
Corroded or damaged outlet NOx sensor connector

Exhaust condensate and moisture at the sensor connector corrode the pins and increase contact resistance to open-circuit levels. Cleaning and inspecting the connector before condemning either the sensor or harness is essential.
steps: Connect Texa Navigator TXTs or Jaltest diagnostic software to the Mercedes-Benz OM471 data link connector. Navigate to Aftertreatment > SCR > NOx Sensors and read SPN 3226 FMI 3. Live data will show outlet NOx sensor voltage above 4.75 V (the ECM reads an open circuit on the sensor signal line).

Locate the outlet NOx sensor on the SCR catalyst outlet pipe (downstream of the catalyst brick on the OM471). Inspect the multi-pin connector for corrosion, heat damage from the exhaust housing, or backed-out terminals. The OM471 exhaust package runs the NOx sensor harness along the catalyst body where heat degrades insulation.

Unplug the outlet NOx sensor connector. Measure the 5 V reference pin voltage at the harness side (key on, engine off): should read 4.75-5.25 V. Measure the signal pin to chassis ground - if it reads above 4.5 V with the sensor disconnected, the signal wire is open between the connector and ECM.

Trace the signal wire continuity from the harness connector back to the ECM. Infinite resistance on the signal wire confirms an open. Inspect the harness where it runs along the SCR canister bracket - this contact point is the most common abrasion failure site on Mercedes-Benz OM471 aftertreatment packages.

After wiring repair or sensor replacement, clear faults with Texa or Jaltest, perform a drive cycle at operating temperature above 60 mph for 15-20 minutes, and confirm SPN 3226 live data returns to normal operating range (typically 50-500 ppm NOx after the SCR catalyst). Verify the inducement countdown has reset.
symptoms: Amber SCR warning lamp and active derate; inducement countdown visible on the driver display.
Engine power progressively reduced by the SCR inducement system if the fault is not corrected quickly.
Red Stop Engine or warning lamp as inducement advances toward the final phase.
DEF system and dosing operation appear normal because the fault is on the outlet NOx sensor circuit only.
Possible companion fault from the inlet NOx sensor or SCR efficiency parameter if the harness has multiple damage points.

procedures_full.overview: The downstream NOx sensor (SPN 3226) measures exhaust NOx concentration after the SCR catalyst. FMI 4 (voltage below normal) is set when the signal circuit reads below the valid minimum — typically indicating a short to ground in the harness, a failed sensor, or water intrusion in the connector. This fault affects SCR efficiency calculations and can cascade to SPN 4364 and SPN 5246.
causes: Shorted harness — pinch point or chafe causing signal wire short to ground
Failed sensor — internal short in NOx sensor module
Water intrusion — moisture in connector causing signal short
Damaged connector — bent or corroded signal pin
Harness damage after frame or aftertreatment service work
Cover edge chafe — harness rubbing on AT box or frame rail
steps: Single Action Gate — Sensor Disconnect
Disconnect the outlet NOx sensor connector. If the fault goes inactive with sensor disconnected, the sensor itself is shorted internally.
Binary Decision Gate — Harness Short Check
With sensor disconnected, measure resistance from signal wire to chassis ground. Any reading below 10k ohms indicates a harness short to ground.
Override Manager — Supply Voltage Verification
Verify battery supply voltage is present at the sensor connector. Low supply voltage can cause false low-voltage faults on smart sensors.
Safety Interceptor — Pin Inspection
Inspect connector pins for corrosion, bending, or moisture. Clean and reseat connector. Verify pin tension with a pin drag test.
Resume Point — Harness Routing Inspection
Trace harness from sensor to ECM/module. Inspect clamp points, cover edges, and any areas disturbed during recent service for chafe damage.
Verification Loop — Circuit Integrity Confirmation
After harness repair, verify signal circuit resistance is within spec with sensor reconnected. Confirm fault does not return with KOEO.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor Replacement
Replace sensor only after circuit integrity is confirmed. Document all findings and repair actions.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Disconnect sensor and perform harness short-to-ground check.
2 . Repair any harness chafe, pinch, or short-to-ground found in circuit.
3 . Clean and reseat connector; replace connector if corrosion or pin damage is found.
4 . Verify supply voltage is present and stable at sensor connector.
5 . Replace sensor if internal short is confirmed with harness proven good ($400–$1,200).
6 . Re-route harness away from heat sources or sharp edges after repair.
Verification Steps
Confirm signal circuit resistance is within spec after repair.
Verify fault does not return with KOEO after repair.
Confirm downstream NOx reading is plausible at operating temperature.
Monitor for return of SPN 3226 FMI 4 over 50+ miles.
Confirm SCR efficiency fault (SPN 4364) does not return.
Preventative Measures
✓ Protect NOx sensor harness from chafe during any AT or frame service.
✓ Inspect harness routing and clamp points at every major service.
✓ Keep connectors sealed and protected from wash-bay moisture.
✓ Replace NOx sensors per OEM recommended intervals.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium severity. FMI 4 circuit low fault will affect SCR efficiency calculations and can escalate to inducement if unresolved. Address promptly. Vehicle may drive normally initially.
symptoms: NOx outlet circuit low voltage fault active
Downstream NOx reading at zero or below minimum
SCR efficiency fault following NOx circuit fault
Electrical fault code on outlet NOx sensor
Possible inducement escalation if unresolved

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3226 FMI 9 means the SCR outlet NOx sensor is not updating on the network fast enough. Inspect CAN wiring and connector integrity before replacing the sensor module. Volvo VNL operators feel SPN 3226 FMI 9 as a creeping derate that follows an aftertreatment light by a day or two. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com logs show many cases fixed by reseating a corroded outlet NOx connector rather than replacing the SCR assembly.
causes: Corroded or loose outlet NOx sensor connector
Intermittent CAN communication drops update rate below the ECM threshold and sets FMI 9.
Failed SCR outlet NOx sensor module
Internal sensor electronics stop transmitting valid frames even with clean wiring.
Low system voltage or poor ground
Voltage sag during regen or cranking slows network updates enough to trigger the fault.
steps: Scan with Jaltest or Noregon JPRO and confirm SPN 3226 FMI 9 with communication timeout counters on the outlet NOx sensor module.
Inspect the sensor harness from the SCR outlet pipe to the aftertreatment control module for pinched clips, green corrosion, or broken CAN shield grounds.
Check battery voltage during crank and idle—low system voltage below 12.5 V can slow sensor network updates below calibrated thresholds.
Perform a forced SCR efficiency test if available and watch outlet NOx response time; replace sensor only if updates remain absent with good wiring and 12.6+ V supply.
After sensor or harness repair, clear codes and drive 20 minutes loaded to confirm outlet NOx updates at least once per second in live data.
symptoms: Check engine and aftertreatment warning lamps with active SPN 3226 FMI 9
Outlet NOx value frozen or updating slower than 1 Hz in Jaltest live data
DEF consumption may drop abnormally while SCR efficiency warnings appear
Progressive torque derate after multiple drive cycles with missing NOx updates
Fault often appears after battery disconnect, harness repair, or sensor replacement

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3226 FMI 13 on Detroit Diesel indicates a critical issue with the outlet NOx sensor, leading to poor SCR efficiency and potential engine derate.
causes: DEF Injector Blockage
Crystallization of DEF at the injector nozzle can block the flow, reducing the efficiency of the SCR system. Regular maintenance and cleaning can prevent this issue.
Faulty NOx Sensor
A malfunctioning outlet NOx sensor can provide inaccurate readings, leading to improper SCR operation. Sensor replacement may be necessary if calibration fails.
Poor DEF Quality
Using contaminated or low-quality DEF can impair the SCR system's ability to reduce NOx emissions effectively. Always use DEF that meets ISO 22241 standards.
SCR Catalyst Degradation
Over time, the SCR catalyst can degrade, reducing its ability to convert NOx gases. This is a less common issue but can occur in high-mileage vehicles.
symptoms: Check Engine Light and Red Stop Engine light are illuminated.
Engine enters derate mode, reducing power and torque.
Noticeable increase in exhaust odor, possibly with blue or white smoke.
Reduced fuel efficiency and increased emissions output.
Potential for increased DEF consumption due to inefficient NOx reduction.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3226 FMI 16 on PACCAR MX-13 Kenworths means the outlet NOx sensor detects moderately low SCR conversion efficiency. It's a high-severity fault most often caused by DEF quality or dosing issues rather than a genuinely failed catalyst. The SCR system's whole job is converting NOx into harmless nitrogen and water, and SPN 3226 FMI 16 flags that it's not doing that job efficiently enough. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com works this fault from the outside in - DEF quality and doser performance first, since those are cheap to check and commonly the actual cause, before ever considering the SCR catalyst itself as degraded or damaged.
causes: Poor or diluted DEF quality
DEF outside the proper urea concentration range reduces the chemical reaction's effectiveness at converting NOx, even with a perfectly healthy catalyst.
DEF injector/doser crystallization or poor spray pattern
A partially blocked or poorly atomizing doser nozzle prevents even DEF distribution across the catalyst, reducing overall conversion efficiency.
Underdosing due to a pressure or flow issue in the DEF system
If the system isn't delivering the commanded DEF quantity, NOx conversion suffers proportionally even with good fluid quality.
SCR catalyst degradation or contamination
Physical damage or chemical poisoning of the catalyst substrate reduces conversion capability, but this is a less common cause than DEF-related issues.
steps: Pull the fault with PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 3226 FMI 16 is active; check DEF quality with a refractometer to rule out contaminated or diluted fluid as a root cause.
Inspect the DEF injector/doser nozzle for crystallization or a blocked spray pattern that would reduce dosing effectiveness even with good fluid quality.

Check the inlet and outlet NOx sensor readings together on Davie4 - if the inlet sensor shows normal NOx levels but the outlet sensor still shows high NOx after the catalyst, the SCR conversion itself is underperforming.
Verify the DEF dosing quantity is tracking correctly against commanded values, since underdosing directly reduces NOx conversion efficiency.
If dosing and DEF quality both check out, inspect the SCR catalyst itself for physical damage, contamination, or thermal degradation using a borescope if accessible.
Clear the code and monitor live NOx efficiency data across a drive cycle to confirm improvement before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Amber dash lamp, potentially escalating toward an inducement warning
Increased DEF consumption as the system attempts to compensate
No immediate power loss in early stages
Possible exhaust odor changes if DEF dosing is significantly off

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3556 FMI 16 – Hydrocarbon Dosing Injector Fault
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3556 FMI 16 – Hydrocarbon Dosing Injector Fault
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3556 FMI 16 indicates a fault with the hydrocarbon dosing injector, which is the component responsible for injecting fuel into the exhaust stream to raise temperatures during active DPF regeneration. When this injector fails on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines the aftertreatment system cannot generate the heat needed to burn off soot and active regeneration cycles will fail to complete.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Active regeneration unable to complete 
DPF soot load continuing to rise 
Engine derate possible as soot accumulates 
May appear alongside incomplete regen or soot load codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects the hydrocarbon dosing injector is not performing within specification during a regeneration cycle. Common causes include:
Clogged or carbon fouled HC dosing injector 
Failed HC dosing injector solenoid 
HC dosing injector stuck open or closed 
Fuel supply issue to the dosing injector 
Damaged or corroded injector wiring or connector 
HC dosing pump failure reducing fuel pressure to injector 
Water or contamination in the HC dosing fuel supply
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but without a functioning HC dosing injector active regeneration cannot be completed. Soot will continue to accumulate in the DPF leading to progressively more severe fault codes and derate conditions. Address this fault before soot reaches critical levels.
Recommended Action
Have the HC dosing injector inspected for carbon fouling or physical damage. Check the injector wiring and connector for corrosion or damage. Test fuel supply pressure to the injector and inspect the HC dosing pump if pressure is low. A clogged injector may be cleanable but replacement is often the most reliable solution.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3556 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the hydrocarbon dosing injector that supplies fuel to the exhaust for DPF regeneration is not functioning correctly, preventing active regeneration cycles from completing.
 
 
What causes SPN 3556 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are a clogged or carbon fouled HC dosing injector, a failed injector solenoid, damaged wiring, or a fuel supply problem to the injector.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3556 FMI 16?
 
Short distances may be possible but without active regeneration capability soot will accumulate in the DPF leading to more severe faults and derate conditions.
 
 
Will SPN 3556 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Not immediately but as soot accumulates due to failed regeneration cycles more severe DPF soot codes will trigger derate conditions.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3556 FMI 16?
 
Inspect clean or replace the HC dosing injector and verify fuel supply and wiring. Once the injector is functioning correctly and a successful active regeneration is completed the code should clear.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 3713 FMI 16 
SPN 3713 FMI 18

SPN 3242 FMI 16

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 5246 FMI 0 – Aftertreatment Fault Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 5246 FMI 0 – Aftertreatment System Fault (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 5246 FMI 0 indicates a malfunction within the aftertreatment system. This fault is commonly associated with SCR, DEF dosing, or sensor-related issues affecting emissions performance.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Aftertreatment warning message
DEF system alerts
Reduced engine power
Possible derate condition
Cause
This code is typically triggered by DEF dosing problems, NOx sensor failure, wiring issues, clogged SCR catalyst, or contamination within the aftertreatment system.
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited operation may be possible, but prolonged driving without repair may result in progressive derate or speed limitation.
Recommended Action
Inspect DEF system components, verify sensor functionality, and perform diagnostic testing on the SCR and aftertreatment system to identify the root cause.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 5246 FMI 0 mean?
 
SPN 5246 FMI 0 indicates that the SCR aftertreatment system has detected a condition that may trigger engine inducement, such as power reduction or speed limitation.
 
 
What causes SPN 5246 FMI 0?
 
This code is commonly caused by DEF system faults, failed sensors, SCR efficiency issues, or repeated unresolved emissions-related errors.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 5246 FMI 0?
 
Driving may be possible initially, but continued operation without repair can result in progressive engine derate or speed restriction.
 
 
Will SPN 5246 FMI 0 limit my speed?
 
Yes. If the issue is not corrected, the engine control module may reduce vehicle speed to enforce emissions compliance.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 5246 FMI 0?
 
The fault will clear only after diagnosing and repairing the underlying SCR or DEF system issue. Clearing the code without repair will not prevent derate.

SPN 3364 FMI 2

Cause
This code is typically triggered by DEF dosing problems, NOx sensor failure, wiring issues, clogged SCR catalyst, or contamination within the aftertreatment system.
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited operation may be possible, but prolonged driving without repair may result in progressive derate or speed limitation.

The fault will clear only after diagnosing and repairing the underlying SCR or DEF system issue. Clearing the code without repair will not prevent derate.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 5246 FMI 31 be cleared at the truck without a shop visit?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Not reliably. A key-off cycle may temporarily change the code status, but the inducement restriction will return if the root cause faults are still active. Proper resolution requires repairing the underlying aftertreatment problem and then using Cummins Insite to reset the inducement counter through the approved procedure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is this code specific to Cummins, or does it appear on other engine brands?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: SPN 5246 is a J1939-defined SPN, so other manufacturers can use it �?but the exact implementation, inducement thresholds, and reset procedures differ by brand. On Cummins CM2350 engines, the inducement system is documented through Cummins Insite and QuickServe. Detroit, Volvo, and other brands have their own inducement strategies.

troubleshooting_faq.question: What happens if the truck is driven indefinitely with this code active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The restriction typically remains in place until a proper reset is performed. Some calibrations escalate the severity of the restriction over additional distance. Running the SCR system in a degraded state for extended periods can also accelerate catalyst wear.

procedures_full.overview: Mack SPN 5246 FMI 0 signals a severe emissions derate, limiting speed to 5 mph. It requires professional diagnostic tools to reset and resolve.
steps: Understand that roadside repairs are not feasible for this code due to its complexity.
Use a heavy-duty diagnostic tablet to perform an 'SCR Induction Reset' command. Ensure the diagnostic tool is updated with the latest software versions to accurately interpret fault codes.
Ensure all related emissions faults are addressed to prevent recurrence of the derate. Check for any additional codes that might indicate underlying issues.
Contact a mobile diesel technician or arrange for towing to an authorized service center. Prioritize facilities with certified emissions specialists.
After resolution, perform a thorough emissions system check to ensure compliance. This includes verifying the functionality of the DEF dosing unit and checking the SCR catalyst for efficiency.
symptoms: The truck is limited to a maximum speed of 5 mph, severely impacting operational capabilities.
A solid red Stop Engine light is illuminated, accompanied by a flashing DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) crystal icon.
Attempts to reset the vehicle by disconnecting the batteries are ineffective.
The vehicle may emit higher levels of exhaust pollutants due to unresolved emissions issues.
Potentially increased fuel consumption as the engine struggles to maintain power within the derate limits.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 5246 FMI 0 means Cummins SCR inducement timer has expired or is in severe stage. Repair underlying DEF/SCR faults — inducement will not clear until root codes are fixed. SCR inducement is the emissions enforcement strategy that limits speed and power when DEF or SCR faults remain unrepaired. Cummins sets SPN 5246 when the compliance timer reaches its threshold.
causes: Unresolved DEF level, quality, or temperature faults
DEF system faults start inducement timers that progress to active derate.
SCR NOx efficiency below threshold
Low conversion efficiency from bad DEF, dosing, or catalyst triggers inducement.
Ignored or cleared root SCR codes without repair
Clearing faults without fixing cause lets timer continue counting in background.
steps: Read all active and pending SCR-related codes in Cummins INSITE — SPN 5246 is a result of unresolved root faults.
Verify DEF tank level, quality at 32.5% with refractometer, and tank temperature plausibility.
Check SCR NOx efficiency in live data — target above 70% at operating temperature.
Repair root cause faults (DEF quality, NOx sensors, dosing, catalyst) before attempting inducement reset.
After repairs, perform inducement reset procedure in Cummins INSITE and verify timer cleared.
symptoms: Inducement warning with countdown timer on dash
Amber or red SCR/DEF warning messages
Stacked DEF, NOx, or SCR efficiency codes in background
Engine power reduced to 55–70% on some calibrations
Timer miles or engine hours counting down to next derate stage

procedures_full.overview: This is the SCR 'inducement' / operator-warning derate — the final stage that forces the truck down to a crawl (often a 5 MPH derate) because an emissions fault (DEF quality, dosing, or NOx) went unresolved. It's a consequence code, not a root cause.
procedures_full.severity_action: Stop as soon as it's safe
causes: An earlier DEF-quality or dosing fault (e.g. SPN 3361/4094) that was never fixed
Empty or contaminated DEF tank
Tampered or disconnected SCR system the ECM has detected
NOx sensor fault that triggered the inducement countdown
first_moves: Get the truck to a safe location now — once full inducement hits, speed is capped to a crawl.
Pull ALL stored emissions codes; the inducement is downstream of an earlier fault — fix that first.
Verify DEF tank level and DEF quality before anything else.
Plan for a mobile diesel tech: clearing inducement reliably needs the underlying fault repaired and a guided reset.
common_misdiagnoses: Trying to clear the 5 MPH derate without fixing the original DEF/dosing fault — it comes right back.
Topping off DEF and assuming that resets it; the inducement often needs the root fault cleared first.
Replacing the NOx sensor when the real issue was DEF quality or dosing.
