procedures_full.overview: Cummins SPN 5246 FMI 15 indicates a DEF quality problem, often leading to vehicle derate. Check DEF concentration, sensors, and for contamination. Immediate attention is required.
causes: Contaminated DEF

Contamination occurs when foreign substances like oil or dirt enter the DEF tank. This can happen during refilling or due to a faulty cap. The SCR system cannot process contaminated DEF, leading to inducement codes.
Incorrect DEF Concentration
DEF should be a 32.5% urea solution. If it's diluted or concentrated incorrectly, the system will detect inadequate quality. This often results from improper mixing or using off-spec DEF.
DEF Quality Sensor Failure
The sensor that monitors DEF quality may fail due to electrical faults or damage. A malfunctioning sensor can falsely report DEF issues, triggering the code.
SCR Catalyst Blockage
Deposits or physical damage to the SCR catalyst can impede the treatment process. This blockage can result from poor DEF quality or prolonged exposure to contaminants.
steps: Check DEF concentration using a refractometer. The ideal concentration is 32.5% urea. Test at the DEF tank access point.
Inspect DEF tank for contamination. Use visual inspection and test strips to check for impurities like oil or dirt.
Examine DEF lines and connectors for leaks or damage. Focus on areas near the tank and pump connections.
Test the DEF quality sensor with a multimeter. Access it near the DEF tank, check for correct voltage readings.
Inspect the SCR catalyst for deposits or damage. Access through the exhaust system. Look for white crystals or obstruction.
Run a diagnostic scan with an ECM tool to confirm stored codes. Use a Cummins-approved tool for accurate data.
Verify NOx sensor functionality. Test at the exhaust outlet. Replace if readings are out of typical range.
Reset the ECM once repairs are complete to clear the code and restore normal operation. Follow Cummins procedures.
symptoms: Sudden activation of a 5 mph speed restriction, typically after a warning period.
Dashboard displays a DEF warning light or check engine light.
Noticeable reduction in engine power, affecting acceleration and hauling capacity.
Increase in diesel fuel consumption due to inefficient exhaust treatment.
Possible unusual exhaust odors or visible emissions that may indicate DEF problems.
Frequent regeneration cycles as the SCR system attempts to compensate for poor DEF quality.
Driver reports of unusual DEF consumption rates compared to normal operations.
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 5246 FMI 15 DEF Quality Issue

procedures_full.overview: PACCAR SPN 5246 FMI 16 indicates a Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) quality issue in the SCR system, leading to potential engine derate. Check DEF quality and system integrity immediately.
causes: Contaminated DEF
DEF contamination is often the result of improper storage or handling. Even a small amount of diesel or dirt can throw off the SCR system, leading to this fault code.
DEF Quality Sensor Failure
The DEF quality sensor might give false readings due to internal failure or wiring issues, leading the ECM to believe the DEF is of poor quality.
SCR Catalyst Blockage
Excessive soot or physical damage can block the SCR catalyst, preventing proper exhaust treatment and triggering the fault code.
ECM Software Glitch
Sometimes, the ECM software might have a bug or require an update, causing it to misinterpret DEF quality readings.
steps: First, inspect the DEF tank. Use a refractometer to check DEF concentration. Ideal range is 32.5% urea. Anything less or more indicates poor quality.
Check the DEF tank for contamination. Look for debris or discoloration. Drain and refill with fresh DEF if contaminated.
Inspect DEF lines for leaks or damage. Use a flashlight to check for blue stains indicating leaks.
Use a multimeter to test the DEF quality sensor. Locate it near the DEF tank. Check resistance values against OEM specs.
Inspect SCR catalyst for damage or excessive soot. If accessible, visually check for blockages or physical damage.
Verify ECM connections. Check for corrosion at connectors, especially at DEF and SCR sensors. Clean with contact cleaner if corroded.
symptoms: Engine derate to 5 mph, making it impossible to maintain highway speeds.
Check Engine Light illuminated alongside SCR system warning on the dashboard.
Noticeable increase in DEF consumption, indicating possible leaks or contamination.
Exhaust smell may become more pronounced if SCR isn't treating emissions effectively.
Frequent regeneration cycles triggered by poor DEF quality affecting SCR performance.
Unusual noises from the SCR system, potentially signaling hardware or sensor issues.

procedures_full.overview: EPA10+ SCR systems use a tiered inducement strategy. When aftertreatment faults (DEF quality, dosing quantity, NOx efficiency, or sensor faults) remain unresolved beyond calibrated thresholds, the ECM activates an inducement condition that limits vehicle speed — typically to 5 mph in severe cases. SPN 5246 FMI 31 signals that this threshold has been crossed. The root cause must be identified and repaired before OEM inducement recovery procedures will succeed.
causes: Unresolved DEF quality fault — contaminated or diluted DEF
DEF dosing failure — clogged injector, weak pump, or frozen lines
NOx sensor fault — upstream or downstream sensor failure
SCR efficiency below threshold — catalyst or dosing path issue
Multi-code SCR cascade — several AT faults triggering inducement together
Operator-ignored derate warnings — inducement escalated from ignored earlier faults
steps: Single Action Gate — Timestamp All AT Codes
Pull all active and inactive aftertreatment codes with timestamps. Identify which codes appeared first — those are the root cause candidates.
Binary Decision Gate — Root vs Consequence Separation
Separate root-cause codes (DEF quality, dosing, NOx sensor, efficiency) from consequence codes (5246 inducement). Do not attempt to clear 5246 first.
Override Manager — DEF Chemistry Verification
Sample DEF from mid-tank and test with a refractometer. Target: ~32.5% urea concentration. Replace DEF if out of spec before any other repair.
Safety Interceptor — Dosing Path Inspection
Inspect DEF pump pressure, filter condition, line integrity, and doser nozzle for crystallization or blockage.
Resume Point — NOx Plausibility Check
Verify upstream and downstream NOx sensor readings are plausible and correlating correctly. Diagnose any NOx sensor faults before reassessing efficiency.
Verification Loop — SCR Efficiency Reassessment
After DEF and dosing corrections, monitor SCR efficiency under load. Efficiency must return to threshold before inducement recovery is attempted.
Repair Ledger Output — OEM Inducement Recovery
Perform OEM-specified inducement recovery procedure only after root cause is confirmed repaired. Document all findings.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Identify and repair the root-cause fault (DEF quality, dosing, NOx sensor, or efficiency).
2 . Drain and refill DEF tank if concentration is out of spec.
3 . Service DEF dosing injector if crystallization or blockage is found ($300–$1,500).
4 . Replace NOx sensor if electrical or plausibility fault is confirmed ($400–$1,200).
5 . Verify SCR efficiency returns to acceptable range after repairs.
6 . Perform OEM inducement recovery procedure with scan tool after root cause is fixed.
7 . Clear all codes and verify no return of inducement condition.
Verification Steps
Confirm SCR efficiency PIDs are within acceptable range at operating temperature.
Verify DEF quality sensor reads within spec after refill.
Confirm inducement condition clears after OEM recovery procedure.
Test drive at highway speed — confirm no speed derate returns.
Monitor for return of root-cause codes over 50+ miles.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use only ISO 22241-compliant DEF from reputable sources.
✓ Inspect DEF dosing injector for crystallization at every major service.
✓ Address DEF quality and NOx sensor faults immediately — do not allow escalation to inducement.
✓ Train operators to respond to first-level derate warnings before inducement activates.
✓ Maintain DEF filter per OEM service intervals.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity

High severity. Inducement can progress to a severe 5 mph speed limit, making the vehicle undriveable on public roads. Drive only to the nearest repair facility. Do not attempt to clear inducement without repairing the root cause — it will return immediately.

SCR inducement warning on dash
DEF-related derate message
Cannot clear inducement with scan tool

procedures_full.overview: SPN 5246 FMI 31 is the most severe SCR inducement stage, cutting road speed significantly. It always follows unresolved earlier DEF or SCR warnings and requires fixing the root cause plus a clean drive cycle to clear.
causes: Unresolved DEF quality issue from earlier warning stages
If the original quality warning was ignored, the system escalates all the way to severe inducement.
DEF tank run empty or nearly empty for an extended period
Running low on DEF without refilling triggers the same escalation path.
Persistent doser/injector clogging
Ongoing dosing problems prevent the system from confirming compliant SCR operation.
steps: Pull the full fault history to identify the original DEF quality, level, or dosing fault that started the inducement escalation.
Check DEF quality and level immediately - a simple bad-fluid or empty-tank issue can be the root cause even at this severe stage.
Inspect the DEF doser/injector for clogging affecting spray pattern.
Verify NOx sensor readings upstream and downstream of the SCR catalyst for plausibility.
Address the root cause completely, since partial fixes may not fully clear the inducement escalation without a successful drive cycle.
symptoms: Severe road speed limitation, often down to a crawl speed
Red inducement warning lamp active
Dash message clearly indicating an emissions-related speed limit
History of earlier, unresolved DEF quality or dosing warnings

İkincil Veri Hattı, Birincil Veri Hattı çalışmadığında kullanılır ve şanzımanın bozulmuş bir modda çalışmasına olanak tanır. Birincil Veri Hattı (J1939A), 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır. İkincil Veri Hattı (J1939B), 20 Yollu TCM Gövde Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 2 on the throttle position circuit indicates the position feedback is erratic or inconsistently follows the commanded position. Carboned throttle plate preventing stable control, failed position sensor, actuator wear, and harness intermittents are the primary causes. Carbon buildup creates false 'sensor erratic' conclusions when the actual problem is mechanical restriction preventing the throttle from following the command signal. Replacing the throttle assembly without cleaning and verifying control is the most common unnecessary repair on this fault.
causes: Carboned throttle plate — carbon buildup preventing stable control
Failed position sensor — internal sensor failure
Actuator wear — motor or gear wear producing erratic movement
Harness intermittents — connector heat or oil exposure
Pin fretting — connector pin fretting from vibration
steps: Single Action Gate — Command Sweep Test

Command a throttle sweep via scan tool and observe position feedback. If the throttle moves but position feedback is erratic during movement, the sensor or harness is suspect. If the throttle does not move smoothly through the full range, carbon buildup or mechanical restriction is the primary suspect.
Binary Decision Gate — Visual Carbon Inspection

Inspect the throttle bore and plate for carbon buildup. Carbon buildup from EGR and crankcase ventilation is a documented cause of throttle control instability that produces false erratic position codes. Significant carbon buildup requires cleaning before any sensor or assembly decision.
Override Manager — Circuit Integrity Check

Verify throttle position sensor circuit integrity. Inspect the throttle body connector for heat and oil exposure. Verify sensor supply, ground, and signal. Pin fretting from vibration is a documented cause of intermittent position faults.
Safety Interceptor — Clean and Retest

Clean the throttle bore and plate per OEM procedure and retest. If the throttle now moves smoothly and position feedback is stable after cleaning, carbon was the cause. If erratic behavior persists after cleaning, proceed to sensor and actuator evaluation.
Resume Point — Actuator Wear Assessment

If cleaning does not resolve the fault, assess actuator wear. A worn motor or gear produces erratic movement that the position sensor accurately reports as erratic — the sensor is not the fault in this case.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Control Confirmation
After repair, verify throttle moves smoothly through the full range and position feedback is stable. Confirm regen performance returns to normal after repair.
Repair Ledger Output — Clean vs Replace Decision
Clean throttle body if carbon is the cause. Replace throttle assembly if sensor or actuator failure is confirmed after cleaning. Do not replace assembly for carbon buildup alone.

Repair Steps
1 . Clean throttle bore and plate per OEM procedure.
2 . Repair connector heat or oil damage.
3 . Replace throttle assembly if sensor or actuator failure is confirmed after cleaning.
4 . Repair harness intermittents found by circuit check.
Verification Steps
Confirm throttle moves smoothly through full range after repair.
Verify position feedback is stable during command sweep.
Confirm SPN 51 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Monitor regen performance returns to normal after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Clean throttle body at every major EGR service.
✓ Inspect throttle body connector for heat and oil damage at every major service.
✓ Address crankcase ventilation issues that contribute to carbon buildup.
✓ Inspect throttle bore for carbon at every major service on high-EGR-rate engines.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. May affect regen performance and drivability. Carbon buildup is a low-cost repair — clean before replacing the assembly.
symptoms: Intake throttle erratic fault active
Throttle plate sensor fault
Regen throttle actuator code
Unstable idle from throttle control issue

procedures_full.overview: SPN 51 FMI 3 is a throttle position sensor circuit high voltage or open class fault where intake throttle position is monitored. Open signal, failed position sensor, connector issues, and reference voltage anomalies are the primary causes. Open circuits after intake service are a documented pattern. Replacing the throttle body assembly before proving the circuit is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Open signal — open signal circuit producing high voltage reading
Failed position sensor — failed position sensor producing high voltage reading
Connector issues — connector issues producing open circuit
Reference voltage anomalies — reference voltage anomalies producing high signal reading
steps: Step 1 — Reference Voltage and Ground Checks

Confirm 5V reference and ground at the throttle connector cavities. Open circuits after intake service are a documented pattern — always inspect the throttle body connector after any recent intake service. Verify reference voltage and ground integrity.
Step 2 — Signal Circuit Verification

Verify the signal circuit. High signal with an open circuit is common. Measure signal voltage at the throttle connector. An open signal circuit producing a high voltage reading confirms a harness or connector fault.
Step 3 — Command Movement Correlation

Correlate signal with commanded movement. A signal that does not change with commanded movement confirms a sensor or circuit fault. A signal that changes correctly with commanded movement confirms the sensor is functional.
Step 4 — Replace Sensor or Assembly After Circuit Proof

Replace the sensor or assembly after circuit proof. Confirm the harness and connector are clean before any replacement. A sensor or assembly replaced without circuit proof may replace a good component into a circuit fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair connector or harness if open circuit is confirmed.
2 . Replace throttle body or sensor assembly if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm throttle position signal is correct after repair.
Verify SPN 51 FMI 3 does not return after repair.
Confirm regen enable and related strategies operate correctly after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect throttle body connector after any intake service.
✓ Inspect throttle harness for damage at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. TPS high-voltage codes are open-circuit electrical diagnostics first.

TPS open circuit intake throttle
Throttle sensor code
Regen enable issues from throttle fault
High signal with open circuit

procedures_full.overview: SPN 51 FMI 3 means the ECM measured accelerator pedal position voltage higher than the calibrated range. On Detroit DD platforms this commonly triggers limp mode or an RPM derate until the APP circuit and sensor output are verified with a scan tool and multimeter. A stuck-high APP signal is one of the most common driveability faults on DD13 and DD15 trucks, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com fields this call weekly from fleets that lost throttle response mid-route. The ECM protects itself by limiting fuel when it cannot trust pedal input, so wiring checks come before parts.
causes: Failed APP sensor internal short
Dual-track pedal sensors wear internally and can pull the signal trace toward the 5V reference, producing a high-voltage reading even with the pedal released.
Signal wire shorted to 5V supply
Chafed harness sections under the pedal bracket or dash can bridge signal to supply, mimicking a wide-open throttle voltage at idle.
Corroded connector pins at pedal or ECM
Moisture intrusion creates resistance paths that skew voltage high; cleaning and dielectric grease often restores normal readings.
steps: Connect Detroit DDDL8 and read live SPN 51 voltage at idle with foot off pedal; expect roughly 0.5-0.8V on dual-sensor circuits, not above 4.5V.
Backprobe the APP connector Pin 1 (+5V supply) and confirm 4.75-5.25V key-on; Pin 2 signal above 4.2V at idle indicates a short to supply.
Measure resistance between APP signal and ground with the connector unplugged; open circuit should read above 1 kΩ, not near 0 ohms.
Inspect the pedal harness under the dash for pinched wires or green corrosion at the 6-pin connector near the firewall.
After repair, cycle key off 30 seconds, clear codes in DDDL8, and verify SPN 51 tracks from 0.6V to 4.0V through full pedal stroke.
symptoms: Check engine lamp active with SPN 51 FMI 3 logged in Detroit DDDL8
Engine holds fixed low RPM or refuses to respond smoothly to pedal input
Intermittent surge or no acceleration despite pedal travel
Cruise control and PTO functions may disable with throttle faults present
Fault may appear after rain, pressure washing, or connector disturbance

procedures_full.overview: SPN 51 FMI 4 is a throttle position circuit low voltage or short class fault. Signal short to ground, failed sensor, crushed harness, and water intrusion are the primary causes. Shorted signal after harness rub-through is a documented pattern. Replacing the throttle body assembly before isolating the short source is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Signal short to ground — signal circuit shorted to ground producing low voltage reading
Failed sensor — failed sensor producing low voltage reading
Crushed harness — harness crushed at intake bracketry producing short to ground
Water intrusion — water intrusion producing short circuit
steps: Step 1 — Disconnect Isolation

Disconnect the sensor and recheck the circuit. A short that clears with the sensor disconnected confirms a sensor fault. A short that remains with the sensor disconnected confirms a harness fault. Shorted signal after harness rub-through is a documented pattern.
Step 2 — Short Checks
Perform short checks on the harness. Inspect pinch points around intake bracketry. A harness crushed at intake bracketry producing a short to ground requires harness repair.
Step 3 — Reference Voltage Verification
Verify reference voltage remains healthy after disconnect. Signal near 0V with the sensor disconnected confirms a harness short. Verify the reference voltage is not affected by the short.
Step 4 — Replace Sensor or Assembly If Circuit Is Clean
Replace the sensor or assembly if the circuit is clean. Confirm the harness is clean before any replacement. A sensor or assembly replaced into a harness short will fail the new component.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair harness if short is confirmed in the harness.
2 . Service connector if water intrusion is confirmed.
3 . Replace sensor or assembly if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
Verification Steps

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on air inlet pressure indicates the ECM detected air inlet pressure below the expected value for the current operating conditions. Restricted filter, collapsed intake hose, sensor bias, debris packing, and installation errors after service are the primary causes. Water-packed filters in storm conditions and incorrect filter installation bypassing seals are documented patterns. No change in the pressure reading after filter service supports a sensor or line fault rather than a physical restriction.
causes: Restricted filter — air filter restriction reducing inlet pressure
Collapsed intake hose — intake hose collapse reducing inlet pressure
Sensor bias — inlet pressure sensor bias producing false low reading
Debris packing — debris accumulation in filter or housing
Installation errors after service — incorrect filter installation bypassing seals
steps: Single Action Gate — Inspect and Replace Filter

Inspect and replace the air filter if restriction is indicated. Water-packed filters in storm conditions and incorrect filter installation bypassing seals are documented patterns. Inspect the filter housing seals for proper seating. Confirm the filter is correctly installed and the housing is properly sealed.
Binary Decision Gate — Check Housing Seals

Check the air filter housing seals for proper seating and condition. An improperly sealed housing allows unfiltered air to bypass the filter and can produce incorrect restriction readings. Confirm all housing seals are intact and properly seated.
Override Manager — Verify Sensor Baseline

Verify the sensor baseline after filter service. A pressure reading that does not change after filter service supports a sensor or line fault. Confirm the sensor reads near atmospheric pressure at KOEO. A sensor that reads below atmospheric at KOEO confirms a sensor bias or circuit fault.
Safety Interceptor — Circuit Checks If Needed

Perform circuit checks if the sensor baseline is incorrect after filter service. Confirm reference voltage, ground, and signal circuit integrity at the inlet pressure sensor connector. A circuit fault producing a false low reading requires circuit repair, not filter service.
Resume Point — Inspect Intake Hose for Collapse

Inspect the intake hose for collapse or restriction. A collapsed intake hose produces a restriction that is not corrected by filter service. Inspect the intake hose from the filter housing to the turbo inlet for collapse, kinking, or damage.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Pressure Confirmation
After repair, verify the inlet pressure reading returns to normal. Confirm SPN 106 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of low inlet pressure events over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Filter, Housing, Hose, or Sensor Decision
Replace filter if restriction is confirmed. Repair housing seals if seal fault is confirmed. Replace intake hose if collapse is confirmed. Replace sensor if bias is confirmed after circuit proof.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on air filter differential pressure indicates the restriction sensor reports above the maximum acceptable restriction for the air filter. A dirty filter is the most common cause and is resolved by filter replacement. Snow or debris packing in severe environments, incorrect filter installation, sensor bias, and wet filter collapse are secondary causes. The restriction sensor should change reading with filter condition — a sensor that reads high with a new filter installed indicates sensor failure or a housing seal issue.
causes: Dirty filter — normal service interval exceeded
Snow or debris packing — severe environment operation
Incorrect filter installation — filter not seated correctly
Sensor bias — reading high without true restriction
Wet filter collapse — water ingestion event
Housing seal failure — unfiltered air bypassing filter
steps: Single Action Gate — Filter Inspection and Replacement

Inspect and replace the air filter before any other diagnostic step. A dirty filter is the most common cause of SPN 107 FMI 0 and is resolved by filter replacement. Inspect the filter element for snow, debris, and water damage.
Binary Decision Gate — Housing Seal Inspection

Inspect air filter housing seals and filter seating. An improperly seated filter or failed housing seal allows unfiltered air to bypass the filter, which can cause restriction sensor anomalies and engine damage.
Override Manager — Sensor Validation with New Filter
If the fault persists after installing a new filter with confirmed proper seating, evaluate the restriction sensor. The sensor should read lower restriction with a new filter installed.
Safety Interceptor — Restriction Sensor Circuit Check
Verify restriction sensor circuit integrity if sensor validation fails. Check sensor connector for moisture and corrosion. Verify sensor supply and signal.
Resume Point — Severe Environment Assessment

In severe environments, assess filter change interval. Snow packing, dust, and debris can plug filters far faster than standard intervals. Adjust maintenance schedule if environment is contributing to rapid plugging.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Restriction Confirmation
After filter replacement, confirm restriction reading returns to normal. Verify fault clears after a full drive cycle.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor Replacement Decision
Replace restriction sensor only after new filter is installed with confirmed proper seating and sensor reading remains high.

1 . Replace air filter element.
2 . Inspect and reseat filter if installation is incorrect.
3 . Repair housing seal if bypass is found.
4 . Replace restriction sensor if reading remains high after new filter installation.
5 . Adjust filter change interval if severe environment is contributing.
Verification Steps
Confirm restriction reading returns to normal after filter replacement.
Verify SPN 107 FMI 0 clears after filter service.
Monitor for rapid return of restriction fault in severe environments.
Confirm power returns to normal after filter service.

✓ Replace air filter per OEM service intervals — shorten interval in severe environments.
✓ Inspect filter housing seals at every filter replacement.
✓ Protect air intake from snow and debris ingestion in severe environments.
✓ Inspect restriction sensor at every major service.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 107 FMI 0 means the Volvo air filter differential pressure sensor is detecting a severely restricted intake air filter. It's a High severity fault causing power loss and dark smoke, but it's typically a simple, inexpensive filter replacement rather than an electrical fault. Air filter restriction codes are refreshingly straightforward compared to most aftertreatment or wiring faults, and SPN 107 FMI 0 is exactly that - a genuine mechanical restriction, not a sensor glitch, in nearly every case. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com likes pointing techs and owner-operators to this code as a reminder that not every dashboard warning means an expensive repair. A severely clogged filter starves the turbo of intake air, hurts fuel economy, and increases soot output heading into the DPF, so it's worth taking seriously even though the fix itself is usually quick and cheap.
causes: Heavily loaded or dirty air filter element
Normal dust and debris accumulation over extended service intervals gradually restricts airflow until the pressure drop across the filter exceeds the threshold.
Oil-contaminated filter from a crankcase ventilation issue
Excessive blow-by or a failing breather can introduce oil mist into the intake tract, saturating the filter and accelerating restriction.
Blocked sense port or pinched restriction gauge line
A blocked sense tube reads a false high restriction even with a perfectly clean filter installed, so the code can persist after a filter change.
Failed differential pressure sensor
The sensor itself can fail and give an inaccurately high reading, though this is uncommon compared to an actual restricted filter.
steps: Connect Volvo Premium Tech Tool (PTT) and confirm SPN 107 FMI 0, then check the live air filter restriction reading against Volvo's specified replacement threshold.
Remove the air filter housing cover and visually inspect the filter element for heavy dirt loading, debris, or oil contamination.
Replace the air filter element with an OEM-spec replacement, ensuring the housing seals properly on reassembly.
Inspect the intake ducting and restriction gauge sense port for any blockage that could cause a false high reading even with a clean filter.
Clear the code with PTT, restart, and verify the restriction reading returns to a normal range at idle and under load.
symptoms: Amber warning lamp illuminated
Noticeable loss of power, especially under load or at highway speed
Black or dark exhaust smoke from incomplete combustion
Poor fuel economy compared to normal operation

procedures_full.overview: FMI 18 on air filter differential pressure indicates the restriction reading is below the expected range. Failed restriction sensor, disconnected hose, filter indicator stuck, and software model conflict after service are the primary causes. A sensor left disconnected after housing service is a documented pattern. A below-normal restriction reading with poor power or boost symptoms indicates a sensing fault — the restriction may be present but not being measured correctly.
causes: Failed restriction sensor — restriction sensor failure producing below-normal reading
Disconnected hose — sense hose disconnected after housing service
Filter indicator stuck — filter indicator stuck in low-restriction position
Software model conflict after service — model conflict after filter service producing incorrect reading
steps: Single Action Gate — Visual Hose and Sensor Check

Inspect the restriction sensor hose and sensor connection. A sensor left disconnected after housing service is a documented pattern. Confirm the sense hose is connected and intact. Confirm the sensor connector is fully seated.
Binary Decision Gate — Verify Sensor Response

Verify sensor response by creating a known restriction or using the OEM test method when possible. A sensor that does not respond to a known restriction confirms sensor failure. A sensor that responds correctly confirms the sensor is functional.
Override Manager — Circuit Checks

Perform circuit checks if sensor response is incorrect. Confirm reference voltage, ground, and signal circuit integrity at the restriction sensor connector. A circuit fault producing a false low reading requires circuit repair.
Safety Interceptor — Do Not Ignore If Other Underboost Symptoms Exist

Do not ignore a below-normal restriction reading if other underboost symptoms exist. A below-normal restriction reading with poor power or boost symptoms indicates a sensing fault — the restriction may be present but not being measured correctly. Correlate the restriction reading with power and boost symptoms before dismissing the fault.
Resume Point — Correlate With Power and Boost Symptoms

Correlate the restriction reading with power and boost symptoms. A below-normal restriction reading with normal power and boost confirms a sensing fault with no operational impact. A below-normal restriction reading with poor power and boost confirms a sensing fault that is masking a true restriction.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Restriction Reading Confirmation

After repair, verify the restriction reading responds correctly to filter condition. Confirm SPN 107 FMI 18 does not return. Monitor for return of restriction reading conflicts over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Hose, Sensor, or Indicator Decision

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 210: Transmission Oil Pressure (Fluid Pressure Sensor)

The transmission oil pump provides the supply oil for the lubrication system. The FPS taps into the lubrication system and provides a pressure input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). troubleshooting_faq.question: What is the correct fluid level check procedure for an Allison transmission?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Allison transmissions require a hot-check procedure: the vehicle must be on level ground, the engine running, the transmission warm and in Park or Neutral, and the dipstick or sight glass must be read within a few seconds of pulling the stick. Checking cold or with the engine off gives an inaccurate level reading. Allison's service documentation and the sticker on the dipstick tube typically describe the model-specific procedure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can Allison SPN 127 FMI 1 be confused with Eaton SPN 127 FMI 1?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The SPN and FMI numbers are identical because both manufacturers follow the J1939 standard, but the transmissions are completely different designs with different diagnostic tools and service procedures. Allison uses DOC; Eaton uses ServiceRanger. Always confirm which transmission brand is installed before selecting a service path.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does this code affect the PTO on a vocational truck?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: In some cases, yes. Allison transmissions equipped with PTO provisions depend on main pressure to engage the PTO. Low main pressure can prevent PTO engagement or cause inconsistent PTO operation. If a fleet truck is also reporting PTO problems alongside this code, both issues likely share the same hydraulic root cause.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton Transmission SPN 127 FMI 1 �?Transmission Oil Pressure Below Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Which fluid does Eaton specify for automated transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies approved fluids for each transmission family in the respective service literature. The correct fluid grade and change interval vary between the Gen 3 UltraShift PLUS and the Endurant HD. Using the wrong grade �?particularly a lighter fluid than specified �?can result in chronic low-pressure codes. Always verify against the Eaton service document for the specific transmission.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 127 FMI 1 cause the transmission to lock in a gear?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: In some cases, yes. If the TCM determines that pressure is too low to safely execute a gear change, it may inhibit shifts to avoid a disengaged or partially-engaged gear. The transmission will attempt to hold the most recently confirmed gear. How aggressively it inhibits depends on ECM calibration and how far pressure has dropped.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is there a hydraulic filter that should be checked alongside this code?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton AMTs have an internal transmission filter that is typically serviced at fluid change intervals. A clogged filter restricts flow to the pump and can contribute to pressure concerns. If the fluid service history is unknown, a filter inspection is worth including in the diagnostic process.

If Fault Code 210 FMI 1, 18 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B If Fault Code 210 FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 20, 21 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step D If Fault Code 210 FMI 13 is Inactive, the Fluid Pressure Sensor and wiring are installed and configured in the TCM. Test Complete, Go to Step V If Fault Code 210 FMI 13 is Active, the Fluid Pressure Sensor and wiring were installed but not configured in the TCM. Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies at 1-800-826-HELP (4357) for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V

B. Verify transmission oil level and inspect for leaks. Key off. Perform Oil Level Inspection Procedure. Note: Reference Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950, Oil Level Inspection Procedure. If FMI 1, 18 and transmission oil level is in range, Go to Step F If FMI 21 and transmission oil level is in range, replace the Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) . Go to Step V If FMI 1, 18, 21 and transmission oil level is out of range, Go to Step C

C. Verify residual transmission oil and inspect internal transmission. Key off. Perform Oil Drain Removal. Notice Place a suitable container under the Oil Drain Plug. Note: Reference Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950, Oil Drain Removal Service Procedure. Record residual oil volume in table. Remove PTO cover and inspect for damage. Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies at 800-826-4357 for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V Residual Oil Volume

D. Verify TCM Fluid Pressure Sensor internal resistance and power supply through vehicle harness. Key off. Disconnect the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector. Inspect the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector, verify the connector is free from contamination and corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. Connect the 3-Way Eaton Diagnostic Adapter (EDA) to the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector. Measure resistance between 3-Way EDA Pin 2 (Ground) and Pin 3 (Signal). Record reading in table. Key on. Measure voltage at the 3-Way EDA Pin 1 (5V) and Pin 2 (Ground). Record reading in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If readings are in range, Go to Step E If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the FPS signal, power and/or ground circuit(s) between the 3-Way FPS Connector and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V Ignition State Pins Range Reading(s) Key off 2 to 3 3k-9k Ohms Key on 1 to 2 4.75-5.25 V

E. Inspect 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and verify Fluid Pressure Sensor signal circuit is not shorted to ground. Key off. Disconnect 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Inspect the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector, verify the connector is free from contamination and corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. Measure resistance between 3-Way EDA Pin 3 (signal) and Ground. Record reading in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 20 and readings are in range, replace the Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) . Go to Step V If FMI 21 and readings are in range, Go to Step B If FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 20, 21 and readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the FPS signal circuit between the 3-Way Fluid Pressure Sensor Connector and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) 3 to ground Open Circuit (OL)

F. Verify transmission oil pressure. Key off. Perform Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) Removal. Install Oil Pressure Adapter (M14x1.5 O-ring Straight Thread) and torque to 19-23 Nm (14-17 lb-ft). Connect Digital Pressure Gauge (or Analog 0-100 psi maximum) to Oil Pressure Adapter. Key on with engine running. Idle engine (650-750 RPM) for 2 minutes to stabilize transmission oil pressure. With engine idling at 650-750 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. Increase and hold engine at 950-1050 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. Increase and hold engine at 1150-1250 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. Increase and hold engine at 1350-1450 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. Key off. Compare reading(s) in table. If readings are in range, replace the Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) . Go to Step V If readings are out of range, Go to Step C Engine RPM Range Reading(s) 650-750 5-15 psi 950-1050 10-20 psi 1150-1250 15-25 psi 1350-1450 20-35 psi

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to "Fault Codes". Select "Clear All Faults". Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 210 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 210 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

Allison tarafından belirtilen sıcak kontrol prosedürünü kullanarak yağ seviyesini kontrol edin: Seviye, motor çalışırken, yağ çalışma sıcaklığındayken ve şanzıman Park veya Nötr konumundayken okunmalıdır. Şanzıman dışını inceleyin…

Şanzıman nötrdeyken ve motor rölantideyken şanzıman yağı seviyesini kontrol edin; Eaton doğru okuma için uygun kontrol prosedürünü ve yağ sıcaklık aralığını belirtir. ServiceRanger'ı bağlayın ve izleyin…
[FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır). Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

procedures_full.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with a Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS) that senses oil pressures and sump oil temperature within the transmission hydraulic system and provides input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The supply oil to the Actuation Control Manifold (ACM) controls all hydraulic operations. The pressure of the supply oil, or Line Pressure, is critical for proper transmission operation. The TPS is mounted to the ACM and is connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Line Pressure signal. If a pressure failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 0 – Data Valid but Above Normal: Line Pressure value greater than TCM command for 2 seconds. FMI 1 – Data Valid but Below Normal (Most Severe): Line Pressure value less than 36.25 psi (2.5 bar) for 2 seconds. FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Line Pressure value out of range for 1 second FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: Line Pressure signal greater than 4.8 V for 1 second. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: Line Pressure signal less than 0.25 V for 1 second. FMI 6 - Current Above Normal or Shorted Circuit: TPS secondary power supply voltage out of range for 1 second. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: Line Pressure calibration failed consistency check. Rising Line Pressure value does not match falling Line Pressure value at same Current value. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: No Line Pressure calibration data stored. FMI 15 – Data Valid but Above Normal: Line Pressure calibration greater than maximum limit. FMI 17 – Data Valid but Below Normal: Line Pressure calibration less than minimum limit. FMI 18 – Data Valid But Below Normal (Moderately Severe): Line Pressure value less than TCM command for 2 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: Line Pressure falsely report
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 0: Line Pressure value matches TCM command for 10 seconds. FMI 1: Line Pressure value greater than 36.25 psi (2.5 bar) for 10 seconds. FMI 2: Line Pressure value in range for 10 seconds. FMI 3: Line Pressure signal less than 4.8 volts for 10 seconds. FMI 5: Line Pressure signal greater than 0.25 volt for 10 seconds. FMI 6: TPS secondary power supply voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 7, 13, 15, 17: Successful Line Pressure Calibration performed. FMI 18, 21: Line Pressure value greater than TCM command for 10 seconds. FMI 20: Line Pressure correctly reported as a valid value for 10 seconds. FMI 31: Transmission detects engine speed and Line Pressure with J1939 reporting engine RPM.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 1: Red and amber warning lamp on PTO Mode prohibited Possible clutch slip or engine flare FMI 0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 13, 20, 21, 31: Amber warning lamp on No degraded performance FMI 7, 15, 17: No degraded performance FMI 18: Amber warning lamp on PTO Mode prohibited Possible clutch slip or engine flare Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 0: Line Pressure value matches TCM command for 10 seconds. FMI 1: Line Pressure value greater than 36.25 psi (2.5 bar) for 10 seconds. FMI 2: Line Pressure value in range for 10 seconds. FMI 3: Line Pressure signal less than 4.8 volts for 10 seconds. FMI 5: Line Pressure signal greater than 0.25 volt for 10 seconds. FMI 6: TPS secondary power supply voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 7, 13, 15, 17: Successful Line Pressure Calibration performed. FMI 18, 21: Line Pressure value greater than TCM command for 10 seconds. FMI 20: Line Pressure correctly reported as a valid value for 10 seconds. FMI 31: Transmission detects engine speed and Line Pressure with J1939 reporting engine RPM.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 0, 15: Line Pressure Valve (LPV) Stuck closed Line Pressure Solenoid (LPS) Stuck open FMI 1, 7, 17, 18: Low oil level Sump Pan Filter Clogged O-ring damaged Neck cracked TPS O-ring leak LPV Stuck open LPS Stuck closed High Pressure Relief Valve (HRV) Stuck open Low Pressure PTO (LPTO) and High Pressure PTO (HPTO) ports External oil leaks Internal oil leaks FMI 2, 3, 5, 6: Transmission Harness Shorted to power, shorted to ground, or open. TPS Internal failure TCM Internal failure FMI 13: No Line Pressure calibration data stored. FMI 20, 21: TPS Internal failure FMI 31: Pump Driven Gear Teeth missing Pump Drive Gear Teeth missing Pump Drive shaft failure Damper Internal failure Dual Clutch Module Input shaft failure

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. 
 If Fault Code 210 is Inactive and there are other Active vehicle or transmission fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes first. Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 0, 15, or 31 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step C 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 1, 7, 17, or 18 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 2, 3, 5, or 6 is Active, Go to Step I 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 2, 3, 5, or 6 is Inactive, Go to Step H 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 13 is Active or Inactive perform Line Pressure Calibration with ServiceRanger. Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 20 or 21 is Active or Inactive, replace Triple Pressure Sensor . Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Verify oil level. 
 Verify oil level per Procision Service Manual TRSM0990 - Oil Level Inspection Procedure. 
 If oil level is low, add correct amount of oil and inspect for leaks. Go to Step V 
 If oil level is within normal operating range, Go to Step C
steps.C:
C. Perform Line Pressure Test. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Service Routines”. 
 Start "Line Pressure Test" and follow on-screen prompts. 
 Note: If equipped with a PTO and PTO or hose(s) are leaking, this may cause Fault Code 210 to set. 
 If Line Pressure Test is successful, create a Service Activity Report, select “Send to Eaton” and Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. For Help Line phone numbers, go to Contact Information . Go to Step V 
 If Line Pressure Test is unsuccessful and Fault Code 210 FMI 0 is Active or Inactive, create a Service Activity Report, select “Send to Eaton” and Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. For Help Line phone numbers, go to Contact Information . Go to Step V 
 If Line Pressure Test is unsuccessful and Fault Code 210 FMI 1, 7, 17, or 18 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step D 
 If Line Pressure Test is unsuccessful and Fault Code 210 FMI 31 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step N
steps.D:
D. Inspect Sump Pan Filter. 
 Key off. 
 Remove Oil Drain Plug and drain oil. 
 Remove Sump Pan and Sump Pan Filter. 
 Inspect for transmission damage and contamination. 
 Inspect Sump Pan Filter and O-ring seal for cracks or other damage. 
 If Sump Pan Filter or O-ring seal is damaged, replace Sump Pan and Filter . Go to Step V 
 If transmission damage and/or contamination is found, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. For Help Line phone numbers, go to Contact Information . Go to Step V 
 If no transmission damage or contamination is found, Go to Step E
steps.E:
E. Inspect Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS). 
 Remove TPS from ACM. 
 Inspect TPS and O-rings for damage. 
 If TPS O-rings are damaged, replace Triple Pressure Sensor . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found. Go to Step F
steps.F:
F. Inspect Line Pressure Solenoid (LPS). 
 Remove LPS from ACM. 
 Inspect LPS for contamination. 
 If contamination is found, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. For Help Line phone numbers, go to Contact Information . Go to Step V 
 If no contamination is found, reinstall LPS in ACM, Go to Step G
steps.G:
G. Inspect ACM to Interface Manifold (IM) gasket. 
 Remove ACM. 
 Inspect ACM to IM gasket for damage. 
 If ACM to IM gasket is damaged, replace gasket. Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, replace Actuation Control Manifold (ACM) . Go to Step V
steps.H:
H. Use Product Diagnostic (PD) Test to locate intermittent failures. 
 Key off. 
 Remove Oil Drain Plug and drain oil. 
 Remove Sump Pan and Sump Pan Filter. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Service Routines”. 
 Start “Product Diagnostic Test” and follow on-screen prompts. 
 Note: Solid “PD” may appear in display when PD Test is active. 
 Note: TCM will not enter PD Test mode when there are Active fault codes. 
 Remove 6 Transmission Harness 10 mm cap screws. 
 Wiggle the Transmission Harness wiring and connections. Look for signs of rubbing or chafing on the wires. 
 To end the test, press the stop button. 
 If fault codes set Active, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If no fault codes set, reinstall 6 Transmission Harness 10 mm cap screws and torque to 8.8-10.4 Nm (77.9-92.0 lb-in). Go to Step I
steps.I:
I. Verify Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS) secondary power supply. 
 Key off. 
 Remove Oil Drain Plug and drain oil. 
 Remove Sump Pan and Sump Pan Filter. 
 Disconnect 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector from TPS Connector. 
 Note: Connector red lock tab must be unlatched and the top of the connector depressed to remove. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Measure voltage between 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 4 and Pin 1. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, Go to Step J 
 If readings are in range, Go to Step K 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 4 to 1 4.75–5.25 V
steps.J:
J. Verify continuity of Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS) secondary power supply circuit. 
 Key off. 
 Remove TCM. 
 Measure resistance between 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 10 and 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 1. Record reading in table. 
 Measure resistance between 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 1 and Ground. Record reading in table. 
 Measure resistance between 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 7 and 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 4. Record reading in table. 
 Measure resistance between 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 4 and Ground. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range, Go to Step K 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 10 to 1 0.0–0.2 Ohms 
 1 to Ground Open Circuit (OL) 
 7 to 4 0.0–0.2 Ohms 
 4 to Ground Open Circuit (OL)
steps.K:
K. Verify Line Pressure signal wire continuity. 
 Key off. 
 Remove TCM. 
 Measure resistance between 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 11 and 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 3. Record reading in table. 
 Measure resistance between 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 3 and Ground. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If all readings are in range. Go to Step L 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 11 to 3 0.0–0.2 Ohms 
 3 to Ground Open Circuit (OL)
steps.L:
L. Verify fault code status. 
 Reinstall TCM. 
 Reconnect all connectors. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Retrieve and record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps. 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 2, 3, 5, or 6 is Inactive, replace Triple Pressure Sensor and Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 210 FMI 2, 3, 5, or 6 is Active, Go to Step M
steps.M:
M. Verify internal resistance of TCM. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector from 8-Way TPS connector. 
 Note: Connector red lock tab must be unlatched and the top of the connector depressed to remove. 
 Measure resistance between 8-Way Transmission Harness Connector Pin 1 and Pin 3. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, replace Transmission Control Module (TCM) . Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range, replace Pump , Triple Pressure Sensor and Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 1 to 3 3.0–9.0 K Ohms
steps.N:
N. Inspect Damper and Dual Clutch Module (DCM) Input Shaft. 
 Remove transmission. 
 Inspect Damper and verify inner splines do not rotate inside assembly. 
 Inspect DCM Input Shaft for damage. 
 If Damper splines rotate inside assembly, replace Damper . Go to Step V 
 If DCM Input Shaft damage is found, replace Transmission and Damper . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step O
steps.O:
O. Remove DCM Clutch and Inspect DCM Input Shaft. 
 Remove Oil Drain Plug and drain oil. 
 Remove Front Cover with DCM. 
 Inspect DCM Input Shaft for damage. 
 If damage is found, replace Transmission and Damper . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step P
steps.P:
P. Inspect Pump Drive Gear and Pump Driven Gear. 
 Inspect Pump Drive Gear and Pump Driven Gear for damage. 
 If damage is found, replace Transmission . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step Q
steps.Q:
Q. Verify Pump Driven Gear rotation. 
 Rotate Pump Driven Gear. 
 Note: Pump should turn freely with no binding. 
 If Pump does not rotate freely, replace Transmission . Go to Step V 
 If Pump rotates freely, contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies +1-800-826-4357 for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to "Fault Codes". 
 Select "Clear All Faults". 
 Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger: 
 If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 210 sets Active, Go to Step A 
 If a fault code other than 210 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) to monitor lubricant oil pressure. The transmission oil pump provides the supply oil for the lubrication system. The FPS taps into the lubrication system and provides a pressure input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM monitors the pressure input to verify the transmission is properly filled with oil to lubricate the transmission. The FPS is mounted externally and connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the FPS. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 1 – Data Valid But Below Normal (Most Severe): FPS reported transmission oil pressure is critically low for 5 seconds. FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: FPS circuit shorted to power for 5 seconds. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: FPS circuit shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: FPS circuit open or shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 6 – Current Above Normal or Grounded Circuit: FPS reference voltage not between 4.75V to 5.25V for 5 seconds. FMI 13 – Out Of Calibration: FPS and OEM wiring installed but not configured in the TCM (Service). FMI 18 – Data Valid But Below Normal Operating Range - Moderately Severe: FPS reported transmission oil pressure is moderately low for 5 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: FPS reporting pressure too high in error when Countershaft is stationary. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: FPS reporting pressure too low in error.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 1: FPS oil pressure in range. FMI 3, 4, 5, 6: FPS in range for 10 seconds. FMI 13: FPS configured in the TCM. FMI 18: FPS oil pressure in range for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 1, 18: Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is moving Red stop lamp on Low start gears only Upshifts prohibited Configurable FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 20, 21: Amber warning lamp on No degraded modes FMI 18: Amber warning lamp on No degraded modes Configurable Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 1: FPS oil pressure in range. FMI 3, 4, 5, 6: FPS in range for 10 seconds. FMI 13: FPS configured in the TCM. FMI 18: FPS oil pressure in range for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 1, 18: Low transmission oil level Not properly filled Leak FPS Damaged Internal failure Internal transmission Lubrication system mechanical failure FMI 3, 4, 5, 6: FPS Damaged Internal failure FPS OEM vehicle harness Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open TCM Software issue Internal failure FMI 13: FPS not configured in the TCM FPS recently installed Replacement TCM installed Configurable Amber warning lamp on If vehicle is moving: Red stop lamp on FMI 20: FPS OEM vehicle harness Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open FPS Internal failure FMI 21: FPS OEM vehicle harness Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open FPS Internal failure Low transmission oil level Not properly filled Leak

 If no fault codes set and vehicle operates properly, test complete.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with a Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) to monitor oil pressure. The transmission oil pump provides the supply oil for the lubrication system. The FPS provides a pressure input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM monitors oil pressure to ensure the transmission is being properly cooled and lubricated. If the oil pressure is out of range, the TCM will adjust transmission operation to perform properly and prevent damage. The FPS is mounted externally to the side of the transmission and connects to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the FPS oil pressure signal. If oil pressure is outside of normal operating range or a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 1 – Data Valid But Below Normal (Most Severe): Transmission oil pressure critically low for 5 seconds. FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: FPS circuit shorted to power for 5 seconds. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: FPS circuit shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: FPS circuit open or shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 6 – Current Above Normal or Grounded Circuit: FPS reference voltage not between 4.75V to 5.25V for 5 seconds. FMI 18 – Data Valid But Below Normal Operating Range (Moderately Severe): Transmission oil pressure moderately low for 5 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: Transmission oil pressure too high in error when Countershaft is stationary. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: Transmission oil pressure too low in error.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 1: Transmission oil pressure in range. FMI 3: FPS circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: FPS circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: FPS circuit not open or shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 6: FPS reference voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 18: Transmission oil pressure in range for 10 seconds. FMI 20, 21: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists.

FMI 3: FPS circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: FPS circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: FPS circuit not open or shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 6: FPS reference voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 18: Transmission oil pressure in range for 10 seconds. FMI 20, 21: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists.

A. Check for active or inactive fault codes.

steps.B:
B. Verify transmission oil level and inspect for leaks. 
 Key off.

 Note: Reference Endurant XD Service Manual TRSM0960, Oil Level Inspection Procedure.

 Key off.

 Notice

steps.D:
D. Verify TCM Fluid Pressure Sensor internal resistance and power supply through vehicle harness. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector. 
 Inspect the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector, verify the connector is free from contamination and corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. 
 Connect the 3-Way Eaton Diagnostic Adapter (EDA) to the 3-Way FPS Harness Connector. 
 Measure resistance between 3-Way EDA Pin 2 (Ground) and Pin 3 (Signal). Record reading in table. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage at the 3-Way EDA Pin 1 (5V) and Pin 2 (Ground). Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are in range, Go to Step E 
 If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the FPS signal, power and/or ground circuit(s) between the 3-Way FPS Connector and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V

 Key off 2 to 3 3k-9k Ohms 
 Key on 1 to 2 4.75–5.25 V
steps.E:
E. Inspect 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and verify Fluid Pressure Sensor signal circuit is not shorted to ground. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. 
 Inspect 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector, verify connector is free from contamination and corrosion; terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to connector body. 
 Measure resistance between 3-Way EDA Pin 3 (signal) and Ground. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 20 and readings are in range, replace the Fluid Pressure Sensor. Go to Step V 
 If FMI 21 and readings are in range, Go to Step B 
 If FMI 3, 4, 5, 6, 20, 21 and readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the FPS signal circuit between the 3-Way Fluid Pressure Sensor Connector and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Connector. Go to Step V 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 3 to ground Open Circuit (OL)
steps.F:
F. Verify transmission oil pressure. 
 Key off. 
 Perform Fluid Pressure Sensor (FPS) Removal. 
 Install Oil Pressure Adapter (M14x1.5 O-ring Straight Thread) and torque to 19-23 Nm (14-17 lb-ft). 
 Connect Digital Pressure Gauge (or Analog 0-100 psi maximum) to Oil Pressure Adapter. 
 Key on with engine running. 
 Idle engine (650-750 RPM) for 2 minutes to stabilize transmission oil pressure. 
 With engine idling at 650-750 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. 
 Increase and hold engine at 950-1050 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. 
 Increase and hold engine at 1150-1250 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. 
 Increase and hold engine at 1350-1450 RPM, monitor pressure gauge and record reading in table. 
 Key off. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are in range, replace the Fluid Pressure Sensor. Go to Step V 
 If readings are out of range, Go to Step C

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on intake manifold pressure indicates the boost is above the severe maximum calibrated threshold. VGT stuck closed, actuator control failure, MAP bias high, control software or response issues, and piping restriction are the primary causes. Stuck VGT after soot events and false overboost from a failed MAP sensor are documented patterns. A pegged MAP reading with no mechanical symptoms supports a sensing fault — confirm true overboost with correlation before any mechanical diagnosis.
causes: VGT stuck closed — VGT vanes stuck in closed position producing overboost
Actuator control failure — actuator failure preventing boost reduction
MAP bias high — MAP sensor bias producing false high reading
Control software or response issues — control strategy fault producing overboost
Piping restriction — downstream restriction producing false high MAP reading
steps: Single Action Gate — Commanded vs Actual Boost

Compare commanded versus actual boost. A pegged MAP reading with no mechanical symptoms supports a sensing fault. A MAP reading that is above the commanded boost confirms true overboost or a sensing fault. A MAP reading that matches the commanded boost confirms the control strategy is commanding the overboost.
Binary Decision Gate — MAP Electrical Proof

Perform MAP electrical proof. Confirm the MAP sensor reference, ground, and signal circuit integrity. A MAP sensor that reads above the maximum specification at KOEO confirms a sensor bias fault. A MAP sensor that reads correctly at KOEO but produces overboost under load requires further diagnosis.
Override Manager — Actuator Freedom Check

Check actuator freedom and response. Command the actuator to the open position and confirm the VGT vanes move freely. A VGT stuck in the closed position after soot events is a documented pattern. Confirm actuator position feedback matches the commanded position.
Safety Interceptor — Inspect for Restrictions

Inspect for downstream restrictions that could produce a false high MAP reading. A restriction downstream of the MAP sensor produces a false high reading that does not reflect true boost. Inspect the charge-air path for restrictions or blockages.
Resume Point — Turbo Mechanical Decision

Make the turbo mechanical decision only after sensing and actuator faults are eliminated. A turbo that produces overboost with a confirmed intact actuator and correct MAP reading requires turbo mechanical assessment. Inspect for VGT vane carbon binding and turbo housing damage.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Boost Confirmation
After repair, verify boost stays within the commanded range under all load conditions. Confirm SPN 132 FMI 0 does not return. Monitor for return of overboost events over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Actuator, MAP, or Turbo Decision

Repair or replace actuator if actuator fault is confirmed. Replace MAP sensor if bias is confirmed after circuit proof. Service or replace turbo if VGT mechanical fault is confirmed after actuator and sensing are eliminated.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair or replace actuator if actuator fault is confirmed.
2 . Replace MAP sensor if bias is confirmed after circuit proof.
3 . Service or replace turbo if VGT mechanical fault is confirmed after actuator and sensing are eliminated.
Verification Steps
Confirm boost stays within the commanded range under all load conditions after repair.
Verify SPN 132 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm no protection derates after repair.
Monitor for return of overboost events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect VGT actuator operation at every major service.
✓ Monitor desired vs actual boost trend over time to identify actuator degradation.
✓ Inspect MAP sensor connector for moisture intrusion at every major service.
✓ Perform VGT actuator sweep at every major service on high-mileage engines.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High. Overboost risks hardware stress. Reduce load immediately. The FSM separates true overboost from false sensor before turbo or actuator replacement.
symptoms: SPN 132 FMI 0 severe overboost
Overboost derate
Turbo overboost shutdown
Boost too high
Engine protection from overboost

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on intake manifold pressure indicates the boost or MAP is below the severe calibrated threshold versus the desired value. Charge-air leaks, failed turbo actuator, stuck VGT vanes, exhaust leaks pre-turbo, sensor bias, and severe intake restriction are the primary causes. Turbo replaced when a CAC boot was split and the reverse — truly stuck VGT — are both documented patterns. Desired versus actual boost graphing is the most efficient first step for severe underboost diagnosis.
causes: Charge-air leaks — CAC boot, pipe, or intercooler leak reducing boost
Failed turbo actuator — VGT actuator failure preventing boost control
Stuck VGT vanes — VGT vane carbon binding preventing boost build
Exhaust leaks pre-turbo — exhaust leak reducing turbo drive energy
Sensor bias — MAP sensor bias producing false low reading
Severe intake restriction — intake restriction preventing boost build
steps: Single Action Gate — Desired vs Actual Boost Graphing

Graph desired versus actual boost under load. A large gap between desired and actual boost confirms the turbo is not producing the commanded boost. A small gap or no gap confirms the turbo is producing the commanded boost — evaluate whether the commanded boost is correct.
Binary Decision Gate — Smoke or Pressure Leak Test

Perform a smoke or pressure leak test on the charge-air system. Turbo replaced when a CAC boot was split is a documented pattern. A leak test that identifies a charge-air leak confirms the underboost source. Repair the leak before any actuator or turbo diagnosis.
Override Manager — Actuator Command and Response

Command the turbo actuator and observe the response. A VGT actuator that does not respond to commands confirms an actuator control fault. Confirm actuator position feedback matches the commanded position. An actuator that responds correctly with no boost build confirms a mechanical turbo fault.
Safety Interceptor — Exhaust Leak Inspection

Inspect for exhaust leaks pre-turbo. An exhaust leak before the turbo reduces the drive energy available to the turbine and produces underboost. Inspect exhaust manifold gaskets, flex pipes, and connections for leaks.
Resume Point — Turbo Mechanical Assessment

Perform a turbo mechanical assessment only after charge-air leaks, actuator faults, and exhaust leaks are eliminated. Inspect turbo shaft play, wheel condition, and housing for damage. A turbo mechanical assessment is the last step, not the first.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Boost Confirmation
After repair, verify boost meets the desired value under load. Confirm SPN 132 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of underboost events over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Boots, Pipes, CAC, Actuator, or Turbo Decision

Repair charge-air boots, pipes, or CAC if leak is confirmed. Repair or replace actuator if actuator fault is confirmed. Repair exhaust leak if confirmed. Replace turbo assembly only with mechanical evidence after all upstream causes are eliminated.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair charge-air boots, pipes, or CAC if leak is confirmed.
2 . Repair or replace actuator if actuator fault is confirmed.
3 . Repair exhaust leak if confirmed.
4 . Replace turbo assembly only with mechanical evidence after all upstream causes are eliminated.
Verification Steps
Confirm boost meets the desired value under load after repair.
Verify SPN 132 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Confirm no power loss under load after repair.
Monitor for return of underboost events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect charge-air boots and pipes for cracks and loose clamps at every major service.
✓ Inspect CAC for leaks at every major service.
✓ Inspect exhaust manifold gaskets for leaks at every major service.
✓ Monitor desired vs actual boost trend over time to identify actuator degradation before it becomes severe.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High for power and towing Severity
High for power and towing. Avoid heavy load until corrected. Severe underboost is air-path and actuator diagnosis before turbo condemnation.
symptoms: SPN 132 FMI 1 severe underboost
No power turbo
Truck will not build boost
Derate from low boost
Severe power loss under load

procedures_full.overview: SPN 132 FMI 1 on Scania engines means inlet air mass flow is below the normal range for current operating conditions. Clogged filters, intake leaks, or a faulty MAF sensor can trigger derate. Check the air filter and test for intake leaks before replacing the turbocharger. Low airflow codes on Scania trucks often start with a forgotten hose clamp. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com compares MAF readings to boost pressure in Jaltest because FMI 1 confirms the ECM sees genuinely low flow data, not a communication error.
causes: Restricted or collapsed air filter element
High restriction reduces measured mass flow even when the turbo can still produce moderate boost.
Intake leak between MAF sensor and turbo compressor inlet
Unmetered air leaks lower MAF reading relative to actual engine demand, setting FMI 1.
Contaminated or failed hot-film MAF sensor
Oil mist from a failed turbo seal coats the sensing element, under-reporting airflow.
steps: Log SPN 132 mass airflow in Jaltest at 1500 RPM no-load versus full-load; compare to OEM spec table for your engine rating.
Inspect and replace the air filter element if restriction indicator is tripped or element is visibly dirty.
Pressure-test intake plumbing from air filter to turbo inlet at 15 psi; soap-test clamps and sensor gaskets for leaks.
Clean the hot-film MAF sensor with approved cleaner only; do not touch the sensing element with tools.
If MAF reads low with clean filter and tight plumbing, measure supply voltage 11-14V and signal output at idle, typically 1-3 g/s on DC13 platforms.
symptoms: Check engine lamp with SPN 132 FMI 1 in SDP3 or Jaltest
Reduced engine power and slow acceleration under load
Black smoke under load indicating rich combustion from low measured airflow
Turbo boost lower than commanded in live data
Fault may appear after air filter service or CAC hose removal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 132 FMI 2 means the mass airflow sensor on a Peterbilt (PACCAR MX engine) is sending an erratic or noisy signal rather than a steady reading. It is Medium severity, causing hesitation and possible smoke, but it does not shut the engine down. Mass airflow sensors give the PACCAR MX engine ECM real-time data on how much air is actually entering the engine, which is essential for calculating correct fuel delivery. SPN 132 FMI 2 flags a signal quality problem rather than a total sensor failure, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com finds that contamination from oiled aftermarket air filters or general dirt buildup on the sensing element is behind the vast majority of these faults, making a simple cleaning the first and often only step needed.
causes: Contaminated sensor element from filter oil or dirt
Oiled aftermarket air filters or accumulated road dust can coat the sensor's delicate wire element, disrupting its ability to accurately measure airflow.
Loose or corroded sensor connector
A partially seated or corroded connector introduces intermittent signal noise that mimics a genuinely erratic sensor.
Cracked or loose intake ducting near the sensor
Unmetered air entering downstream of the sensor, or turbulence from a loose clamp upstream, can cause inconsistent readings even with a clean, healthy sensor.
Failed sensor element
The sensor's internal hot-wire or hot-film element can degrade over time from normal wear and heat cycling.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 132 FMI 2, then monitor live mass airflow data while varying engine RPM to check for erratic jumps.
Inspect the mass airflow sensor connector for corrosion and confirm it's fully seated in its mounting location in the intake tract.
Remove the sensor and visually inspect the sensing element for dirt, oil contamination, or damage from aftermarket air filter oils.
Clean the sensor element carefully with dedicated mass airflow sensor cleaner if contamination is found, avoiding any physical contact with the delicate wire element.
Inspect the intake ducting upstream and downstream of the sensor for cracks or loose clamps that could cause unmetered air or turbulence affecting the reading, then clear codes and re-test.
symptoms: MIL illuminated
Hesitation or flat spots in power delivery, especially during acceleration
