procedures_full.overview: SPN 164 FMI 0 means fuel rail pressure has spiked above safe operating levels. It's a Critical fault with a real shutdown risk - do not attempt to nurse the truck along once this sets.
causes: Stuck-closed fuel rail pressure relief valve
A mechanical valve failure that prevents excess pressure from bleeding off as designed, letting rail pressure climb unchecked.
Failing fuel control actuator/valve
An electromechanical component that over-commands pump output, driving pressure higher than the ECM's own target.
Rail pressure sensor circuit fault
An electrical/sensor issue where the reported pressure is inaccurate, causing the ECM to react to a false high reading.
Restricted fuel return line
A mechanical restriction that prevents excess fuel from returning to the tank, indirectly allowing pressure to build.
steps: Do not attempt to restart the engine if it has shut down under this fault.
Once safe, visually check the fuel rail pressure relief valve for signs of sticking or fuel wetness at its seat.
Connect Caterpillar Electronic Technician (Cat ET) and pull commanded vs. actual rail pressure from freeze-frame data captured at the moment the fault set.
Inspect the fuel control actuator/valve wiring connector for looseness or corrosion that could cause the ECM to over-command pressure.
If actual pressure genuinely exceeded commanded pressure by a wide margin, suspect a stuck relief valve or a failing pressure regulator rather than a sensor issue.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power or an unexpected engine shutdown
Loud knocking or clattering noise from the injectors
Red Stop Engine lamp with high-priority alarm
Possible visible fuel leakage at rail fittings under extreme cases

procedures_full.overview: SPN 164 FMI 1 means fuel rail pressure is running below its commanded target on a PACCAR MX engine. It's a High severity fault causing rough running - check the fuel supply side before assuming the high-pressure pump has failed. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this fixed with a filter and lift pump check far more often than with an expensive high-pressure pump replacement - work the system in the right order.
causes: Restricted primary fuel filter or weak lift pump
A mechanical supply-side issue, not an electrical fault - it starves the high-pressure pump of adequate fuel to build target rail pressure.
Air trapped in the fuel system after service
A supply-side priming issue that produces erratic low readings without a true mechanical failure.
Worn high-pressure pump
A genuine mechanical wear failure that limits maximum achievable rail pressure regardless of supply.
Rail pressure sensor circuit fault
An electrical/sensor issue where the reading itself is inaccurate despite normal actual pressure.
steps: Check the primary fuel filter for restriction and replace it if it's near or past its service interval.
Verify low-pressure lift pump output ahead of the high-pressure pump using a fuel pressure gauge - a weak lift pump starves the high-pressure side.
Connect PACCAR Davie4 and compare commanded vs. actual rail pressure through an idle-to-load sweep test.
Inspect for air in the fuel system after any recent filter or line service, since trapped air causes erratic low readings that mimic a real fault.
If supply pressure and priming are confirmed good but rail pressure still lags under load, suspect wear in the high-pressure pump itself.
symptoms: Rough running or misfire-like symptoms, especially under load
Reduced power and possible hesitation on acceleration
Check engine light
Harder starting, particularly in cold weather
procedures_full.source_title: PACCAR SPN 164 FMI 1: Fuel Rail Pressure Below Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 164 FMI 1 means the common rail is running below its commanded pressure target. It's a High severity fault - the truck is generally drivable but will run rough and lose power until the fuel supply or pump issue is resolved. This is a bread-and-butter diagnostic call at ProfessionalDieselRepair.com, and the fix is almost always cheaper than it sounds if you work the fuel system in the right order - supply side first, high-pressure pump last.
causes: Restricted fuel filter or weak lift pump
This is a mechanical supply-side issue, not an electrical fault - it starves the high-pressure pump of adequate fuel, so it physically cannot build target rail pressure.
Leaking injector or rail fitting
A mechanical fuel leak bleeding pressure off the rail faster than the pump can maintain it.
Failing IMV/FCA fuel control actuator or rail pressure sensor
An electrical/sensor-side fault - the control valve or sensor circuit itself is misreporting or mismanaging pressure even though the mechanical system is healthy.
Worn high-pressure pump
A genuine mechanical wear failure inside the pump that limits maximum achievable pressure regardless of supply.
steps: Check the primary fuel filter and water separator for restriction - a starved low-pressure supply is the single most common cause of a low high-pressure rail reading.
Verify lift pump supply pressure ahead of the high-pressure pump; it should be in the 5-15 psi range depending on platform - anything noticeably lower points to a supply-side problem.

Connect Cummins INSITE and compare commanded vs. actual rail pressure across idle, cruise, and load; a gap that widens under load points to pump wear or an IMV/FCA control issue rather than a sensor fault.
Inspect injector return line volumes for excessive fuel return, which indicates a leaking injector bleeding off rail pressure.
If actual pressure tracks commanded closely but both are lower than spec, suspect the high-pressure pump itself rather than the rail pressure sensor.
symptoms: Hard starting or extended crank time, especially cold
Rough idle or a noticeable stumble under load
Reduced power and poor fuel economy
Check engine light with intermittent or steady illumination

procedures_full.overview: This fault condition indicates a Quantity Control Valve High Side driver error. This condition can occur when:‪
causes: This fault condition indicates a Quantity Control Valve High Side driver error. This condition can occur when:‪
steps: MCM pin 1 circuit is shorted to ground
Internal short of the Quantity Control Valve
Check for multiple codes
If 164/1 is stored along with 164/0, service 164/1 first.
If only 164/0 is active, go to the next step.
Disconnect the Quantity Control Valve harness connector.
Ensure the multi meter (DVOM) resistance is zero.
If meter can auto zero, perform this function before making a resistance measurement.
If meter can not auto zero, note the resistance of the leads and subtract it from the measurement taken in step 4
Measure the resistance across pins 1 and 2 of the Quantity Control Valve.
If the resistance is less than 1.3 Ω, replace Quantity Control Valve. Refer to "8.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is between 1.3 Ω and 1.4 Ω, go to next step.
Disconnect the 120-pin MCM connector and check for corroded, bent or broken pins. Ensure both the MCM and harness connector pins are checked. Repair or replace if needed.
Measure the resistance between pin 1 of the Quantity Control Valve harness connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, replace Quantity Control Valve. Refer to "8.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short circuit between pin 1 of the Quantity Control Valve and ground. Refer to "8.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
ENGINE EXHAUST
To avoid injury from inhaling engine exhaust, always operate the engine in a well-ventilated area. Engine exhaust is toxic.‪
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
DD15 Fuel System Technician's Guide - DDC-SVC-MAN-0037

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on exhaust gas temperature indicates the EGT sensor reports above the maximum calibrated limit. True causes include excessive fueling, restricted exhaust, failed regen control, and boost problems increasing exhaust heat. Sensor bias high — a failed EGT sensor reading extreme values — is a common cause that produces the fault without any actual thermal problem. Correlating multiple EGT sensors is the most efficient first step — one sensor extreme while others are normal confirms sensor failure. Performing major fueling or turbo teardown based on a single failed EGT sensor is the most expensive misdiagnosis on this fault.
causes: True excessive fueling — injector fault or fueling control issue
Restricted exhaust — restriction downstream of EGT sensor
Failed regen control — uncontrolled regen fueling event
Sensor bias high — failed EGT sensor reading extreme values
Boost problems — underboost increasing exhaust heat from incomplete combustion
steps: Single Action Gate — Multi-Sensor EGT Correlation

Cross-check all available EGT sensors. One sensor reading extreme while adjacent sensors read normal confirms sensor failure. All sensors reading high simultaneously confirms a true thermal event. This is the mandatory first step before any major component diagnosis.
Binary Decision Gate — Restriction Inspection

Inspect for exhaust restriction downstream of the EGT sensor. A restricted exhaust system causes heat to back up and produce elevated EGT readings at the monitored location. Inspect DPF loading, exhaust backpressure, and any physical restrictions.
Override Manager — Fueling and Boost Contributor Evaluation

Evaluate fueling and boost contributors to exhaust heat. Underboost from a charge air leak or turbo fault increases exhaust heat from incomplete combustion. Injector faults producing excessive fueling increase exhaust heat directly.
Safety Interceptor — EGT Circuit Check

Verify EGT sensor circuit integrity if sensor correlation suggests bias. EGT harness open or short can create irrational readings — verify before any major fueling teardown. Inspect harness near heat shields and clamps for brittleness.
Resume Point — Regen Control Assessment

If the fault occurred during or after a regen event, assess regen control. An uncontrolled regen fueling event produces true high EGT that requires regen system diagnosis rather than injector or turbo diagnosis.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair EGT Confirmation
After repair, verify EGT readings are within OEM specification under normal operating conditions. Confirm all EGT sensors are correlated after repair.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor, Restriction, or Fueling Decision

Replace EGT sensor if bias is confirmed by multi-sensor correlation. Address restriction if exhaust backpressure is confirmed elevated. Proceed to fueling or turbo diagnosis only after sensor and restriction are proven not to be the cause.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace EGT sensor if bias is confirmed by multi-sensor correlation.
2 . Address exhaust restriction if confirmed.
3 . Repair regen control fault if uncontrolled regen is confirmed.
4 . Address fueling or boost contributors after sensor and restriction are proven not to be the cause.
Verification Steps
Confirm all EGT sensors are correlated and within OEM specification after repair.
Verify derate does not activate after repair.
Confirm SPN 173 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of EGT overtemp under high load conditions.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect EGT sensor harness for heat brittleness at every major aftertreatment service.
✓ Monitor DPF loading to prevent restriction-induced EGT elevation.
✓ Address regen abort causes promptly to prevent uncontrolled regen events.
✓ Maintain boost system integrity to prevent underboost-induced EGT elevation.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High if true overtemp. Reduce load immediately and diagnose. Multi-sensor correlation takes less time than major fueling teardown and prevents unnecessary component replacement.
symptoms: Exhaust temperature high fault active
EGT overtemp derate
Turbo inlet overtemp indication
Aftertreatment overtemp indication
Reduce load immediately from EGT protection strategy

procedures_full.overview: FMI 2 on exhaust gas temperature indicates the EGT signal is erratic or inconsistently matches expected values. Failing thermocouple or RTD, harness intermittents, connector fretting, and probe tip contamination or damage are the primary causes. High-heat zone wiring becomes brittle over time and breaks at flex points — this is a documented pattern after aftertreatment service that disturbs the harness. Comparing adjacent EGT sensors is the most efficient first step to isolate the erratic sensor before any harness or probe work.
causes: Failing thermocouple or RTD — probe degradation in heat zone
Harness intermittents — flex point breaks after AT service
Connector fretting — vibration-induced pin fretting
Probe tip contamination or damage — physical probe damage
High-heat zone wiring brittleness — thermal degradation over time
steps: Single Action Gate — Adjacent Sensor Correlation

Compare the erratic EGT sensor to adjacent EGT sensors. If one sensor is erratic while adjacent sensors are stable, the fault is isolated to the erratic sensor circuit. If multiple sensors are erratic simultaneously, a shared ground or harness fault is more likely.
Binary Decision Gate — Hot Wiggle Test

Perform a harness wiggle test at operating temperature near the suspect EGT sensor. High-heat zone wiring becomes brittle and breaks at flex points — wiggling the harness while monitoring EGT PIDs exposes intermittent breaks that are not visible during cold inspection.
Override Manager — Circuit Continuity Check

Perform continuity test on the EGT sensor circuit. Inspect harness near heat shields and clamps for brittleness and breaks. Harness breaks at flex points after aftertreatment service are a documented cause of erratic EGT faults.
Safety Interceptor — Connector Fretting Inspection

Inspect the EGT sensor connector for fretting corrosion. Vibration-induced pin fretting in the high-heat aftertreatment zone is a documented cause of intermittent EGT faults that appear as erratic readings.
Resume Point — Probe Tip Inspection
Inspect the EGT probe tip for contamination and physical damage. A contaminated or damaged probe tip produces erratic readings that cannot be corrected by harness repair alone.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair EGT Stability Confirmation
After repair, verify EGT reading is stable and correlates with adjacent sensors. Confirm regen performance returns to normal after repair.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor and Pigtail Decision
Replace sensor and pigtail together when both are suspect in the heat zone. Replacing only the sensor with a brittle pigtail produces repeat erratic faults.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair harness flex point breaks found by hot wiggle test.
2 . Repair connector fretting corrosion.
3 . Replace EGT sensor and pigtail together when both are suspect.
4 . Reroute harness away from heat shields and clamps if damage is recurring.
Verification Steps
Confirm EGT reading is stable and correlates with adjacent sensors after repair.
Verify regen performance returns to normal after repair.
Confirm SPN 173 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of erratic EGT during regen events.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect EGT sensor harness for heat brittleness at every major aftertreatment service.
✓ Inspect EGT connector for fretting corrosion at every major service.
✓ Avoid disturbing EGT harness unnecessarily during aftertreatment service.
✓ Replace EGT sensor and pigtail together when harness shows heat brittleness.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. Can disable successful regen strategy. Erratic EGT data prevents the ECM from confirming regen completion temperatures. Address before extended operation.
symptoms: EGT sensor erratic fault active
Intermittent regen temperature fault
Fluctuating exhaust temperature indication
Failed regen from erratic EGT data
DOC temperature fault from erratic upstream EGT

procedures_full.overview: SPN 173 FMI 3 means an exhaust gas temperature sensor circuit on a Freightliner is reading voltage above normal, typically an open sensor or heat-damaged wire. It's Medium severity and can affect regeneration timing, though the engine keeps running normally. Exhaust gas temperature sensors are scattered throughout the aftertreatment system on modern Freightliners to give the ECM real-time visibility into exhaust heat at multiple points. SPN 173 FMI 3 flags an open circuit condition on one of these sensors, and while it won't cause any immediate drivability problem, ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always recommends addressing it promptly since it can quietly interfere with regeneration timing decisions the ECM needs to keep the DPF and SCR system healthy.
causes: Heat-damaged sensor wiring near the exhaust system
Sustained high exhaust temperatures gradually crack wire insulation, eventually breaking the conductor and opening the circuit.
Corroded or loose sensor connector
Heat cycling and road grime degrade connector seals over time, corroding pin contacts and creating an intermittent or open connection.
Failed sensor element
The thermocouple or thermistor element inside the sensor can fail from repeated extreme heat cycling.
Physical damage from a recent exhaust or turbo repair
Sensor wiring or connectors can be accidentally damaged during nearby component service if care isn't taken during reassembly.
steps: Connect a Freightliner-compatible diagnostic tool and confirm SPN 173 FMI 3, noting which specific EGT sensor location is affected if the truck has multiple.
Inspect the affected sensor connector for corrosion, and check the wiring for heat damage near the exhaust piping and turbo.
Unplug the sensor and verify the expected reference voltage and ground are present at the harness side.
Check sensor resistance with a multimeter against spec, since an open EGT sensor will read infinite resistance (OL), consistent with a voltage-above-normal fault.
Replace the sensor or repair the harness as needed, clear the code, and monitor regeneration behavior on the next drive cycle.
symptoms: Amber MIL illuminated
Possible DPF regeneration timing changes or hesitancy to initiate regen
No immediate drivability change in most cases
Slightly reduced fuel economy on some calibrations as the ECM runs conservative defaults

field_evidence.excerpt: The Peterbilt 579 truck may encounter sensor faults and engine performance problems associated with the SPN 177 code. This diagnostic trouble code specifically indicates an issue with the turbocharger boost pressure sensor or its related circuit. Common symptoms that accompany the SPN 177 code include a reduction in engine power and the illumination of the check engine light. These signs suggest that the turbocharger system is not functioning correctly, potentially affecting overall vehicle performance. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 212: Transmission Oil Temperature (Fluid Temperature Sensor)
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Fluid Temperature Sensor (FTS) to monitor sump oil temperature. Sump oil temperature represents the overall operating temperature of the transmission. The FTS provides a temperature input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The FTS is mounted in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-way Transmission Harness Connector.
causes: Maximum vehicle Gross Combination Weight (GCW) and/or operating grade exceeded Low transmission oil level Not properly filled Leak FTS not configured in the TCM Replacement TCM installed FTS Internal failure Internal transmission Lubrication system mechanical failure FMI 2, 4, 5, 6, 10: MTM FTS Internal Failure Harness wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open TCM Internal failure Additional Tools Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950 Digital Volt/Ohm Meter (DVOM) Eaton Breakout Box with 74-Way Eaton Diagnostic Adapter (RR1029TR)

If FMI 0, 15, 16 and transmission oil level is in range, FTS reported a higher than expected oil sump temperature. Based on transmission model, verify maximum vehicle Gross Combination Weight (GCW) and operating grade is not exceeded. D. Verify condition of 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector. Key off. Remove the TCM from the MTM with the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector connected. V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to "Fault Codes". oem_troubleshooting.title: Allison Transmission SPN 177 FMI 0 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature Above Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the transmission recover from an overtemperature event without damage?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: A single, brief overtemperature event that clears quickly may not cause lasting damage, especially in a transmission with good fluid and recent service. Repeated events or sustained high temperatures accelerate fluid and seal degradation. Allison DOC's thermal event history can help a technician assess whether the transmission has experienced chronic overheating.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does adding a transmission cooler eliminate this code?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: An external auxiliary cooler can reduce operating temperatures in high-demand applications and may prevent the code from recurring. However, if the code was originally caused by a restricted existing cooler or a low fluid level, adding a new cooler without fixing the root cause may only partially address the problem.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How often should transmission fluid be changed in a vocational Allison application?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Allison specifies fluid change intervals based on application severity. High-cycle vocational applications �?refuse, transit, severe on/off highway �?use shorter intervals than on-highway linehaul applications. Consult Allison's service documentation for the TranSynd or approved fluid intervals for the specific series and application. Using fluid beyond its service life contributes to thermal degradation.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 177 FMI 0 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature Above Normal | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What fluid does the Eaton UltraShift use?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton UltraShift transmissions require Eaton-approved transmission fluid, typically a 50-weight mineral gear oil meeting Eaton PS-164 or equivalent for older units, and synthetic fluid for newer PLUS-generation units. Confirm the fluid specification in the Eaton maintenance guide for the specific transmission model and generation.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Does the Eaton UltraShift have an auxiliary cooler option for vocational applications?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. Eaton offers an auxiliary cooler option for UltraShift transmissions in demanding duty cycles �?heavy construction, refuse, or extreme mountain grades �?where the standard cooler circuit cannot maintain acceptable fluid temperatures. An auxiliary cooler is mounted in the air stream and supplements the engine coolant-based transmission cooler.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How does SPN 177 FMI 0 differ from FMI 16 on the Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: FMI 0 indicates temperature is above normal range �?a measurement that exceeds the normal operating spec. FMI 16 indicates an above-normal moderate-severity condition on some J1939 implementations, which may represent an earlier-stage warning threshold. In practice, both FMI values indicate the transmission is running hotter than intended and require the same diagnostic approach: investigate the cooling circuit and fluid condition.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 177 FMI 16 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature High | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What transmission fluid specification does the Eaton UltraShift require?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies PS-386 approved fluids for UltraShift and Fuller Advantage transmissions. This includes several synthetic and conventional transmission lubricants from major suppliers. Using a non-approved fluid can affect thermal protection and shift quality. Verify the correct specification using Eaton's fluid guide for the specific transmission model.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can driving habits cause SPN 177 FMI 16 on an Eaton UltraShift in a vocational application?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. In vocational applications such as construction or refuse trucks, frequent stops with heavy loads and high launch torque demands generate significant heat. If the cooler is sized adequately but the duty cycle is exceptionally demanding, the fluid may still reach the warning threshold during peak operation. Operating parameters within the application's rated duty cycle should not cause chronic temperature faults.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How often should the transmission fluid be changed on an Eaton UltraShift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton specifies fluid change intervals based on application and fluid type �?typically every 250,000 to 500,000 miles for approved synthetic fluids in standard applications, with shorter intervals for severe duty. High-temperature events can accelerate fluid degradation and may warrant an earlier change. Eaton ServiceRanger tracks fluid temperature history and can flag conditions that suggest the fluid has been thermally stressed.

oem_troubleshooting.title: ZF AS-Tronic / TraXon SPN 177 FMI 16 �?Transmission Fluid Temperature High | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What ZF transmission fluid specification should be used in an AS-Tronic or TraXon?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF specifies TE-ML 02, 12, or 16 approved fluids for AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions depending on the application. Always verify the correct specification using the ZF lubrication table for the specific transmission model and application �?using an incorrect fluid grade can affect thermal protection and shift behavior.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the ZF TraXon transmission reduce power or limit shifting when SPN 177 FMI 16 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The ZF TCU may modify its shift strategy �?for example, skipping shift points to reduce clutch slip heat �?when fluid temperature exceeds the warning threshold. This is a protective response designed to reduce heat generation and prevent the temperature from escalating to the critical shutdown level.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the transmission cooler on a ZF AS-Tronic part of the engine coolant circuit?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes, on most heavy-duty truck applications the ZF transmission cooler is integrated into the engine coolant circuit �?hot transmission fluid passes through a heat exchanger cooled by engine coolant. This means that if the engine is running hot (elevated coolant temperature), the transmission cooler becomes less effective, which can contribute to high transmission fluid temperature.

procedures_full.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with a Triple Pressure Sensor (TPS). The TPS monitors 3 specific oil pressures in the hydraulic system and provides input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of ensuring proper hydraulic system control. The TPS also monitors sump oil temperature. Sump oil temperature represents the overall operating temperature of the transmission. Temperature input is provided to the TCM for the purpose of making clutch engagement and shift decisions. If the temperature is extreme, the TCM will adjust transmission operation to perform properly and prevent damage. The normal operating range is approximately 140-212° F (60-100° C). The TPS is located in the Actuation Control Manifold (ACM) and connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the TPS sump oil temperature signal. If the temperature is outside of the normal operating range or a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 0 – Data Valid but Above Normal (Most Severe): Sump oil temperature greater than 275°F (135°C) for 1 second. FMI 1: Data Valid but Below Normal (Most Severe): Sump Oil Temperature lower than -4.9°F (-20.5°C) for 1 second. FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Sump Oil Temperature out of range for 5 seconds. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: Sump Oil Temperature circuit shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: Sump Oil Temperature circuit open or shorted to power for 5 seconds. FMI 6 - Current Above Normal or Shorted Circuit: Sump Oil Temperature supply voltage out of range for 5 seconds. FMI 10 – Abnormal Rate of Change: Sump Oil Temperature rate of change greater than 20°F (11°C) per second. FMI 11 – Root Cause Unknown: Sump and Cooler Oil temperature differential too large for 5 seconds. At least 54°F (30°C) difference. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Sump Oil Temperature below threshold after warm up cycle and significantly below Cooler Oil Temperature after warm up cycle. FMI 15 – Data Valid but Above Normal (Least Severe): Sump Oil Temperature greater than 230°F (110°C) for 10 seconds. FMI 16 – Data Valid but Above Normal (Moderately Severe)

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with a Fluid Temperature Sensor (FTS) to monitor sump oil temperature. Sump oil temperature represents the overall operating temperature of the transmission. The FTS provides a temperature input to the Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM monitors oil temperature to ensure the transmission is being properly cooled and lubricated. If the oil temperature is extreme, the TCM will adjust transmission operation to perform properly and prevent damage. The normal temperature operating range is 86 - 250°F (30 - 121°C). The FTS is mounted in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the FTS oil temperature signal. If oil temperature is outside of normal operating range or a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 0 – Data Valid but Above Normal (Most Severe): Transmission oil temperature greater than 275°F (135°C) for 10 seconds. FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Transmission oil temperature out of range, greater than 302°F (150°C) or less than -41.8°F (-41°C), for 5 seconds. FMI 4 - Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: FTS circuit shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 5 - Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: FTS circuit open or shorted to power for 5 seconds. FMI 6 - Current Above Normal or Shorted Circuit: FTS reference voltage not between 4.75V to 5.25V for 5 seconds. FMI 10 - Abnormal Rate of Change: Transmission Oil Temperature rate of change greater than 20°F (11°C) per second. FMI 15 - Data Valid but Above Normal (Least Severe): Transmission oil temperature greater than 252°F (122°C) for 15 minutes or above 273°F (134°C) for 1 minute. FMI 16 – Data Valid but Above Normal (Moderately Severe): Transmission oil temperature greater than 252°F (122°C) for 30 minutes or above 273°F (134°C) for 2 minutes.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 0, 15, 16: Transmission oil temperature below 252°F (122° C) for 1 minute. FMI 2: Transmission oil temperature in range for 10 seconds. FMI 4: FTS circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: FTS circuit not open or shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 6: FTS reference voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 10: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 0, 15, 16 Amber warning lamp on (OEM specific) Red stop lamp on (OEM specific) Shift performance may be degraded FMI 2, 4, 5, 6, 10 Amber warning lamp on (OEM specific) No degraded modes Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 0, 15, 16: Transmission oil temperature below 252°F (122° C) for 1 minute. FMI 2: Transmission oil temperature in range for 10 seconds. FMI 4: FTS circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: FTS circuit not open or shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 6: FTS reference voltage in range for 10 seconds. FMI 10: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 0, 15, 16: Low transmission oil level Not properly filled Leak FTS not configured in the TCM Replacement TCM installed FTS Internal failure Internal transmission Lubrication system mechanical failure FMI 2, 4, 5, 6, 10: FTS Internal Failure MTM Harness Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open TCM Internal failure

steps.D:

 Key off.

 If no contamination or damage is found, Go to Step E

procedures_full.source_title: SPN 411 FMI 0 — EGR diff pressure high | Causes & Fixes | RoadService.app

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 indicates the EGR delta-P is above the expected value for current conditions. Causes include sensor bias high, a restricted or kinked sense line creating an imbalance, valve over-open condition, and wiring high-signal faults. A classic pattern is one tube plugged while the other remains open — this creates an asymmetric pressure reading that appears as a false high. Signal shorts toward the high reference and connector moisture are electrical causes. Baseline equalization testing — opening both ports to atmosphere and checking the sensor output — is the most efficient first gate.
causes: One tube plugged, one open — asymmetric pressure creating false high reading
Sensor bias high — internal sensor failure reading above actual
Restricted or kinked sense line — imbalanced measurement
Valve over-open — true excess EGR flow
Signal short toward high reference — wiring fault
Connector moisture — corrosion affecting signal
steps: Single Action Gate — Baseline Equalization Test

Disconnect both sense tubes from the sensor and open both ports to atmosphere. Check sensor output with both ports equalized. A reading significantly above zero with both ports open to atmosphere confirms sensor bias or internal failure — not a valve problem.
Binary Decision Gate — Sense Tube Inspection
Inspect both sense tubes for restriction, kinking, and plugging. One tube plugged while the other is open creates an asymmetric pressure that reads as a false high. Clean both tubes and retest.
Override Manager — EGR Valve Position Verification
Verify EGR valve actual position at idle. If valve is commanding closed but actual position shows open, investigate valve mechanical condition and actuator control.
Safety Interceptor — Signal Circuit Check
Check for signal short toward high reference. Measure signal voltage with sensor disconnected. A high signal with sensor disconnected confirms a wiring fault, not a sensor or valve problem.
Resume Point — Valve Seating Inspection
If baseline equalization and tube inspection are normal, inspect EGR valve seating. A valve that does not fully close allows excess EGR flow that can produce a true high delta-P reading.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Delta-P Baseline
After any repair, recheck baseline equalization and confirm delta-P responds correctly to commanded EGR flow changes.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor or Valve Decision
Replace sensor only after baseline equalization confirms internal bias. Address valve only after sensor and measurement path are confirmed good.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean both sense tubes if asymmetric plugging is found.
2 . Replace sensor if baseline equalization confirms internal bias.
3 . Repair any signal circuit shorts found.
4 . Service EGR valve if over-open or poor seating is confirmed.
5 . Repair any kinked or restricted measurement lines.
Verification Steps
Confirm baseline equalization reads near zero after repair.
Verify delta-P responds correctly to commanded EGR flow changes.
Confirm SPN 411 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Monitor combustion stability returns to normal after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Clean EGR sense tubes at every EGR system service.
✓ Inspect both tubes for asymmetric plugging — not just one.
✓ Address EGR valve carbon buildup before it affects seating.
✓ Inspect sensor connector for moisture at every EGR service.

procedures_full.overview: The EGR delta-P sensor measures the pressure difference across the EGR system to infer flow rate. FMI 1 indicates the reported delta-P is below the expected value for current operating conditions. On Cummins and other platforms using delta-P EGR measurement, plugged sense tubes are the most common cause — soot accumulates in the small-bore tubes connecting the sensor to the EGR passages. A failed sensor, true low EGR flow from a stuck valve, and leaks in the measurement lines are secondary causes. Replacing the sensor without cleaning the tubes is the most common repeat-code pattern on this fault.
causes: Plugged sense tubes — soot accumulation in small-bore measurement tubes
Failed sensor — internal failure after tube cleaning
True low EGR flow — stuck valve reducing actual flow
Leaks in measurement lines — false low from pressure loss
Sensor connector corrosion — harness heat damage near EGR plumbing
steps: Single Action Gate — Sense Tube Inspection and Cleaning

Remove and clean both sense tubes before any other diagnostic step. Soot-plugged sense tubes are the classic cause of SPN 411 FMI 1. Replacing the sensor without cleaning the tubes produces repeat codes within hours of operation.
Binary Decision Gate — Sensor Supply and Signal Check

Verify 5V reference, ground, and signal integrity at the sensor connector. A stuck signal with clean tubes and valid supply indicates sensor failure. Sensor connector corrosion from heat exposure near EGR plumbing is common.
Override Manager — EGR Flow Command Test

Command EGR valve open and observe delta-P response. If delta-P does not respond to commanded EGR flow with clean tubes and a valid sensor, the EGR valve is not flowing — investigate valve position and movement.
Safety Interceptor — Measurement Line Leak Check
Inspect measurement lines for cracks, loose fittings, and heat damage. A leak in the measurement line between the sensor and the EGR passage creates a false low reading.
Resume Point — EGR Valve Position Correlation
Correlate EGR valve commanded position with delta-P response. If valve is commanding open but delta-P remains low with clean tubes and a good sensor, investigate valve mechanical condition.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Delta-P Response
After tube cleaning and any repairs, command EGR flow and confirm delta-P responds appropriately. Verify fault does not return after a full drive cycle.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor or Valve Decision
Replace sensor only after tubes are clean and circuit is proven. Address EGR valve only after sensor and measurement path are confirmed good.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean both sense tubes — this resolves the majority of SPN 411 FMI 1 cases.
2 . Inspect and clean sense tube ports in the EGR passages.
3 . Repair any measurement line leaks found.
4 . Replace sensor if circuit is good and response is absent after tube cleaning.
5 . Address EGR valve if flow is confirmed absent with good sensor and clean tubes.
Verification Steps
Confirm delta-P responds to commanded EGR flow after repair.
Verify SPN 411 FMI 1 does not return after a full drive cycle.
Monitor NOx output returns to normal after repair.
Confirm EGR valve position and delta-P are correlated correctly.
Preventative Measures
✓ Clean EGR sense tubes at every EGR system service.
✓ Inspect sense tube condition at every major service interval.
✓ Address EGR valve carbon buildup before it affects flow measurement.
✓ Inspect sensor connector for heat damage at every EGR service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. Elevated NOx from reduced EGR flow. Address before extended operation. Tube cleaning is a quick, low-cost first step that resolves most cases.
symptoms: EGR delta pressure low fault active
EGR DP sensor fault
Insufficient EGR flow code
Tube plugged EGR sensor indication
Elevated NOx from EGR flow reduction

procedures_full.overview: SPN 411 FMI 3 indicates a voltage issue with the EGR Delta Pressure Sensor on International engines. This can lead to reduced engine efficiency and should be addressed promptly. The International SPN 411 FMI 3 fault code is a common issue that affects the EGR Delta Pressure Sensor. This sensor plays a critical role in managing the EGR system by monitoring the pressure differential across the EGR valve. When this code is triggered, it indicates that the voltage from the sensor is above normal, suggesting potential issues such as soot blockage or sensor failure. Understanding and addressing this fault code is essential for maintaining optimal engine performance and preventing further damage. In this guide, we'll explore the symptoms, root causes, and effective solutions to resolve this issue, ensuring your International engine runs smoothly. The EGR system's efficiency is crucial for emission control and engine longevity, making timely intervention important.
causes: Soot Blockage

Over time, soot can accumulate in the small ports of the EGR Delta Pressure Sensor, leading to incorrect readings. Regular cleaning can prevent this buildup and ensure accurate sensor performance. Soot is a byproduct of diesel combustion, and its accumulation can be exacerbated by poor fuel quality or incomplete combustion cycles.
Sensor Failure

The sensor itself may fail due to internal electronic issues or damage from excessive heat. Replacement of the sensor is necessary if cleaning does not resolve the issue. Sensors can degrade over time due to thermal cycling and exposure to harsh engine conditions.
Wiring Issues

Damaged or corroded wiring can cause signal interference or false readings. Inspecting the wiring harness for damage can help identify and resolve this issue. Look for signs of wear such as frayed wires or corroded connectors, which can interrupt the sensor's signal to the ECM.
steps: Identify the EGR Delta Pressure Sensor, typically located near the EGR mixing pipe on the engine. Refer to the vehicle's service manual for exact location details.
Carefully disconnect the metal sensor tubes from the exhaust manifold to the sensor base. Ensure you have the correct tools to avoid damaging the connections.
Use a stiff mechanical wire or speedometer cable to clear any soot or carbon buildup within the tubes. This may require multiple passes to ensure thorough cleaning.
Inspect the sensor ports for blockage and clean them with brake cleaner if necessary. Use a soft brush to gently remove any stubborn deposits.
Reassemble the components, ensuring all connections are secure, and clear the fault code using a diagnostic tool. Verify that the sensor is functioning correctly by checking live data readings.
symptoms: Amber Check Engine light remains on, indicating a persistent issue.
Noticeable drop in fuel efficiency, leading to increased operational costs.
Engine idle may become rougher, particularly when the engine is cold.
Potential for increased exhaust emissions due to improper EGR function.
Slight hesitation or power loss during acceleration.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 412 FMI 0 indicates EGR temperature above the calibrated maximum. Failed EGR cooler efficiency, coolant flow restriction to the cooler, sensor bias high, excessive EGR mass, and debris-packed cooling package are the primary causes. Plugged EGR coolers and cooler internal restriction with progressive overtemp are documented patterns. Replacing the EGR cooler for a sensor bias fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Failed EGR cooler efficiency — failed EGR cooler efficiency producing above-normal EGR temperature
Coolant flow restriction — coolant flow restriction to cooler producing above-normal EGR temperature
Sensor bias high — EGRT sensor bias high producing false above-normal reading
Excessive EGR mass — excessive EGR mass producing above-normal temperature
Debris-packed cooling package — debris-packed cooling package reducing coolant flow to cooler
steps: Step 1 — Sensor Correlation

Compare EGRT with ECT and exhaust temperatures. An extreme offset between EGRT and related temperatures supports a sensor fault. A sensor bias high producing a false above-normal reading confirms a sensing fault. Confirm sensor circuit integrity before any cooler assessment.
Step 2 — Inspect EGR Cooler Coolant Flow

Inspect EGR cooler coolant flow. Plugged EGR coolers and cooler internal restriction with progressive overtemp are documented patterns. Verify coolant flow to the EGR cooler. A coolant flow restriction to the cooler requires cooling system diagnosis.
Step 3 — Evaluate EGR Valve Command
Evaluate EGR valve command. Excessive EGR mass producing above-normal temperature requires EGR valve command evaluation. Verify the EGR valve is not commanding excessive EGR mass.
Step 4 — Cooling Package Inspection

Inspect the cooling package. A debris-packed cooling package reducing coolant flow to the cooler requires cooling package cleaning. Inspect the radiator, charge air cooler, and cooling package for debris and restriction.
Step 5 — EGR Cooler Service After Evidence

Service or replace the EGR cooler only after confirming thermal evidence. Confirm sensor, coolant flow, and EGR command integrity before any cooler service. An EGR cooler replaced for a sensor bias fault will not resolve the fault.

Repair Steps
1 . Repair EGRT sensor circuit if sensor bias is confirmed.
2 . Repair coolant flow restriction if confirmed.
3 . Address EGR valve command if excessive EGR mass is confirmed.
4 . Clean cooling package if debris restriction is confirmed.
5 . Service or replace EGR cooler only after confirming thermal evidence.
Verification Steps
Confirm EGRT readings are within specification after repair.
Verify SPN 412 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm EGR cooler efficiency is correct after repair.
Monitor for return of high EGR temperature events over extended operation.

✓ Inspect cooling package for debris at every major service.
✓ Inspect EGRT sensor connector at every major service.

EGR cooler inefficient
High EGR gas temperature

procedures_full.overview: SPN 412 FMI 1 indicates EGR temperature below the expected minimum. Sensor bias low, open circuit, stuck-open cooler flow in conditions expecting higher temperature, and wiring faults are the primary causes. Unplugged EGRT after cooler service is a documented pattern. Replacing or servicing the EGR cooler for a sensor or circuit fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Sensor bias low — EGRT sensor bias low producing below-normal reading
Open circuit — open circuit in EGRT sensor harness producing stuck-low reading
Stuck-open cooler flow — stuck-open cooler flow in conditions expecting higher temperature
Wiring faults — wiring faults producing below-normal sensor reading
steps: Step 1 — Ambient Correlation

Correlate the EGRT reading with ambient temperature at cold soak. Cold soak should be near ambient. Stuck unrealistically low in operation suggests a sensor or circuit fault. Unplugged EGRT after cooler service is a documented pattern — always inspect the EGRT connector after any recent cooler service.
Step 2 — Circuit Continuity Check

Check circuit continuity. Open signal conditions and connector corrosion producing below-normal readings are documented causes. Verify continuity through the EGRT sensor circuit. An open circuit confirms a harness or connector fault.
Step 3 — Sensor Resistance Checks
Check sensor resistance against OEM specification. A sensor resistance fault confirms a sensor failure. Compare to OEM specification at the measured temperature.
Step 4 — Evaluate Cooler Control Only After Sensing Proof

Evaluate cooler control only after sensing proof. A true overcooling event with correct sensor readings requires cooler control evaluation. Confirm sensor and circuit integrity before any cooler control diagnosis.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair connector or harness if open circuit is confirmed.
2 . Replace EGRT sensor if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
3 . Address cooler control if true overcooling is confirmed after sensing proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm EGRT readings are within specification after repair.
Verify SPN 412 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of below-normal EGR temperature events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect EGRT connector after any cooler service.
✓ Inspect EGRT harness for corrosion at every major service.
✓ Verify EGRT reading at cold soak at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Low to Medium Severity
Low to Medium. Below-normal EGR temp is usually sensing or circuit first.
symptoms: EGR temp low
EGRT sensor cold
EGR cooler overcooling
Efficiency monitor issues EGR temp
Stuck unrealistically low in operation

procedures_full.overview: SPN 412 FMI 5 indicates a problem with the turbocharger boost control circuit in Peterbilt trucks, often due to low current or open circuit, leading to reduced engine performance. The Peterbilt SPN 412 FMI 5 fault code is a critical alert concerning the turbocharger boost control. This issue arises when the current in the boost control circuit is below normal or there is an open circuit. Such a fault can significantly impact engine performance, leading to reduced power and efficiency. Understanding and addressing this fault promptly is crucial for maintaining optimal vehicle performance. Ignoring this warning can lead to further engine complications and increased operational costs. This guide will walk you through the symptoms, causes, and steps to diagnose and repair this issue effectively. The turbocharger is a vital component in a diesel engine, designed to improve efficiency and power output by forcing more air into the combustion chamber. When the boost control circuit fails, it disrupts this process, causing a cascade of performance issues. Addressing SPN 412 FMI 5 is not just about fixing a code; it's about ensuring your vehicle runs smoothly and reliably. By following the outlined diagnostic steps and understanding the potential causes, you can prevent further damage and maintain your engine's integrity.
causes: Damaged wiring or connectors

Wiring issues are prevalent and can lead to open circuits or low current. Regular inspection and maintenance can prevent these problems. Look for signs of wear, such as frayed wires or corroded connectors, especially in areas exposed to heat and vibration.
Faulty boost control solenoid
The solenoid may fail due to wear or manufacturing defects, affecting the boost control circuit's operation. Testing the solenoid's resistance and operation can confirm its condition.
ECM malfunction

An ECM fault can disrupt signals to the boost control system, though this is less common and typically requires advanced diagnostics. Reflashing or replacing the ECM might be necessary if faults are detected.
symptoms: Reduced engine power, noticeable during acceleration.
Turbo lag, causing delayed response from the engine.
Increased exhaust smoke, indicating inefficient combustion.
Possible engine derate, limiting vehicle speed and power.
Check Engine Light illuminated, alerting to the fault.
procedures_full.source_title: Peterbilt SPN 412 FMI 5: Turbo Boost Control Diagnosis and Repair

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the Driver Demanded Torque message over the Primary Data Link. The message is determined by a vehicle module based off of accelerator pedal position and other inputs. This information is used to determine transmission performance.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Driver Demanded Torque message. If the message is not available or in error, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: Driver Demanded Torque message not available for 5 seconds. FMI 19 – Received Network Data in Error: Driver Demanded Torque message received but in error for 5 second.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: Driver Demanded Torque message available and valid for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs Amber warning lamp on Lowest available start gear only Urge to Move and Creep mode prohibited Launch quality may degrade PTO mode prohibited Note: If the vehicle is moving: Red stop lamp on Clutch engagement prohibited, vehicle may coast to a stop Transmission downshifts to lowest available start gear Note: Vehicle fallback modes may vary. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: Driver Demanded Torque message available and valid for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: All FMIs: Vehicle Components Module(s) Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system.

steps.A:

field_evidence.title: 2014 Cascadia Evolution DT12 Transmission Code SPN 523 FMI 19 Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Cascadia Evolution equipped with the DT12 transmission can experience drivability issues linked to sensor faults and communication errors. One specific problem identified by technicians is the transmission code SPN 523 FMI 19. This code indicates a fault with the transmission output speed sensor in the DT12 system. Such a fault can stem from several factors related to the sensor and its associated components. To address SPN 523 FMI 19, it is important to check the sensor wiring harness for any signs of damage or corrosion that could disrupt signal transmission. Inspecting the sensor itself for debris or misalignment is also crucial. Often, cleaning or replacing the sensor can resolve the issue. Beyond the sensor, verifying the transmission control module connections is recommended

dd_procedures.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) is connected to the J1939 data link at the 38-Way Connector. This link transmits information to the HCM and communicates with other modules on the network such as the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

dd_procedures.title: ePTO Test
dd_procedures.overview: The ePTO feature allows the diesel engine to remain off for extended periods of time during PTO usage. The DC/DC Converter is energized only in ePTO mode so it can charge the 12-volt battery system. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) operates the Motor/Generator to power the transmission mounted PTO. If the high-voltage batteries are low, the HCM will start the engine with the Motor/Generator or the standard 12-volt system. To select the ePTO mode press the Mode button on the Push Button Shift Control. Some applications use a Chassis or Body Controller to control the PTO and send information to t

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 48 - J1939 Transmission Message Fault (HCM)
dd_procedures.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with a 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) is connected to the J1939 Data Link at the 38-Way Connector. The link is used to transmit information to the HCM as well as communicate or receive data from the other modules on the network like the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
causes: FMI 2, 9 J1939 Data Link TECU

dd_procedures.title: ePTO Test
dd_procedures.overview: The ePTO feature allows the diesel engine to remain off for extended periods of time during PTO usage. The DC/DC Converter is energized only in ePTO mode so it can charge the 12-volt battery system. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) operates the Motor/Generator to power the transmission mounted PTO. If the high-voltage batteries get low, the HCM starts the engine with the Motor/Generator or the standard 12-volt system. Select ePTO mode by pressing the Mode button on the Push Button Shift Control. Some applications use a Chassis or Body Controller to control the PTO and send information to the HC

B. Hidrolik kaldırıcının çalışmasını doğrulayın. Hidrolik kaldırıcıyı kumandaları kullanarak çalıştırın. Hidrolik kaldırıcı çalışıyorsa Adım C'ye gidin. Hidrolik kaldırıcı çalışmıyorsa Adım K'ye gidin.

C. Uygulamaya uygun çalışma süresini belirleyin ve PTO pompasının kapandığını doğrulayın. Hidrolik kaldırıcı kumandalarını bırakın ve aracı bekletin. D. Verify the State of Charge and verify that diesel engine turns on and shuts down. Operate the Hydraulic controls until the diesel engine turns on. Go to Step V If diesel engine never cycles on and PID 133 "Battery SOC" is less than 23%, concern with engine. The hybrid system will attempt to start the engine when the SOC goes below 23%. Continue to operate the hydraulic controls until the engine comes on. E. Confirm "Request Engine Run" signal is present at low State Of Charge. Connect ServiceRanger to the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector. If the PID 152 "Request Engine Run" reads 0 (No Request) and PID 133 "Battery SOC" is greater than 68%, contact Eaton at 1-800-826-HELP (4357). procedures_full.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) is connected to the J1939 data link at the 38-Way Connector. This link transmits information to the HCM and communicates with other modules on the network such as the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: HCM ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. J1939 data link communication fault is Inactive.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 9 is set when the HCM fails to receive TECU data for 30 consecutive messages or greater, while it continues communicating with other modules on J1939. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 48 is set the following conditions occur: Amber “Check Hybrid” light illuminates. Fault is stored in HCM memory. Red “Service” light may illuminate and a “F” may flash in the gear display due to an Active Fault Code 24. Operation mode changes to “AutoShift Only” mode. Electric Motor/Generator Assist and Regeneration are disabled; however, the high-voltage relays remain powered. If the fault sets at power up, the engine will not crank. If the fault sets while driving, the vehicle will shift; however, when the vehicle stops the clutch opens and remains in the open position. Transmission defaults start gear to 1st. procedures_full.overview: FMI 5 on the fan drive output indicates the ECM control circuit is open or not drawing expected current when the fan is commanded. Open control wire, failed fan clutch coil or control valve circuit, blown fuse, and unplugged fan connector are the primary causes. Connector fretting at the fan clutch from vibration and open circuit after radiator R&R are documented patterns. Replacing the fan clutch for a broken control wire is the primary wasted-cost pattern on this fault.
causes: Open control wire — open between ECM and fan clutch connector
Failed fan clutch coil or control valve circuit — internal open in fan clutch
Blown fuse — fuse in fan drive circuit
Unplugged fan connector — connector not reconnected after radiator R&R
Connector fretting — vibration-induced pin fretting at fan clutch connector
steps: Single Action Gate — Command Fan On with OEM Tool

Command the fan on with the OEM diagnostic tool if available. Observe whether the fan engages during the command. No engagement with a confirmed command confirms the circuit or clutch is not responding. This is the most efficient first step before any electrical measurements.
Binary Decision Gate — Check Power and Control at Connector

Verify power and control signal at the fan clutch connector during a fan-on command. No power at the connector confirms an open feed circuit or blown fuse. Power present but no control signal confirms an open control wire or ECM output fault.
Override Manager — Resistance Checks

Measure fan clutch coil or control valve circuit resistance versus OEM specification. Infinite resistance or OL at the fan clutch connector confirms an internal open in the fan clutch. A reading within specification confirms the fan clutch is not the open source.
Safety Interceptor — Connector Fretting Inspection

Inspect the fan clutch connector for fretting corrosion. Vibration-induced pin fretting at the fan clutch connector is a documented cause of intermittent open faults. Clean or replace fretting-damaged connectors before any fan clutch replacement.
Resume Point — Mechanical Fan Clutch Engagement Verification

Verify mechanical fan clutch engagement after circuit integrity is confirmed. A fan clutch that does not engage mechanically after the circuit is proven good confirms a mechanical clutch failure rather than a circuit fault.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Fan Engagement Confirmation
After repair, verify the fan engages during a fan-on command. Confirm overheat does not recur. Monitor for return of FMI 5 over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Connector, Harness, or Fan Clutch Decision

Repair connector fretting or open wire if circuit fault is found. Replace fan clutch only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation. Verify fan clutch engages mechanically after replacement.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Reconnect fan connector if found unplugged after radiator R&R.
2 . Repair connector fretting corrosion at fan clutch.
3 . Repair open control wire between ECM and fan clutch.
4 . Replace blown fuse in fan drive circuit.
5 . Replace fan clutch only after internal open is proven by circuit integrity confirmation.
Verification Steps
Confirm fan engages during fan-on command after repair.
Verify overheat does not recur after repair.
Confirm SPN 975 FMI 5 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of fan engagement fault over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify fan connector reconnection after every radiator R&R.
✓ Inspect fan clutch connector for fretting corrosion at every major service.
✓ Inspect fan drive circuit fuse at every major service.
✓ Address vibration sources near fan clutch connector to prevent fretting.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High in hot ambient and load Severity
High in hot ambient and load if fan cannot engage. Risk of true overheat. Fan drive open circuit is electrical proof first — do not replace fan clutch for a broken control wire.
symptoms: Fan drive circuit open fault active
Cooling fan not engaging
Overheat with fan code
Electronic fan control fault
Fan not responding to command

procedures_full.overview: FMI 7 on the fan drive indicates the ECM commanded fan engagement but the response — speed, cooling effect, or feedback — was not achieved. Failed fan clutch mechanically, oil loss in viscous clutch, seized bearing, control solenoid failure, and belt drive issues are the primary causes. A clutch that engages electrically but slips mechanically under load is a documented pattern. Confirming the control signal is reaching the fan clutch before mechanical condemnation prevents replacing a fan clutch for an electrical open that produces the same symptom.
causes: Failed fan clutch mechanically — internal mechanical failure
Oil loss in viscous clutch — viscous fluid loss reducing clutch engagement
Seized bearing — bearing failure preventing fan rotation
Control solenoid failure — solenoid not converting electrical command to mechanical engagement
Belt drive issues — belt slip or failure preventing fan drive
steps: Single Action Gate — Verify Control Signal During Command

Verify the control signal is reaching the fan clutch during a fan-on command. Confirm the electrical circuit is not the fault before mechanical condemnation. A confirmed control signal with no fan response confirms a mechanical clutch failure.
Binary Decision Gate — Observe Fan Response During Command

Observe fan response during a commanded fan-on event. Where fan speed sensors exist, compare commanded state versus fan speed PID. No speed change with a confirmed control signal confirms mechanical failure. A fan that partially engages but slips under load confirms viscous clutch wear.
Override Manager — Belt Condition Check
Check belt condition if the fan is belt-driven. A slipping or failed belt prevents fan engagement regardless of clutch condition. Inspect belt tension and condition before condemning the fan clutch.
Safety Interceptor — Viscous Clutch Oil Loss Assessment

Assess the viscous clutch for oil loss. A viscous clutch that has lost fluid engages electrically but slips mechanically under load. Inspect for oil leakage from the clutch body. A clutch with confirmed oil loss requires replacement.
Resume Point — Mechanical Slip Under Load Confirmation

If the fan engages at idle but slips under high-load conditions, the viscous clutch is worn. Confirm mechanical slip under load before clutch replacement — a clutch that appears to engage at idle may still be failing under load.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Fan Response Confirmation
After repair, verify the fan responds to commands and maintains engagement under load. Confirm overheat does not recur. Monitor for return of FMI 7 over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Fan Clutch or Belt Decision

Replace fan clutch when mechanical slip is proven after control signal confirmation. Replace belt or drive component if belt failure is confirmed. Verify fan engages and maintains speed under load after replacement.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace fan clutch when mechanical slip is proven after control signal confirmation.
2 . Replace belt or drive component if belt failure is confirmed.
3 . Replace viscous clutch if oil loss is confirmed.
4 . Verify fan engages and maintains speed under load after replacement.
Verification Steps
Confirm fan responds to commands and maintains engagement under load after repair.
Verify overheat does not recur after repair.
Confirm SPN 975 FMI 7 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of fan slip under high-load conditions after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect fan clutch for oil loss at every major service.
✓ Inspect belt condition and tension at every major service.
✓ Verify fan engagement under load at every major service on high-mileage engines.
✓ Address cooling system issues that cause chronic fan-on conditions accelerating clutch wear.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High under load and heat Severity
High under load and heat. Stop if temperatures climb severely. Electrical-versus-mechanical response split is the key gate — confirm control signal before condemning the clutch.
symptoms: Fan not responding fault active
Fan clutch slipping under load
No fan engagement during command
Overheating under load with fan code
Fan speed not increasing with command

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that there is a short to power.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that there is a short to power.‪
steps: Short to Power Check
Check for short to power as follows:‪
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11.5 volts, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "78.1.2.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, refer to "78.1.2 Voltage Check".
Voltage Check
The voltage check performed indicate that you should not be getting a code. The following is a recheck before requesting a new MCM.‪
Turn vehicle ignition OFF. Reconnect all connectors.
Turn ignition ON. Clear codes with diagnostic tool.
Start and run the engine for one minute. Stop engine.
Put the ignition switch in the OFF position
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11.5 volts, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "78.1.2.1 Verify Repairs".
Of the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center (313–592–5800) for authorization to replace the MCM.
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for open as follows:‪
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).

If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, go to step 5.

If the voltage is greater than 11.5, repair the open between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "78.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".

Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 – EGR Valve Fault Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 – EGR Valve Position Fault (Meaning & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 indicates an issue with EGR valve position. This code appears when the EGR valve is not responding correctly to commanded position signals.
Symptoms
Check engine light illuminated
Rough idle
Reduced fuel efficiency
Increased exhaust smoke
Possible aftertreatment warnings
Cause
This fault is commonly caused by a sticking EGR valve, carbon buildup, faulty actuator, wiring issues, or inaccurate position sensor readings.
Can You Keep Driving?
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR valve issues can lead to additional emissions faults and engine derate.
Recommended Action
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup and proper movement. Test actuator operation and verify sensor readings. Clean or replace faulty components as needed.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 2659 FMI 0 mean?
 
SPN 2659 FMI 0 indicates that the EGR valve position is not responding correctly to commanded signals from the engine control module.
 
 
What causes SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Common causes include carbon buildup, a sticking EGR valve, faulty actuator, damaged wiring, or a failed position sensor.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Driving may be possible temporarily, but unresolved EGR valve faults can lead to emissions issues and possible engine derate.
 
 
Will SPN 2659 FMI 0 cause reduced power?
 
Yes. Improper EGR valve operation can trigger engine protection strategies, including power reduction.
 
 
How do I fix SPN 2659 FMI 0?
 
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon buildup, test actuator movement, verify wiring integrity, and replace faulty components as needed.

SPN 3719 (DPF)
SPN 1569 (Derate)

causes: EGR cooler partially plugged with soot or cracked internally

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on EGR mass flow indicates the ECM's flow model calculates more EGR than commanded. The ECM uses multiple sensor inputs (MAP, MAF, delta-P as applicable) to estimate EGR flow — a skewed input can produce a false high flow calculation without any actual valve problem. True causes include a valve stuck open, actuator control fault commanding high, and sensor inputs skewed high. Carbon holding the valve off-seat after hot soak is a classic pattern on high-mileage engines. Replacing the EGR cooler early without proving valve seating and sensor inputs is the most common misdiagnosis path.
causes: Valve stuck open — carbon holding valve off-seat
Actuator control fault — commanding high position
Position sensor skewed high — false open reading
MAP/MAF/DP sensor inputs skewed — false flow calculation
Intermittent open-stick after hot soak — carbon release pattern
Cooler leak affecting control strategy on some platforms
steps: Single Action Gate — Desired vs Actual Position

Compare commanded EGR position to actual position feedback. If actual position is higher than commanded, the valve is not following commands — investigate mechanical seating and actuator control. If actual matches commanded but flow is still high, investigate sensor inputs used in the flow calculation.
Binary Decision Gate — Valve Seating Inspection

Remove and inspect EGR valve seating. Carbon deposits holding the valve off-seat are a classic cause of above-normal flow on high-mileage engines. Inspect after a hot soak to catch intermittent open-stick patterns.
Override Manager — Flow Calculation Sensor Validation

Validate all sensor inputs used in the EGR flow calculation — MAP, MAF, and delta-P as applicable for the platform. A skewed input produces a false high flow calculation without any actual valve problem.
Safety Interceptor — Actuator Control Circuit Check
Verify actuator control signal is not commanding high position. Check for position sensor short toward high reference that could cause the ECM to see a false open valve.
Resume Point — Hot Soak Retest
If fault is intermittent, retest after a hot soak. Carbon release patterns cause intermittent open-stick that may not be present during cold inspection.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Flow Confirmation
After repair, confirm EGR flow calculation returns to expected values for commanded position. Verify no above-normal flow faults return after a full drive cycle.
Repair Ledger Output — Valve or Sensor Decision

Replace or clean valve only after seating inspection confirms the problem. Correct sensor inputs only after flow calculation validation confirms the skewed input. Address cooler only with specific evidence of cooler contribution.

Repair Steps
1 . Clean EGR valve seating if carbon off-seat condition is found.
2 . Replace EGR valve if seating cannot be restored.
3 . Correct any skewed sensor inputs identified in flow calculation validation.
4 . Repair actuator control circuit faults if found.
5 . Address EGR cooler only with specific evidence of cooler contribution to the fault.
Verification Steps
Confirm EGR flow calculation returns to expected values after repair.
Verify valve actual position tracks commanded position correctly.
Confirm SPN 2659 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Monitor combustion stability and smoke output return to normal.
Preventative Measures
✓ Perform EGR valve cleaning per OEM service intervals.
✓ Address carbon buildup before it causes seating problems.
✓ Inspect EGR valve seating at every major EGR system service.
✓ Maintain sensor calibration for MAP, MAF, and delta-P inputs.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High if driveability is unstable. Excess EGR causes rough idle, black smoke, and power loss. DPF soot loading accelerates with excess EGR. Address before extended operation.

Over-EGR condition
Black smoke under acceleration
Rough idle from excess EGR
Power loss from excess recirculation

procedures_full.overview: SPN 2659 FMI 7 means the wastegate actuator did not respond to ECM commands. Inspect linkage binding and run a sweep test before replacing the actuator or turbo. Kenworth T680 and W900 operators feel SPN 2659 FMI 7 as lazy boost recovery long before the check engine light tells the whole story. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com tracks this code to carbon-frozen wastegate arms on high-mileage MX engines more often than failed turbochargers.
causes: Carbon-bound wastegate linkage or valve seat
Soot buildup prevents the valve from opening or closing fully even when the actuator motor is healthy.
Failed wastegate actuator motor or internal gearbox
The actuator stalls mid-travel and cannot match ECM position commands during boost transitions.
Low supply voltage or poor ground at actuator connector
Voltage drop under load reduces actuator force enough to set FMI 7 without a mechanical jam.
steps: Read active faults and perform a wastegate actuator sweep test in PACCAR Davie4 or Noregon JPRO with engine off and key on.
Inspect the wastegate linkage at the turbo for carbon binding, bent rods, or a disconnected clip at the actuator arm.
Apply 12 V briefly to the actuator per service procedure and confirm full travel without grinding or stall mid-stroke.
Check supply voltage at the actuator connector during command: many PACCAR setups require 12.4-14.2 V under load; low voltage mimics mechanical FMI 7.
If linkage moves freely but commanded vs actual error exceeds 10%, replace the wastegate actuator and recalibrate per MX-13 service manual torque and stroke specs.
symptoms: Check engine lamp with reduced boost on the dash gauge during acceleration
Audible wastegate flutter, boost spikes, or loss of power climbing grades
High exhaust gas temperature warnings under steady cruise load
SPN 2659 FMI 7 active alongside SPN 646 or SPN 1188 companion codes
Actuator fails commanded vs actual position test in PACCAR Davie4
