procedures_full.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The HCM is connected to the J1939 data link at the 38-Way Connector. This link is used to transmit information to the HCM and communicate with the other modules on the network such as the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) module.
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: HCM ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. J1939 data link communication fault is Inactive.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 9 is set when the HCM fails to receive ABS message “Anti-Lock Braking Active” for 30 consecutive messages or greater, while it continues communicating with other modules on J1939. FMI 14 is set when the HCM detects messages coming from the ABS module; however, the “Anti-Locking Braking Active” message is received as an error or not available. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 47 is set the following conditions occur: Amber “Check Hybrid” light illuminates. Fault is stored in HCM memory. If the fault occurs while moving, the operation goes into AutoShift Only mode. Electric Motor/Generator Assist and Regeneration are disabled; however, the high-voltage relays remain powered. Transmission defaults start gear to 1st. Note: If the vehicle experiences an ABS event, the hybrid regenerative braking is stopped until ABS communication continues, but the vehicle will still have motor assist. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.possible_causes: This fault code can be caused by any of the following: FMI 9 J1939 Data Link ABS Module FMI 14 ABS module configured to communicate on J1708 or analog instead of J1939. ABS Module

steps.A:
A. Verify Active and Inactive fault code status and present FMIs. 
 Retrieve the Active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector. 
 Which FMIs are present? 
 If Fault Code 47 FMI 9 is listed, concern is either with the ABS Module or the J1939 Data Link from ABS Module to J1939 Data Link Backbone. Refer to OEM for repair procedures. 
 If Fault Code 47 FMI 14 is listed, concern is with the ABS Module being configured for J1708 instead of J1939 communication, or with the ABS Module. Refer to OEM for repair procedures.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 22 - J1939 ABS Message Fault
procedures_full.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The HCM is connected to the J1939 Data Link at the 38-Way Connector. This link is used to transmit information to the HCM as well as communicate or receive data from the other modules on the network like the ABS module.
procedures_full.detection: Fault is detected when: HCM ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. J1939 Data Link communication fault is not Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions may set the fault Active: FMI 9 is set when the HCM fails to receive ABS messages and there are no Active J1939 faults. In PDM mode (FMI 2) this fault is set if 3 consecutive messages (EBC1) are not received. FMI 14 is set when the HCM receives an Active ABS signal (SPN563) out of range or the ABS “Fully Operational Signal” (SPN1243) is not present for 1 second. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 22 is set the following conditions occur: Amber “Check Hybrid” light displays. Fault is stored in HCM memory. If the fault occurs while moving, the operation mode goes into AutoShift only. Electric motor/generator Assist and Regeneration are disabled; however, the high-voltage relays remain powered. Transmission defaults start gear to 1st.

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault code status. 
 Retrieve the Active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector. 
 Which FMIs are present? 
 If Fault Code 22 FMI 9 is listed, problem is with the Data Link Backbone ABS Module or with the J1939 Data Link from ABS Module to J1939. Refer to OEM for repair procedures. 
 If Fault Code 22 FMI 14 is listed, problem is with the Data Link ABS Module being configured for J1708 instead of J1939 communication, and/or with the ABS Module itself. Refer to OEM for repair procedures.

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that there is a short to power.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that there is a short to power.‪
steps: Short to Power Check
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key On, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11.5 volts, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "81.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, replace the fan control solenoid. Refer to "81.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 81.1 SPN 1071/FMI 3 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This fault indicates that there is a short to ground.‪
causes: This fault indicates that there is a short to ground.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the fan control solenoid.
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid and ground.
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "81.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 2 of the fan control solenoid and pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "81.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 81.2 SPN 1071/FMI 4 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for multiple codes.
If SPN 647/5, SPN 1072/5 and SPN 1071/5 are active repair the open in between the pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector and the fan and the Jake Brake solenoids. Refer to "81.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If only SPN 1071/5 is active, go to step 2.
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key On, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 and 2 of the fan control solenoid connector.
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, go to step 5.
If the voltage is between 11.5 and 13.5 volts, replace the fan control solenoid. Refer to "81.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the voltage between pin 2 of the fan control solenoid connector and ground.
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, repair the open between pin 2 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "81.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is greater than 11.5, repair the open between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 33 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "81.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on CAC outlet temperature indicates the sensor reports above the maximum calibrated limit. Debris-packed CAC, internal restriction, missing air seals recirculating engine heat, high ambient combined with high load, and sensor bias are the primary causes. Vocational trucks with packed coolers and aftermarket bug screens blocking airflow are documented patterns. An IR comparison at the sensor boss versus scan data is the most efficient first step to separate sensor bias from true high charge temperature.
causes: Debris-packed CAC — external fins blocked by debris
Internal restriction — internal CAC restriction reducing airflow
Missing air seals — recirculating hot engine bay air
High ambient plus high load — thermal accumulation
Sensor bias high — thermistor reading above actual temperature
Aftermarket bug screens — blocking CAC airflow
steps: Single Action Gate — IR Comparison at Sensor Boss

Compare CAC outlet temperature scan data to an infrared measurement at the sensor boss. A large offset between scan data and IR measurement supports sensor bias. A reading that correlates with IR measurement supports true high charge temperature.
Binary Decision Gate — Visual Cooler Package Inspection

Inspect the CAC external fins for debris packing. Vocational trucks and trucks operating in debris-heavy environments are prone to packed coolers. Inspect for aftermarket bug screens blocking airflow.
Override Manager — Duct Seal Verification
Inspect air seals between the CAC and the intake manifold. Missing seals allow hot engine bay air to recirculate into the intake, elevating charge temperature without any CAC efficiency loss.
Safety Interceptor — Clean External Fins and Retest

Clean external CAC fins and retest under load. If charge temperature returns to normal after cleaning, debris packing was the cause. If charge temperature remains elevated after cleaning, proceed to internal restriction and sensor evaluation.
Resume Point — Load Retest
Retest under hard-pull conditions after cleaning and seal repair. True CAC efficiency loss produces elevated charge temperatures under high load that may not be apparent at idle.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation
After repair, verify CAC outlet temperature remains within OEM specification under high ambient and high load conditions.
Repair Ledger Output — Clean, Seal, or Replace Decision

Clean CAC if debris packing is the cause. Repair or replace missing air seals. Replace CAC if internal restriction or damage is confirmed after cleaning. Replace sensor if bias is confirmed after CAC and seal integrity are proven.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Clean external CAC fins if debris packing is found.
2 . Remove aftermarket bug screens blocking CAC airflow.
3 . Repair or replace missing air seals between CAC and intake manifold.
4 . Replace CAC if internal restriction or damage is confirmed after cleaning.
5 . Replace sensor if bias is confirmed after CAC and seal integrity are proven.
Verification Steps
Confirm CAC outlet temperature remains within OEM specification under high ambient and load after repair.
Verify derate does not activate after repair.
Confirm SPN 2630 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of power loss under high ambient conditions.
Preventative Measures
✓ Clean CAC external fins at every major service.
✓ Inspect air seals between CAC and intake manifold at every major service.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on CAC outlet temperature indicates the sensor reports below the minimum expected temperature for conditions. Sensor bias cold, open circuit, extremely cold ambient with sensor at the edge of calibration, and airflow sensor placement issues are the primary causes. A sensor left unplugged after CAC service is a documented cause. If the CAC outlet temperature is stuck unrealistically low during operation when the engine is fully warmed, the sensor or circuit is the fault — not the CAC assembly.
causes: Sensor bias cold — thermistor failure producing cold bias
Open circuit — open signal or ground producing cold bias
Extremely cold ambient — sensor at edge of calibration in extreme cold
Airflow sensor placement issues — sensor not in representative airflow
Sensor left unplugged after CAC service
steps: Single Action Gate — Ambient Correlation Check

Compare CAC outlet temperature to ambient temperature at cold soak. CAC outlet temperature should be near ambient at cold soak. If stuck significantly below ambient at cold soak, the sensor or circuit is biased cold.
Binary Decision Gate — Sensor Connection Verification
Verify the sensor is connected and properly seated. A sensor left unplugged after CAC service produces a cold bias. Inspect the sensor connector for proper engagement and pin condition.
Override Manager — Harness Continuity Check
Perform continuity test on the CAC outlet temperature sensor circuit. An open signal or ground produces a cold bias reading. Inspect connector for corrosion.
Safety Interceptor — Operating Temperature Rise Assessment
If cold-soak reading is near ambient but temperature never rises during operation, the sensor is stuck. This confirms sensor failure rather than a circuit fault.
Resume Point — Extreme Cold Assessment

In extreme cold ambient conditions, verify the fault is not at the edge of the calibrated range. Some platforms have calibrated windows that produce faults at extreme cold ambient without any sensor failure.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation
After repair, verify CAC outlet temperature rises appropriately during operation and correlates with ambient at cold soak.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor or Harness Decision
Replace sensor after circuit integrity is confirmed and sensor failure is proven. Repair harness if open circuit or corrosion is found. Do not replace CAC assembly for a sensing fault.

Verify temperature rises appropriately during operation.
Confirm SPN 2630 FMI 1 does not return after repair.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 2630 FMI 2 indicates CAC outlet temperature signal erratic or implausible. Failing sensor, intermittent harness, connector fretting, and moisture intrusion are the primary causes. Intermittent derates from unstable charge-temp inputs are a documented pattern. Replacing the CAC or charge-air system components for a sensor or harness fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Failing sensor — failing CAC outlet temperature sensor producing unstable readings
Intermittent harness — intermittent harness producing unstable signal
Connector fretting — connector fretting at charge pipe or CAC outlet producing intermittent signal
Moisture intrusion — moisture intrusion producing short circuit
steps: Step 1 — Wiggle Test

Perform a wiggle test on the sensor connector and harness. Monitor the CAC outlet temperature PID while wiggling the harness. A PID dropout during the wiggle test confirms a harness intermittent. Inspect the sensor connector on the charge pipe and CAC outlet for chafe at clamps.
Step 2 — Continuity Check
Check continuity through the sensor circuit. Verify continuity and compare against IAT and ambient plausibility. A continuity fault confirms a harness or connector fault.
Step 3 — Sensor Replace After Proof

Replace the sensor after proof of sensor failure. Confirm the harness and connector are clean before sensor replacement. A sensor replaced without proof may replace a good sensor into a harness fault.
Step 4 — CAC Efficiency Evaluation Only If Values Are Stable But High

Evaluate CAC efficiency only if values are stable but high. A stable but high CAC outlet temperature confirms a true thermal event that requires CAC efficiency evaluation. A CAC efficiency evaluation performed before sensing proof may miss a sensing fault.

Verify SPN 2630 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm no intermittent derate from charge temp after repair.
Monitor for return of erratic CAC outlet temperature events over extended operation.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 4353 FMI 18 - DEF Injection Quantity Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 – DEF Injection Quantity Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 indicates that the amount of DEF being injected into the exhaust stream is below the quantity required by the ECM to properly reduce NOx emissions. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and points to a problem within the DEF delivery system that will affect SCR performance and can trigger a derate condition if not resolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition possible 
Reduced SCR system efficiency 
May appear alongside other DEF dosing or pump related codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM determines that the actual DEF injection quantity is less than the commanded amount. Common causes include:
Worn or failing DEF pump not delivering adequate flow 
Clogged or partially blocked DEF dosing injector 
Low DEF level in tank Restricted DEF supply lines 
Faulty DEF metering valve Air in the DEF supply system 
DEF filter clogged restricting flow to injector
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but with insufficient DEF injection the SCR system cannot properly control NOx emissions. The engine will enter a derate condition if the delivery shortfall is not corrected. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking DEF tank level and refilling if low. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if clogged. Check DEF supply lines for restrictions or air ingestion points. If level and filter are good have the DEF pump output and dosing injector tested as wear or partial blockage in either component is a common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4353 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF system is injecting less fluid into the exhaust than the ECM requires to properly reduce NOx emissions through the SCR catalyst.
 
 
What causes SPN 4353 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a worn DEF pump, a partially clogged dosing injector, low DEF level, a clogged DEF filter, or restricted supply lines.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4353 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but insufficient DEF injection will cause SCR efficiency to drop and a derate condition will follow if not addressed.
 
 
Will SPN 4353 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. When DEF injection quantity falls below required levels the SCR system cannot meet emissions thresholds and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4353 FMI 18?
 
Check DEF level and filter first then inspect the dosing injector and pump for wear or blockage. Once the system confirms DEF is being delivered at the correct quantity the code should clear.

SPN 4094 FMI 18 
SPN 3362 FMI 1

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 100 FMI 1 – Oil Pressure Low Fix
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 – DEF Doser Valve Current Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 indicates that the electrical current to the DEF doser valve is below the expected threshold. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and points to an electrical fault in the DEF dosing circuit that is preventing the doser valve from operating correctly, which will affect SCR system performance and can lead to a derate condition.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition possible 
DEF dosing system not functioning correctly 
May appear alongside other doser valve or DEF system codes
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects lower than expected current draw from the DEF doser valve circuit. Common causes include:
Open circuit in the doser valve wiring harness 
Damaged or corroded doser valve connector 
Failed doser valve solenoid with low resistance 
Broken wire between ECM and doser valve 
Water intrusion in the doser valve connector 
Faulty ECM output driver for the doser valve circuit
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving may be possible but without proper electrical function the DEF doser valve cannot operate correctly and the SCR system will be unable to control DEF delivery. A derate condition is likely if the fault is not resolved promptly.
Recommended Action
Inspect the DEF doser valve wiring harness and connector for damage, corrosion, or broken wires. Check for water intrusion at the connector. Test the doser valve solenoid resistance against specification. If wiring and connector are intact and the solenoid tests good have the ECM output circuit evaluated by a qualified technician.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4374 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the electrical current to the DEF doser valve is below the expected level, indicating an electrical fault in the dosing circuit that prevents proper valve operation.
 
 
What causes SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are an open circuit or broken wire in the doser valve harness, a corroded connector, water intrusion at the connector, or a failed doser valve solenoid.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but without correct electrical supply the doser valve cannot function and the SCR system will be compromised, leading to a likely derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 4374 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If the doser valve cannot operate due to low current the SCR system will be unable to deliver DEF correctly and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4374 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and repair the doser valve wiring and connector. Test the solenoid and replace the valve if faulty. Once the ECM confirms correct current draw to the doser valve the code should clear.

SPN_5018.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on DOC efficiency indicates the DOC is not performing at the expected oxidation efficiency level. Contaminated or damaged DOC, EGT sensor bias, regen fueling issues, upstream combustion problems, and exhaust leaks are the primary causes. DOC condemned when the outlet EGT sensor was failed is a documented pattern — a failed outlet EGT sensor produces a flat temperature response that appears as DOC failure without any actual catalyst problem. Temperature-correlation gate before DOC replacement prevents this misdiagnosis.
causes: Contaminated or damaged DOC — DOC contamination or substrate damage
EGT sensor bias — outlet EGT sensor reading below actual temperature
Regen fueling issues — regen fueling not enabling or insufficient
Upstream combustion problems — upstream combustion issues reducing DOC inlet temperature
Exhaust leaks — exhaust leak reducing DOC inlet temperature
steps: Single Action Gate — Correlate DOC Inlet and Outlet EGTs

Correlate DOC inlet and outlet EGT readings during regen. A flat temperature response across the DOC during regen with good fueling supports DOC or sensing issues. A DOC inlet EGT that is rising with a flat outlet EGT confirms outlet EGT sensor failure or exhaust leak near the outlet sensor.
Binary Decision Gate — Verify Regen Fueling Enable

Verify regen fueling is enabled and sufficient. A DOC that does not receive adequate regen fueling cannot reach light-off temperature regardless of catalyst condition. Confirm regen fueling enable conditions are met and fueling quantity is within specification.
Override Manager — Inspect for Exhaust Leaks

Inspect for exhaust leaks near the DOC and EGT sensors. An exhaust leak near the DOC outlet EGT sensor reduces the measured temperature below the actual DOC outlet temperature. Inspect exhaust connections, gaskets, and sensor bosses for leaks.
Safety Interceptor — EGT Circuit Checks

Perform EGT circuit checks on the DOC inlet and outlet sensors. A failed outlet EGT sensor produces a flat temperature response that appears as DOC failure. Verify sensor circuit integrity before any DOC hardware decision.
Resume Point — DOC Assessment After Sensing and Fueling Proof

Assess DOC condition only after sensing and fueling integrity are confirmed. A DOC with confirmed sensing and fueling integrity that still shows flat temperature response confirms DOC contamination or damage. Inspect DOC for physical damage and contamination.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Rise Confirmation
After repair, verify DOC temperature rise meets OEM specification during regen. Confirm regen completes successfully. Monitor for return of DOC efficiency faults over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor, Fueling, or DOC Decision

Replace EGT sensor if bias or circuit fault is confirmed. Repair regen fueling fault if confirmed. Repair exhaust leak if confirmed. Replace DOC only after sensing and fueling integrity are confirmed and DOC failure is proven.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 5018 FMI 18 indicates DOC oxidation or light-off efficiency below expected. Contaminated or damaged DOC, EGT sensor bias, regen fueling issues, exhaust leaks, and upstream combustion problems are the primary causes. DOC replaced when the outlet EGT sensor was failed is a documented pattern. Replacing the DOC before proving EGT sensor integrity and regen fueling is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Contaminated or damaged DOC — contaminated or damaged DOC producing below-normal efficiency
EGT sensor bias — EGT sensor bias producing false efficiency reading
Regen fueling issues — regen fueling issues preventing DOC light-off
Exhaust leaks — exhaust leaks producing false temperature differential
Upstream combustion problems — upstream combustion problems producing insufficient DOC inlet temperature
steps: Step 1 — Correlate DOC Inlet and Outlet EGTs

Correlate DOC inlet and outlet EGT sensors during regen. Evaluate temperature rise across the DOC during regen. DOC replaced when the outlet EGT sensor was failed is a documented pattern. A flat response with proven fueling supports a DOC or sensing issue. Confirm both EGT sensors are reading correctly before any DOC assessment.
Step 2 — Verify Regen Fueling Enable

Verify regen fueling enable. Confirm regen fueling is enabled and commanded correctly. A regen fueling issue preventing DOC light-off requires fueling diagnosis. Verify the regen fueling command and actual fueling quantity.
Step 3 — Inspect Exhaust Leaks

Inspect for exhaust leaks. Exhaust leaks producing a false temperature differential are a documented cause. Inspect the exhaust system between the DOC inlet and outlet EGT sensors for leaks. An exhaust leak producing a false temperature differential requires exhaust repair.
Step 4 — DOC Decision Last

Make the DOC replacement decision last. Confirm EGT sensor integrity, regen fueling, and exhaust leak integrity before any DOC replacement. A DOC replaced without proving EGT and fueling may replace a good catalyst into a sensing or fueling fault.

2 . Repair regen fueling if fueling fault is confirmed.
3 . Repair exhaust leak if confirmed.
4 . Replace DOC if contamination or damage is confirmed after EGT and fueling proof.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 5357 FMI 0 means multiple cylinders on an International A26 are receiving more fuel than commanded. It's a High severity fault - check shared rail pressure before assuming individual injectors have failed. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats multi-cylinder fuel quantity codes the same way we treat multi-cylinder misfire codes - look at what's shared across those cylinders before isolating down to any single injector.
causes: Fuel rail pressure running above commanded target
A mechanical/hydraulic fault affecting the shared rail - excess pressure pushes more fuel through every injector on that circuit simultaneously.
Stuck-open fuel pressure regulator or relief valve
A mechanical component failure that directly causes the rail overpressure driving multi-cylinder over-fueling.
Worn injectors on specific cylinders allowing excess flow
A genuine mechanical wear issue isolated to particular injectors rather than a shared rail problem.
Fuel pressure sensor circuit fault causing incorrect ECM fueling commands
An electrical/sensor issue where inaccurate pressure feedback causes the ECM to over-command fuel delivery.
steps: Pull the full fault list with a scan tool to see which specific cylinders show fuel quantity errors alongside this multi-cylinder code.
Check fuel rail pressure in live data - pressure running above commanded target can cause multiple injectors to deliver more fuel than intended simultaneously.
Inspect for a stuck-open fuel pressure regulator or relief valve, since this affects fuel delivery to all cylinders on the shared rail.
Run individual injector flow or balance tests to see if the over-fueling clusters on specific cylinders or is spread evenly across the bank.
If pressure is confirmed normal but specific injectors are over-fueling, those individual injectors likely have worn internal components allowing excess fuel through.
symptoms: Rough idle with a noticeable shake through the cab
Excessive black or white smoke depending on which cylinders are over-fueling
Reduced fuel economy despite normal driving habits
Check engine light, sometimes with individual cylinder trim codes alongside it

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on secondary fuel level indicates the secondary tank level is below the normal threshold. True low secondary tank, failed secondary sender, transfer pump failure, clogged transfer lines or valves, and control switch faults are the primary causes. Transfer pump failures misdiagnosed as primary supply pump issues are a documented pattern on dual-tank systems. Dual-tank logic prevents wrong-tank and wrong-pump repairs by evaluating the transfer system before any pump diagnosis.
causes: True low secondary tank — secondary tank genuinely low from consumption or transfer failure
Failed secondary sender — secondary fuel level sender failure
Transfer pump failure — transfer pump not moving fuel from secondary to primary
Clogged transfer lines or valves — restriction in transfer path
Control switch faults — transfer control switch fault preventing transfer
steps: Single Action Gate — Physical Levels in Both Tanks

Verify physical fuel levels in both the primary and secondary tanks. Physical level proof in both tanks identifies whether the secondary tank is genuinely low or the sender is reading incorrectly. A secondary tank that is confirmed full with a low reading confirms a sender or wiring fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Command and Observe Transfer

Command the transfer system and observe transfer operation. A transfer system that does not move fuel when commanded confirms a transfer pump, line, or valve fault. A transfer system that moves fuel confirms the transfer path is functional.
Override Manager — Voltage at Transfer Pump

Verify voltage at the transfer pump when commanded. No voltage at the transfer pump confirms a control circuit fault — switch, relay, or wiring. Voltage present with no transfer pump operation confirms a failed transfer pump.
Safety Interceptor — Line Restriction Checks

Inspect transfer lines and valves for restriction or blockage. A clogged transfer line or valve prevents fuel transfer even when the pump is operating. Inspect transfer lines, check valves, and selector valves for restriction.
Resume Point — Secondary Sender Tests

Perform secondary sender tests if the physical level and transfer system are confirmed normal but the level reading remains low. Inspect the secondary sender connector and ground integrity. Perform sender resistance sweep where applicable.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Level and Transfer Confirmation

After repair, verify secondary tank level reads correctly and transfer system operates normally. Confirm SPN 38 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of secondary level faults over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Refuel, Transfer System, or Sender Decision

Refuel secondary tank if true low volume is confirmed. Repair transfer pump, lines, or valve if transfer fault is confirmed. Repair control circuit if switch or relay fault is confirmed. Replace secondary sender if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Refuel secondary tank if true low volume is confirmed.
2 . Replace transfer pump if pump failure is confirmed.
3 . Repair transfer lines or valve if restriction is confirmed.
4 . Repair control circuit if switch or relay fault is confirmed.
5 . Replace secondary sender if failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm secondary tank level reads correctly after repair.
Verify transfer system operates normally after repair.
Confirm SPN 38 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of secondary level faults over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Test transfer system operation at every major service.
✓ Inspect transfer lines and valves for restriction at every major service.
✓ Inspect secondary sender connector and ground at every major service.
✓ Monitor secondary tank level before every dispatch on dual-tank trucks.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High if transfer fails and primary runs dry. Dual-tank logic prevents wrong-tank and wrong-pump repairs.
symptoms: SPN 38 FMI 1 secondary fuel level low
Right tank empty or low
Dual tank level fault
Transfer system not working
Secondary fuel level low warning

If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the vehicle’s Service Brake Switch message over the vehicle J1939 Data Link. This information is used to determine transmission operation.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Service Brake Switch message. If the message is not received or invalid, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: Service Brake Switch message not received for 10 seconds. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: Service Brake Switch message not available for 10 seconds. FMI 19 – Received Network Data in Error: Service Brake Switch message invalid for 10 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: Service Brake Switch message continuously indicates “Depressed” during acceleration.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 9, 13, 19: Valid Service Brake Switch message received for 10 seconds. FMI 20: Service Brake Switch message indicates “released”.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system. Brake system fallback modes may vary. Amber warning lamp on PTO Mode prohibited Creep Mode prohibited Transmission may not allow a shift out of Neutral Note: If powered down in gear and Fault Code 160 is Active, engine may not crank. Apply Parking Brake to crank engine. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 9, 13, 19: Valid Service Brake Switch message received for 10 seconds. FMI 20: Service Brake Switch message indicates “released”.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 9, 13, 19: Vehicle Components Service Brake Switch and/or associated wiring Other Vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) Internal failure Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system. FMI 20: Driver Induced Brake pedal continuously depressed while accelerating (two foot) Brake Pedal Linkage Obstruction or binding causing brake pedal to stay depressed Vehicle Components Service Brake Switch and/or associated wiring Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system.

steps.V:

procedures_full.overview: The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) normally commands the different gears shifts which are done through the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The HCM also controls the Electric Clutch Actuator (ECA), which changes the position of the Clutch. Note: This symptom-based test should only be performed if you were sent here from the Diagnostic Procedure and you have no active fault codes. Transmission will not engage a gear from Neutral and warning tone sounds (Solid “N” in Gear Display). Transmission will not engage a gear from Neutral (Flashing Gear in Gear Display). This symptom is addressed in the Front Box Symptom Test. Transmission will not move from a stop (Solid Gear number in Gear Display).
procedures_full.detection: The following symptoms may have been experienced: Transmission does not engage a gear from neutral and warning tone sounds (solid “N” in gear display). Transmission does not engage a gear from neutral (flashing gear in gear display). This symptom is addressed in the Front Box symptom test. Transmission does not move from a stop (solid gear number in gear display).
procedures_full.fallback: No fallback condition exists for this symptom.

steps.A:
A. Visually observe the gear display after power-up. 
 You should only perform this symptom test if you were sent here from the Diagnostic Procedure and you have no Active fault codes. 
 Depress “N” on the Push Button Shift Control: 
 If “N” is present on the Gear Display, Go to Step B 
 If “N” is not present on the Gear Display, refer to the Diagnostic Procedure for the correct symptom based test to perform.
steps.B:
B. Visually observe the gear display when placing the transmission into Drive. 
 Key on. 
 Start engine. 
 Depress Service Brake and select "D." 
 If gear display shows a “N” and a warning tone sounds, Go to Step D 
 If Gear Display shows a flashing gear with no arrows, go to Front Box Test . 
 If Gear Display shows a solid gear, but vehicle will not move, Go to Step C
steps.C:
C. Confirm the proper parameter configuration to prohibit driving. 
 Key on. 
 Connect ServiceRanger and view the following Data Monitor parameter PID 154 “Prohibit Driving”: 
 “Prohibit Driving” reads 0 (Allow Driving) 
 Contact Eaton at 1-800-826-HELP [4357] 
 “Prohibit Driving” reads 1 (Prohibit Driving) 
 Ensure boom and outriggers are fully retracted. Contact your OEM for repair procedures, Go to Step V 
 Parameter Reading 
 PID 154 “Prohibit Driving”
steps.D:
D. Verify proper brake status signal. 
 Key on. 
 View the following Data Monitor parameter while depressing the service brake: 
 SPN 597 “Service Brake Status” 
 If the Service Brake Switch status is depressed when you apply the brakes, contact Eaton at 1-800-826-HELP [4357]. 
 If the Service Brake Switch does not change status, repair Service Brake Wiring or Switch. Contact your OEM for repair procedures, Go to Step V 
 Parameter Reading 
 SPN 597 “Service Brake Status”
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors. 
 Place Shift Control into neutral. 
 Key on: 
 If the Transmission will engage a gear and move from a stop, test is complete. 
 If the Transmission will not engage a gear or move from a stop, find error in testing, Go to Step A

causes: This fault is typically the J1939 Cruise Control Coast Switch signal from Source #1, #2, or #3 is missing.‪
steps: Missing Cruise Control Coast Switch Signal from Source #1, #2, or #3 Check
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, repair the CAN line faults.
If only a “J1939 Error” fault is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, check the proper configuration of the CPC.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.

causes: This fault is typically J1939 Cruise Control Coast Switch signal from Source #1, #2, or #3 is erratic.‪
steps: Erratic Cruise Control Coast Switch Signal from Source #1 Check
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot and repair these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, troubleshoot and repair the CAN line.
If only a “J1939 Error” fault is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, check the proper configuration of the CPC.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.

field_evidence.title: 2009 Freightliner Cascadia Intake Air Pressure Sensor Code SPN 3563 FMI 4
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2009 Freightliner Cascadia frequently experiences issues related to the intake air pressure sensor, which can lead to engine performance problems. One common diagnostic code encountered is SPN 3563 FMI 4, which specifically points to a low or shorted voltage condition from the Engine Intake Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor. This sensor code can stem from several underlying causes. Damage or corrosion in the MAP sensor wiring harness may disrupt voltage signals. Additionally, leaks in the intake manifold can alter sensor accuracy, contributing to faults. Voltage irregularities detected on the sensor output are often an indicator of these issues. To address Code SPN 3563 FMI 4, it is advisable to inspect the MAP sensor wiring harness thoroughly for any signs of wear or corrosion.

field_evidence.title: 2013 Freightliner Cascadia SPN 679-FMI 7 Pressure Valve Issue
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 Freightliner Cascadia is known to experience pressure limiting valve failures, particularly indicated by the diagnostic code SPN 679-FMI 7. This fault code signals that the pressure limiting valve is failing to close properly, which can result in a noticeable loss of power once the engine warms up. This issue in Cascadia models often stems from the valve's inability to regulate pressure as expected. However, replacing the valve alone does not always resolve the problem. Additional factors may contribute, such as potential faults within the electronic control module (ECM), wiring harness problems, or issues in the transmission control system and hydraulic pressure sensors. field_evidence.title: 2014 Freightliner Cascadia DD15 SPN 70 FMI 19 Engine Code Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2014 Freightliner Cascadia equipped with the DD15 engine may display the SPN 70 FMI 19 engine code, which relates to a turbocharger boost pressure fault. This problem is commonly associated with issues affecting the engine's turbocharger system. Such turbocharger boost pressure faults can stem from several causes. Notably, a faulty Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor may trigger this code. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 23: Urge to Move Brake Switch Signal
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be configured with the Urge to Move (UTM) feature. If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

Service brake released, monitor ServiceRanger and record “Brake pedal position” value in table. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 140: EBS Brake Switch
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the vehicle’s Electronic Braking System (EBS) Brake Switch message from a vehicle Electronic Control Unit (ECU) over the Primary Data Link (J1939A). This information is used to determine vehicle state.
causes: Vehicle Components - Vehicle ECU(s) Vehicle EBS Brake Switch J1939 message not enabled Other vehicle ECU(s) faulted Vehicle Harness - Primary Data Link (J1939A) Shorted to power, shorted to ground or open circuit Terminals bent, spread, corroded, or loose Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system. Additional Tools None
steps: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 140 is Inactive and there are other Active vehicle or transmission fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes. Go to Step V If Fault Code 140 FMI 13 is Active, refer to OEM and enable vehicle EBS Brake Switch message (SPN 1121). Go to Step V If Fault Code 140 FMI 13 is Inactive, Go to Step V . If Fault Code 140 FMI 19 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B

B. Monitor vehicle EBS Brake Switch signal message. Key on with engine running. Allow air pressure to build to governor cut off. Key off. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To “Data Monitor”. Select “Status”. Select “EBS brake switch”. Select all of the “- 1121” SPN sources. Note: Not all sources will indicate a value. Monitor 1121 - EBS brake switch value. Record reading in table. Depress and hold service brake. Release vehicle parking brake. Monitor 1121 - EBS brake switch value. Record reading in table. Set vehicle parking brake. Compare reading(s) in table. If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair of the vehicle EBS Brake Switch signal message (SPN 1121). Go to Step V If readings are in range, no fault was found. The intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is in the vehicle EBS Brake Switch signal message (SPN 1121). Contact OEM for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V EBS Brake State Parameter Range Reading(s) Set 1121-EBS brake switch Set Released 1121-EBS brake switch Not set

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 140 sets Active, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 140 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

dd_procedures.title: Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 - DPF Soot Load High
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated soot beyond the moderate high threshold and requires regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a step above a routine regen request — if regeneration is not completed promptly the engine will enter a derate condition and the DPF may require forced regeneration or service.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regen inhibited or unable to complete 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible 
Exhaust back pressure increased
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates soot accumulation in the DPF has exceeded the moderate high threshold. Common causes include:
Frequent short trips preventing passive regeneration 
Excessive idling preventing exhaust temperatures from reaching regen levels 
Failed or incomplete active regeneration cycles 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor giving incorrect readings 
Clogged or damaged DPF requiring cleaning or replacement 
Engine running issues causing excessive soot production 
Regen inhibit switch left in the off position
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but soot load will continue to increase without a successful regeneration. The engine will enter a progressive derate condition if soot reaches critical levels. A parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. Ensure the regen inhibit switch is not active. If the parked regen completes successfully and the code clears, monitor for recurrence. If regen fails to complete or the code returns frequently, have the DPF differential pressure sensor, DPF condition, and engine fueling system inspected.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF soot load has reached a high level and the engine requires a regeneration cycle to burn off accumulated soot before derate conditions are triggered.
 
 
What causes SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed regeneration cycles, or a faulty DPF differential pressure sensor reporting incorrect soot levels.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Short distances are possible but a parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to prevent the code from escalating to a more severe derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 3713 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If soot load continues to rise without a successful regeneration the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to protect the DPF from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Perform a successful parked regeneration. Once the DPF soot level drops below the threshold the code should clear. If it returns frequently have the DPF system and regeneration process inspected for underlying issues.
 
 
Related codes

SPN 3216 FMI 21 
SPN 5246 FMI 0 
SPN 1569 FMI 31

Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 18 – DPF Soot Load Critical (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 18 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter soot load has reached a critical level requiring immediate attention. This is a more severe version of the FMI 16 fault and appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines when soot accumulation has exceeded the point where normal regeneration may be sufficient. Immediate action is required to avoid severe derate or DPF damage.
Symptoms

DPF warning light illuminated 
Active derate condition 
Significantly reduced engine power 
Vehicle speed may be limited 
Parked regen may be blocked or unable to complete 
Exhaust back pressure significantly elevated
Cause
This code triggers when soot load in the DPF has reached the critical threshold, typically after the FMI 16 warning was not addressed. Common causes include:
FMI 16 fault left unresolved allowing soot to continue accumulating 
Multiple failed regeneration attempts 
Regen inhibit switch preventing regeneration cycles 
Severely clogged DPF beyond normal regen capability 
Engine fueling or combustion issues causing excessive soot output 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor 
Operating conditions preventing regeneration temperatures from being reached

This is a severe fault and the engine will be in an active derate condition. Continued operation risks permanent DPF damage and potential engine damage from excessive exhaust back pressure. A parked regeneration should be attempted immediately and if unsuccessful the vehicle should be taken to a qualified diesel technician.

Attempt a parked regeneration immediately if conditions allow. If the parked regen fails or cannot initiate, the vehicle needs professional service. At this soot level a forced regeneration using diagnostic software may be required. In severe cases the DPF may need to be removed for professional cleaning or replacement.

It means the DPF soot load has reached a critical level that requires immediate action. This is more severe than the FMI 16 warning and indicates the regeneration process has not kept up with soot accumulation.

Most commonly this fault develops when the FMI 16 warning was not addressed in time. Other causes include failed regeneration attempts, a severely clogged DPF, or engine issues causing excessive soot production.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3713 FMI 18?
 
Not recommended. The engine is in active derate and continued operation risks permanent DPF damage and increased exhaust back pressure that can harm the engine.
 
 
Will SPN 3713 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. This is a severe derate triggering fault and power and speed will be significantly restricted until the soot load is reduced.

dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 – DPF Soot Load High (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 indicates that the Diesel Particulate Filter has accumulated soot beyond the moderate high threshold and requires regeneration. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and is a step above a routine regen request — if regeneration is not completed promptly the engine will enter a derate condition and the DPF may require forced regeneration or service.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DPF or regen warning light illuminated 
Regen inhibited or unable to complete 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate possible 
Exhaust back pressure increased
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM calculates soot accumulation in the DPF has exceeded the moderate high threshold. Common causes include:
Frequent short trips preventing passive regeneration 
Excessive idling preventing exhaust temperatures from reaching regen levels 
Failed or incomplete active regeneration cycles 
Faulty DPF differential pressure sensor giving incorrect readings 
Clogged or damaged DPF requiring cleaning or replacement 
Engine running issues causing excessive soot production 
Regen inhibit switch left in the off position
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but soot load will continue to increase without a successful regeneration. The engine will enter a progressive derate condition if soot reaches critical levels. A parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible.
Recommended Action
Perform a parked regeneration as soon as possible. Ensure the regen inhibit switch is not active. If the parked regen completes successfully and the code clears, monitor for recurrence. If regen fails to complete or the code returns frequently, have the DPF differential pressure sensor, DPF condition, and engine fueling system inspected.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3713 FMI 16 mean?
 
It means the DPF soot load has reached a high level and the engine requires a regeneration cycle to burn off accumulated soot before derate conditions are triggered.
 
 
What causes SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
The most common causes are frequent short trips, excessive idling, failed regeneration cycles, or a faulty DPF differential pressure sensor reporting incorrect soot levels.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Short distances are possible but a parked regeneration should be performed as soon as safely possible to prevent the code from escalating to a more severe derate condition.
 
 
Will SPN 3713 FMI 16 cause a derate?
 
Yes. If soot load continues to rise without a successful regeneration the ECM will trigger progressive derate conditions to protect the DPF from damage.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3713 FMI 16?
 
Perform a successful parked regeneration. Once the DPF soot level drops below the threshold the code should clear. If it returns frequently have the DPF system and regeneration process inspected for underlying issues.

This issue relates specifically to the turbocharger system and its ability to maintain proper boost levels for engine performance. This turbocharger boost problem can stem from several potential causes. A faulty turbo actuator or boost sensor may trigger the fault code. Additionally, leaks in the intake system, such as loose hoses or damaged intercooler pipes, can contribute to incorrect boost pressure readings. Clogged exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valves can also affect engine performance and are related concerns to investigate. SPN_4357.description_en: Fault: return line heater circuit open and short to ground
causes: Deutz and MAN service bulletins recommend applying dielectric grease to heater circuit connectors and performing firmware updates to recalibrate heater switching thresholds, effectively eliminating nuisance faults caused by aggressive factory debounce parameters in early ECM software revisions
This code commonly appears after a forced DPF regeneration or when a replacement ECM is not properly configured for the DEF line heater layout
The heater request logic is transmitted via the 'Aftertreatment 1 SCR Dosing System Requests 2' parameter group
Technicians frequently encounter this fault after replacing the ECM without performing a complete system calibration, leading to a mismatch between the expected and actual heater control signals
In response to persistent faults like SPN 4357 FMI 16, the ECM may trigger safety fallback mechanisms such as torque derate to protect the engine and aftertreatment system
Understanding these mechanisms is essential for technicians to ensure the vehicle remains operational while addressing the root issue
Torque derate helps mitigate emissions non-compliance by reducing engine output

procedures_full.overview: SPN 5571 FMI 0 is a rail pressure relief or control above normal or overpressure protection class fault depending on OEM mapping. Stuck pressure control valve, restricted return, sensor bias high, control logic issues, and debris after contamination events are the primary causes. Contamination events causing control valve sticking and false highs from sensor circuit opens on some systems are documented patterns. Replacing the HP pump for a sensor or control valve fault is the most documented and most expensive misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Stuck pressure control valve — stuck pressure control valve producing above-normal rail pressure
Restricted return — restricted return path producing above-normal rail pressure
Sensor bias high — FRP sensor bias high producing false overpressure reading
Control logic issues — control logic fault producing above-normal pressure command
Debris after contamination — debris after contamination event causing control valve sticking
steps: Step 1 — Sensor Circuit Proof

Validate the FRP sensor electrically and against desired and actual response before condemning pump or relief components. A false high from a sensor circuit open on some systems produces an overpressure fault without true overpressure. Verify FRP sensor reference voltage, ground, and signal circuit integrity.
Step 2 — Desired vs Actual Pressure

Compare desired and actual rail pressure. A desired pressure that is within specification with an actual pressure that is above specification confirms a control or mechanical fault. A desired pressure that is above specification confirms a control logic or command fault.
Step 3 — Return-Path Inspection
Inspect the return path. A restricted return path producing above-normal rail pressure requires return-path service. Inspect return lines, fittings, and the return restriction for blockage.
Step 4 — Control Valve Tests

Test the pressure control valve. A stuck pressure control valve producing above-normal rail pressure requires control valve service or replacement. Contamination events causing control valve sticking are a documented cause — inspect for debris after any contamination event.
Step 5 — Pump and Relief Diagnosis Only With Evidence

Perform pump and relief diagnosis only with evidence. Confirm sensor, return path, and control valve integrity before any HP pump or relief valve assessment. An HP pump replaced without evidence may replace a good pump into a control or sensor fault ($1,500–$6,000+).

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair FRP sensor circuit if sensor fault is confirmed.
2 . Service return path if restriction is confirmed.
3 . Service or replace control valve if sticking is confirmed.
4 . Replace HP pump or relief valve only with confirmed evidence.
Verification Steps
Confirm rail pressure is within specification after repair.
Verify SPN 5571 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm overpressure protection does not activate after repair.
Monitor for return of overpressure events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect FRP sensor circuit at every major service.
✓ Inspect return path for restriction at every major service.
✓ Use clean fuel and OEM-specification filters to prevent contamination events.
✓ Inspect control valve after any contamination event.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High — overpressure can damage components Severity
High. Overpressure can damage components. Reduce load and diagnose promptly.

steps: Missing J1939 DM1 Message Check
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, troubleshoot and repair the CAN line.
If only a “J1939 Error” fault is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, check the proper configuration of the CPC.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
causes: This fault code indicates that there is an open circuit.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for open as follows:‪
Check for multiple codes.
If SPN 704/5, SPN 708/5, and SPN 709/5 are active, repair the open in between pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector and the fan and the Jake Brake solenoids. Refer to "68.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If only SPN 709/5 is active, go to step 1.
Disconnect the fan control solenoid connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 and 2 of the fan control solenoid connector.
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, go to step 4.
If the voltage is between 11.5 and 13.5 volts, replace the fan control solenoid. Refer to "68.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the voltage between pin 2 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 91 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "68.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is less than 11.5 volts, repair the open between pin 2 of the fan control solenoid connector and ground. Refer to "68.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is greater than 11.5, repair the open between pin 1 of the fan control solenoid connector and pin 98 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "68.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: MBE 4000 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 68.3 SPN 709/FMI 5 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

causes: Short to Ground: Sensor signal wire chafed against engine block or exhaust manifold causing direct ground contact

Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM monitors the O2 sensor heater circuit current using a precision shunt resistor
When current exceeds 2.5 A for more than 500 ms, the microcontroller sets FMI 6. The
Electrical analysis focuses on the sensor heater circuit and signal ground reference

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2018 Freightliner truck model can experience a derate issue linked to the SPN 5841 FMI 14 fault code. This problem is related to the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) system, which plays a critical role in controlling emissions and maintaining engine performance. The SPN 5841 FMI 14 code indicates a fault specifically in the DEF dosing valve or injector. When this fault occurs, the engine automatically enters a derate mode as a protective measure to safeguard the emissions systems from damage. This derate issue can stem from blockages or faults within the DEF dosing valve, including electrical problems. field_evidence.title: SPN 4357 Code on Truck: Causes and Fixes Explained
field_evidence.excerpt: The SPN 4357 code on a truck indicates a fault in the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) system. This fault can stem from low DEF fluid levels or sensor malfunctions within the system. Trucks commonly encounter DEF fluid level errors and issues with interruptions during the regeneration process. When the DEF tank does not contain adequate fluid or when sensors relay incorrect information, the truck may attempt regeneration but fail to complete it properly. To address the SPN 4357 code, practical steps include checking the DEF tank to verify sufficient fluid levels and inspecting the wiring harnesses connected to the DEF sensors for any damage. Cleaning or replacing the DEF quality sensor can also resolve sensor-related problems contributing to the fault. Check DEF tank for adequate fluid levels In

field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 International School Bus can experience an SPN 609 FMI 19 fault, which signifies that the Data Communication Unit (DCU) is not detected. This issue is a type of communication fault within the vehicle’s electronic control system. Such communication errors and module detection failures are common problems in school bus models, often stemming from issues with the wiring and electronic components that connect the DCU to the engine control module (ECM). To address this problem, it is important to check the wiring harnesses and connectors between the DCU and ECM for any signs of damage or corrosion. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 205: TCM Operation 2
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with a Transmission Control Module (TCM). The TCM communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs), receives feedback from sensors and actuates solenoids to control transmission operation. The TCM is mounted to the transmission and connected to the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector and 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector. The TCM is connected to the transmission sensors and solenoids at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
causes: TCM Software issue Internal failure Additional Tools Endurant HD Service Manual TRSM0950
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 205 FMI 9, 12, 19 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B

B. Verify TCM software. Key off. Allow TCM to perform a complete power down. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Programming”. Under "Software Information", record TCM software in table. If a TCM software update is available, update TCM software. Go to Step V If the TCM is at the latest available software, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Contact Information . Go to Step V TCM Software

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 205 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 205 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

procedures_full.overview_tr: Endurant HD şanzımanı bir Şanzıman Kontrol Modülü (TCM) ile donatılmıştır. TCM, diğer araç Elektronik Kontrol Üniteleri (ECU'lar) ile iletişim kurar, sensörlerden geri besleme alır ve şanzıman çalışmasını kontrol etmek için solenoidleri çalıştırır. TCM şanzımana monte edilmiştir ve 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörü ile 20 Yollu TCM Gövde Kablo Demeti Konnektörüne bağlıdır. TCM, 74 Yollu Şanzıman Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe şanzıman sensörlerine ve solenoidlerine bağlıdır.

Motor kapalıyken kontağı açın.

“Programming” (Programlama) bölümüne gidin.

field_evidence.title: Freightliner Cascadia 2016: Understanding SPN 924 FMI 5 and SPN 523531 FMI 31 Codes
field_evidence.excerpt: The Freightliner Cascadia 2016 model often encounters engine sensor faults and communication errors that trigger specific fault codes. Two common codes are SPN 924 FMI 5 and SPN 523531 FMI 31, each pointing to distinct issues within the vehicle’s systems. SPN 924 FMI 5 indicates that the sensor data is out-of-range. This problem is frequently associated with the turbocharger or the boost pressure sensor. On the other hand, SPN 523531 FMI 31 relates to a communication loss with a control module, which can affect the overall operation of the vehicle's network. To address these faults, begin by inspecting the sensor wiring and connectors for any signs of damage or corrosion. Maintaining clean electrical connections is essential to prevent recurring faults. SPN_924.description_en: Auxiliary output #1 - data valid but below normal operating range (most severe level)
causes: Short to Ground: Output wire chafed against chassis or engine block, creating a direct ground path

Failed Actuator Coil: Internal winding short in relay or solenoid reduces resistance below 5 Ω. ECM Driver Damage: Overcurrent event has permanently degraded the internal MOSFET in the ECM. Corroded Connector: High resistance at pin 1 of the J1939 output connector causes voltage drop
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM continuously monitors the voltage at the Auxiliary Output #1 pin using a 12‑bit ADC sampled at 100 Hz
A reading below 2.5 V for more than 500 ms sets the active
This code can appear after ECM replacement or software updates
Technicians often encounter it when dealing with complex electrical systems in heavy machinery where auxiliary functions are critical
It requires a detailed analysis of electrical circuits and ECM logic to resolve, highlighting the importance of understanding both the machinery and its control systems
Technicians in workshops commonly employ oscilloscopes to trace signal paths and identify abnormalities

SPN_924.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the vehicle’s Accelerator Interlock Switch message over the vehicle J1939 Data Link. This information is used to determine transmission performance.
causes: Vehicle Components Accelerator Interlock Switch Sensor and/or Wiring Other Vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) Internal failure Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system
steps: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 166 sets Active, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 166 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

SPN_1075.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_1075.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 116: Secondary Data Link (J1939 B)
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) via the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages called the Primary Data Link and Secondary Data Link. The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to communicate with the Engine, ABS, Body, and other vehicle ECUs during normal operation. The Secondary Data Link is used as a backup in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Secondary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector.
