oem_troubleshooting.title: Eaton UltraShift SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What diagnostic tool is used for Eaton UltraShift transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Eaton ServiceRanger is the primary diagnostic software for UltraShift, Fuller Advantage, and Endurant transmissions. It provides fault code access, live data monitoring, and service routines. It can also identify which J1939 source address message is missing when SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can SPN 1231 FMI 9 on an Eaton UltraShift cause it to lock in a single gear?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Depending on the TCM calibration and the severity of the communication loss, the transmission may default to a specific gear or a limited gear range rather than locking in a single ratio. The behavior varies by application and how critical the missing message is to the shift control algorithm.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the J1939 bus resistance check the same on Eaton UltraShift as on Allison or Detroit transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The J1939 physical layer standard specifies 120-ohm terminating resistors at each end of the bus, resulting in approximately 60 ohms when measured between CAN High and CAN Low with all modules unpowered. This check is valid across all vehicles using the J1939 CAN standard regardless of manufacturer.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Mack mDrive SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the Mack mDrive the same transmission as the Volvo I-Shift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The Mack mDrive is essentially the same automated manual transmission as the Volvo I-Shift, badged for Mack trucks. The underlying transmission hardware, control software architecture, and J1939 communication protocols are closely related. VCADS Pro serves both Mack and Volvo platforms.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will a failed engine EMS cause SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the Mack mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. If the engine EMS loses power or fails, the J1939 messages the mDrive TCM expects from the EMS will stop arriving, triggering SPN 1231 FMI 9. In this case, engine-related faults would also be present. Check all active codes in VCADS Pro to determine whether the communication loss is isolated to the transmission or is part of a broader network failure.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can corroded wiring cause intermittent SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. Intermittent CAN bus communication faults are often caused by connector corrosion, partially damaged wiring, or loose terminating resistors that cause the bus resistance to vary. VCADS Pro may record the fault as inactive if the corrosion is not severe enough to cause a persistent loss of communication. Thorough connector cleaning and a wiring inspection under the truck are worthwhile steps for intermittent cases.

oem_troubleshooting.title: Volvo I-Shift SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the Volvo I-Shift operate in manual mode if SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes. The I-Shift typically falls back to a manual shift mode when J1939 communication with the engine EMS is lost, allowing the driver to select gears manually. Full automatic operation �?including automated clutch control and engine torque management during shifts �?requires intact J1939 communication.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the Volvo I-Shift J1939 network the same as the Mack mDrive?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The Volvo I-Shift and Mack mDrive are closely related �?the mDrive is the Mack-branded version of the I-Shift. The J1939 network architecture is essentially the same across both, and VCADS Pro or the equivalent Mack diagnostic tool is used for network diagnosis.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How do I test whether the CAN backbone or a branch harness is causing SPN 1231 FMI 9 on the I-Shift?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: If multiple modules across the vehicle are reporting communication faults simultaneously, the CAN backbone or a terminating resistor is typically the cause. If only the I-Shift TCM is affected and other modules communicate normally, the fault is more likely in the branch harness from the backbone to the TCM connector. Resistance measurements and visual inspection of the specific harness branch can isolate the fault.

oem_troubleshooting.title: ZF AS-Tronic / TraXon SPN 1231 FMI 9 �?J1939 Network Communication Failure | Truck Fault Codes

troubleshooting_faq.question: What diagnostic software is used for ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF TOOLBOX Plus (formerly ZTSE) is the primary diagnostic software for ZF AS-Tronic, TraXon, and EcoMat transmissions. It provides fault code access, live data monitoring, and service routines including identification of absent J1939 source addresses.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Is the J1939 network fault on a ZF AS-Tronic the same repair process as on an Eaton or Allison transmission?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The physical layer diagnosis is the same �?measure bus resistance, check terminating resistors, inspect wiring and connectors. The diagnostic software differs by brand, but the network architecture and failure modes are identical across J1939-compliant transmissions.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can the ZF AS-Tronic or TraXon continue to operate in a manual mode if SPN 1231 FMI 9 is active?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: The ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon can typically operate in a manual shift fallback mode when J1939 communication is lost, allowing the driver to manually select gears. Full automatic operation requires the engine data provided over J1939, so full automation is restored only when the network communication is repaired.

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) over the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages: the Primary Data Link (J1939A) and the Secondary Data Link (J1939B). The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to send and receive messages to and from the Engine ECU, Anti-Lock Brake ECU and other vehicle ECUs to complete transmission shift operations. The Secondary Data Link is used in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Primary Data Link (J1939A) is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. The Secondary Data Link (J1939B) is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors vehicle and Engine ECU broadcast messages. If messages are not received or are invalid, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: Secondary Data Link (J1939B) vehicle ECU(s) messages not received for 5 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Secondary Data Link (J1939B) Engine ECU messages not received for 5 seconds while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECU(s).
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 9: Secondary Data Link (J1939B) vehicle ECU(s) messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939B) Engine ECU messages received for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 9, 14: Amber warning lamp on If Fault Code 115, 165, 171, or 185 is Active and the transmission is in gear: Coast Mode and Neutral Coast prohibited Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Inertia Brake activation prohibited Upshifts prohibited Clutch engagements prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO mode prohibited Hill Start Aid prohibited If Fault Code 115, 165, 171, or 185 is Active and the transmission is not in gear: Red stop lamp on Coast Mode and Neutral Coast prohibited Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Inertia Brake activation prohibited Upshifts prohibited Clutch disengagements prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited Hill Start Aid prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 9: Secondary Data Link (J1939B) vehicle ECU(s) messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939B) Engine ECU messages received for 10 seconds.

procedures_full.overview_tr: Şanzıman Kontrol Modülü (TCM), diğer araç Elektronik Kontrol Üniteleri (ECU'lar) ile araç J1939 veri hattı üzerinden iletişim kurar. TCM, mesaj gönderip almak için iki araç J1939 veri hattı kullanır: Birincil Veri Hattı (J1939A) ve İkincil Veri Hattı (J1939B). Birincil Veri Hattı, TCM tarafından şanzıman vites değişimi işlemlerini tamamlamak için Motor ECU'su, Kilitlenme Önleyici Fren ECU'su ve diğer araç ECU'ları ile mesaj gönderip almak üzere kullanılır. İkincil Veri Hattı, Birincil Veri Hattı çalışmadığında kullanılır. Birincil Veri Hattı (J1939A), 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır. İkincil Veri Hattı (J1939B), 20 Yollu TCM Gövde Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır.
procedures_full.detection_tr: TCM, araç ve Motor ECU'su yayın mesajlarını izler. Mesajlar alınmazsa veya geçersizse arıza aktif olarak ayarlanır.

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) communicates with other vehicle Electronic Control Units (ECUs) via the vehicle J1939 data link. The TCM uses two vehicle J1939 data links to send and receive messages called the Primary Data Link and Secondary Data Link. The Primary Data Link is used by the TCM to communicate with the Engine, ABS, Body, and other vehicle ECUs during normal operation. The Secondary Data Link is used as a backup in the event that the Primary Data Link is inoperative. The Secondary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors messages broadcast over the vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B). If engine or vehicle messages are not received or in error, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: Vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) messages not received for 5 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) Engine messages not received for 5 seconds while the TCM is receiving messages from other vehicle ECUs.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 9: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) messages received for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) Engine messages received for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 9, 14: Amber warning lamp on If Fault Code 115, 165 or 176 is Active and the transmission is in neutral: Non neutral modes prohibited PTO Mode prohibited If Fault Code 115, 165 or 176 is Active, the vehicle is moving or the transmission is in a gear higher than the lowest available start gear: Red stop lamp on Clutch engagement prohibited, vehicle may coast to a stop Transmission downshifts to lowest available start gear Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 9: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) messages received for 10 seconds. FMI 14: Valid vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) Engine messages received for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 9: Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) not configured correctly in the TCM Vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Bent, spread, or loose terminals Excessive electrical noise Missing or additional terminating resistors Other Vehicle ECU(s) Internal failure FMI 14: Vehicle Secondary Data Link (J1939 B) – Between Engine ECU and TCM Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Bent, spread, or loose terminals Excessive electrical noise Missing or additional terminating resistors Engine ECU Not powering up Internal failure

SPN_1669.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_1669.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically the Electronic Unit Pump Cylinder #1, Circuit Shorted to Battery.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically the Electronic Unit Pump Cylinder #1, Circuit Shorted to Battery.‪
steps: Circuit Shorted to Battery
Turn ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120-pin connector.
Using the J-48475 Breakout Box and J-48583 overlay, connect the MCM side of the harness ONLY.
Turn ignition ON.
Measure the voltage between pin 14 of the J-48475 Breakout box and ground.
If voltage is greater than 0.5v, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement.
Figure 1. Electronic Unit Pump #1
If voltage is present, repair short to power between pin 14 of the MCM 120-pin connector and the Electronic Unit Pump Cylinder #1. See Figure
"Electronic Unit Pump #1".
procedures_full.source_title: MBE 4000 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 121.1 SPN 3659/FMI 6 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
steps: Open Circuit, Short to Ground or Short to Power Check
Check for multiple codes.
If fault code 168/1 is active , service 168/1 first. Refer to "32.2 SPN 168/FMI 1".
If fault 3660/14 and 3661/14 are active in addition to 3659/14, go to step 2.
If only fault code 3659/14 is active, go to step 10.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 5.
Measure the resistance between pins 9 and 2 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω,.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 9 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 8.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 9 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the negative battery cable.
Measure the resistance between the positive battery post and pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to power between battery positive and pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector".
Figure 1. 120–pin MCM Connector
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 and pin 1 on the valve cover side of the injector harness. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω,.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 18.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #1.

Measure the resistance between pin 9 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and pin 3 of the injector #1 harness connector. If usingJ-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 3 and the injector #1 harness connector pin 3.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.

Measure the resistance between pin 2 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and pin 4 of the injector #1 harness connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 4 and the injector #1 harness connector pin 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 17.
Measure the resistance between pin 2 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 4 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #1. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 2 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 4 and ground.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 14 of the 120–pin MCM connector and pin 2 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 19.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect the injector #1 connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 2 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 4 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #1. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "118.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically the Electronic Unit Pump Cylinder #2 Circuit is Shorted to Battery.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically the Electronic Unit Pump Cylinder #2 Circuit is Shorted to Battery.‪
steps: Circuit is Shorted to Battery
Turn ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120-pin connector.
Using the J-48475
Breakout Box and the J-48583 overlay, connect the MCM side of the harness ONLY.
Run ignition ON.
Measure the voltage between pin 10 of the J-48475
Breakout Box and ground.
If voltage is greater than 0.5v, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement.
Figure 1. Electronic Unit Pump #2
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 10 of the MCM 120-pin connector and the # 2 Electronic Unit Pump. See Figure
"Electronic Unit Pump #2".

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
steps: Open Circuit, Short to Ground or Short to Power Check
Check for multiple codes.
If fault code 168/1 is active , service 168/1 first. Refer to "32.2 SPN 168/FMI 1".
If fault 3659/14 and 3661/14 are active in addition to 3660/14, go to step 2.
If only fault code 3660/14 is active, go to step 10.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 5.
Measure the resistance between pins 9 and 4 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 9 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 8.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 9 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the negative battery cable.
Measure the resistance between the positive battery post and pin 11of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to power between battery positive and pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector"
. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. 120–pin MCM Connector
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 9 and pin 4 on the valve cover side of the injector harness. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 18.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #2.

Measure the resistance between pin 9 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and pin 3 of the injector #2 harness connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 3 and the injector #2 harness connector pin 3.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.

Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and pin 4 of the injector #2 harness connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 4 and the injector #2 harness connector pin 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 17.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 4 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #2. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 4 and ground.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 10 of the 120–pin MCM connector and pin 2 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 19.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect the injector #2 connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 4 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #2. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "119.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
steps: Open Circuit, Short to Ground or Short to Power Check
Check for multiple codes.
If fault code 168/1 is active , service 168/1 first. Refer to "32.2 SPN 168/FMI 1".
If fault 3663/14 and 3664/14 are active in addition to 3662/14, go to step 2.
If only fault code 3662/14 is active, go to step 9.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 5.
Turn the ignition ON (ignition ON, engine OFF).
Measure for voltage between pin 4 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 4 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 5 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, go to step 7.
Measure for voltage between pin 7 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 7 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 7 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, go to step 8.
Measure for voltage between pin 11 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 11 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 7 of the 120–pin MCM connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector"
. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs"
If no voltage is present, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
Figure 1. 120–pin MCM Connector
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 and pin 1 on the valve cover side of the injector harness. If usingJ-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 12.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 4 of the Rear Injector Harness and pin 5 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #4.

Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and pin 3 of the injector #4 harness connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 3 and the injector #4 harness connector pin 3.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.

Measure the resistance between pin 1 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and pin 4 of the injector #4 harness connector. If using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 4 and the injector #4 harness connector pin 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace injector #4. Refer to "121.1.1.1 Verify Repairs"
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically an open circuit, short to ground or short to power.‪
steps: Open Circuit, Short to Ground or Short to Power Check
Check for multiple codes.
If fault code 168/1 is active in addition to 3662/5, service 168/1 first. Refer to "32.2 SPN 168/FMI 1".
If fault 3662/14 and 3663/14 are active in addition to 3664/14, go to step 2.
If only fault code 3664/5 is active, go to step 9.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 5.
Turn the ignition ON (ignition ON, engine OFF).
Measure for voltage between pin 4 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 4 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 5 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present,go to step 7.
Measure for voltage between pin 7 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 7 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 7 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, go to step 8.
Measure for voltage between pin 11 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short to power between pin 11 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 9 of the 120–pin MCM connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector"
. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. 120–pin MCM Connector
If no voltage is present, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 11 and pin 12 on the valve cover side of the injector harness. If using J-48671–10, measure between injector #6 pins 3 and 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 12.
Measure the resistance between pin 12 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and ground. If using J-48671–10, measure between injector #6 pin 3 and ground.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair the open between pin 12 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector on the harness side and pin 6 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #6.

Measure the resistance between pin 11 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and pin 3 of the injector #6 harness connector. If using J-48671–10, measure between injector #6 pin 3 and the injector #6 harness connector pin 3.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 16.

Measure the resistance between pin 12 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness and pin 4 of the injector #6 harness connector. If using J-48671–10, measure between injector #6 pin 4 and the injector #6 harness connector pin 4.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace injector #6. Refer to "123.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

field_evidence.title: Understanding Cummins ISL Fault SPN 5585 FMI 18 SA 0
field_evidence.excerpt: The Cummins ISL engine may experience sensor communication errors associated with emission controls, including intermittent fault codes like SPN 5585 FMI 18 SA 0. This specific fault indicates a problem related to the Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve position sensor. The SPN 5585 FMI 18 code points to a communication fault with the EGR valve position sensor. Such faults can lead to engine derate conditions or trigger check engine lights, affecting overall engine performance. Possible causes of this fault can stem from damage or loose connections in the EGR valve wiring harness. Additionally, issues with the sensor’s voltage or resistance might contribute to the fault being registered by the engine control module. Inspect the EGR valve wiring harness for any damage or loose connections

causes: This fault often appears after maintenance activities, such as replacing fuel injectors, and can lead to challenging starting conditions

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1675 FMI 5 indicates a starter enable or mode circuit open class depending on OEM mapping of starter control logic. Open enable wire, failed interlock switch, neutral safety open, clutch switch open, and poor ignition feed are the primary causes. No-crank caused by a range sensor or clutch switch rather than starter motor failure is a documented pattern. Replacing the starter motor before proving the enable and interlock path is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Open enable wire — open enable wire producing open circuit on starter enable path
Failed interlock switch — failed interlock switch producing open enable circuit
Neutral safety open — neutral safety switch open producing no enable signal
Clutch switch open — clutch switch open producing no enable signal
Poor ignition feed — poor ignition feed producing open enable circuit
steps: Step 1 — Verify Range/Clutch Status

Verify range and clutch status. Confirm enable status PIDs match actual range and clutch state. No-crank caused by a range sensor or clutch switch rather than starter motor failure is a documented pattern. Confirm the transmission range sensor and clutch switch are reporting correctly.
Step 2 — Check Enable Voltage Path

Check the enable voltage path. Measure enable voltage during a start request. A poor ignition feed producing an open enable circuit requires ignition feed diagnosis. Verify enable voltage is present at the enable relay or ECM enable input during a start request.
Step 3 — Switch Continuity

Check switch continuity. Verify continuity through the interlock switches — neutral safety, clutch switch, and any other enable switches in the circuit. A failed interlock switch producing an open enable circuit confirms a switch fault.
Step 4 — Relay/Starter Power Tests Only After Interlock Proof

Perform relay and starter power tests only after interlock proof. Confirm range/clutch status, enable voltage path, and switch continuity before any relay or starter power-side assessment. A starter replaced before proving the enable and interlock path will not resolve an enable circuit fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace failed interlock switch if confirmed.
2 . Replace range sensor if failure is confirmed.
3 . Repair open enable wire if confirmed.
4 . Repair ignition feed if poor feed is confirmed.
5 . Service relay as needed after enable path is proven.
Verification Steps
Confirm starter enable circuit operates correctly after repair.
Verify SPN 1675 FMI 5 does not return after repair.
Confirm no-crank condition is resolved after repair.
Verify interlock status PIDs match actual range and clutch state after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect interlock switch connectors at every major service.
✓ Verify range sensor and clutch switch operation after any transmission or clutch service.
✓ Inspect enable wiring for damage at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High operational impact when disabled. Safety-critical to verify interlocks work correctly. Severity
High operational impact when disabled. Safety-critical to verify interlocks work correctly. Starter enable open codes are interlock and control-path diagnostics.
symptoms: Starter enable open
Starter mode circuit fault
No crank enable signal
Interlock open circuit
No-crank from range sensor or clutch switch

SPN_2798.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 needle control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 needle control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
steps: Short to Battery/Power Check
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 2 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 2 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 16 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "96.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, go to step 4.
Measure the voltage between pin 2 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 3 of the Rear Injector Harness connector and pin 22 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "96.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 5 of the Rear Injector Harness connector and pin 24 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "96.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 96.1 SPN 2798/FMI 3 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector # 4, 5, or 6 needle control valve circuit is shorted to ground.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector # 4, 5, or 6 needle control valve circuit is shorted to ground.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary.
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 3.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 4.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 5.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Measure the resistance between pin 9 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #6 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #4.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #4 injector. Refer to "96.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 9.
Disconnect injector #5.
Measure the resistance between pin 5 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #5 injector. Refer to "96.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 11.
Disconnect injector #6.
Measure the resistance between pin 9 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #6 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #6 injector. Refer to "96.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "96.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.

If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 10 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "96.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.

procedures_full.overview: The DEF dosing system delivers precise quantities of urea solution to the exhaust upstream of the SCR catalyst. FMI 18 (below normal) is set when actual dosing quantity falls below the commanded target. This reduces SCR efficiency and can escalate to SPN 4364 (efficiency) and SPN 5246 (inducement). Clogged doser nozzles, weak pump pressure, and frozen or restricted lines are the most common causes.
causes: Clogged doser nozzle — urea crystallization blocking spray pattern
Weak DEF pump pressure — insufficient pressure to deliver commanded quantity
Frozen or restricted DEF lines — cold weather or blockage
DEF filter restriction — reducing pump output
Electrical control fault — pump or doser control circuit issue
Poor DEF quality — crystallization from contaminated fluid
steps: Single Action Gate — DEF Quality & Level Check
Verify DEF quality with refractometer (~32.5%) and confirm adequate tank level. Poor quality DEF causes crystallization that clogs the doser nozzle.
Binary Decision Gate — DEF Pump Pressure Test
Measure DEF pump pressure per OEM specification (typically 8–10 bar). Low pressure indicates pump wear, filter restriction, or supply line issue.
Override Manager — Line Restriction Inspection
Inspect DEF supply and return lines for kinks, freezing, or blockage. Check DEF filter condition and replace if restricted.
Safety Interceptor — Doser Nozzle Inspection
Inspect doser nozzle for crystallization deposits. Remove and inspect spray pattern if OEM procedure allows. Crystallized nozzles are a common cause of low dosing quantity.
Resume Point — Doser Spray Pattern Test
Perform doser spray pattern test per OEM procedure if supported. Verify spray pattern is correct and quantity matches commanded value.
Verification Loop — Post-Service Dosing Confirmation
After service, verify dosing quantity PIDs return to expected range and SCR efficiency improves.
Repair Ledger Output — Doser Replacement Decision
Replace doser only after pump pressure, line integrity, and filter are proven good. Document all findings.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace DEF if quality is out of spec.
2 . Replace DEF filter if restricted.
3 . Repair or replace DEF pump if pressure is below spec.
4 . Repair any DEF line restrictions or freeze damage.
5 . Clean or replace doser nozzle if crystallization is found.
6 . Replace doser assembly if spray pattern or quantity is confirmed low after supply is proven good.
Verification Steps
Confirm DEF pump pressure meets OEM spec after repair.
Verify dosing quantity PIDs return to expected range.
Confirm SCR efficiency improves after dosing repair.
Monitor for return of SPN 3482 FMI 18 over 50+ miles.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use only ISO 22241-compliant DEF to prevent crystallization.
✓ Replace DEF filter per OEM service intervals.
✓ Inspect doser nozzle for crystallization at every major service.
✓ Maintain DEF system per OEM cold-weather procedures.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium progressing to High with SCR efficiency and inducement follow-on. Address promptly to prevent escalation to SPN 4364 and SPN 5246 inducement derate.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 598 FMI 2 indicates clutch switch signal erratic or implausible. Misadjusted switch, failed switch, harness intermittents, and pedal mechanism wear are the primary causes. Start-inhibit complaints from clutch switch adjustment drift are documented patterns. Replacing the starter or ECM for a clutch interlock fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Misadjusted switch — clutch switch out of adjustment producing erratic signal
Failed switch — failed switch producing erratic signal
Harness intermittents — harness intermittents producing erratic signal
Pedal mechanism wear — pedal mechanism wear producing inconsistent switch actuation
steps: Step 1 — PID Toggle Through Pedal Travel

Monitor the clutch switch PID through the full pedal travel. A clean state change through pedal travel confirms correct switch operation. Intermittent dropouts during pedal travel indicate a switch or wiring fault. Start-inhibit complaints from clutch switch adjustment drift are a documented pattern.
Step 2 — Adjust Per OEM Specification

Adjust the switch per OEM specification if adjustment is required. A misadjusted switch produces erratic signals and start-inhibit complaints. Verify the switch actuation point matches OEM specification after adjustment.
Step 3 — Circuit Wiggle Test

Perform a circuit wiggle test on the switch connector and harness. Harness intermittents producing erratic signals are a documented cause. Wiggle the harness while monitoring the PID. A dropout during the wiggle test confirms a harness intermittent.
Step 4 — Replace Switch If Unstable
Replace the switch if it remains unstable after adjustment and circuit proof. Confirm the circuit is clean before switch replacement.
Step 5 — Verify After Repair
Verify clutch switch operation after repair. Confirm the PID toggles cleanly through pedal travel. Confirm start interlock and cruise disengage operate correctly after repair.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Adjust switch per OEM specification if adjustment is required.
2 . Repair harness if intermittent is confirmed.
3 . Replace switch if failure is confirmed after adjustment and circuit proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm PID toggles cleanly through pedal travel after repair.
Verify SPN 598 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm start interlock and cruise disengage operate correctly after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify clutch switch adjustment at every major service.
✓ Inspect clutch switch harness for chafe at every major service.
✓ Inspect pedal mechanism for wear at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. Can strand vehicle if start interlock fails. Erratic clutch switch data is adjustment and input integrity diagnosis.
symptoms: Clutch switch intermittent
Hard start from clutch switch fault
Cruise disengages from clutch fault
Clutch input erratic
Start inhibit from clutch switch adjustment drift

causes: This fault is typically the J1939 EBC1 (Engine Brake Switches) is missing.‪
steps: Missing EBC1 (Engine Brake Switches) via J1939
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, troubleshoot and repair the CAN line.
If only SPN 973/FMI 9 is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, ensure the CPC Group PGR001 parameter “EBC1 Source Address SAE J1939” is configured properly: 33 = non multiplex switches, 49 = multiple switches.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.

steps: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault code status. Retrieve the Active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector. Which FMIs are present? If Fault Code 22 FMI 9 is listed, problem is with the Data Link Backbone ABS Module or with the J1939 Data Link from ABS Module to J1939. Refer to OEM for repair procedures. If Fault Code 22 FMI 14 is listed, problem is with the Data Link ABS Module being configured for J1708 instead of J1939 communication, and/or with the ABS Module itself. Refer to OEM for repair procedures

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on outlet NOx indicates the SCR system is not reducing NOx to the expected level. The ECM compares upstream and downstream NOx to calculate conversion efficiency. High outlet NOx can result from insufficient DEF dosing, contaminated DEF, degraded SCR catalyst, NOx sensor bias, exhaust leaks diluting the reading, or abnormally high engine-out NOx from combustion faults. High outlet NOx after DEF quality events and doser deposit recurrence are the most common fleet patterns. Replacing the SCR catalyst without proving DEF chemistry and dosing is the most expensive misdiagnosis on this fault.
causes: Insufficient DEF dosing — low quantity reaching SCR catalyst
Contaminated DEF — diluted or contaminated urea solution
Degraded SCR catalyst — catalyst efficiency loss
NOx sensor bias — outlet sensor reading high without true high NOx
Exhaust leaks — ambient air diluting upstream reading
Abnormally high engine-out NOx — combustion fault contribution
steps: Single Action Gate — DEF Chemistry Verification

Test DEF concentration with a refractometer. Target: ~32.5% urea. Out-of-spec DEF is the highest-ROI first step on high outlet NOx complaints. Replace DEF before any other diagnostic step if concentration is outside the acceptable range.
Binary Decision Gate — Dosing Quantity and Pressure

Verify DEF dosing quantity and pressure are within OEM specification. Insufficient dosing from a weak pump, clogged injector, or restricted lines reduces NOx conversion without any catalyst degradation.
Override Manager — Upstream vs Outlet NOx Comparison

Compare upstream (inlet) NOx to outlet NOx. Calculate conversion efficiency. Low conversion with correct DEF chemistry and dosing supports catalyst degradation or exhaust leak dilution of the upstream reading.
Safety Interceptor — Engine-Out NOx Evaluation

Evaluate engine-out NOx contributors. Abnormally high engine-out NOx from EGR faults, combustion issues, or injection timing problems can overwhelm a healthy SCR system and produce high outlet NOx without any aftertreatment failure.
Resume Point — NOx Sensor Plausibility Check
Evaluate outlet NOx sensor plausibility against upstream NOx and dosing state. A sensor reading high with correct dosing and good upstream NOx supports sensor bias rather than true high outlet NOx.
Verification Loop — Post-Service NOx Conversion Confirmation
After any repair, verify NOx conversion efficiency returns to expected levels. Monitor outlet NOx over extended operation to confirm the repair is stable.
Repair Ledger Output — SCR Catalyst Decision
Replace SCR catalyst only after DEF chemistry, dosing, engine-out NOx, and sensor plausibility are all proven. Catalyst replacement without upstream proof produces repeat failures.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace DEF if refractometer confirms out-of-spec concentration.
2 . Service DEF dosing system if quantity or pressure is insufficient.
3 . Address engine-out NOx contributors if combustion faults are found.
4 . Replace outlet NOx sensor if bias is confirmed after plausibility check.
5 . Replace SCR catalyst only after all upstream causes are proven not to be the cause.
Verification Steps
Confirm NOx conversion efficiency returns to expected levels after repair.
Verify outlet NOx is within threshold after repair.
Monitor for return of SPN 3228 FMI 0 over extended operation.
Confirm inducement condition does not return after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use only ISO 22241-compliant DEF from verified sources.
✓ Test bulk DEF concentration monthly with a refractometer.
✓ Maintain DEF dosing system per OEM service intervals.
✓ Address EGR faults promptly to prevent elevated engine-out NOx.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High with progressive derate strategy risk. High outlet NOx triggers SCR efficiency monitoring that can escalate to inducement. Address promptly.
symptoms: High tailpipe NOx fault active
SCR not converting NOx
Outlet NOx above threshold
Emissions derate active
SCR efficiency declining

Look for any visible damage, loose connections, or misalignment. Cleaning away debris from the sensors can also help restore proper readings. Additionally, if there is a low crankcase breather oil separator speed indicated by SPN 5444, this may suggest clogging or wear. field_evidence.excerpt: The SPN-904 code indicates a fault with the front axle speed sensor, which is essential for the proper operation of the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) and traction control in this vehicle model. steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. SPN 5246 is generally related to a fault in a sensor or actuator that is part of the engine control system. Meanwhile, SPN 4375 points to a communication or data error within the ECM. These issues can stem from damaged wiring harnesses, corroded connectors, or faulty sensors such as the camshaft or crankshaft position sensors associated with these codes. SPN_925.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_925.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 indicates that the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to properly supply the dosing system. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the SCR system cannot receive adequate DEF flow, which will affect emissions control and typically trigger a derate condition if left unresolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition 
Reduced engine performance 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds 
Possible low DEF flow related codes appearing together
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects DEF pump pressure falling below the minimum required threshold. Common causes include:
Worn or failing DEF pump 
Low DEF level in tank 
Air in the DEF supply lines 
Clogged DEF filter restricting supply 
DEF line leak reducing system pressure 
Frozen DEF in cold weather conditions 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but without adequate DEF pump pressure the dosing system cannot supply DEF to the SCR catalyst. The engine will enter a derate condition if the fault is not addressed. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and refilling if low. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if clogged. Check DEF lines for leaks or air ingestion points. If the level and filter are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if it is not generating adequate pressure.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 mean?
 
It means the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to supply the dosing system, preventing the SCR system from properly controlling NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
The most common causes are a worn or failing DEF pump, a clogged DEF filter, low DEF level, air in the supply lines, or a DEF line leak.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will derate if the DEF system cannot supply adequate pressure to the dosing injector.
 
 
Will SPN 3362 FMI 1 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without sufficient DEF pump pressure the SCR system cannot function and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Check DEF level and filter first. If those are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if necessary. Once the system confirms adequate pressure and proper dosing the code should clear.

dd_procedures.title: SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 – DEF Pump Pressure Low (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 indicates that the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to properly supply the dosing system. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the SCR system cannot receive adequate DEF flow, which will affect emissions control and typically trigger a derate condition if left unresolved.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Engine derate condition 
Reduced engine performance 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds 
Possible low DEF flow related codes appearing together
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects DEF pump pressure falling below the minimum required threshold. Common causes include:
Worn or failing DEF pump 
Low DEF level in tank 
Air in the DEF supply lines 
Clogged DEF filter restricting supply 
DEF line leak reducing system pressure 
Frozen DEF in cold weather conditions 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but without adequate DEF pump pressure the dosing system cannot supply DEF to the SCR catalyst. The engine will enter a derate condition if the fault is not addressed. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and refilling if low. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if clogged. Check DEF lines for leaks or air ingestion points. If the level and filter are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if it is not generating adequate pressure.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 3362 FMI 1 mean?
 
It means the DEF pump is not generating enough pressure to supply the dosing system, preventing the SCR system from properly controlling NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
The most common causes are a worn or failing DEF pump, a clogged DEF filter, low DEF level, air in the supply lines, or a DEF line leak.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will derate if the DEF system cannot supply adequate pressure to the dosing injector.
 
 
Will SPN 3362 FMI 1 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without sufficient DEF pump pressure the SCR system cannot function and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 3362 FMI 1?
 
Check DEF level and filter first. If those are good, have the DEF pump tested and replaced if necessary. Once the system confirms adequate pressure and proper dosing the code should clear.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3362 FMI 9 means Cummins is not receiving reliable DEF tank temperature data. Inspect the tank module connector and wiring before replacing the sensor. DEF must stay above 12°F for reliable dosing. The tank temperature sensor feeds the ECM and heater control strategy. When updates become erratic, Cummins sets SPN 3362 FMI 9.
causes: Corroded DEF tank module connector
DEF vapor and road salt attack pins on the tank top module harness.
Failed DEF temperature sensor element
NTC thermistor failure sends stuck or out-of-range readings.
DEF tank heater circuit short affecting signal
Heater shorts can corrupt temperature sensor voltage on shared circuits.
steps: Monitor DEF tank temp in Cummins INSITE — plausibility range is ambient to 120°F under normal operation.
Inspect DEF tank module connector for corrosion and bent pins at the 4-pin harness.
Check sensor resistance: most units read 1,000–10,000 ohms across temperature range.
Verify DEF tank heater operation — shorted heater circuits can pull down temp sensor signal.
Test wiring continuity from ECM to tank module — target less than 2 ohms on signal circuit.
symptoms: DEF heater codes may stack with temperature fault
DEF temperature reading stuck at -40°F or 300°F in scan tool
Amber MIL with DEF system warning
Intermittent fault during cold weather
DEF consumption may be inhibited until fault clears
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 3362 FMI 9: DEF Tank Temperature Abnormal Update

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 17 - Start Enable Relay
dd_procedures.overview: The Start Enable Relay is wired into the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) on the coil side of the relay. At key on, the HCM determines which starting method to use (high-voltage Motor/Generator or Engine Starter). If the HCM uses the standard engine Starter, the 12-volt Cranking Relay is energized supplying battery power to the Start Enable Relay main feed, which then powers the Starter Solenoid.

Measure resistance between Vehicle Harness 38-Way Connector Pin 32 and Pin 4: If resistance between Pin 32 and Pin 4 is 40–120 ohms, Go to Step D If resistance is outside of range, repair the Vehicle Harness for an open circuit, then Go to Step V Connection Measurement Pin 32 to Pin 4

Voltage should remain at 5 volts for 1–2 seconds after initial key on. Go to Step V Connection Measurement Pin 32 to ground

procedures_full.overview: The Start Enable Relay is wired into the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) on the coil side of the relay. At key on, the HCM determines which starting method to use (high-voltage Motor/Generator or Engine Starter). If the HCM uses the standard engine Starter, the 12-volt Cranking Relay is energized supplying battery power to the Start Enable Relay main feed, which then powers the Starter Solenoid.
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 3 is set when the TECU detects an open or short in the control circuit of the Start Enable Relay for 1 second or greater. FMI 4 is set if the TECU detects a short to ground in the control circuit of the Start Enable Relay for 1 second or greater. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears the faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after it has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 17 is set the following conditions occur: Red “Service” light illuminates and an “F” flashes in the gear display. Fault is stored in TECU memory. If the fault sets at power up the engine still cranks, provided the high-voltage batteries have a sufficient State of Charge (SOC). If the fault sets while driving, the vehicle continues to operate. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after it has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.possible_causes: This fault code can be caused by any of the following: FMI 3, 4 Loose or corroded connections, bent or burnt pins, short to ground, open, or short to VBATT on the circuit. Start Enable Relay TECU

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 50 - J1939 Body Controller Message (HCM)
dd_procedures.overview: J1939 is a high-speed twisted pair 250K data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Hybrid Control Module (HCM) connects to the J1939 data link at the 38-Way Connector. This link transmits information to the HCM and communicates with the other modules on the network such as the Body Controller.
causes: FMI 9 J1939 Data Link Body Controller Additional Tools Basic hand tools Eaton® Test Adapter Kit Digital Volt/Ohm Meter ServiceRanger
steps: A. Verify Active or Inactive fault code status. Retrieve Active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector: If Fault Code 50 is Active, concern is either with the Body Controller or the Data Link from Body Controller to J1939 Data Link Backbone. Refer to OEM for repair procedure. If Fault Code 50 is Inactive, test is complete

dd_procedures.title: SPN 4094 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Low Flow
dd_procedures.procedure_text:
Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 – DEF Dosing Low Flow (Meaning, Causes & Fix)
 
 
 
← Back to Detroit Diesel Fault Codes
Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 indicates that the DEF dosing system is delivering less fluid than required to the SCR system. This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the aftertreatment system cannot properly reduce NOx emissions, which will typically trigger a derate if not addressed.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate condition possible 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects insufficient DEF flow through the dosing system. Common causes include:
Clogged or failing DEF dosing injector 
DEF pump wear or failure 
Frozen or restricted DEF supply lines 
Low DEF level in tank Contaminated 
DEF blocking the dosing system 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but the SCR system cannot function correctly without proper DEF dosing. The engine will likely enter a progressive derate condition if the fault is not resolved. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and fluid quality. If DEF is low or contaminated, refill or replace it. If the level is acceptable, have the DEF dosing injector, pump, and supply lines inspected for blockages or wear. A clogged dosing injector is a very common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF dosing system is not delivering enough fluid to the SCR system to properly reduce NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a clogged DEF dosing injector, a failing DEF pump, contaminated DEF fluid, or restricted DEF supply lines.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will likely derate if the dosing system cannot supply adequate DEF to the SCR system.
 
 
Will SPN 4094 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without proper DEF dosing the SCR system cannot control NOx emissions and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and address the root cause — typically a clogged dosing injector or DEF pump issue. Once the dosing system is flowing correctly and the SCR system confirms proper operation, the code should clear.

SPN 3364 FMI 2
 
SPN 4334 FMI 16

This code appears on DD13, DD15, and DD16 engines and means the aftertreatment system cannot properly reduce NOx emissions, which will typically trigger a derate if not addressed.
Symptoms
Check engine light on 
DEF or SCR warning light illuminated 
Reduced engine performance 
Engine derate condition possible 
SCR system unable to meet emissions thresholds
Cause
This code triggers when the ECM detects insufficient DEF flow through the dosing system. Common causes include:
Clogged or failing DEF dosing injector 
DEF pump wear or failure 
Frozen or restricted DEF supply lines 
Low DEF level in tank Contaminated 
DEF blocking the dosing system 
Faulty DEF pressure sensor
Can You Keep Driving?
Limited driving is possible but the SCR system cannot function correctly without proper DEF dosing. The engine will likely enter a progressive derate condition if the fault is not resolved. Do not ignore this code.
Recommended Action
Start by checking the DEF tank level and fluid quality. If DEF is low or contaminated, refill or replace it. If the level is acceptable, have the DEF dosing injector, pump, and supply lines inspected for blockages or wear. A clogged dosing injector is a very common cause of this fault.
What does Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 18 mean?
 
It means the DEF dosing system is not delivering enough fluid to the SCR system to properly reduce NOx emissions.
 
 
What causes SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
The most common causes are a clogged DEF dosing injector, a failing DEF pump, contaminated DEF fluid, or restricted DEF supply lines.
 
 
Can I keep driving with SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Short distances may be possible but the engine will likely derate if the dosing system cannot supply adequate DEF to the SCR system.
 
 
Will SPN 4094 FMI 18 cause a derate?
 
Yes. Without proper DEF dosing the SCR system cannot control NOx emissions and the ECM will trigger a derate condition.
 
 
How do I clear SPN 4094 FMI 18?
 
Inspect and address the root cause — typically a clogged dosing injector or DEF pump issue. Once the dosing system is flowing correctly and the SCR system confirms proper operation, the code should clear.

procedures_full.overview: Caterpillar SPN 4094 FMI 1 means the DPF soot load percentage is reporting below the expected minimum, signaling a sensor or plumbing fault - not necessarily a clean filter. This can suppress DPF regen triggers, leading to undetected soot overloading and eventual derate risk. Inspect the differential pressure hoses first with Texa or Jaltest before condemning any hardware. Caterpillar SPN 4094 FMI 1 is an aftertreatment fault on C13 and C15 engines indicating the DPF Soot Load Percent parameter is reporting a data-valid but below-minimum-range value. Soot load is derived from the DPF differential pressure sensor readings and regen modeling in the Caterpillar Regeneration System. When the ECM sees a soot percentage below the minimum plausible range, it flags FMI 1. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com recommends a sensor and plumbing inspection first - cracked differential pressure hoses are the most common cause by far. Left uncorrected, the engine may skip scheduled regens, silently overload the DPF, and trigger a forced parked regen or DPF replacement on the road. Check SPN 3609 alongside this fault for a complete aftertreatment picture before ordering any parts.
causes: Cracked or disconnected DPF differential pressure sensor hose
Very Common

The small-diameter hoses connecting the upstream and downstream DPF taps to the differential pressure sensor degrade through heat cycling. A cracked upstream hose bleeds off exhaust pressure, collapsing the differential reading to near zero and producing an implausibly low soot load estimate.
Failed or drifted DPF differential pressure sensor

The sensor element drifts low over time in high-heat applications. A sensor reporting falsely low differential pressure causes the ECM to calculate an erroneously low soot percentage, triggering FMI 1 even when the filter is genuinely loaded.
Ash saturation of DPF after extended service without cleaning

A DPF saturated with non-combustible ash after 300,000+ miles without cleaning produces unusual differential pressure patterns that confuse the soot load algorithm. The ECM may calculate a paradoxically low soot load while backpressure is actually rising from ash accumulation.
steps: Connect Texa Navigator TXTs or Jaltest diagnostic software to the truck J1939 data link. Navigate to Aftertreatment and read SPN 4094 live data. A healthy value with a partially loaded filter reads 20-80% at idle. An FMI 1 value below 5% or at 0% after substantial mileage since last DPF service indicates a sensor or logic fault.

Locate the DPF differential pressure sensor (mounted near the DPF canister inlet, connected by two small-diameter hoses from each side of the filter). Inspect both hoses for cracks, kinks, or disconnections. A cracked upstream hose bleeds off exhaust pressure, collapsing the differential reading to near zero and producing a falsely low soot load estimate.

Disconnect the differential pressure sensor harness and measure sensor supply voltage (5 V reference) and signal voltage at key-on engine-off. Signal should read approximately 0.5-1.0 V at zero differential pressure. Outside this range, test the reference and ground wires back to the ECM for continuity.

If hoses and wiring are intact, use Texa or Jaltest to force a DPF soot load recalibration and observe whether the new baseline matches the filter operating history. An excessively low recalibrated baseline at high mileage suggests the sensor has drifted and requires replacement.

Install replacement DPF differential pressure sensor, reconnect hoses with new clamps, re-run the calibration procedure via Texa or Jaltest, then clear faults and confirm SPN 4094 reads a plausible value before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Amber aftertreatment warning lamp active on the instrument cluster.
DPF regeneration counter shows abnormally long intervals between regens, as the ECM incorrectly believes the filter is clean.
No perceptible driveability change initially, but long-term risk of DPF overloading and high exhaust backpressure derate.
Fault may co-occur with SPN 3609 (DPF intake pressure) or SPN 3246 (DPF outlet temp) if the aftertreatment sensor cluster is degraded.
Possible extended regen duration when a regen does eventually occur due to accumulated untracked soot load.
