procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on DEF quality indicates the DEF concentration is below the minimum acceptable threshold for SCR operation. Diluted DEF, contaminated bulk fluid, wrong fluid, failed quality sensor, and stratified tank are the primary causes. Fleet bulk tank contamination events are common real-world causes — a contaminated bulk tank produces quality faults across multiple trucks simultaneously. Electrical sensor diagnosis only after chemistry is proven good prevents replacing the quality sensor for a fluid problem.
causes: Diluted DEF — DEF diluted with water or other fluid
Contaminated bulk fluid — bulk DEF tank contamination
Wrong fluid — incorrect fluid added to DEF tank
Failed quality sensor — quality sensor failure producing false low reading
Stratified tank — DEF stratification in tank producing low-concentration sample
steps: Single Action Gate — Refractometer Chemistry Check

Sample DEF from mid-tank and test with a refractometer. The target DEF concentration is approximately 32.5% urea. A refractometer reading below the minimum specification confirms diluted or contaminated DEF. Electrical sensor diagnosis only after chemistry is proven good.
Binary Decision Gate — Contamination Inspection

Inspect the DEF tank and supply for contamination. Fleet bulk tank contamination events are common real-world causes — a contaminated bulk tank produces quality faults across multiple trucks simultaneously. Inspect the DEF tank for discoloration, sediment, or foreign fluid contamination.
Override Manager — Drain, Flush, and Refill with Verified DEF

Drain, flush, and refill the DEF tank with verified ISO 22241-compliant DEF if contamination or dilution is confirmed. Use a verified DEF source — not the same bulk tank that produced the contamination. Confirm the new DEF meets specification with the refractometer before refilling.
Safety Interceptor — Filter Service After Contamination

Service the DEF filter after any contamination event. Contamination that passes through the filter can damage the pump and doser. Replace the DEF filter after any confirmed contamination event before returning to service.
Resume Point — Quality Sensor Electrical Diagnosis After Fluid Proof

Perform quality sensor electrical diagnosis only after fluid chemistry is confirmed good. A quality sensor that reads below threshold with confirmed good DEF chemistry confirms sensor failure. Inspect the header connector for corrosion from DEF crystal contamination.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Quality Confirmation
After repair, verify DEF quality returns to normal. Confirm SPN 4094 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of quality faults over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Fluid, Filter, or Sensor Decision

Drain, flush, and refill with verified DEF if contamination or dilution is confirmed. Replace DEF filter after contamination event. Replace quality sensor only after fluid chemistry is confirmed good and sensor failure is proven.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Drain, flush, and refill DEF tank with verified ISO 22241-compliant DEF.
2 . Replace DEF filter after contamination event.
3 . Replace quality sensor only after fluid chemistry is confirmed good and sensor failure is proven.
Verification Steps
Confirm DEF quality returns to normal after repair.
Verify SPN 4094 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Confirm SCR efficiency monitoring returns to normal after repair.
Monitor for return of quality faults over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use only ISO 22241-compliant DEF from verified sources.
✓ Inspect bulk DEF tank for contamination regularly.
✓ Replace DEF filter per OEM service intervals.
✓ Inspect DEF tank header connector for crystal corrosion at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium progressing to High Severity
Medium progressing to High as inducement approaches. Mandatory chemistry-first gate prevents replacing the quality sensor for a contaminated or diluted DEF supply.

DEF quality below threshold
Bad DEF quality fault

SCR efficiency fault following quality fault

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 3 means the DPF soot load sensor circuit on International trucks reads voltage above normal, typically 4.5-5.0V indicating a short to high source. The ECM may report 100% soot load and trigger derate even when the filter is clean. Compare soot percentage to intake pressure before replacing the DPF. The DPF soot load reading on International LT and RH Series trucks determines when regeneration runs and when derate begins. When SPN 4094 FMI 3 sets, the soot sensor circuit is shorted high, and the ECM believes the filter is fully loaded regardless of actual restriction. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com recommends comparing SPN 4094 to SPN 3609 intake pressure and measuring signal voltage at the sensor before authorizing expensive DPF service.
causes: Signal wire shorted to 5V reference or battery positive
Chafed harness at frame rail clips shorts the soot sensor signal to 12V or 5V, producing a pegged-high reading the ECM interprets as 100% soot load.
Corroded connector causing signal-to-reference short
Moisture intrusion at the sensor connector bridges signal and reference pins, reading 4.5-5.0V and setting FMI 3.
Failed soot load sensor with internal short
Internal sensor failure can short the signal output to the supply pin, though wiring faults are more common on International platforms.
steps: Connect International DLB or Snap-on NEXIQ and read SPN 4094 soot load percentage and SPN 3609 intake pressure — if soot reads 100% but intake pressure is below 5 kPa, suspect a circuit fault not actual plugging.
Locate the DPF soot load sensor (differential pressure-based or ECU-calculated model depending on year) and inspect the connector for corrosion, bent pins, or damaged insulation.

With the key on and sensor connected, measure signal voltage at the sensor — 0.5-1.5V indicates low soot (0-30%), 2.0-3.5V is moderate (30-70%), and 4.5-5.0V indicates a short to high source (FMI 3), not actual 100% soot.
Disconnect the sensor and measure resistance between signal and ground — an open or infinite reading with 5V on the signal wire confirms a wiring short to battery or 5V reference, not sensor failure.
Inspect the harness between the sensor and ECM for chafing at frame clips — repair any wire where signal insulation is compromised and signal reads continuity to 12V or 5V supply.
Repair wiring or replace the sensor, clear codes, and verify soot load reads proportionally to SPN 3609 intake pressure after a 15-minute drive cycle.
symptoms: Soot load percentage reads 100% on International DLB or NEXIQ despite recent DPF service
Amber aftertreatment lamp with forced regen that does not clear the soot reading
SPN 3609 (DPF intake pressure) reads normal but soot load remains pegged high
Signal voltage at the soot sensor reads 4.5-5.0V — normal range is 0.5-4.5V proportional to soot level
Progressive torque derate based on ECM-calculated soot load, not actual restriction

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 16 means DPF soot load is above normal on a Mack engine, common on vocational trucks with heavy idle time where regen cycles fall behind. This is an early warning stage, not an emergency. A completed parked regeneration resolves most of these cases without parts.
causes: Interrupted or incomplete regen cycles
Job-site idling and short cycles never let soot fully burn off.
Vocational duty cycle with heavy idle time
Mixer, dump, and refuse routes rarely reach sustained regen-friendly exhaust temps.
Diff pressure sensor hose cracking or clogging
Gives a falsely elevated reading independent of actual soot load.
steps: Check soot load percentage on a scan tool and review whether recent regens completed or were interrupted.
Review the truck's duty cycle - vocational Macks running mixer, dump, or refuse routes with heavy idle time load up soot faster.
Command a parked regeneration and monitor whether soot load drops as expected.
Inspect differential pressure sensor hoses for cracking or clogging.
Check for any EGR or turbo faults increasing soot production upstream.
symptoms: Dash DPF status indicator showing elevated soot load

Trucks that rarely reach sustained highway exhaust temps rely more heavily on active regen.

Gives a falsely elevated soot load reading independent of actual filter condition.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 16 means DPF soot load percentage is running above the moderately severe threshold on your Peterbilt's PACCAR MX engine. This is a high-severity warning that directly precedes a derate - run a forced regen now before it escalates. This is one of the most actionable codes in the aftertreatment system because it gives a clear window to act before the truck loses power on its own. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats a forced regen at this stage as routine maintenance, not an emergency repair, since catching it here avoids a full derate on the road.
causes: Incomplete regeneration from short-trip or heavy-idle duty cycles
Frequent short trips or extended idling don't generate the sustained exhaust temperature needed for normal passive regeneration, letting soot accumulate.
steps: Pull the fault and check current soot load percentage on PACCAR Davie4 against the threshold that triggers derate.
Review recent duty cycle history for excessive idling or short trips that prevented normal passive or active regeneration.
Initiate a stationary forced regeneration through Davie4 in a safe, well-ventilated area away from combustibles.
Monitor soot load percentage decrease throughout the regen to confirm it's trending back toward normal.
Inspect for any related EGR, turbo, or fueling faults that could be accelerating soot production beyond normal levels.
If a forced regen fails to reduce soot load, the DPF may need to be removed for professional cleaning or inspection.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp with a dash soot load or regen request indicator
No power loss yet, but a derate is imminent if ignored
Possible reduced fuel economy as the ECM compensates for rising soot
procedures_full.source_title: Peterbilt SPN 4094 FMI 16: DPF Soot Load Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 16 on Caterpillar engines means DPF soot load has climbed to a moderately high level. It's a high-severity warning that a regeneration is needed soon - address it now to avoid a more restrictive derate later. Soot load percentage is one of the most-searched aftertreatment parameters because it directly answers the question every driver wants to know: how much trouble is this really? ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats SPN 4094 FMI 16 as an actionable warning rather than a crisis - the filter isn't damaged, it just needs to burn off accumulated soot, and catching it at this moderately-high stage avoids the harder derate that follows if soot load keeps climbing unaddressed.
causes: Extended idle time or short-trip duty cycle preventing natural regeneration
Exhaust temperatures during idling and short trips often don't reach the threshold needed for passive or automatic active regeneration, letting soot accumulate faster than it burns off.
Failed or incomplete previous regeneration attempts
If prior regen cycles didn't complete successfully due to a sensor or air-leak issue, soot load keeps climbing even though the system was attempting to address it.
EGT sensor fault affecting regen monitoring
Inaccurate exhaust temperature data can cause the ECM to end regen cycles prematurely, believing the target was reached when it wasn't.
Genuine DPF restriction from ash accumulation
Even with successful regenerations that burn off soot, non-combustible ash builds up over time and eventually requires a physical cleaning service rather than just another regen.
steps: Pull the fault with Cat ET and confirm SPN 4094 FMI 16 is active; check the exact soot load percentage and how quickly it's been climbing across recent drive cycles.
Determine why regeneration hasn't been keeping up - check for a pattern of short trips or excessive idle time that prevents the exhaust from reaching regen temperatures naturally.
If the truck has been driven normally without unusual short-trip patterns, check for any EGT sensor faults or air/exhaust leaks that could be interfering with successful automatic regenerations.
Initiate a parked (stationary) regeneration through Cat ET in a safe, well-ventilated area away from combustible materials.
Monitor the regen cycle to confirm soot load percentage drops as expected once the cycle completes successfully.
If soot load doesn't drop after a successful-seeming regen, or the regen fails to complete, escalate to inspecting the DPF itself for ash loading or physical restriction.
symptoms: Amber dash lamp with a soot load or 'regen needed' style message
Slightly reduced fuel economy as the engine works harder against rising backpressure
procedures_full.source_title: Caterpillar SPN 4094 FMI 16: Diagnosing and Resolving High DPF Soot Load

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 16 on Detroit Diesel means DPF soot load has hit the moderately severe high threshold. The truck is in derate and needs an active regen. Run a forced stationary regen through DDDL before assuming the DPF needs replacement — a plugged sense tube can cause identical symptoms with a clean filter. A high soot load code on a Detroit is a normal aftertreatment event — regens happen every few hundred miles and occasionally a regen gets inhibited long enough for the soot to stack up. Most SPN 4094 FMI 16 calls resolve in under an hour with a forced regen through DDDL. The cases that don't resolve cleanly either have an HC dosing problem preventing proper regen temperatures or a blocked sense tube making the filter look worse than it is. Either way, the diagnosis takes an hour, not a day.
causes: Incomplete or inhibited active regens (aftertreatment)

Short-haul duty cycles, frequent cold starts, or inhibit switches left engaged prevent the active regen from completing. Soot accumulates with each missed regen cycle until the FMI 16 threshold is crossed.
HC doser malfunction preventing regen temperature (aftertreatment)
Moderate

If the hydrocarbon doser is not delivering fuel to the DOC at the correct rate, the DPF cannot reach or sustain the 500-600°C regen temperature. Regens initiate but fail to burn off soot, allowing load to increase over successive partial cycles.
Blocked DPF differential pressure sense tube (mechanical)
Moderate

The sense tube connecting the DPF housing to the differential pressure sensor packs with carbon deposits over time. A blocked tube traps a pressure reading higher than actual, causing the ACM to calculate falsely elevated soot load even after a successful regen.
Engine oil consumption adding soot and ash (mechanical)
Less Common

Excessive oil burning past worn valve seals or piston rings adds combustion soot and ash to the exhaust stream at a rate beyond what normal regeneration can handle. High ash load reduces filter capacity and triggers earlier soot load alarms.
steps: 1. Connect Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) and check SPN 4094 soot load percentage live. Detroit's typical derate thresholds are: >80% = moderate derate (FMI 16), >100% = severe derate, >120% = maximum derate/speed limit. Also check SPN 4095 (ash load) — high ash load limits the space available for soot and can trigger elevated soot load readings sooner.

2. Attempt a stationary (parked) forced active regen through DDDL. Pre-conditions: parking brake set, coolant temp >60°C, no inhibit switch active, no secondary faults on the HC dosing or aftertreatment system. During a successful regen, engine speed rises to ~1,200 RPM and DPF outlet temp should reach 550-650°C.

3. If the regen initiates but will not complete, check the HC doser pressure via DDDL. On Gen1 Detroit platforms, HC doser rail pressure should be ~52 psi (360 kPa); on Gen2, approximately 58 psi (400 kPa). A pressure fault or zero-dosing condition means the DPF won't reach regen temperature.

4. After a completed regen, clear the fault and recheck SPN 4094. If the soot load percentage has not dropped significantly after a full regen cycle, suspect the DPF differential pressure sense tube packed with carbon soot — this is a frequent cause of false-high soot load readings. Disconnect the sense tube at the DPF and blow it out.

5. If genuine soot load is confirmed high and regen cannot complete, connect Texa for a second-opinion live data read, then assess whether the DPF requires physical cleaning (hydrojet or thermal) or replacement based on mileage and ash load.
symptoms: Overview: Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 16

A high soot load code on a Detroit is a normal aftertreatment event — regens happen every few hundred miles and occasionally a regen gets inhibited long enough for the soot to stack up. Most SPN 4094 FMI 16 calls resolve in under an hour with a forced regen through DDDL. The cases that don't resolve cleanly either have an HC dosing problem preventing proper regen temperatures or a blocked sense tube making the filter look worse than it is. Either way, the diagnosis takes an hour, not a day.
procedures_full.source_title: Detroit Diesel SPN 4094 FMI 16: DPF Soot Load Above Normal — Regen Required

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 16 on Kenworth means the DPF soot load is dangerously high. Check regen inhibit conditions, attempt a stationary regen in Davie4, and only consider filter replacement if regen consistently fails to complete. SPN 4094 FMI 16 is the moderately severe soot overload alarm — the ECM is telling you the filter is overloaded and needs to burn it off now. On Kenworth trucks, this is often a regen-inhibit problem rather than a filter problem. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com works the regen system first and only pulls the filter when the burn cycle itself has been confirmed broken.
causes: Regen inhibited by driver, duty cycle, or active fault (operational)
Very Common
City delivery routes, excessive idle time, and inhibit switches prevent passive and active regens from completing, allowing soot to accumulate.
Faulty DOC or regen fuel doser preventing sufficient temperature for burn-off (mechanical)
If the DOC is not lighting off properly or the HC doser is not delivering fuel for active regen, the filter temperature never reaches the required burn point.
DPF differential pressure sensor fault giving falsely elevated soot calculations (electrical)
A plugged sense line or failed delta-P sensor inflates the soot load reading even if the actual filter is not badly loaded.
Actual DPF ash and soot overload from extended service intervals (mechanical)
Filters do eventually reach end-of-life even with normal regen cycles. Ash is not burned off and accumulates over time.
steps: 1. Connect PACCAR Davie4 or Diesel Laptops and read soot load percentage, regen inhibit status, and the date/count of the last completed regeneration.

2. Verify no regen inhibit inputs are active: check that the parking brake is not blocking stationary regen, that coolant temp is above the enable threshold, and that no active hard faults are blocking regen.
3. Attempt a manual stationary regeneration from Davie4 and monitor DPF outlet temperature — it should climb above approximately 550°C (1020°F) and hold for the duration of the active regen cycle.
4. If regen completes and soot load drops below threshold, clear the fault and road-test with a loaded pull to confirm the passive regen can maintain the filter going forward.
5. If regen is not completing, check the DOC outlet temperature sensor, the HC doser/fuel injection system for regen, and DPF differential pressure sensor for plausibility.
6. A filter above 100% calculated soot load or repeated failed regens may need a parked forced regen at a dealer, or the filter may need a cleaning/replacement evaluation.
symptoms: DPF or regen warning lamp illuminated on the dash
Power derate under load as soot load increases
Regen inhibited or unable to complete if an underlying issue is present
Excessive backpressure possibly noted in aftertreatment data
Reduced fuel economy from repeated short-trip regen attempts
procedures_full.source_title: Kenworth SPN 4094 FMI 16: DPF Soot Load Above Moderately Severe Threshold

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 18 means the ECM calculated DPF soot load below the expected range. Inspect differential pressure plumbing and regen history before assuming the filter is damaged. Mercedes-Benz aftertreatment estimates soot load from differential pressure, temperature, and mileage models. When SPN 4094 FMI 18 sets, the reported soot percentage is valid but lower than the ECM expects for current exhaust conditions. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com usually finds a recent regen, a cleared ash event, or a skewed diff-pressure reading — not a missing DPF.
causes: Recent forced or parked regen dropped soot model below threshold
A completed regen can temporarily push calculated soot load low until driving miles rebuild the model.
DPF differential pressure sensor or hose fault reading low
Leaking or blocked sense lines make the filter appear cleaner than it is, pulling soot percentage down.
ECM soot model calibration drift after filter service
Ash cleaning or DPF replacement without proper reset can leave the soot estimator out of sync.
Failed DPF substrate with abnormal flow path
A cracked or melted brick can pass exhaust with lower than expected pressure drop, confusing the soot algorithm.
steps: Connect Jaltest or Texa and read SPN 4094 alongside SPN 3251 differential pressure and SPN 3719 soot load model values.
Review recent regen history — a completed forced regen or dealer ash service often precedes an artificially low soot percentage.
Inspect DPF differential pressure sense hoses for cracks, disconnects, or soot blockage that can skew soot estimation low.
Compare calculated soot load to differential pressure at idle and under load; large disagreement points to sensor or model drift.
Perform a stationary regen only if soot load climbs back into range — clearing the code without confirming data integrity allows it to return.
symptoms: Amber aftertreatment or check-engine lamp with SPN 4094 active
DPF soot load percentage stuck unusually low on scan tool live data
Regen requests suppressed or delayed despite normal driving
Possible companion SPN 3251 differential pressure codes
No immediate power loss unless paired with inducement faults
procedures_full.source_title: Mercedes-Benz SPN 4094 FMI 18: DPF Soot Load Percent Below Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 4094 FMI 31 indicates a DEF quality condition is present — concentration or quality rationality has failed. Diluted or contaminated DEF, wrong fluid, failed quality sensor, header wiring issues, and stratified tank after poor refill are the primary causes. Bulk DEF contamination, roadside bad fills, and sensor replaced before fluid proof are documented patterns. Replacing the quality sensor before proving fluid chemistry is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Diluted or contaminated DEF — diluted or contaminated DEF producing below-specification concentration
Wrong fluid — wrong fluid in DEF tank producing quality fault
Failed quality sensor — failed quality sensor producing false quality fault
Header wiring issues — header wiring issues producing quality sensor fault
Stratified tank after poor refill — stratified tank after poor refill producing inconsistent quality reading
steps: Step 1 — Sample Mid-Tank and Refractometer Check

Sample the DEF mid-tank and check with a refractometer. DEF concentration should be approximately 32.5% urea. Bulk DEF contamination and roadside bad fills are documented causes. A refractometer reading outside specification confirms a fluid quality fault.
Step 2 — Inspect Contamination

Inspect for contamination. Inspect the DEF tank for signs of contamination — discoloration, odor, or visible debris. A contaminated tank requires drain, flush, and refill with fresh OEM-specification DEF.
Step 3 — Drain and Refill If Failed

Drain and refill if fluid quality has failed. Drain the DEF tank completely. Flush the tank if contamination is present. Refill with fresh OEM-specification DEF. Inspect the DEF filter and replace if contaminated.
Step 4 — Sensor or Circuit Tests Only If Chemistry Is Proven Good

Perform sensor or circuit tests only if chemistry is proven good. Electrical sensor checks are only valid after fluid chemistry is confirmed within specification. Quality sensor connector corrosion from urea crystals is a documented cause. Inspect the quality sensor and header connector for corrosion after fluid proof.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Drain, flush, and refill with fresh OEM-specification DEF if quality is failed.
2 . Replace DEF filter if contaminated.
3 . Repair quality sensor connector if corrosion is confirmed.
4 . Replace quality sensor if failure is confirmed after fluid proof.
Verification Steps
Confirm DEF quality condition clears after refill.
Verify SPN 4094 FMI 31 does not return after repair.
Confirm SCR efficiency returns to normal after repair.
Monitor for return of DEF quality conditions over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use OEM-specification DEF only.
✓ Inspect DEF quality at every DEF fill.
✓ Inspect quality sensor connector for urea crystal corrosion at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium progressing to High as inducement approaches. Severity
Medium progressing to High as inducement approaches. DEF quality conditions are fluid diagnoses before parts replacement.
symptoms: DEF quality condition
Bad DEF code
Quality inducement warning
Contaminated DEF fault
Sensor replaced before fluid proof
procedures_full.source_title: SPN 4094 FMI 31 — DEF Quality Condition Exists

procedures_full.overview: The system has determined the DEF doesn't meet the required quality spec (the fluid should be ~32.5% urea). Poor DEF quality cripples NOx reduction and triggers an inducement/derate countdown if not corrected.
procedures_full.severity_action: Power derate likely — plan to stop soon
causes: Contaminated, diluted, expired, or counterfeit DEF in the tank
Water or fuel accidentally added to the DEF tank
DEF quality sensor fault reporting bad fluid
Old DEF that degraded from heat or long storage
first_moves: Test or refractometer-check the DEF; if in doubt, drain and refill with fresh in-spec DEF.
Make sure nothing but DEF went in the tank — water or diesel will fail quality immediately.
After refilling with good fluid, the system needs to re-evaluate quality over a drive cycle.
If fresh, verified DEF still fails, suspect the quality sensor.
common_misdiagnoses: Assuming the sensor is bad when the DEF was actually contaminated or diluted.
Topping off bad DEF with good DEF instead of draining — it still reads out of spec.
Ignoring it until the inducement derate caps the truck's speed.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 136: Transmission Primary Shift Up Selector
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the Transmission Requested Gear (PRNDL) message from the Primary and Secondary Automated Driving System (ADS) sources in the ADS Electronic Control Unit (ECU) over the Primary Data Link (J1939A). This redundancy allows the TCM to maintain transmission function in a degraded mode in the event the message is not available from one of the ADS sources.

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) communicates with the Hybrid Control Module (HCM) over the J1939 data link during vehicle operation to exchange requested gear and current gear information.
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: TECU ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. No J1939 data link fault currently Active in the TECU.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 9 is set when the TECU fails to receive transmission data (such as a requested gear) for 2 seconds or greater from the HCM, and it is still communicating with other modules on J1939. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the) Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after it has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: When Code 24 is set the following conditions occur: Red “Service” light illuminates, and an “F” flashes in the gear display. Fault is stored in TECU memory. Operation mode changes to AutoShift Fallback mode. If the fault sets at power up, the engine does not crank. If the fault sets while driving, the vehicle remains in current gear. When the vehicle stops the clutch opens and remains in this position. Amber “Check Hybrid” light may display on the dash due to an Active Fault Code 48. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after it has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.possible_causes: This fault code can be caused by any of the following: FMI 9 J1939 Data Link HCM

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 24 - J1939 HCM Message Fault
procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) communicates with the Hybrid Control Module (HCM) over the J1939 Data Link during vehicle operation to exchange requested gear and current gear information.
procedures_full.detection: Fault is detected when: TECU ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. No J1939 Data Link fault currently Active in the TECU.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions may set the fault Active: FMI 9 is set when the TECU fails to receive transmission data (such as requested gear) for 2 seconds or greater from the HCM, while still communicating with other modules on J1939. Note: When troubleshooting an Inactive code refer to the Product Diagnostic Mode (PDM) .
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 24 is set, the following conditions occur: Red “Service” light illuminates and an “F” and flashes in the gear display. Fault is stored in TECU memory. Operation mode changes to AutoShift Fallback If the fault sets at power up, the engine does not crank. If the fault sets while driving, the vehicle remains in current gear. When the vehicle stops, the clutch opens and remains in this position. Amber “Check Hybrid” light may display on the dash due to an Active Fault Code 48.

steps.A:
A. Check for active or inactive fault code status and perform Electrical Pretest. 
 Retrieve Active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector. Verify Fault Code 24 is Active. 
 Perform Electrical Pretest. 
 If no issues found during the Electrical Pretest, Go to Step B 
 If issue was repaired during the Electrical Pretest, Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Verify continuity of Vehicle Harness. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect negative battery cable. 
 Disconnect HCM Vehicle Harness 38-Way Connector. 
 Measure resistance between HCM Vehicle Harness 38-Way Connector Pin 2 and Pin 3. 
 Note: Make sure the volt/ohm meter is on the proper scale (around 200 ohm scale). 
 If resistance between Pin 2 and Pin 3 is between 50–70 ohms, replace HCM. See Warnings & Cautions procedure in TRSM2000, then Go to Step V 
 If resistance is outside of range, repair J1939 Data link Harness, then Go to Step V 
 Connection Measurement 
 Pin 2 to Pin 3

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with position sensors to monitor shift rail positions and speed sensors to monitor shaft speeds. The sensor information is provided to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of making shift decisions, confirming gear engagement, and monitoring shift rail positions. The TCM compares the shift rail commands to the shift rail positions and shaft speeds (ratio calculation) to ensure the transmission is operating properly. The sensors and shift rails are located in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the transmission operation. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: Inappropriate requested gear commanded relative to the selected gear.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 12: Amber warning lamp on Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO Mode prohibited If vehicle is moving: Red stop lamp on Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.

procedures_full.overview_tr: Endurant XD Serisi şanzımanlar, vites rayı konumlarını izlemek için konum sensörleri ve mil devirlerini izlemek için devir sensörleri ile donatılmıştır. Sensör bilgileri, vites değişimi kararları vermek, vites takılmasını doğrulamak ve vites rayı konumlarını izlemek amacıyla Şanzıman Kontrol Modülüne (TCM) iletilir. TCM, şanzımanın düzgün çalıştığından emin olmak için vites rayı komutlarını vites rayı konumları ve mil devirleriyle (oran hesaplaması) karşılaştırır. Sensörler ve vites rayları Mekatronik Şanzıman Modülünde (MTM) bulunur ve 74 Yollu Şanzıman Kablo Demeti Konnektöründe TCM'ye bağlıdır.
procedures_full.detection_tr: TCM, şanzıman çalışmasını izler. Bir sistem arızası tespit edilirse arıza aktif olarak ayarlanır.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically both Cruise Control switches, SET and RES, are shorted to ground.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically both Cruise Control switches, SET and RES, are shorted to ground.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF) and place the Cruise Control Switch in the OFF position. DO NOT start the engine.
Check the driver console display.
If Cruise Control switch status RES is displayed, go to step 3.
If Cruise Control switch status SET is displayed, go to step 4.
Unplug the RES Cruise Control Switch.
If RES status is no longer displayed, replace the Cruise Control RES Switch. Refer to "47.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If RES status is still displayed, repair the short to ground in the wire from the RES switch to pin 16 of the CPC #1 connector. Refer to "47.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Unplug the SET Cruise Control Switch.
If SET status is no longer displayed, replace the Cruise Control SET Switch. Refer to "47.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If SET status is still displayed, repair the short to ground in the wire from the SET switch to pin 12 of the CPC #1 connector. Refer to "47.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 47.1 SPN 599/FMI 4 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

field_evidence.title: Freightliner Cascadia 2024 ABS SPN 627 FMI 17 Code Fix
field_evidence.excerpt: The Freightliner Cascadia 2024 may experience issues related to its Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), specifically displaying an SPN 627 FMI 17 error code. This code points to a fault in the ABS wheel speed sensor circuit, which plays a crucial role in maintaining safe braking performance. These ABS sensor faults can stem from problems such as damaged or dirty wheel speed sensors, as well as issues with the sensor wiring and connectors. Common wiring problems include corrosion, breaks, or loose connections that interfere with proper sensor operation. To address this error code, begin by inspecting the affected wheel speed sensor for any visible damage or debris buildup. Cleaning the sensor and its tone ring can sometimes resolve the issue. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 37 - Power Supply
dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates excessive resistance has been detected between the power supply source (battery or starter) and the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
causes: Corrosion on power supply or ground supply connections or wires to the
steps: A. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Inspect starter/battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. Measure voltage across batteries. If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required. Go to Step B If voltage is outside of range Repair or replace batteries and charging system as required. Repeat this step.

B. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port. Locate diagnostic port on Transmission Harness. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. If voltage is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step C If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.

C. Measure battery voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Locate diagnostic port on Transmission Harness. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step D If voltage is outside of rang, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

D. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E If voltage is outside of range, repair ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

E. Visually inspect batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Disconnect negative battery cable. Disconnect the Vehicle Harness 38-way. Inspect main power 38-way connector terminals Pin 36 and Pin 38, in-line fuse holder, and power supply connections for integrity and corrosion. If no problem found, Go to Step V If problem is found, repair power/ground path for the main power supply. Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Clean and reconnect all connectors. Key on. Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code Check for codes See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no codes, test complete. If Fault Code 37 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 37 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 37: Power Connect
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with electronic components that require a high current. It is critical that the OEM power supply be able to deliver the proper voltage and current in these high-load situations for smooth and efficient shifting. Additional resistance introduced into the system can cause the supplied voltage to drop low enough to cause performance issues. Fault Code 37 indicates an excessive resistance between the power supply source (battery or starter) and the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. Notice Fault Code 37 indicates there is high resistance in the vehicle power supply to the TECU. Consult OEM diagnostics for more detailed troubleshooting. If Fault Code 37 is Inactive and there are Active vehicle faults, refer to OEM for additional diagnostic instructions. If Fault Code 37 is Inactive and there are Active transmission faults, troubleshoot all Active fault codes per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . If Fault Code 37 is Active or Inactive, and there are no Active vehicle or transmission faults, Go to Step B

SPN_627.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_627.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with electronic components that require a high current. It is critical that the OEM power supply be able to deliver the proper voltage and current in these high-load situations for smooth and efficient shifting. Additional resistance introduced into the system can cause the supplied voltage to drop low enough to cause performance issues. Fault Code 37 indicates an excessive resistance between the power supply source (battery or starter) and the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
procedures_full.detection: The TECU monitors the OEM power supply circuit for excessive resistance by measuring the voltage drop during high current demands, such as a shift request, and calculates a resistance value based on those demands. Fault Code 37 sets Active when the calculated resistance during high-load conditions exceeds 0.4 ohms and the TECU has not detected any low or weak battery system faults.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: TECU calculates a resistance value based on high current demands and sets the fault code Active when that resistance exceeds 0.4 ohms.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: TECU calculates a resistance value below 0.4 ohms.
procedures_full.fallback: No fallback mode is associated with this fault; however, transmission performance issues may be presented. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive TECU calculates a resistance value below 0.4 ohms.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 5 Vehicle Power Supply In-line fuse corrosion or loose connection Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals Vehicle Batteries Internal failure or high resistance Component Identification 1. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 2. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU)

SPN_748.pgn_description: This message will be transmitted by several types of retarding devices such as engine compression release brakes, exhaust system restriction brakes, and driveline retarders using hydraulic, electric, or mechanical friction to slow the vehicle. procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) sends and receives the Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control message to and from a vehicle Electronic Control Unit (ECU) over the Primary Data Link (J1939A). This message is used by the TCM to confirm the Engine ECU is receiving messages and responding to its messages.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control messages. If messages are not received or are invalid, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: Engine ECU did not respond TCM command messages for 5 seconds. FMI 13 – Out Of Calibration: Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control message not available for 5 seconds. FMI 19 – Received Network Data In Error: Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control message received but in error for 5 seconds.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 12: Engine ECU responding to TCM messages for 1 second. FMI 13, 19: Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control messages available and valid for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 12, 13, 19: Amber warning lamp on Note: Vehicle may have additional fallback modes. Refer to OEM. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 12: Engine ECU responding to TCM messages for 1 second. FMI 13, 19: Source Address of Controlling Device for Engine Control messages available and valid for 10 seconds.

field_evidence.title: MaxxForce 13 Injector Codes SPN 2797 & 2798 Troubleshooting
field_evidence.excerpt: The MaxxForce 13 engine frequently encounters issues with injector misfires and persistent fault codes, specifically SPN 2797 and 2798 accompanied by FMI 3 and 4. These fault codes point to problems in the injector circuits or mechanical injector failures. Even after replacing injectors 3 and 6, these codes can remain, indicating underlying issues beyond the injectors themselves. Persistent fault codes after injector replacement can stem from damaged wiring harnesses, poor electrical connections, or faults within the engine control module (ECM). To address these concerns, it is important to carefully inspect the injector wiring connectors for signs of corrosion or breaks. field_evidence.excerpt: The MaxxForce 11/13 engines from model years 2010 to 2012 commonly experience crank no start problems linked to camshaft sensor signal loss. This issue is identified by the diagnostic code SPN 636 FMI 10, which points to a fault in the camshaft position sensor signal. A camshaft position sensor signal fault can cause the engine to fail to start because the Engine Control Module (ECM) relies on this signal to manage fuel injection and ignition timing. Without a proper camshaft signal, the ECM cannot properly control these critical engine functions, resulting in a no-start condition. procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, 2, or 3 needle control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, 2, or 3 needle control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
steps: Short to Battery/Power Check
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 on the MCM side of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 26 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "95.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, go to step 4.
Measure the voltage between pin 2 on the MCM side of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 3 of the Front Injector Harness connector and pin 22 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "95.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 5 of the Front Injector Harness connector and pin 24 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "95.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 95.1 SPN 2797/FMI 3 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, 2, or 3 needle control valve circuit is shorted to ground.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, 2, or 3 needle control valve circuit is shorted to ground.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Disconnect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary.
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 3.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 11.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 4.
Remove the valve cover.
Disconnect injector #1.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #1 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #1 injector. Refer to "95.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 7.
Disconnect injector #2.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 of the valve cover side on the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #2 pin 1 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #2 injector. Refer to "95.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 9.
Disconnect injector #3.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 on the valve cover side of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #3 injector. Refer to "95.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover Injector Harness. Refer to "95.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 10 on the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #3 pin 1 and ground.

If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 11 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 10 of the Front Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "95.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 95.2 SPN 2797/FMI 4 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, #2 and #3 unit pump control circuits are shorted to battery/power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #1, #2 and #3 unit pump control circuits are shorted to battery/power.‪
steps: Short to Battery/Power Check
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Using the J-48475 breakout box and appropriate overlay, connect the MCM side of the harness ONLY.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 15 of the J-48475 breakout box and ground.
If voltage is greater than 0.5 V, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for authorization to replace the MCM..
If no voltage is present, go to the next step.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Connect the Engine Harness side of the J-48475 breakout box.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Disconnect the #1 unit pump.
Measure the voltage between pin 14 of the MCM 120–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short circuit to power between pin 14 of the MCM 120–pin connector and the #1 unit pump. See Figure
"Unit Pumps #1, 2, and 3"
. Refer to "99.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, go to the next step.
Figure 1. Unit Pumps #1, 2, and 3
Disconnect the #2 unit pump.
Measure the voltage between pin 10 of the MCM 120–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short circuit to power between pin 10 of the MCM 120–pin connector and the #2 unit pump. See Figure
"Unit Pumps #1, 2, and 3"
. Refer to "99.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, go to the next step.
Disconnect the #3 unit pump.
Measure the voltage between pin 12 of the MCM 120–pin connector and ground.
If voltage is present, repair the short circuit to power between pins 12 of the MCM 120–pin connector and the #3 unit pump. See Figure
"Unit Pumps #1, 2, and 3"
. Refer to "99.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no voltage is present, repair the short circuit to power between pins 10, 12 and/or 14 of the MCM 120–pin connector and unit pumps #1, 2, or 3. Refer to "99.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to the next step.

If “PTO 2” Current Value indicates “Disabled” and a PTO is properly installed and wired, select a “Hardwire Control Only” option and follow on-screen prompts. procedures_full.overview: The Endurant HD Transmission incorporates enhanced controls for Power Take-Off (PTO) operation. When PTO operation is required the Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives a request (Input) for PTO operation, determines if operating conditions are suitable, and supplies a signal (Output) to engage the PTO. Once engaged the TCM receives a confirmation to complete the operation. Reference Endurant HD Driver Instructions based on transmission model (TRDR0950/TRDR0955) for PTO operation. The TCM can be configured to operate a PTO with messages over the vehicle Primary Data Link J1939A or from a PTO switch circuit hardwired directly to the TCM. The TCM is equipped to receive 4 switch inputs and control 3 relay outputs that can be configured in an Input/Output (I/O) Package to support various vocational features. If the TCM is configured to "J1939 Control Only", PTO operation messages are exchanged between the TCM and a OEM vehicle ECU. If the TCM is configured to "Hardwire Control Only, PTO operation is controlled by Input and Output signals from a hardwired switch circuit. The TCM has the functionality to support operation of two PTOs at the same time; one over the Primary Data Link
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the PTO 2 Confirm J1939 messages or the hardwired PTO 2 Confirm circuit input signal. If the messages or signal are not received or are invalid, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: PTO 2 Confirm circuit output signal shorted to ground for 5 seconds. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: PTO 2 Confirm message or signal received but PTO 2 Engage not commanded. FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: PTO 2 Confirm messages not received for 5 seconds. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: TCM has detected an internal processing error. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: PTO 2 Confirm message not available for 5 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: The TCM detected invalid I/O Package calibration. FMI 19 – Received Network Data in Error: PTO 2 Confirm messages invalid for 5 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: PTO 2 Confirm circuit input signal out of range (4.00-5.25 V) for 5 seconds. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: The TCM detected invalid I/O Package calibration.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 4: PTO 2 Confirm circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 7: PTO 2 Confirm circuit signal not continuously grounded. FMI 9, 13, 19: PTO 2 Confirm messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exits. FMI 14, 31: Valid I/O Package calibration file is configured in TCM. FMI 20: PTO 2 Confirm circuit input signal in range for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Amber warning lamp on PTO 2 Mode prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 4: PTO 2 Confirm circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 7: PTO 2 Confirm circuit signal not continuously grounded. FMI 9, 13, 19: PTO 2 Confirm messages received and valid for 10 seconds. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exits. FMI 14, 31: Valid I/O Package calibration file is configured in TCM. FMI 20: PTO 2 Confirm circuit input signal in range for 10 seconds.

procedures_full.overview: The Procision Transmission incorporates enhanced controls for Power Takeoff (PTO) operation. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives a request (input) to actuate the PTO, determines if conditions are suitable for PTO operation and supplies an output to engage the PTO. Once the PTO is engaged, the TCM receives a confirmation (input) that the PTO is engaged to complete the operation. The TCM can be configured to control the PTO with messages over the vehicle J1939 Data Link (J1939 controlled) and/or relay circuit hardwired directly to the TCM (Hardwire controlled). The PTO J1939 controlled messages are received by the TCM from an OEM Body Control Module. The PTO Hardwire controlled signal wiring connects to the TCM through the 20-Way TCM Body Harness Connector. The PTO 2 Confirm switch input is Pin 16 (2.5 - 5.5 V reference voltage). Once the PTO is engaged, the PTO 2 Confirm switch is closed to vehicle ground causing the reference voltage to go to 0 V and PTO 2 operation to occur. The PTO and associated wiring are installed by the OEM or body builder, reference Eaton PTO Information Guide TRIG2600 for PTO system installation and wiring diagrams.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the PTO 2 Confirm Hardwire (HW) controlled input signal (Pin 16) and/or the J1939 controlled message from the OEM Body Control Module. If the PTO 2 Confirm input signal or J1939 message is out of range, the fault is set Active.

FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: PTO 2 Engage command not given, but PTO 2 Confirm message or signal indicates engaged. FMI 9 – Abnormal Update Rate: PTO 2 Confirm J1939 controlled message not received for 5 seconds. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: PTO 2 Confirm J1939 controlled message not available for 5 seconds. FMI 19 – Received Network Data in Error: PTO 2 Confirm J1939 controlled message invalid for 5 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: PTO 2 Confirm hardwire controlled signal indicated 4.0–5.25 V for 1 second. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: PTO 2 Confirm hardwire controlled signal indicated 1.5–2.5 V for 1 second.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmission incorporates enhanced controls for Power Take-Off (PTO) operation. When PTO operation is required the Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives a request (Input) for PTO operation, determines if operating conditions are suitable, and supplies a signal (Output) to engage the PTO. Once engaged the TCM receives a confirmation to complete the operation. Reference Endurant XD Driver Instructions TRDR0960 for PTO operation. The TCM can be configured to operate a PTO with messages over the vehicle Primary Data Link J1939A or from a PTO switch circuit hardwired directly to the TCM. The TCM is equipped to receive 4 switch inputs and control 3 relay outputs that can be configured in an Input/Output (I/O) Package to support various vocational features. If the TCM is configured to "J1939 Control Only", PTO operation messages are exchanged between the TCM and a OEM vehicle ECU. If the TCM is configured to "Hardwire Control Only, PTO operation is controlled by Input and Output signals from a hardwired switch circuit. The TCM has the functionality to support operation of two PTOs at the same time; one over the Primary Data Link J1939A and one from a hardwired
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the PTO 2 Confirm J1939 messages or the hardwired PTO 2 Confirm circuit input signal. If the messages or signal are not received or are invalid, the fault is set Active.

causes: Upon activation, the ECM engages a torque derate strategy, reducing maximum fuel injection quantity by up to 40% to limit peak cylinder pressure below 180 bar
On Bosch EDC17 systems, the engine speed is also capped at 1800 rpm
The fault remains active until the pressure drops below the threshold for 10 seconds and a manual reset is performed via

Harness Chafing: Wiring insulation worn through against metal brackets, causing a direct ground path

steps: Missing ESS Message Check
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, troubleshoot and repair the CAN line.
If only a “J1939 Error” fault is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, check the proper configuration of the CPC.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 2789 FMI 14 means the VGT actuator couldn't reach its commanded vane position. It's a High severity fault causing turbo lag and boost problems, often from a soot-packed unison ring or a failing actuator. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com fields this call constantly on high-mileage DD15s that spend a lot of time idling - soot accumulation on the turbo's unison ring is the usual culprit, and it's an easy one to misdiagnose as a bad actuator.
causes: Soot-packed unison ring inside the turbo
A mechanical restriction, not an electrical fault - carbon buildup physically prevents the vanes from moving even when the actuator is commanding correctly.
Failing actuator motor or internal gear train
An electromechanical actuator failure where the motor itself can no longer produce enough force to move the vanes through their full range.
Corroded or chafed actuator harness connector
An electrical/wiring fault - a poor connection can make a mechanically healthy actuator appear to lag or fail position feedback.
Carbon-fouled exhaust piping restricting vane movement indirectly
A secondary mechanical issue where backpressure downstream makes vane movement harder even with a functioning actuator.
steps: Connect Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) and run the VGT actuator sweep test to command the vanes through their full range.
Watch actual vs. commanded position on the sweep - a lag of more than a couple percent or vanes that stop short indicate mechanical binding.
With the engine off and cool, access the turbo actuator linkage and manually check for smooth travel through its full arc; gritty or seized movement points to soot-packed unison ring binding.
Inspect the actuator's electrical connector and 5-pin harness for corrosion or chafing against the turbo housing, since heat-cycled wiring in this location fails often.

If the actuator sweeps freely on the bench but binds on the engine, the turbo's internal unison ring is soot-packed and needs cleaning or the turbo needs replacement - a new actuator alone won't fix it.
symptoms: Noticeable turbo lag or flat power delivery under acceleration
Whistling, fluttering, or surging exhaust note
Check engine light, sometimes with a companion boost or exhaust pressure code
Elevated exhaust gas temperatures under load

procedures_full.overview: FMI 2 on vehicle control module data indicates the ECM received erratic or inconsistent data from a vehicle control source. Intermittent network, module power dropouts, poor grounds, failing module, and aftermarket device interference are the primary causes. Intermittent grounds creating erratic data across multiple systems are a documented pattern on multiplexed HD chassis. Replacing a module for erratic data without proving power, ground, and network integrity produces repeat faults when the root cause is a ground or network fault.
causes: Intermittent network — network physical layer fault producing erratic data
Module power dropouts — intermittent module power supply
Poor grounds — poor module ground producing erratic data
Failing module — module degradation producing erratic output
Aftermarket device interference — aftermarket node interfering with network data
steps: Single Action Gate — Check System Voltage Events

Check for system voltage events coinciding with erratic data faults. Intermittent grounds creating erratic data across multiple systems are a documented pattern. Confirm system voltage is stable during the fault condition. A voltage event coinciding with erratic data confirms a power or ground fault rather than a module fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Module Power and Ground Integrity

Verify module power and ground integrity. Perform voltage-drop tests on module power and ground circuits. A significant voltage drop on the module power or ground circuit confirms a wiring fault. Confirm module power and ground integrity before any network or module diagnosis.
Override Manager — Isolate Aftermarket Nodes

Identify and isolate aftermarket nodes on the network. Aftermarket devices connected to the J1939 network can interfere with network data and produce erratic data faults. Disconnect aftermarket nodes one at a time and retest for erratic data. A fault that clears when an aftermarket node is disconnected confirms aftermarket interference.
Safety Interceptor — Network Physical Layer Tests

Perform network physical layer tests. Verify network termination resistance, bias voltage, and backbone integrity. A network physical layer fault produces erratic data across multiple modules simultaneously. Repair network physical layer faults before any module replacement.
Resume Point — Identify Missing or Erratic Source Address

Identify the missing or erratic source address on the network. A specific source address that is consistently erratic or missing confirms the fault is isolated to that module or its network connection. A fault that moves between source addresses confirms a network physical layer fault.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Data Stability Confirmation
After repair, verify network data is stable across all modules. Confirm SPN 612 FMI 2 does not return. Monitor for return of random warning lights or multiple module faults.
Repair Ledger Output — Ground, Network, Aftermarket, or Module Decision

Repair ground or power fault if confirmed. Repair network physical layer fault if confirmed. Remove or correct aftermarket node if interference is confirmed. Replace module only after power, ground, network, and aftermarket interference are eliminated and module failure is proven.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair module ground or power fault.
2 . Repair network physical layer fault.
3 . Remove or correct aftermarket node if interference is confirmed.
4 . Replace module only after power, ground, and network integrity are confirmed.
Verification Steps
Confirm network data is stable across all modules after repair.
Verify SPN 612 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm no random warning lights or multiple module faults after repair.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect module ground connections at every major service.
✓ Verify aftermarket network nodes are compatible and properly installed.
✓ Inspect network backbone connectors for corrosion at every major service.
✓ Inspect module power supply fuses and connections at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High depending on affected brakes or powertrain controllers. Erratic control-module data is usually power, ground, or network health — module replacement is the last step.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 117: Engine Source Address
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives a Source Address message from the engine control module over the Primary Data Link (J1939A). This information is used to determine transmission operation.
causes: Vehicle Components Engine Source Address message not enabled Other vehicle ECU(s) faulted Vehicle Harness - Primary Data Link (J1939A) Shorted to power, shorted to ground or open circuit Terminals bent, spread, corroded, or loose Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system. Additional Tools None
steps: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 117 is Inactive and there are other Active vehicle or transmission fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes. Go to Step V If Fault Code 117 FMI 9 is Active or Inactive, refer to OEM guidelines for repair of the Engine Source Address (SPN 2000). Go to Step V

V. Verify Repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 117 sets Active, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 117 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code 175: Engine Requested Torque .

SPN_2000.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_2000.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: This fault is typically the J1939 CCVS message from Source #1, #2, or #3 is missing.‪
causes: This fault is typically the J1939 CCVS message from Source #1, #2, or #3 is missing.‪
steps: Missing J1939 CCVS Message from Source #1, #2, or #3 Check
Check for multiple codes:
If CPC SPN 168/FMI 0/14/18 (Battery Voltage) are present troubleshoot these first.
If MCM SPN 625/FMI 9 is present, troubleshoot and repair the CAN line.
If only a “J1939 Error” fault is present, go to step 2.
Has the CPC been recently reprogrammed?
If yes, check the proper configuration of the CPC.

If no, connect ServiceLink to determine which modules are configured for the vehicle and their communication status. Once this is done, follow the appropriate module communication troubleshooting procedures for the affected module.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 43.1 SPN 527/FMI 9 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

SPN_4376.description_en: Fault: urea reversing valve top end drive control circuit short to power supply
causes: The valve controls whether DEF flows to the injector or returns to tank
Technicians often see this code after a failed system self-test following a DEF tank replacement or after a frozen pump event
Electrically, the valve coil resistance should measure 4.5-5.5 ohms at 20°C. A debouncing timer in the ECM firmware filters transient noise
As a safety fallback, the ECM commands the diverter valve to 100% recirculation (full return to tank) and disables all DEF dosing
Simultaneously, the engine torque is derated by 75% to prevent NOx breakthrough
The fault must be cleared via
Upon activation, the ECM forces the diverter valve to 0% duty (full recirculation) to stop DEF delivery
Simultaneously, a torque derate of 25% is applied immediately, increasing to 40% after 1 hour of operation

[FMI 2 katalog] Aktüatör konum geri bildirimini ve sinyal tutarlılığını izleyin; aralıklı temassızlık arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

[FMI 4 katalog] Aktüatör besleme hattında gerilim düşüklüğü ve şasi teması arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

[FMI 12 katalog] Aktüatör sürücü modülünün beslemesini ve haberleşmesini kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 985: Two Speed Axle Message
procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmission can be combined with a 2-speed axle for additional gear ratio coverage. When 2-speed axle operation is required the Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives an axle gear engagement signal (Input) then adjusts the transmission shift strategy and launch characteristics for the new axle gear ratio. Reference Endurant XD Driver Instructions TRDR0960 for Two-Speed Axle operation. The TCM can be configured for operation with a 2-speed axle with messages over the vehicle Primary Data Link J1939A or from a switch circuit hardwired directly to the TCM. The TCM is equipped to receive 4 switch inputs and control 3 relay outputs that can be configured in an Input/Output (I/O) Package to support various vocational features. If the TCM is configured to "2-Speed Axle - J1939", axle gear engagement messages are provided to the TCM by an OEM vehicle ECU.
