procedures_full.overview: SPN 1188 FMI 3 means the wastegate actuator position feedback sensor circuit is reading above normal voltage, an electrical fault distinct from a mechanically stuck wastegate. It's a medium-severity code with no derate - check the harness before replacing the sensor. This is a feedback circuit fault, not a mechanical turbo problem, so don't let the word wastegate send you straight to the actuator or drive circuit. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com always confirms which specific wastegate-related SPN is active before diagnosing, since several closely related codes cover different parts of the same system.
causes: Chafed or heat-damaged signal wire near the turbocharger
Prolonged heat exposure near the turbo can degrade wire insulation, allowing the signal wire to short against a powered or grounded surface.
Corroded connector pin
Moisture intrusion at the turbo-area connector can corrode pins, producing an intermittent high-voltage reading.
Internally failed position sensor
Heat cycling can degrade the sensor's internal element, presenting as an open circuit that mimics the same fault.
steps: Pull the fault and freeze-frame data on PACCAR Davie4 to confirm the position reading is pinned at an unrealistic value.
Locate the wastegate actuator position sensor at the turbocharger and unplug the connector.
Back-probe signal and ground with a multimeter, key on engine off - a reading near 5V with the sensor disconnected confirms a harness-side fault.
Inspect the signal wire for chafing or heat damage along its routing near the turbocharger housing.
Test the sensor directly at the connector if a bench specification is available to rule out an internally open sensor.
Repair the wiring or replace the sensor as needed, then clear the code and confirm accurate position feedback returns during a boost sweep.
symptoms: Check engine lamp illuminated, typically no derate
Possible inconsistent boost pressure or minor turbo lag
No major drivability complaint in most cases
procedures_full.source_title: PACCAR SPN 1188 FMI 3: Wastegate Actuator Position Circuit Voltage High

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1188 FMI 3 means wastegate position feedback voltage is above normal. Unplug the sensor and test for a harness short to power before replacing the actuator or sensor. Peterbilt operators often get SPN 1188 FMI 3 as a standalone electrical fault without immediate derate, but ProfessionalDieselRepair.com still treats it as a boost-control priority because the ECM may revert to safe fueling that feels like a soft power cut on grades.
causes: Signal wire shorted to 5 V or 12 V supply
Rubbed harness or pinched loom ties force the position signal high regardless of actual wastegate angle.
Open sensor ground or return circuit
High resistance on the ground side floats the signal high and mimics a shorted sensor.
Internally failed position sensor potentiometer
Sensor internal open pulls the ECM input high through pull-up circuitry.
steps: Record freeze-frame wastegate position voltage in Davie4 when SPN 1188 FMI 3 set—values stuck above 4.8 V confirm a high circuit fault.
Disconnect the position sensor at the turbo actuator and measure signal wire to ground with key on: above 4.5 V with sensor unplugged indicates harness short to power.
Inspect the three-wire harness along the turbo heat shield for melted insulation or contact with the actuator bracket.
Test sensor resistance per Peterbilt spec—typically 1-5 kΩ sweep across travel on potentiometer-type sensors; an open sensor reads infinite resistance.
Repair harness shorts or replace the position sensor, then clear codes and verify 0.5-4.5 V sweep during a commanded wastegate test.
symptoms: Check engine lamp with no immediate shutdown on most calibrations
Boost gauge may hunt or lag compared with throttle demand
Position sensor pinned near 5 V in PACCAR Davie4 live data
Occasional turbo whistle or mild overboost on hard acceleration
Fault may appear after pressure-washing the engine bay or connector service
procedures_full.source_title: Peterbilt SPN 1188 FMI 3: Wastegate Actuator Position Voltage High

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1188 FMI 3 on Detroit engines means the wastegate actuator position circuit is reading voltage above normal, consistent with a short to a high-voltage source. This is a medium-severity, largely electrical fault best fixed by checking the harness before replacing the actuator. SPN 1188 covers the wastegate actuator's position feedback circuit, and FMI 3 specifically points to a voltage-above-normal condition on that signal wire. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this fault almost exclusively from harness damage - the actuator sits right against the turbocharger housing in an area that runs extremely hot, and insulation there degrades faster than almost anywhere else on the engine. Diagnosing it correctly means pin-testing the circuit for a short before assuming the actuator itself has failed.
causes: Chafed or heat-damaged wiring harness near the turbo
The high-temperature environment around the turbocharger degrades wire insulation over time, eventually allowing the signal wire to short against a power source or ground.
Corroded or damaged connector at the actuator
Moisture intrusion or physical damage at the connector can create an unintended electrical path that mimics a short-to-high fault.
Internal actuator sensor failure
The position sensor inside the actuator itself can fail electrically, though this is less common than external harness damage.
ECM-side driver circuit fault
A failure inside the ECM's input circuit for this signal is uncommon but possible, usually only after ruling out the harness and actuator.
steps: Pull the fault with Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) and confirm SPN 1188 FMI 3 is active or stored, and check whether it's accompanied by any actuator response codes.

Locate the wastegate actuator connector near the turbocharger and visually inspect for melted insulation, heat damage, or a pinched wire against the exhaust manifold - this circuit runs in a very hot area and is prone to chafing.
Disconnect the connector and use a multimeter to check the position sensor signal wire for a short to the 5V reference or battery voltage with the harness disconnected from the ECM.
Check resistance to ground on the signal circuit - it should read as an open circuit (infinite resistance); any continuity to ground or to a power source confirms a chafed or pinched wire.
Repair or replace the damaged section of harness with heat-resistant loom appropriate for the turbo's high-temperature environment, rather than standard wire loom that will degrade again quickly.
Clear the code and verify actuator position tracks correctly through a commanded sweep test on DDDL before considering the repair complete.
symptoms: Inconsistent boost behavior - sometimes normal, sometimes sluggish
Amber Check Engine lamp
Occasional rough transitions between boost levels during acceleration
No consistent drivability complaint in many cases - purely a stored electrical fault

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 spill control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 spill control valve circuit has a short to battery/power.‪
steps: Short to Battery/Power Check
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 1 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and pin 4 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, go to step 4.
Measure the voltage between pin 8 on the MCM side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If there is voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 8 of the Rear Injector Harness connector and pin 8 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If there is no voltage present, repair the short to power between pin 12 of the Rear Injector Harness connector and pin 6 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 spill control valve circuit has a short to ground.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically injector #4, 5, or 6 spill control valve circuit has a short to ground.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Disconnect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Inspect the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector for bent or spread pins, inspect the connector seal for damage (signs of water or oil intrusion).
If the water or oil intrusion, bent or spread pins are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If connector shows no signs of damage, go to step 3.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 4.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Measure the resistance between pin 7 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 5.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Measure the resistance between pin 11 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #6 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 13.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 6.
Remove the upper valve cover.
Disconnect injector #4.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #4 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #4. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 9.
Disconnect injector #5.
Measure the resistance between pin 7 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #5 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace injector #5. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, go to step 11.
Disconnect injector #6.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 on the valve cover side of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground. If you are using J-48671–10 , measure between injector #6 pin 3 and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the #6 injector. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the under valve cover injector harness. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 15.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 5 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 4 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 7 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, go to step 16.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 7 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 7 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector. Refer to "131.2.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 11 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement authorization.
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 9 of the MCM 120–pin connector and pin 11 of the Rear Injector Harness 12–pin connector.
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

SPN_4811.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_4811.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).
causes: Sensor Failure: Internal ASIC or microcontroller within the pressure sensor has failed, reporting a
Sensor Replacement Event: New piston cooling gallery pressure sensor installed requiring manufacturer-specific calibration sequence through proprietary service software interface
ECM Programming Update: Engine control module software update necessitates special initialization procedures for piston cooling oil pressure monitoring system
System Maintenance Mode: Triggered during scheduled maintenance requiring special
steps: Kılavuz Sensör Verilerini Doğrulama: J1939 arıza tespit cihazı kullanarak yağ galerisi basıncını ana yağ basıncıyla karşılaştırın; galeri basıncı 100-200 kPa daha düşük olmalıdır. Emniyet Valfini İnceleme: Piston soğutma galerisi basınç tahliye valfini söküp temizleyin

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Silindir kapağı yakınındaki motor kablo demetini özellikle son onarımlardan sonra ezilmiş veya sürtünmüş kablolar açısından kontrol edin. Sensör Konnektör Testi: Sensörde sinyal (pin B) ile şasi (pin C) arasındaki gerilimi ölçün
Kılavuz Arıza Kodu Taraması: Tüm aktif ve pasif arıza kodlarını okumak için bir J1939 arıza tespit cihazı kullanın
steps_en_archive: Guide Verify Sensor Data: Use J1939 tool to compare gallery pressure with main oil pressure. Gallery should be 100-200 kPa lower. Inspect Relief Valve: Remove and clean the piston cooling gallery pressure relief valve

Guide Visual Inspection: Check engine harness for chafed or pinched wires near cylinder head, especially after recent repairs. Sensor Connector Test: Measure voltage between signal (pin B) and ground (pin C) at sensor
Guide Scan for Codes: Use a J1939 diagnostic tool to read all active and inactive codes

causes: Technicians should ensure that all components are calibrated post-repair
Real-world examples include workshops installing updated sensors and control modules to enhance system reliability, preventing future occurrences of this fault
steps: Kılavuz Komut Sinyalini Doğrulama: Valf konnektöründe PWM görev döngüsünü (duty cycle) ölçmek için osiloskop kullanın
Kılavuz Görsel Tesisat Muayenesi: ECM konnektöründen valfe giden 2 kablolu devreyi motor bloğu kenarlarındaki aşınmalar açısından inceleyin. Valf Direncini Ölçme: Valf konnektörünü ayırın
Kılavuz PWM Sinyalini Osiloskopla İnceleme: Osiloskobu valf sinyal pimine bağlayın
Solenoid Direncini Ölçün: Valf soketini ayırın

Kılavuz Aktif Arızaları Okuma: SPN 4813 FMI 13'ü doğrulamak ve yağ sıcaklığıyla ilgili dondurulmuş çerçeve verilerini kontrol etmek için J1939 cihazı kullanın. Konnektörü İnceleme: Aktüatör konnektörünü korozyon, eğilmiş pimler veya gevşek terminal tutucuları açısından SAE J1939 standartlarına göre kontrol edin
Valf Süpürme Testi Yapın: Açık ve kapalı konumları yeniden öğrenmek için fabrika onaylı kalibrasyon rutinini başlatın. Yağ Kalitesini Doğrulayın: Yağda çapak/tortu numunesi alın

Kılavuz Kablo Tesisatını İnceleme: ECM'den valfe giden tesisatı her iki konnektörde sürtünme, korozyon veya gevşek pimler açısından kontrol edin. Solenoid Direncini Ölçme: Valf pimlerinde multimetre kullanın
steps_en_archive: Guide Verify Command Signal: Use oscilloscope to measure PWM duty cycle at valve connector
Guide Visual harness inspection: Examine the 2-wire circuit from ECM connector to valve for abrasion near engine block edges. Measure valve resistance: Disconnect valve connector
Guide Scope PWM Signal: Connect scope to valve signal pin
Measure Solenoid Resistance: Disconnect valve

Guide Read Active Faults: Use J1939 tool to confirm SPN 4813 FMI 13 and check associated freeze-frame data for oil temp. Inspect Connector: Check actuator connector for corrosion, bent pins, or loose terminal retention per SAE J1939/
Perform Valve Sweep: Initiate factory-recommended calibration routine to re-learn closed and open positions. Verify Oil Quality: Sample oil for debris
Guide Inspect wiring: Check harness from ECM to valve for chafing, corrosion, or loose pins at both connectors. Measure solenoid resistance: Use multimeter on valve pins

causes: FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.
FMI 6: Current above normal or grounded circuit.
FMI 7: Mechanical system not responding properly.
steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 8 katalog] Sensör sinyal frekansını/nabız genişliğini referans değerle karşılaştırın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.

causes: Technicians often encounter it after replacing an ECM without properly cloning the original source address configuration
When SPN 2029 FMI 11 is active, the ECM activates a safety fallback: it sets the source address to the null address (254) and enters a limited-functionality mode
Torque is derated to 40% in many MAN and Deutz applications to prevent unsafe operation when a critical controller is unreachable
The system will not clear this fault until a valid address claim is received
Long-term prevention involves verifying that all replacement ECUs have their source address correctly programmed via factory
Preventative strategies, such as regular software updates and thorough inspections during ECM replacements, are vital
Technicians should document each step during repairs to avoid recurring faults

Real-world scenarios such as post-ECM replacement checks can prevent SPN 2029 FMI 12. In workshops, ensuring proper component alignment and system recalibrations post-repair minimizes the risk of future issues
steps: Kılavuz Düğüm Adresini Doğrulama: Tüm aktif kaynak adreslerini listelemek ve kaynak adresini (SA) yalnızca tek bir cihazın talep ettiğini doğrulamak için bir J1939 teşhis cihazı kullanın

field_evidence.title: 2013 KW T660 EGR Outlet Pressure Sensor SPN 5019 FMI 2 Issue
field_evidence.excerpt: The 2013 KW T660 truck can experience problems related to the Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) outlet pressure sensor, specifically indicated by the diagnostic code SPN 5019 FMI 2. This code signals an invalid or intermittent signal from the EGR outlet pressure sensor, which can cause the truck’s engine to derate due to inaccurate pressure readings. Faults in the sensor’s signal can stem from a variety of underlying factors including issues with the wiring harness or connector, which may have damage or corrosion. procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on SCR intake temperature indicates the sensor reports above the maximum calibrated temperature for conditions. True excessive upstream temperatures, sensor bias high, abnormal regen control, restriction effects, and severe engine-out conditions are the primary causes. False overtemp from a failed EGT sensor and true overtemp during uncontrolled thermal events are documented patterns. One extreme sensor reading while adjacent sensors read normally is the key indicator of sensor bias — cross-checking adjacent temperature sensors is the mandatory first step.
causes: True excessive upstream temperatures — true overtemp from engine or regen control fault
Sensor bias high — SCR inlet EGT sensor reading above actual temperature
Abnormal regen control — regen control fault producing excessive temperatures
Restriction effects — restriction increasing upstream temperatures
Severe engine-out conditions — engine fault producing excessive exhaust temperatures
steps: Single Action Gate — Multi-EGT Correlation

Cross-check the SCR inlet EGT against adjacent temperature sensors. One extreme sensor reading while adjacent sensors read normally confirms sensor bias. All temperature sensors reading high simultaneously confirms a true thermal event. Multi-EGT correlation is the mandatory first step before any hardware diagnosis.
Binary Decision Gate — EGT Circuit Checks

Perform EGT circuit checks on the SCR inlet sensor if sensor bias is suspected. A sensor circuit fault can produce a false high reading. Verify sensor circuit integrity before any AT hardware decision.
Override Manager — Inspect for Restriction

Inspect for restriction in the aftertreatment system. Restriction increases upstream temperatures and can produce true SCR inlet overtemp. Evaluate delta-P and pressure readings to identify restriction.
Safety Interceptor — Evaluate Fueling and Regen Behavior

Evaluate fueling and regen behavior. An abnormal regen control fault producing excessive temperatures is a documented cause of true SCR inlet overtemp. Confirm regen fueling is within specification and regen control is functioning normally.
Resume Point — Reduce Load If True Overtemp Is Confirmed
Reduce load immediately if true overtemp is confirmed. True SCR inlet overtemp can damage the SCR catalyst. Reduce load and diagnose the source of excessive temperatures before returning to service.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation

After repair, verify SCR inlet temperature returns to normal range under all operating conditions. Confirm SPN 5019 FMI 0 does not return. Monitor for return of overtemp conditions over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor, Control, or Restriction Decision

Replace EGT sensor if bias or circuit fault is confirmed. Repair regen control fault if confirmed. Repair restriction if confirmed. Address engine fault if severe engine-out conditions are confirmed. Do not replace major AT hardware for a sensor bias fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace SCR inlet EGT sensor if bias or circuit fault is confirmed.
2 . Repair regen control fault if confirmed.
3 . Repair restriction if confirmed.
4 . Address engine fault if severe engine-out conditions are confirmed.
Verification Steps
Confirm SCR inlet temperature returns to normal range after repair.
Verify SPN 5019 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm no regen abort from overtemp after repair.
Monitor for return of overtemp conditions over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect SCR inlet EGT sensor connector at every major aftertreatment service.
✓ Monitor regen fueling quantity at every major aftertreatment service.
✓ Inspect aftertreatment system for restriction at every major service.
✓ Address engine faults promptly to prevent excessive exhaust temperatures.

High if true overtemp. Reduce load and diagnose immediately. True-versus-false temperature split protects components and budget.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 74 - Engine Failed to Respond
procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) communicates with the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) over the J1939 data link during normal operation; however, engine control is accomplished by the ECU during hybrid mode. The TECU changes mode to AutoShift Only or AutoShift
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: TECU ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. J1939 Communication Link Fault (TECU) Inactive. J1939 Engine Message Fault (TECU) Inactive. J1939 engine speed is greater than 300 RPM if the TECU is in speed control mode, or greater than 1000 RPM if the TECU is in torque control mode. Desired engine speed is less than J1939 engine configuration map speed.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 7 is set when the difference between actual engine percent torque and desired engine percent torque is greater than 50 for 2 continuous seconds, or when the difference between desired engine speed and actual engine speed is greater than 400 RPM for four continuous seconds.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the TECU or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: mode. Then the TECU requests changes in engine speed and torque instead of the Hybrid Control Module (HCM). Detection The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: TECU ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts. J1939 Communication Link Fault (TECU) Inactive. J1939 Engine Message Fault (TECU) Inactive. J1939 engine speed is greater than 300 RPM if the TECU is in speed control mode, or greater than 1000 RPM if the TECU is in torque control mode. Desired engine speed is less than J1939 engine configuration map speed. Conditions to Set Fault Code Active The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 7 is set when the difference between actual engine percent torque and desired engine percent torque is greater than 50 for 2 continuous seconds, or when the difference between desired engine speed and actual engine speed is greater than 400 RPM for four continuous seconds. Fallback When Fault Code 74 is set the following conditions occur: Fault is stored in TECU memory. If the fault sets while driving, the vehicle remains in the current gear position. Once the vehicle stops, start and reverse gears can be engaged.

dd_procedures.overview: This fault indicates the system cannot disengage from the current gear. The system will continue attempting to disengage the current gear after the fault is set. Vehicle must be moving and attempting to change gear position and no electrical faults are active.
causes: Shift Bar Housing Mechanical issue with the shift bar housing Damaged shift bar housing interlock parts Electric Shifter New Electric Shifter installed and not recalibrated per the L-Letter (L-2003-30) Mechanical issue with the Electric Shifter Badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leak Worn center shaft bushing (TAIB-0814.) Base Transmission Main box mechanical failure Sliding clutch / shift yoke wear Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) New
steps: A. Determine if an Electric Shifter was installed without recalibrating the transmission. Key off. Was a new Electric Shifter or TECU just installed without recalibrating the transmission? Yes , perform transmission calibration. Turn key on, and allow the transmission to power up. Turn key off, wait 2 minutes and Go to Step V . No , Go to Step B

B. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect the batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Inspect starter, battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. Measure voltage across batteries. If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required and Go to Step C If voltage is outside of range , repair or replace batteries and charge system as required. Repeat test.

C. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port. Locate the diagnostic port on the Transmission Harness - located at the left rear corner of the transmission. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. If voltage between Pin C and battery negative post is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step D If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.

D. Measure batter voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E If voltage is outside of range, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

E. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step F If voltage is outside of range, repair Ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

F. Visually inspect the Shift bar housing, Electric Shifter and base transmission for signs of mechanical damage. Key off. Remove electric shifter from Shift Bar Housing. Inspect the Shift Bar Housing Visually inspect shift rails and blocks. Verify shift bar housing operation by confirming shift rails can physically engage each gear individually. Confirm the shift bar housing can not engage 2 gears at the same time. Inspect Electric Shifter Check for mechanical issues with the Electric Shifter. Visually inspect for badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leaks. Check for a worn center shaft bushing (see TAIB-0814). Inspect Base Transmission Drain and inspect oil for debris. Remove I-brake or PTO cover and inspect for main box mechanical failure. Inspect sliding clutches and shift yokes for wear. If no problem found, replace Electric Shifter and the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V If problem found, repair as required and Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Key on. Clear fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code. Check for fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no fault codes, test complete. If Fault Code 71 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 71 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 75 - Power Down In Gear
dd_procedures.overview: This fault is detected when the vehicle is powered-down in any gear position other than neutral. Note: This code will only be set Inactive
causes: Improper shut down procedure
steps: A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Key on. Retrieve Codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 75 is Inactive, no action necessary. This code indicates the driver powered down the system prior to selecting neutral. Explain to driver, shift selector must be in neutral before powering down to prevent a stuck-in-gear situation and/or a power-up no crank situation.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 71: Unable to Disengage Gear
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the X-Y Shifter to engage and disengage a gear based on the driver’s selected mode of operation. Gear disengagement is achieved by activating the X-Y Shifter Gear Motor, which controls the fore-and-aft movement of the Shift Finger. Pushing the Shift Finger against one of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks guides the Shift Yoke to disengage the Sliding Clutch from a gear. The position of the X-Y Shift Finger is monitored by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) by way of the X-Y Gear Position Sensor and Rail Position Sensor. Fault Code 71 is set w
causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. Note: If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Inactive and there are other Active fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes first. If Fault Code 71 FMI 11 is Active, Go to Step I If Fault Code 71 FMI 11 is Inactive, Go to Step V If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Active or Inactive and/or Fault Codes 27, 33, 34, 51, 52, 61, 63 or 64 are Active or Inactive, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Inactive, Go to Step B If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Active, Go to Step C

If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Inactive, Go to Step B If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Active, Go to Step C

B. Use Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode to locate intermittent failures. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Place transmission in PD Mode. See more about Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode . Note: Fault Code 71 does not set Active during PD Mode. Other fault codes may set Active during PD Mode that could indicate an issue with the wiring. Note: Transmission does not enter PD Mode when Active fault codes exist. Wiggle wiring and connections of the Transmission Harness from the X-Y Shifter to the TECU. Wiggle wiring and connections of the Vehicle Power Supply Harness from the batteries to the TECU. Exit PD Mode by powering down. Notice Allow 2-3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. If any fault sets Active while wiggling the Transmission Harness, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V If any fault sets Active while wiggling the Power Supply harness, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of Power Supply wiring. Go to Step V If no fault codes set Active, Go to Step C

C. Inspect the batteries, in-line fuse and power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Notice Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. Inspect Starter, battery terminals and transmission 30-amp In-line Fuse Holder Connections for corrosion, loose terminals and bent or spread pins. Inspect Battery Positive (+) and Negative (-) wires from the batteries to the TECU including all connections. Ensure a clean ground connection on the chassis. Verify no damage or corrosion to connectors. If damage is found, repair or replace Power Supply Harness per OEM guidelines. Go to Step V If no damage is found, Go to Step D

D. Perform a Load Test on each vehicle battery. Key off. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Load test each vehicle battery per OEM specifications. Record reading(s). If any battery does not pass the Load Test, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of batteries. Go to Step V If all batteries pass the Load Test, Go to Step E Battery Voltage Drop Load Test Status (Pass/Fail) 1 2 3 4 5

E. Inspect X-Y Shifter and Transmission Harness for physical damage. Key off. Notice Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. Inspect the physical condition of X-Y Shifter and all connections. Inspect Transmission Harness for any pinched, chafed, corroded or shorted wiring. Disconnect both 2-Way X-Y Gear and Rail Position Sensor Connectors. Disconnect both 2-Way X-Y Motor Connectors to the Transmission Harness. Inspect connectors for corrosion, loose terminals, bent or spread pin or damage to the connector bodies. If damage to the X-Y Shifter or X-Y Shifter wiring is found, replace X-Y Shifter . Go to Step V If damage to the Transmission Harness is found, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V If no damage is found, Go to Step F

F. Inspect condition of X-Y Shifter internal components. Key off. Remove the X-Y Shifter. Inspect condition of the X-Y Shift Finger and Cross Shaft for damage or wear. Inspect the X-Y Shifter ball screw for signs of coolant contamination. For the latest Service Bulletin updates, visit Roadranger.com. If coolant contamination is found, repair the vehicle coolant system leak and follow Service Bulletin TMIB0124 for complete repair procedure. X-Y Shifter must be replaced upon completion of service bulletin. Go to Step V If damage to the X-Y Shifter is found, replace X-Y Shifter . Go to Step V If no damage is found, Go to Step G

G. Inspect condition of Shift Bar Housing. Key off. Inspect condition of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks. Look for uneven gaps between the Shift Blocks or excessive wear to the block faces. Verify Shift Blocks are tight to the rails and there are no other mechanical issues with the Shift Bar Housing. Verify transmission shifts fully in and out of each gear. Test the Shift Interlock to verify that the transmission will not engage two gears at once. See the Shift Interlock Inspection Procedure Shift Interlock Inspection . If damage to the Shift Bar Housing is found, repair Shift Bar Housing . Go to Step V If no damage is found, Go to Step H

H. Inspect condition of the internal transmission components. Key off. Drain and save the transmission oil. Inspect oil for significant metal fragments. Remove 8-bolt PTO cover. Inspect main case gears for damage or excessive movement. Inspect Shift Yokes and Sliding Clutches for damage or excessive wear. If damage is found or there are significant metal fragments in the oil, replace damaged, worn or failed transmission components. Go to Step V If no damage is found within the transmission main case, replace X-Y Shifter and Transmission Harness . Go to Step V Note: If unsure whether damage or wear is significant, take pictures of the transmission gearing. Ensure these pictures are clear and the components are easily visible. Email these pictures to auto.rtw@eaton.com and contact Eaton at (800) 826-4357.
I. Clear Fault Code 71 FMI 11 Refer to RRMT0019. Clear Fault Code 71 FMI 11 per RRMT0019. Go to Step J

J. Verify TECU Software Version Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To Programming. Under "Software Information", record TECU software version. If TECU software is less than 5570064, update TECU software to 5570064 or greater. Go to Step K If TECU software is 5570064 or greater, Go to Step K

K. Verify Clutch Serial Number Information Per CLIB0035 Key Off. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Go to Service Bulletin CLIB0035. Review and follow steps outlined in Service Bulletin CLIB0035, Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed, including X-Y Shifter. Reinstall 8-bolt PTO cover. Refill transmission with lubricant. Key on with engine off. Clear fault codes using ServiceRanger. Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set Active and vehicle operates properly, test complete. If a fault code other than 71 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . If Fault Code 71 sets Active, refer to Contact Information and contact Eaton for further diagnostics.

Kontağı kapatın, 2 dakika bekleyin ve Adım V'ye gidin. - Hayır ise, Adım B'ye gidin.

B. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect the batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Inspect starter, battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. Measure voltage across batteries. If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required and Go to Step C If voltage is outside of range , repair or replace batteries and charge system as required. Repeat test.

C. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port. Locate the diagnostic port on the Transmission Harness - located at the left rear corner of the transmission. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. If voltage between Pin C and battery negative post is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step D If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.

D. 4 yollu teşhis portunda akü gerilimini ölçün. Kontağı açın. Pin B ile Pin C arasındaki gerilimi ölçün. Gerilim akü geriliminin 0,6 V dahilindeyse Adım E'ye gidin. Gerilim aralık dışındaysa TECU'ya giden akü besleme hattını onarın. Sigorta atmış olabilir. Testi tekrarlayın.

E. 4 yollu teşhis portunda kontak gerilimini ölçün. Kontağı açın. Pin A ile Pin C arasındaki gerilimi ölçün. Gerilim akü geriliminin 0,6 V dahilindeyse Adım F'ye gidin. Gerilim aralık dışındaysa TECU'ya giden kontak güç beslemesini onarın. Sigorta atmış olabilir. Testi tekrarlayın.

F. Visually inspect the Shift bar housing, Electric Shifter and base transmission for signs of mechanical damage. Key off. Remove electric shifter from Shift Bar Housing. Inspect the Shift Bar Housing Visually inspect shift rails and blocks. Verify shift bar housing operation by confirming shift rails can physically engage each gear individually. Confirm the shift bar housing can not engage 2 gears at the same time. Inspect Electric Shifter Check for mechanical issues with the Electric Shifter. Visually inspect for badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leaks. Check for a worn center shaft bushing (see TAIB-0814). Inspect Base Transmission Drain and inspect oil for debris. Remove I-brake or PTO cover and inspect for main box mechanical failure. Inspect sliding clutches and shift yokes for wear. If no problem found, replace Electric Shifter and the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V If problem found, repair as required and Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Key on. Clear fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code. Check for fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no fault codes, test complete. If Fault Code 71 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 71 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

A. Aktif veya pasif arıza kodlarını kontrol edin. Kontağı açın. Kodları okuyun. "Arıza Kodu Okuma/Silme" bölümüne bakın. Arıza Kodu 75 pasifse herhangi bir işleme gerek yoktur. Bu kod, sürücünün vitesi boşa (N) almadan önce sistemi kapattığını gösterir. Sürücüye, viteste takılı kalma ve/veya marş basmama durumunu önlemek için kapatmadan önce vites seçicinin mutlaka boşta olması gerektiğini açıklayın.
[FMI 2 katalog] CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal bütünlüğünü osiloskopla inceleyin; aralıklı paket kaybı ve yansıma arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 9 katalog] CAN veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve düğüm adresleme çakışmasını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 12 katalog] İlgili ECU/modülün beslemesini ve toprağını teyit edin; modül yazılım sürümünü ve hatasını okuyun. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Alınan ağ verisinde hata bayrağını kontrol edin; gönderen düğümün durumunu ve hata sayacını inceleyin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

steps_en_archive: A. Determine if an Electric Shifter was installed without recalibrating the transmission. Key off. Was a new Electric Shifter or TECU just installed without recalibrating the transmission - Yes , perform transmission calibration. Turn key on, and allow the transmission to power up. Turn key off, wait 2 minutes and Go to Step V . No , Go to Step B

D. Measure batter voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E If voltage is outside of range, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

E. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step F If voltage is outside of range, repair Ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Key on. Retrieve Codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 75 is Inactive, no action necessary. This code indicates the driver powered down the system prior to selecting neutral. Explain to driver, shift selector must be in neutral before powering down to prevent a stuck-in-gear situation and/or a power-up no crank situation.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 71: Unable to Disengage Gear
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the X-Y Shifter to engage and disengage a gear based on the driver’s selected mode of operation. Gear disengagement is achieved by activating the X-Y Shifter Gear Motor, which controls the fore-and-aft movement of the Shift Finger. Pushing the Shift Finger against one of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks guides the Shift Yoke to disengage the Sliding Clutch from a gear. The position of the X-Y Shift Finger is monitored by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) by way of the X-Y Gear Position Sensor and Rail Position Sensor. Fault Code 71 is set when the X-Y Shift Finger attempts to pull out of gear, but the X-Y Gear Position Sensor indicates that the transmission was unable to disengage that gear. The TECU detected a system failure, but was unable to detect the specific root cause.
procedures_full.detection: This fault can only be detected when there are no failures of the TECU, X-Y Gear or Rail Motors, X-Y Position Sensors or Battery Supply voltage. This fault code is set when the system is unable to pull the transmission out of gear.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: After the first failed attempt to pull to neutral, the system opens the clutch to break torque and attempts to pull to neutral again. If the system is unable to achieve neutral after three consecutive attempts, the fault code sets Active. FMI 11 – Root Cause Unknown: When the engine is running and the vehicle comes to a complete stop, the system opens the clutch. If neutral is requested or commanded, the system attempts to shift to neutral. If the system is unable to achieve neutral after 4 seconds, the fault code sets Active. The system will continue to attempt to pull to neutral for 2 seconds. If the system is unable to obtain neutral, the system requests the engine to shut down.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 7: The system successfully completes a shift into Neutral. FMI 11: Refer to troubleshooting steps.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 7 Transmission may not be able to complete a shift to neutral. Transmission will attempt to move the Shift Finger to neutral. Engine may not crank. Gear display may flash current or destination gear. Until the fault becomes Inactive, driver may have to shut off engine with transmission in gear. FMI 11 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Engine may shut down (if engine shutdown message is supported by the Engine). Engine may be shut down with transmission in gear. If neutral was achieved, Low range gears are available (if engine shutdown message is not supported by the Engine). Engine may not crank if the transmission cannot shift to neutral. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 7: The system successfully completes a shift into Neutral. FMI 11: Refer to troubleshooting steps.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 7 Vehicle Power Supply Poor power or ground supply to TECU Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals Vehicle Batteries Internal failure Transmission Harness Damaged wiring between the TECU and X-Y Shifter Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals X-Y Shifter Worn or damaged X-Y Shifter ball screw, center shaft bushing, or other internal components Contamination of X-Y Shifter ball screw due to coolant leak or oil contamination Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals Mechanical Transmission Worn or damaged Shift Bar Housing Worn or damaged Sliding Clutch slot width Worn or damaged Shift Yokes Worn or damaged internal transmission components Clutch Not properly disengaging (clutch drag) FMI 11 Refer to troubleshooting steps. Component Identification 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Transmission Harness Connector 3. Gear Position Sensor 4. 3-Way Gear Position Sensor Connector 5. 2-Way Gear Motor Connector (blue) 6. 2-Way Gear Motor Connector Body (blue) 1. X-Y Shifter 2. 2-Way Rail Motor Connector (black) 3. 2-Way Rail Motor Connector Body (black) 4. 3-Way Rail Position Sensor Connector 5. Rail Position Sensor 6. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector

steps.A:
A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. 
 Note: If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Inactive and there are other Active fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes first. 
 If Fault Code 71 FMI 11 is Active, Go to Step I 
 If Fault Code 71 FMI 11 is Inactive, Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Active or Inactive and/or Fault Codes 27, 33, 34, 51, 52, 61, 63 or 64 are Active or Inactive, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . 
 If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Inactive, Go to Step B 
 If Fault Code 71 FMI 7 is Active, Go to Step C
steps.B:
B. Use Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode to locate intermittent failures. 
 Set parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Place transmission in PD Mode. See more about Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode . 
 Note: Fault Code 71 does not set Active during PD Mode. Other fault codes may set Active during PD Mode that could indicate an issue with the wiring. 
 Note: Transmission does not enter PD Mode when Active fault codes exist. 
 Wiggle wiring and connections of the Transmission Harness from the X-Y Shifter to the TECU. 
 Wiggle wiring and connections of the Vehicle Power Supply Harness from the batteries to the TECU. 
 Exit PD Mode by powering down. 
 Notice
 Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. 
 If any fault sets Active while wiggling the Transmission Harness, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If any fault sets Active while wiggling the Power Supply harness, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of Power Supply wiring. Go to Step V 
 If no fault codes set Active, Go to Step C
steps.C:
C. Inspect the batteries, in-line fuse and power and ground supplies to the TECU. 
 Key off. 
 Notice
 Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. 
 Inspect Starter, battery terminals and transmission 30-amp In-line Fuse Holder Connections for corrosion, loose terminals and bent or spread pins. 
 Inspect Battery Positive (+) and Negative (-) wires from the batteries to the TECU including all connections. Ensure a clean ground connection on the chassis. Verify no damage or corrosion to connectors. 
 If damage is found, repair or replace Power Supply Harness per OEM guidelines. Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step D
steps.D:
D. Perform a Load Test on each vehicle battery. 
 Key off. 
 Set parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Load test each vehicle battery per OEM specifications. Record reading(s). 
 If any battery does not pass the Load Test, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of batteries. Go to Step V 
 If all batteries pass the Load Test, Go to Step E 
 Battery Voltage Drop Load Test Status (Pass/Fail) 
 1 
 2 
 3 
 4 
 5
steps.E:
E. Inspect X-Y Shifter and Transmission Harness for physical damage. 
 Key off. 
 Notice
 Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. 
 Inspect the physical condition of X-Y Shifter and all connections. 
 Inspect Transmission Harness for any pinched, chafed, corroded or shorted wiring. 
 Disconnect both 2-Way X-Y Gear and Rail Position Sensor Connectors. 
 Disconnect both 2-Way X-Y Motor Connectors to the Transmission Harness. 
 Inspect connectors for corrosion, loose terminals, bent or spread pin or damage to the connector bodies. 
 If damage to the X-Y Shifter or X-Y Shifter wiring is found, replace X-Y Shifter . Go to Step V 
 If damage to the Transmission Harness is found, replace Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step F
steps.F:
F. Inspect condition of X-Y Shifter internal components. 
 Key off. 
 Remove the X-Y Shifter. 
 Inspect condition of the X-Y Shift Finger and Cross Shaft for damage or wear. 
 Inspect the X-Y Shifter ball screw for signs of coolant contamination. 
 For the latest Service Bulletin updates, visit Roadranger.com. 
 If coolant contamination is found, repair the vehicle coolant system leak and follow Service Bulletin TMIB0124 for complete repair procedure. X-Y Shifter must be replaced upon completion of service bulletin. Go to Step V 
 If damage to the X-Y Shifter is found, replace X-Y Shifter . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step G
steps.G:
G. Inspect condition of Shift Bar Housing. 
 Key off. 
 Inspect condition of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks. Look for uneven gaps between the Shift Blocks or excessive wear to the block faces. 
 Verify Shift Blocks are tight to the rails and there are no other mechanical issues with the Shift Bar Housing. 
 Verify transmission shifts fully in and out of each gear. 
 Test the Shift Interlock to verify that the transmission will not engage two gears at once. See the Shift Interlock Inspection Procedure Shift Interlock Inspection . 
 If damage to the Shift Bar Housing is found, repair Shift Bar Housing . Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found, Go to Step H
steps.H:
H. Inspect condition of the internal transmission components. 
 Key off. 
 Drain and save the transmission oil. Inspect oil for significant metal fragments. 
 Remove 8-bolt PTO cover. 
 Inspect main case gears for damage or excessive movement. 
 Inspect Shift Yokes and Sliding Clutches for damage or excessive wear. 
 If damage is found or there are significant metal fragments in the oil, replace damaged, worn or failed transmission components. Go to Step V 
 If no damage is found within the transmission main case, replace X-Y Shifter and Transmission Harness . Go to Step V 
 Note: If unsure whether damage or wear is significant, take pictures of the transmission gearing. Ensure these pictures are clear and the components are easily visible. Email these pictures to auto.rtw@eaton.com and contact Eaton at (800) 826-4357.
steps.I:
I. Clear Fault Code 71 FMI 11 
 Refer to RRMT0019. 
 Clear Fault Code 71 FMI 11 per RRMT0019. Go to Step J
steps.J:
J. Verify TECU Software Version 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To Programming. 
 Under "Software Information", record TECU software version. 
 If TECU software is less than 5570064, update TECU software to 5570064 or greater. Go to Step K 
 If TECU software is 5570064 or greater, Go to Step K
steps.K:
K. Verify Clutch Serial Number Information Per CLIB0035 
 Key Off. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Go to Service Bulletin CLIB0035. 
 Review and follow steps outlined in Service Bulletin CLIB0035, Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed, including X-Y Shifter. 
 Reinstall 8-bolt PTO cover. 
 Refill transmission with lubricant. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Clear fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 If no fault codes set Active and vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If a fault code other than 71 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . 
 If Fault Code 71 sets Active, refer to Contact Information and contact Eaton for further diagnostics.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with solenoid valves that direct vehicle Supply Air to and from the Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) and shift rail cylinders for clutch and shift rail actuation. Position sensors monitor clutch and shift rail positions, and speed sensors monitor shaft speeds. The sensor information is provided to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of making clutch engagement or disengagement decisions, making shift decisions, and confirming gear engagement. The TCM compares the clutch and shift rail commands to the clutch and shift rail positions and the shaft speeds (ratio calculation) to ensure the transmission is operating properly. The solenoids, sensors, LCA and shift rails are located in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors clutch and shift rail operation. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with solenoids to direct pneumatic flow to actuate the clutch and shift rails and sensors to monitor the clutch and shift rail positions. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) compares the clutch and shift rail commands with the clutch and shift rail positions including speed sensors (ratio calculation) to ensure proper operation. The solenoids, sensors, Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) and shift rails are located in the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM) and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector. The TCM monitors the clutch and shift rail operation. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: During a Clutch Calibration, the speed sensors could not confirm the main shaft was neutralized while Rail C or D Position Sensor reported neutral. FMI 11 - Root Cause Unknown: Transmission output shaft speed sensor direction mismatch with counter shaft speed sensor for 2 seconds. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device or Component: Speed sensors did not confirm the main shaft was neutralized during clutch engagement. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Shift rail engagement was commanded that would result in a drive line engagement with the vehicle stationary. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: Rail C or E Position Sensors indicated gear engagement when not expected for 2 seconds. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: Rail D or E Position Sensors indicated gear engagement when not expected for 2 seconds. FMI 31 – Condition Exists: Urge to Move and Creep Mode were not commanded when expected.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 71 - Unable to Disengage Gear
procedures_full.overview: This fault indicates the system cannot disengage from the current gear. The system will continue attempting to disengage the current gear after the fault is set. Vehicle must be moving and attempting to change gear position and no electrical faults are active.
procedures_full.detection: The system is unable to select the neutral position after 3 consecutive attempts.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: Conditions to Set the Fault Code Active FMI 7 - The system is unable to select the neutral position after 3 consecutive attempts.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Conditions to Set the Fault Inactive FMI 7 - The fault becomes Inactive when neutral is achieved.
procedures_full.fallback: Fallback mode During Power-Up None. This fault can not be set at power-up. Fallback Mode During Operation When this fault is Active, the transmission will continue to attempt to select neutral. The system will alternate the engine speed up and down in an attempt to achieve disengagement. The gear display may blink the destination gear. The service light will not flash, nor will an F be displayed on the dash. The diagnostic code will not be transmitted on the J1587 bus until fault codes have been requested by a service tool. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive Conditions to Set the Fault Inactive FMI 7 - The fault becomes Inactive when neutral is achieved.

steps.A:
A. Determine if an Electric Shifter was installed without recalibrating the transmission. 
 Key off. 
 Was a new Electric Shifter or TECU just installed without recalibrating the transmission? 
 Yes , perform transmission calibration. Turn key on, and allow the transmission to power up. Turn key off, wait 2 minutes and Go to Step V . 
 No , Go to Step B
steps.B:
B. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect the batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. 
 Key off. 
 Inspect starter, battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. 
 Measure voltage across batteries. 
 If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required and Go to Step C 
 If voltage is outside of range , repair or replace batteries and charge system as required. Repeat test.
steps.C:
C. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port. 
 Locate the diagnostic port on the Transmission Harness - located at the left rear corner of the transmission. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. 
 If voltage between Pin C and battery negative post is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step D 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.
steps.D:
D. Measure batter voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. 
 If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.
steps.E:
E. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. 
 If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step F 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair Ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.
steps.F:
F. Visually inspect the Shift bar housing, Electric Shifter and base transmission for signs of mechanical damage. 
 Key off. 
 Remove electric shifter from Shift Bar Housing. 
 Inspect the Shift Bar Housing 
 Visually inspect shift rails and blocks. 
 Verify shift bar housing operation by confirming shift rails can physically engage each gear individually. 
 Confirm the shift bar housing can not engage 2 gears at the same time. 
 Inspect Electric Shifter 
 Check for mechanical issues with the Electric Shifter. 
 Visually inspect for badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leaks. 
 Check for a worn center shaft bushing (see TAIB-0814). 
 Inspect Base Transmission 
 Drain and inspect oil for debris. 
 Remove I-brake or PTO cover and inspect for main box mechanical failure. 
 Inspect sliding clutches and shift yokes for wear. 
 If no problem found, replace Electric Shifter and the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V 
 If problem found, repair as required and Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. 
 Key on. 
 Clear fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code. 
 Check for fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no fault codes, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 71 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. 
 If fault code other than 71 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 75: Power Down in Gear
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) monitors gear and rail position sensors to determine the position of the X-Y Shifter Shift Finger. Fault Code 75 indicates the transmission was powered down with the Shift Finger in a non-neutral gear position.
procedures_full.detection: Ignition key is turned off with the X-Y Shifter Shift Finger in a non-neutral position.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 14 – Special Instructions: TECU detects a non-neutral gear position during power down.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 14: Fault code sets Inactive upon the next power-up cycle.
procedures_full.fallback: No fallback mode is associated with this fault. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 14: Fault code sets Inactive upon the next power-up cycle.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 14 Driver Behavior Driver turned the ignition off with the transmission in a non-neutral state Vehicle Ignition Supply Unintentional loss of ignition supply to TECU Component Identification None

steps.A:

 If Fault Code 75 is Inactive, no action necessary. This code indicates the driver powered down the system before selecting neutral. Test complete.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 75 - Power Down In Gear
procedures_full.overview: This fault is detected when the vehicle is powered-down in any gear position other than neutral. Note: This code will only be set Inactive
procedures_full.detection: The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) monitors shift device position and electric shifter position during vehicle shut down. If a non-neutral shift device position and in gear position are detected during vehicle shut down, this code will be set.
procedures_full.fallback: No Fallback mode. This is a non driving, power-down fault. It may cause a dash to appear in the gear display during power-up if the transmission is torque locked after shutting down in gear.

steps.A:

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1381 FMI 1 means fuel suction pressure has dropped to a severely low level. This is a high-severity code with real power loss and stalling risk - check filters and suction lines immediately rather than assuming pump failure. By the time this most-severe FMI level sets, the engine is genuinely fuel-starved on the suction side. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats it as a same-day fix, not a schedule-it-for-later item, since continued operation risks stalling in traffic or on a grade.
causes: Severely plugged primary or secondary fuel filter
Extended service intervals or heavily contaminated fuel can restrict flow enough to starve the low-pressure pump entirely.
Blocked fuel tank vent or pickup screen
A fully blocked vent creates a severe vacuum inside the tank that no filter change alone will fix.
Collapsed suction hose or major air leak
A failing hose or loose fitting on the suction side introduces air or restricts flow enough to cause a severe pressure drop.
steps: Install a fuel pressure/vacuum gauge on the suction side ahead of the primary filter and compare readings against Cat's specification at idle and under load.
Replace the primary and secondary fuel filters immediately if vacuum readings are excessive or the filters show heavy contamination.
Check the fuel tank vent cap and pickup screen for a severe blockage creating an artificial vacuum inside the tank.
Inspect all suction-side hoses and fittings for collapse, cracking, or air leaks that would starve the pump under demand.
Prime and bleed the fuel system fully after any filter change before attempting to restart, since trapped air compounds a low suction pressure fault.
Retest suction pressure under load on Cat ET after repairs to confirm the fault is fully resolved before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Amber or red check engine lamp with noticeable power loss
Engine stalling or struggling under heavy load or acceleration
Hard starting, especially after the truck has sat for a period
Fuel filter housing showing severe restriction or contamination
procedures_full.source_title: Caterpillar SPN 1381 FMI 1: Severe Low Fuel Supply Pump Inlet Pressure

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1381 FMI 1 on PACCAR MX-13 engines means the fuel supply pump's inlet pressure is below normal - most severe level. It's a high-severity, early-warning fault most often caused by a restricted primary filter or a suction-side air leak. SPN 1381 catches fuel supply problems right at the pump's inlet, before they've had a chance to cascade into a bigger rail pressure or delivery pressure fault. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as a genuinely useful early warning rather than just another nuisance code - catching a restricted filter or a small suction leak here is far cheaper than dealing with the fuel starvation damage that follows if the same restriction is left to worsen.
causes: Restricted primary fuel filter or water separator
A filter loaded with debris ahead of the pump inlet directly reduces available suction pressure, especially as engine demand increases with RPM.
Suction-side air leak at a loose fitting or cracked line
Any point where air can enter the suction line ahead of the pump will cause inlet pressure to read low and unstable.
Partially blocked tank pickup tube or screen
Sediment or debris accumulation at the tank pickup restricts flow before fuel even reaches the supply line.
Weak fuel supply pump
A pump losing its ability to generate adequate suction will show low inlet-side readings even with an unobstructed supply path.
steps: Pull the fault with PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 1381 FMI 1 is active; check the reported inlet pressure value against the expected minimum for the current RPM.
Inspect the fuel/water separator and primary filter for restriction, since a plugged filter ahead of the pump inlet is the most common cause of this specific reading.
Check the suction line and fittings between the tank and the pump for a loose connection or a hairline crack that could be drawing in air rather than fuel.
Use a hand vacuum pump on the suction side with the engine off to confirm the line holds vacuum without bleeding down - a leak here will fail this test immediately.
Inspect the tank pickup tube and screen for a partial blockage from debris or sediment, especially if the truck has recently had fuel system contamination.
Clear the code and road test while monitoring live inlet pressure to confirm it holds within spec across the RPM range before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Power loss under load, particularly at higher RPM
Hard starting or extended crank time
Amber dash lamp with a fuel system warning
Fuel-starvation-related stalling in more advanced cases

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1381 FMI 4 means the fuel supply pump inlet pressure sensor circuit voltage is below normal. Prime the system, compare mechanical pressure to INSITE, then test the 5 V circuit. Cummins X15 operators call ProfessionalDieselRepair.com about SPN 1381 FMI 4 most often after a fuel filter service that introduced air or left a connector loose at the inlet pressure sensor on the gear pump housing.
causes: Short to ground in inlet pressure sensor harness
Frame-rail chafing pulls the signal voltage low and sets FMI 4 even when fuel pressure is normal.
Weak lift pump or clogged primary filter
Real low inlet pressure produces low sensor output that the ECM reports as a valid but low reading—verify with a mechanical gauge.
Failed inlet pressure sensor
Internal diaphragm or electronics failure drives signal voltage below the valid range.
steps: Connect Cummins INSITE and verify SPN 1381 voltage and pressure readings at idle and during lift-pump command.
Check fuel level and filter installation—air ingestion after service mimics low inlet pressure until primed to 25-35 psi on many X15 setups.
Back-probe the sensor connector: supply 5.0 V ±0.5 V, signal 0.5-4.5 V range at normal pressure, ground less than 0.1 V drop.
Measure inlet pressure with a mechanical gauge tee on the supply line; compare to ECM reading—matching low mechanical pressure indicates pump or restriction, not sensor.
Repair harness shorts or replace the inlet pressure sensor per Cummins spec, prime until 30 psi, clear faults, and confirm stable reading above 15 psi at idle.
symptoms: Amber or red fault lamp with active SPN 1381 FMI 4 in Cummins INSITE
Hard start, long crank, or stall after sitting overnight
Inlet pressure reading stuck at 0 psi or 0 V in live data
Torque reduction when ECM substitutes default fueling limits
Code may appear after fuel filter change if the sensor was bumped or unplugged
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 1381 FMI 4: Fuel Supply Pump Inlet Pressure Voltage Low

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1381 FMI 18 means the ECM sees fuel suction-side pressure below normal at a moderately severe level. It's a medium-severity early-warning code with no derate - check the primary fuel filter and suction lines before the condition worsens into a delivery pressure fault. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this code as the fuel system's early smoke detector. It's set well ahead of a true low-pressure fault, which means catching it now with a simple filter change avoids the harder starts and power loss that show up once suction restriction gets bad enough to starve the high-pressure pump.
causes: Plugging primary fuel filter or water separator element
Contaminated fuel or extended service intervals gradually restrict flow through the filter media, increasing suction-side vacuum.
Restricted fuel tank vent or pickup screen
A blocked vent creates a vacuum inside the tank itself, starving the pump regardless of filter condition.
Collapsed or kinked suction hose
A soft or damaged hose section can collapse under suction, especially at higher fuel demand.
Faulty suction pressure sensor
A drifting sensor can report low pressure without an actual restriction, though this is uncommon compared to genuine filter plugging.
steps: Install a fuel pressure/vacuum gauge on the suction side ahead of the primary fuel filter, per OEM test port location.
Run the engine at idle and moderate RPM, comparing suction-side vacuum against the OEM specification (typically no more than 6-8 in-Hg maximum vacuum on most Cummins platforms).
Replace the primary fuel filter and water separator element if vacuum exceeds spec or the filter shows visible contamination.
Check fuel tank vent caps to ensure they aren't clogged and drawing a structural vacuum inside the fuel tank.
Inspect suction-side hose and fitting connections for collapsed hose walls or loose clamps that can restrict flow under load.
Clear the code with Cummins INSITE and retest suction pressure under load to confirm the repair holds.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp, no derate at this stage
Slight hesitation or power dip that may not yet be obvious to the driver
Fuel filter housing showing early signs of restriction on a vacuum gauge
Possible harder starts if restriction has progressed

SPN_5848.pgn_description: This message contains aftertreatment intermediate ammonia information for aftertreatment system 1 (or bank 1).
causes: Sensor Element Degradation: NH3 sensor ceramic element contamination or thermal stress causing unstable resistance characteristics and signal drift
Wiring Harness Problems: Intermittent connector corrosion, damaged shielding, or loose terminals creating erratic electrical signal transmission patterns
ECM Software Corruption: Control module firmware issues preventing proper interpretation of NH3 sensor data and fault classification algorithms
Exhaust System Leaks: Air intrusion upstream of sensor causing false readings and confusing ECM
Sensor Internal Failure: NH3 sensor's internal reference electrode or heater circuit has degraded beyond acceptable limits
CAN Bus Corruption: Short or open in CAN lines between sensor and ECM disrupts intelligent device communication
Supply Voltage Fault: Sensor supply voltage below 10V or above 16V during cranking or transient load conditions
ECM Software Mismatch: After ECM replacement, software calibration does not support the installed NH3 sensor revision
steps: Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: NH3 (amonyak) sensörü kablo demetini egzoz ve şasi kolları yakınında sürtünme, erime veya ezilme açısından inceleyin. Direnç Testi: Sensör sinyali ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün

Kılavuz Sensör Gücünü Doğrulama: Kontak açık, motor kapalıyken sensör Pin 1'de 12 V olduğunu ve Pin 2'de şasi sürekliliğini kontrol edin. CAN Veri Yolunu İnceleme: Sensör konnektöründe CAN_H ile CAN_L arasındaki direnci ölçün

Kılavuz Dondurulmuş Çerçeveyi Okuma: Çalışma koşullarını belirlemek için arıza anındaki motor devrini, yükü ve egzoz sıcaklığını kaydedin. DEF Kalitesini Doğrulama: DEF konsantrasyonunu refraktometre ile test edin
steps_en_archive: Guide Visual Inspection: Check NH3 sensor harness for chafing, melting, or pinched wires near exhaust and frame rails. Resistance Test: Measure resistance between sensor signal and ground
Guide Verify sensor power: Check for 12V at sensor pin 1 and ground continuity at pin 2 with key-on, engine-off. Inspect CAN bus: Measure resistance between CAN_H and CAN_L at sensor connector
Guide Read Freeze Frame: Record engine speed, load, and exhaust temperature at fault onset to identify operating conditions. Verify DEF Quality: Test DEF concentration with a refractometer

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) requires a battery power and ground supply.
