 If fault found, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the vehicle charging/battery system. Go to Step V 
 Note: Some chassis use a power distribution system separate from the batteries, inspect all connections.
steps.D:
D. Verify 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector condition. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. 
 Inspect the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector, verify the connector is free from contamination and corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. 
 Inspect the TCM side of the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector, verify the connector is free from contamination and corrosion; the terminals are not bent, spread or loose; and there is no damage to the connector body. 
 If contamination or damage is found, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V 
 If no contamination or damage is found, Go to Step E
steps.E:
E. Verify Battery Voltage2 at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. 
 Key off. 
 Measure voltage between 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector Pin 15 (-) and Pin 16 (+). Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the vehicle charging/battery system, Vehicle Harness and/or 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range, no fault was found. The intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is between the vehicle charging/battery system and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the Vehicle Harness and/or 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Go to Step V 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 15 to 16 11–15 V
steps.F:
F. Verify Battery Voltage2 supply to the TCM with ServiceRanger. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To “Data Monitor”. 
 From the “Default Parameter Files” tab, select “Transmission Supplied Voltages”. 
 Monitor 168 - Battery voltage value. Record reading in table. 
 Monitor 444 - Battery 2 voltage value. Record reading in table. 
 Key on with engine running. 
 Monitor 168 - Battery voltage value. Record reading in table. 
 Monitor 444 - Battery 2 voltage value. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the vehicle charging/battery system. Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range and Fault Code 105 FMI 0 is Inactive, vehicle may have been jump-started or the intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is with the vehicle charging/battery system. Refer to OEM guidelines for diagnosing the vehicle charging/battery system. Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range and Fault Code 105 FMI 0 is Active, replace the Transmission Control Module (TCM) . Go to Step V 
 Note: Troubleshooting indicates no fault found with the wiring or connections to the TCM. Ensure an intermittent issue does not exist with the wiring or connections. 
 Condition Parameter Range Reading(s) 
 Key on with engine off 168-Battery voltage 11–13 V 
 Key on with engine off 444-Battery 2 Voltage 11–13 V 
 Key on with engine running 168-Battery voltage 13–15V 
 Key on with engine running 444-Battery 2 Voltage 13–15V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Fault Codes”. 
 Select “Clear All Faults”. 
 Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 105 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A 
 If a fault code other than 105 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index

procedures_full.detection_tr: TCM, Akü Gerilimi2 güç ve şasi kaynağını izler. Sistem gerilimi aralık dışı algılarsa arıza aktif olarak ayarlanır.

steps_tr.C:
C. Şarj/akü sisteminin, sigortanın, TCM'ye giden güç ve şasi beslemelerinin durumunu doğrulayın.
Kontağı kapatın.
Araç şarj/akü sistemini ve sigortaları inceleyin; konnektörlerin kirlenme ve korozyondan uzak olduğunu, klemenslerin eğilmediğini, açılmadığını veya gevşemediğini ve konnektör gövdelerinde hasar olmadığını doğrulayın.
Arıza bulunamazsa Adım D'ye gidin.
Arıza bulunursa araç şarj/akü sisteminin onarımı veya değişimi için OEM yönergelerine başvurun. Adım V'ye gidin.
Not: Bazı şasiler akülerden ayrı bir güç dağıtım sistemi kullanır; tüm bağlantıları inceleyin.
steps_tr.D:
D. 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünün durumunu doğrulayın.
Kontağı kapatın.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünü sökün.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünü inceleyin; konnektörün kirlenme ve korozyondan uzak olduğunu, klemenslerin eğilmediğini, açılmadığını veya gevşemediğini ve konnektör gövdesinde hasar olmadığını doğrulayın.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünün TCM tarafını inceleyin; konnektörün kirlenme ve korozyondan uzak olduğunu, klemenslerin eğilmediğini, açılmadığını veya gevşemediğini ve konnektör gövdesinde hasar olmadığını doğrulayın.
Kirlenme veya hasar bulunursa 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünün onarımı veya değişimi için OEM yönergelerine başvurun. Adım V'ye gidin.
Kirlenme veya hasar bulunamazsa Adım E'ye gidin

SPN_611.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. steps: Kılavuz ECM Güç Beslemesini Doğrulama: ECM Pin A1 (12 V) ve Pin A2 (şasi) gerilimini ölçün
Kılavuz CAN Sonlandırmasını Doğrulama: ECM konnektöründe CAN_H ile CAN_L arasındaki direnci ölçün

Kablo Demeti Sürtünmesini İnceleyin: Şasi kolları ve motor kulakları yakınındaki CAN omurgasını aşınma veya ezilme açısından görsel olarak takip edin. Düğüm Varlığını Kontrol Edin: Tüm aktif kaynak adreslerini listelemek için teşhis cihazı kullanın
Kılavuz Dondurulmuş Çerçeve Taraması: Arıza anındaki motor devrini ve yükünü belirlemek için dondurulmuş çerçeve verilerini okuyun. 5V Referans Kontrolü: Sensör konnektöründeki gerilimi ölçün

Kılavuz Kalibrasyon Kimliğini Okuma: Kalibrasyon sürümünün motor için en güncel OEM sürümüyle eşleştiğini doğrulamak üzere J1939 DM14'ü kullanın. Öğrenme İşlemini Yapın: Kontak açık, motor kapalıyken yetkili servis cihazıyla ECM kalibrasyon öğrenme prosedürünü başlatın. EEPROM CRC Kontrolü: Teşhis cihazıyla EEPROM sağlama toplamını (checksum) inceleyin

Kılavuz ECM Yazılım Sürümünü Doğrulama: İncelemeye devam etmeden önce yetkili servis arıza tespit cihazını kullanarak ECM bellenim ve kalibrasyon dosyası sürümlerinin OEM spesifikasyonlarına uyduğunu onaylayın. Besleme Gerilimini İnceleme: Yük altında akü ve alternatör çıkışını ölçün

Kılavuz Akü Gerilimini Ölçme: Dinlenme durumunda (min 12,5 V) ve marş sırasında (min 9,6 V) kontrol edin; spesifikasyonun altındaysa değiştirin. Sonlandırma Dirençlerini İnceleme: Aküyü ayırın, omurgada CAN_H ile CAN_L arasındaki direnci ölçün: 60 Ω olmalıdır. Konnektör Pim Bütünlüğünü Test Etme: ECM Pin 1 ve Pin 2'ye arkadan prob ile temas edin

steps_en_archive: Guide Verify ECM Power Supply: Measure voltage at ECM pin A1 (12V) and pin A2 (ground)
Guide Verify CAN Termination: Measure resistance between CAN_H and CAN_L at ECM connector
Inspect Harness Chafing: Visually trace the CAN backbone near frame rails and engine mounts for abrasion or pinching. Check Node Presence: Use a diagnostic tool to list all active source addresses
Guide Scan Freeze Frame: Retrieve freeze frame data to identify engine speed and load at fault occurrence. Check 5V Reference: Measure voltage at sensor connector

Guide Read Calibration ID: Use J1939 DM14 to verify calibration version matches the latest OEM release for the engine. Perform Learn-In: Initiate ECM calibration learn procedure using factory scan tool after key-on, engine-off. Check EEPROM CRC: Inspect EEPROM checksum with diagnostic tool

Guide Verify ECM Software Version: Confirm ECM firmware and calibration file versions match OEM specifications using a factory diagnostic tool before further investigation. Inspect Supply Voltage: Measure battery and alternator output under load

Guide Measure Battery Voltage: Check at rest (min 12.5V) and during cranking (min 9.6V). Replace if below spec. Inspect Termination Resistors: Disconnect battery, measure resistance between CAN_H and CAN_L at backbone: must be 60 ohms. Test Connector Pin Integrity: Back-probe ECM pins 1 and 2

SPN_5746.pgn_label: Aftertreatment 1 Diesel Exhaust Fluid Pump 1 Information
causes: Wiring Harness Damage: Physical damage to the wiring harness can cause shorts or open circuits, leading to this fault code
Relay Failure: A defective relay may not properly switch states, causing abnormal current flow in the DEF heater circuit
ECM Software Glitch: Software errors in the ECM can misinterpret signals, triggering false fault codes related to the DEF heater
Corroded Connectors: Moisture ingress leading to corroded connectors can disrupt the signal, resulting in this
steps: Kılavuz Röle Bobin Direncini Ölçme: Röleyi sökün ve bobin pimleri arasındaki direnci ölçün

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: DEF pompası montaj braketi yakınındaki röle kablo demetini sürtünme, yanık veya korozyon açısından inceleyin. Direnç Ölçümü: Röleyi ayırın, kontrol pimi ile şasi arasındaki bobin direncini ölçün
Kılavuz Röle Bobinini Ölçme: Röleyi sökün
Kılavuz Mesaj Hızını Doğrulama: Röle durumu PGN 64950'yi izlemek için J1939 teşhis cihazı kullanın

Kılavuz Röle Konnektörünü İnceleme: Isıtıcı rölesi konnektöründe korozyon, eğilmiş pimler veya gevşek terminaller olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Geri Bildirim Gerilimi Ölçümü: Kontak açık, motor kapalıyken röle geri bildirim pimindeki gerilimi ölçün

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Dozaj ünitesi yakınında röle konnektörünü korozyon, eğilmiş pimler veya erimiş plastik açısından kontrol edin. Direnç Kontrolü: Pin 85 ile Pin 86 arasındaki röle bobin direncini ölçün
steps_en_archive: Guide Measure Relay Coil Resistance: Disconnect relay and measure across coil pins

Guide Visual Inspection: Check relay harness for chafing, burns, or corrosion near the DEF pump mounting bracket. Measure Resistance: Disconnect relay and measure coil resistance between control pin and ground
Guide Measure Relay Coil: Disconnect relay
Guide Verify Message Rate: Use J1939 scan tool to monitor relay status PGN 64950

Guide Inspect Relay Connector: Check for corrosion, bent pins, or loose terminals at the heater relay connector. Measure Feedback Voltage: With key on, engine off, measure voltage at relay feedback pin
Guide Visual Inspection: Check relay connector for corrosion, bent pins, or melted plastic near the dosing unit. Resistance Check: Measure relay coil resistance between pins 85 and 86

causes: ECM Internal Corruption: Microprocessor memory corruption or flash storage degradation affecting internal
Wiring Issues: Damaged or corroded wiring can lead to voltage drops, triggering the fault code
Connector Problems: Loose or oxidized connectors can cause poor electrical connections, resulting in voltage issues
Sensor Malfunction: Faulty sensors may provide incorrect readings, causing the ECM to misinterpret voltage levels
ECM Fault: A malfunction within the ECM might misread voltage data, leading to erroneous fault codes
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM's microcontroller is pivotal in managing sensor input and power distribution
It monitors voltage levels continuously, ensuring they remain within specified parameters
Internal ECM Circuit: Failed microprocessor

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically Grid Heater circuit failed open.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically Grid Heater circuit failed open.‪
steps: Disconnect the Grid Heater harness connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 2 of the Grid Heater harness connector and ground.
Note: Voltage measurement must be taken with the first minute of key ON. If this was not done, cycle the key and recheck voltage.
If the voltage is greater than 11 volts, go to step 6.
If the voltage is less than 11 volts, go to the next step.
Cycle the ignition switch.
Recheck the voltage between pin 2 of the Grid Heater harness connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11 volts, go to the next step.
If voltage is still less than 11 volts, go to step 11.
Measure the voltage between pin 3 of the Grid Heater harness connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11 volts, go to step 10.
If voltage is less than 11 volts, go to the next step.
Turn the Ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 of the Grid Heater harness connector and pin 92 of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 ohms, repair open between pin 3 of the Grid Heater harness connector and pin 92 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "65.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 ohms, go to the next step.
Measure the resistance between pin 1 of the Grid Heater harness connector and ground.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, replace the Grid Heater. Refer to "65.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, repair short to ground between pin 3 of the Grid Heater harness connector and pin 79 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "65.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Measure the resistance between pin 2 of the Grid Heater harness connector and pin 41 of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3 Ω, repair open between pin 2 of the Grid Heater harness connector and pin 41 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "65.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3 Ω, replace the Grid Heater. Refer to "65.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
ENGINE EXHAUST
To avoid injury from inhaling engine exhaust, always operate the engine in a well-ventilated area. Engine exhaust is toxic.‪
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: DD15 Troubleshooting - Section 65.1 SPN 698/FMI 5 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

SPN_1070.description_en: Vehicle deceleration control - mechanical system not responding correctly or out of adjustment
causes: Upon detecting below-range deceleration control parameters, the ECM activates predetermined safety protocols including progressive torque reduction and auxiliary brake system isolation
Mercedes-Benz OM471 and MAN D2676 engines implement sophisticated fallback strategies limiting engine output to 75% rated power while maintaining essential vehicle mobility
These protective measures prevent potential drivetrain damage from uncontrolled deceleration events during system malfunctions
Effective long-term
ECM safety fallback mechanisms are critical in managing unexpected conditions
In response to SPN 1070 FMI 3, the ECM may initiate torque derating to protect the vehicle
This safety mode ensures controlled deceleration but can affect vehicle performance
Understanding the conditions triggering such responses helps in diagnosing underlying electrical issues and restoring normal operations effectively
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] CAN hattında veri trafiğini izleyin; bu düğümden beklenen mesajların (PGN) gelip gelmediğini doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal bütünlüğünü osiloskopla inceleyin; aralıklı paket kaybı ve yansıma arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Düğüm besleme gerilimini ve CAN transceiver beslemesini ölçün; aşırı gerilim koruma devresini kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 4 katalog] Düğüm besleme ve toprak bağlantısını ölçün; gerilim düşüklüğü/şasi teması arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 5 katalog] Düğümün güç hattında açık devre, sigorta ve konektör durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Düğüm güç hattında kısa devre/şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 8 katalog] Osiloskop ile PWM sinyal doluluk oranını (Duty Cycle) ve gürültü seviyesini inceleyin.
[FMI 9 katalog] CAN veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve düğüm adresleme çakışmasını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör içindeki elemanın gevşediğini veya soket pini korozyonunu inceleyin.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] İlgili ECU/modülün beslemesini ve toprağını teyit edin; modül yazılım sürümünü ve hatasını okuyun. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_1070.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_1070.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 17: Start Enable Relay
dd_procedures.overview: Vehicles with an UltraShift PLUS transmission are required to disable engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral gear position. Some vehicles prevent non-neu-tral engine cranking through the use of a normally open Start Enable Relay actuated by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) to interrupt power to the Starter. Other vehicles require the TECU to send a transmission engine crank enable message over the J1939 Data Link before the engine ECU will allow cranking. The Start Enable Relay cir-cuit is supplied and wired by the OEM. For vehicles equipped with a physical St
causes: Start Enable Relay Internal Failure Start Enable Relay Wiring Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occur-rences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. Note: If Fault Code 17 is Inactive and engine cranks, but does not run, troubleshoot vehicle engine system per OEM recommendations. Note: Some OEMs and chassis may use an alter-nate wiring pattern, which may include the use of a second relay for other vehicle systems. Please con-sult chassis specific OEM wiring schematics and verify which relay is in place for the Eaton automated transmission. If Fault Code 17 FMI 14 is Active, Go to Step B If Fault Code 17 FMI 14 is Inactive, Start Enable Relay may have been incorrectly wired and repaired or bypassed (jumped). Test complete, Go to Step V If Fault Code 17 FMI 3 or 4 is Active, Go to Step D If Fault Code 17 FMI 3 or 4 is Inactive, Go to Step C

B. Procedure to set FMI 14 Inactive. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Key off. Verify the Start Enable Relay circuit is correctly connected and wired per the wiring diagram. Con-sult OEM for specific wire routing locations. Cor-rect wire routing if necessary. Key on with engine off. Wait for Neutral (N) to appear in the gear display Turn and hold the key in the crank position for 5 seconds. A momentary crank should occur, but will be interrupted after 0.5 second. This test verifies the transmission can interrupt the Start Enable Relay circuit. The system does not allow engine cranking until the next power-up cycle. Key off. Notice Allow 2-3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Retrieve and record the transmission fault codes and FMIs, and their occurrences and timestamps. If Fault Code 17 FMI 14 is now Inactive and the engine will now crank, Start Enable Relay may have been incorrectly wired and repaired or bypassed (jumped). Test complete, Go to Step V If Fault Code 17 FMI 14 is Active or engine will not crank, Go to Step F

C. Use Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode to locate intermittent failures. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Place transmission in PD Mode. See more about Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode Wiggle Start Enable Relay wiring from the 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector to the Start Enable Relay. Look for signs of rubbing or chafing. Consult OEM for specific wire routing locations. Exit PD Mode by powering down. Notice Allow 2-3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. If Fault Code 17 became Active during wiggle wire test, repair or replace the Start Enable Relay wiring per OEM requirements. Go to Step V If Fault Code 17 remains Inactive, Go to Step E

D. Verify Start Enable Type (Relay or J1939) configured in the TECU and installed on the vehicle. Key off. Notice Allow 2–3 minutes for the TECU to perform a complete power-down sequence before proceeding. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Select “Configuration”. Select “Vehicle”. Record the “Current Value” for the “Start Enable Type”. Record the “Start Enable Type” installed on the vehicle. Note: The vehicle's “Start Enable Type” (hardwired relay or J1939 controlled), is determined by the OEM. Refer to the OEM regarding “Start Enable Type” installed on the vehicle. Compare reading(s) in table. If “Start Enable Type” is configured correctly, Go to Step E If “Start Enable Type” is not configured cor-rectly, select the correct configuration from the “New Value” drop down, select “Apply” and follow on screen prompt. Go to Step V Location Start Enable Type TECU (ServiceRanger) Vehicle

E. Verify proper voltage is supplied to the Start Enable Relay. Key off. Remove Start Enable Relay Inspect Relay Connector body for damage and bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals. Key on with engine off. Wait for Neutral (N) to appear in the gear display. Note: Flashing “F” may appear in the gear display. Measure voltage between Start Enable Relay socket Pin 86 (power) and Pin 85 (ground). Record read-ing(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If all readings are in range, Go to Step F If any readings are out of range, Go to Step G Pins Range Reading(s) 85 to 86 Within 1.5 V of Battery Voltage

F. Verify the proper resistance of the Start Enable Relay. Key off. Determine if vehicle uses a 12-volt or a 24-volt electrical system. Measure the resistance across relay Pin 85 and Pin 86. Record reading(s) in table. Note: The allowable relay resistance range is differ-ent for 12-volt and 24-volt systems. Measure the resistance across relay Pin 30 and Pin 87. Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If readings are in range, Go to Step G If readings are out of range, replace Start Enable Relay. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) 85 to 86 12 V System 40-200 Ohms 24 V System 40-500 Ohms 30 to 87 Open Circuit (OL)

G. Verify connection across the Start Enable Relay circuit wiring. Key off. Disconnect the 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector at the TECU. Inspect 38-Way Connector body for damage and bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals. Remove the Start Enable Relay. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 32 and Start Enable Relay socket Pin 86. Record reading(s) in table. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 4 and Start Enable Relay socket Pin 85. Record reading(s) in table. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 26 and Start Enable Relay Socket Pin 87. Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If all readings are in range, Go to Step H If readings are out of range, repair or replace the Start Enable Relay wiring per OEM guide-lines. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) VH 32 to SER 86 0.0-0.3 Ohms VH 4 to SER 85 0.0-0.3 Ohms VH 26 to SER 87 0.0-0.3 Ohms

H. Measure Start Enable Relay wiring (-) for indications of a short to ground or short to power. Key off. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 4 and ground. Record read-ing(s) in table. Measure resistance between 38-Way Connector Pin 4 and Battery Positive (+). Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If all readings are in range, Go to Step I If readings are out of range, repair or replace the Vehicle Harness per OEM guide-lines. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) 4 to Ground Open Circuit (OL) 4 to Battery Positive (+) Open Circuit (OL)

I. Measure Start Enable Relay wiring (+) for indications of a short to ground or short to power. Key off. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 32 and ground. Record read-ing(s) in table. Measure resistance between 38-Way Vehicle Har-ness Connector Pin 32 and Battery Positive (+). Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If all readings are in range, Go to Step J If readings are out of range, repair or replace the Vehicle Harness per OEM guide-lines. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) 32 to Ground Open Circuit (OL) 32 to Battery Positive (+) Open Circuit (OL)

J. Test the latch side of the Start Enable Relay circuit for a short to power. Key off. Measure voltage between Start Enable Relay socket Pin 87 and ground. Record reading(s) in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If all readings are in range, Go to Step K If readings are out of range, repair or replace the Start Enable Relay Latch wire per OEM guide-lines. Go to Step V Pins Range Reading(s) 87 to Ground Less than 0.5 volt
K. Determine which FMI was set in Step A. Verify which FMI was set for Fault Code 17 in Step A. If Fault Code 17 FMI 3 or 4 was set, Go to Step L If Fault Code 17 FMI 14 was set, Go to Step M

L. Verify wiring and test Start Enable Relay Circuit. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Key off. Verify the Start Enable Relay circuit is correctly connected and wired per the wiring diagram. Con-sult OEM for specific wire routing locations. Cor-rect wire routing if necessary. Key on with engine off. Wait for Neutral (N) to appear in the gear display. Attempt to crank the engine. If Fault Code 17 FMI 3 or 4 is now Inactive and the engine will now crank, no problem was found. The intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is in the Start Enable Relay wiring. Contact OEM for further help troubleshooting the wiring. Go to Step V If Fault Code 17 FMI 3 or 4 is Active, replace Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) . Go to Step V

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 120: Start Enable Relay
dd_procedures.overview: The Endurant HD transmission disables engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral gear position. Some vehicles prevent non-neutral engine cranking through the use of a normally open Start Enable Relay (SER) actuated by the Transmission Control Module (TCM) to interrupt power to the starter. Other vehicles rely on the TCM to send a Transmission Engine Crank Enable message over the Primary Data Link before the engine ECU will allow cranking. The SER and control circuits are contained within the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Consult OEM wiring diagrams. This fault indicates
causes: Start enable type not configured correctly in the TCM SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground, or open. Terminals may be bent, spread, or corroded. FMI 7: SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Incorrectly wired Bypassed or “jumped” circuit wiring FMI 12: TCM Internal failure Software issue Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system. C. Verify SER Connector condition. Key off. Remove SER from 4-Way relay socket. If contamination or damage is found, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the SER and/or 4-Way relay socket. Go to Step V If no contamination or damage is found, Go to Step D

SPN_1321.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: Vehicles with an UltraShift PLUS transmission are required to disable engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral gear position. Some vehicles prevent non-neu-tral engine cranking through the use of a normally open Start Enable Relay actuated by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) to interrupt power to the Starter. Other vehicles require the TECU to send a transmission engine crank enable message over the J1939 Data Link before the engine ECU will allow cranking. The Start Enable Relay cir-cuit is supplied and wired by the OEM. For vehicles equipped with a physical Start Enable Relay cir-cuit, the relay will only latch when the following three condi-tions exist: Driver Interface Device is in the neutral position. Transmission has confirmed that it is physically in neutral. Engine is not running. Under these conditions the TECU supplies a voltage source and a ground path to the Start Enable Relay coil, latching the relay. The latched relay allows Engine-Starter engage-ment when the ignition key is turned to the crank position. If these conditions are not met, the TECU removes the volt-age source and ground path to the Start Enable Relay, opening the relay a
procedures_full.detection: This fault can only be detected on transmission systems that are configured for Start Enable Relay. When the ignition key is on, the engine is not running, and the Start Enable Relay coil is not latched, this fault can be detected.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: TECU detects a short to voltage or an open circuit for at least 1 second. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: TECU detects a short to ground for at least 1 second. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: TECU detects an engine start when the Start Enable Relay was not intentionally latched. This is typically an indication that the Start Enable Relay circuit is incorrectly wired or bypassed (jumped).
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 3, 4: An electrical short or open circuit is not detected for 2 seconds. FMI 14: Start Enable Relay wiring issue is corrected and Start Enable Relay fault code is unlatched.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 3, 4: “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Engine will not crank. FMI 14: “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). If the Start Enable Relay circuit is incorrectly wired or bypassed (jumped), the TECU may not be able to prevent the engine from cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral position. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 3, 4: An electrical short or open circuit is not detected for 2 seconds. FMI 14: Start Enable Relay wiring issue is corrected and Start Enable Relay fault code is unlatched.

Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. 5-Way Start Enable Relay Socket 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 3. 5-Way Start Enable Relay Socket 4. 5-Way Start Enable Relay Start Enable Relay Circuit States (Normally Open) 1. Open Relay - Key On and Transmission is Unable to Confirm Neutral 2. Open Relay - Key Start and Transmission is Unable to Confirm Neutral 3. Closed Relay - Key On and Transmission Confirmed in Neutral 4. Closed Relay - Key Start and Transmission Confirmed in Neutral

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) disables engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral gear position. The TCM configuration parameter "Start Enable Type" is set to one of two different options depending on the method used on the particular vehicle. One method uses the TCM and a normally-open Start Enable Relay (SER) to interrupt power to the engine Starter. The second method relies on the TCM to send a Transmission Engine Crank Enable message to the engine ECU over the vehicle J1939 Data Link when engine cranking is allowed. The SER and J1939 Data Link wiring connect to the TCM through the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the SER control circuits. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active. Note: This fault code will not set on vehicles that use the Transmission Engine Crank Enable message on the J1939 Data Link to allow engine cranking.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: SER circuit shorted to power for 1 second. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: SER circuit shorted to ground for 1 second. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: SER circuit open for 1 second. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: Engine cranked when SER was not energized by the TCM. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: SER enabled under inappropriate conditions. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: Hardwired SER invalid configuration for 1 second.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring problem corrected and key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists. FMI 13: Hardwired SER valid configuration for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Amber warning lamp on No degraded performance Engine may not crank Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring problem corrected and key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exists. FMI 13: Hardwired SER valid configuration for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 3, 4, 5: SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground, or open Terminals bent, spread, corroded or loose “Start Enable Type” is incorrectly configured as “Relay” in the TCM on a vehicle equipped with a “J1939” start enable system. FMI 7: SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Incorrectly wired Bypassed or “jumped” circuit wiring FMI 12: TCM Internal failure Software issue FMI 13: “Start Enable Type” is incorrectly configured as “J1939” in the TCM on a vehicle equipped with a “Relay” start enable system. procedures_full.overview: The Endurant HD transmission disables engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-neutral gear position. Some vehicles prevent non-neutral engine cranking through the use of a normally open Start Enable Relay (SER) actuated by the Transmission Control Module (TCM) to interrupt power to the starter. Other vehicles rely on the TCM to send a Transmission Engine Crank Enable message over the Primary Data Link before the engine ECU will allow cranking. The SER and control circuits are contained within the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector. Consult OEM wiring diagrams. This fault indicates an electrical failure was detected in the SER or control circuits when the start enable type is configured for a relay in the TCM. This fault code will not set on vehicles that use J1939 messaging to enable engine cranking.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the SER control circuits. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: SER circuit shorted to power for 1 second. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: SER circuit shorted to ground for 1 second. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: SER circuit open for 1 second. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: Engine cranked when SER was not energized by the TCM for 2 seconds. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: SER enabled under inappropriate conditions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring issue corrected and ignition key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 3, 4, 5, 7: Amber Warning lamp on No degraded modes Engine may not crank FMI 12: Engine cranking prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring issue corrected and ignition key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 3, 4, 5: Start enable type not configured correctly in the TCM SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground, or open. Terminals may be bent, spread, or corroded. FMI 7: SER Internal failure SER circuit wiring Incorrectly wired Bypassed or “jumped” circuit wiring FMI 12: TCM Internal failure Software issue Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system.

procedures_full.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) disables engine cranking when the transmission is in a non-Neutral gear position. The TCM configuration parameter "Start Enable Type" is set to one of two different options depending on the method used on the vehicle. One method uses the TCM and a normally-open Start Enable Relay (SER) to interrupt power to the engine Starter. The second method relies on the TCM to send a Transmission Engine Crank Enable message to the Engine ECU over the vehicle Primary Data Link (J1939A) when engine cranking is allowed. The SER and Primary Data Link (J1939A) wiring connect to the TCM through the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the SER control circuits. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active. Note: This fault code will not set on vehicles that use the Transmission Engine Crank Enable message on the Primary Data Link (J1939A).
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: SER circuit shorted to power for 1 second. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: SER circuit shorted to ground for 1 second. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: SER circuit open for 1 second. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: Engine cranked when SER was not energized by the TCM for 2 seconds. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: SER enabled under inappropriate conditions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring issue corrected and ignition key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 3, 4, 5, 7: Amber Warning lamp on No degraded modes FMI 12: Engine cranking prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 3: SER circuit not shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 4: SER circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: SER circuit not open for 10 seconds. FMI 7: SER wiring issue corrected and ignition key cycle. FMI 12: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 3, 4, 5, 7: Vehicle Components SER internal failure Vehicle Harness - SER Circuit Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open Terminals bent, spread, corroded, or loose TCM “Start Enable Type” incorrectly configured as “Relay” on vehicle equipped with a “J1939” start enable system. FMI 12: TCM Internal failure Software issue Note: Refer to OEM for troubleshooting a failed system.

 86 to Ground Open Circuit (OL) 
 86 to Battery Positive (+) Open Circuit (OL)
steps.J:
J. Verify fault code status. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To “Fault Codes”. 
 Retrieve and record transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps. 
 If Fault Code 120 is Inactive, the intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely there is a wiring problem between the SER and 20-Way TCM Vehicle Connector. Refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the vehicle harness. Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 120 is Active and no fault was found with vehicle SER wiring, replace Transmission Control Module (TCM) . Go to Step V 
 Note: If troubleshooting indicates no fault found in wiring or connections to TCM, ensure an intermittent issue does not exist in wiring or connections before replacing TCM.
steps.K:
K. Verify if fault was inadvertently set. 
 Key off. 
 Note: FC 120 FMI 7 will only set Active during engine cranking. 
 Allow TCM to power down. 
 Key on with engine off 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To “Fault Codes”. 
 Retrieve and record transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps. 
 Verify Fault Code 120 FMI 7 is Inactive. 
 If Fault Code 120 FMI 7 is Inactive and engine cranks, SER may have been incorrectly wired and repaired or bypassed (jumped). Test complete. Go to Step V 
 If Fault Code 120 FMI 7 sets Active, Go to Step L
steps.L:
L. Verify SER latch control circuits are not shorted together. 
 Key off. 
 Remove SER. 
 Measure resistance between SER socket Pin 30 and Pin 87. Record reading in table. 
 Note: SER types may vary, refer to OEM wiring diagrams and connector views. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of SER latch control circuits. Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range, Go to Step M 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 30 to 87 Open Circuit (OL)
steps.M:
M. Verify SER latch (internal) is not shorted closed. 
 Key off 
 Measure resistance across the SER Pin 30 and Pin 87. Record reading in table. 
 Compare reading(s) in table. 
 If readings are out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for SER replacement. Go to Step V 
 If readings are in range, Go to Step V 
 Pins Range Reading(s) 
 30 to 87 Open Circuit (OL)
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To “Fault Codes”. 
 Select “Clear All Faults”. 
 Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 If no fault codes set and vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 120 sets Active, Go to Step A 
 If a fault code other than 120 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

steps_tr.F:
F. 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünün durumunu doğrulayın.
Kontağı kapatın.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünü TCM'den sökün.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünü inceleyin; konnektörün kirlenme ve korozyondan uzak olduğunu, klemenslerin eğilmediğini, açılmadığını veya gevşemediğini ve konnektör gövdesinde hasar olmadığını doğrulayın.
20 Yollu TCM Araç Konnektörünü inceleyin; konnektörün kirlenme ve korozyondan uzak olduğunu, klemenslerin eğilmediğini, açılmadığını veya gevşemediğini ve konnektör gövdesinde hasar olmadığını doğrulayın.
Kirlenme veya hasar bulunursa 20 Yollu TCM Araç Kablo Demeti Konnektörünün onarımı veya değişimi için OEM yönergelerine başvurun. Adım V'ye gidin.
Kirlenme veya hasar bulunamazsa Adım G'ye gidin

causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.
FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] CAN hattında veri trafiğini izleyin; bu düğümden beklenen mesajların (PGN) gelip gelmediğini doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 1 katalog] Ağ üzerinde beklenen veri akışının kesildiğini teyit edin; düğüm adreslemesini (Address Claim) kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal bütünlüğünü osiloskopla inceleyin; aralıklı paket kaybı ve yansıma arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Düğüm besleme gerilimini ve CAN transceiver beslemesini ölçün; aşırı gerilim koruma devresini kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 4 katalog] Düğüm besleme ve toprak bağlantısını ölçün; gerilim düşüklüğü/şasi teması arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 5 katalog] Düğümün güç hattında açık devre, sigorta ve konektör durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 14 katalog] Üreticinin özel servis prosedürüne başvurun; ağ tanılama kılavuzunu uygulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. When current falls below the calibrated threshold (typically Electrical analysis shows that an open circuit causes the ECM input voltage to float to 5V, but the
This code commonly appears after a forced DPF regeneration when the VGT actuator is cycled aggressively, or after replacing the ECM without proper calibration
Technicians frequently encounter this fault on Deutz TCD engines during cold weather operation when condensation affects connector integrity
steps: Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: ECM ile VGT aktüatörü arasındaki tesisatı erime, sürtünme veya kopuk kablolar açısından kontrol edin. Besleme Gerilimi Ölçümü: Aktüatör konnektöründe, referans ve şasi pimleri arasında 5 V ±0,2 V olduğunu doğrulayın. Süreklilik Kontrolü: ECM ve aktüatörü ayırın

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically a CAN3 communication error.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically a CAN3 communication error.‪
steps: CAN3 Check
Check for multiple codes.
If codes other than SPN 2795/FMI 9 are present, repair those first.
If only SPN 2795/FMI 9 is present, go to step 2.
Disconnect the turbo actuator connector.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin 1 of the turbo actuator connector and ground.
If the voltage is less than 11 volts, repair the cause of low or no voltage between pin 1 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 93 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is greater than 11 volts, go to step 5.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 of the turbo actuator connector and ground.
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 4 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 75 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, go to step 8.
Measure the resistance between pin 2 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 38 of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, repair the open between pin 2 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 38 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, go to step 9.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 74 of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, repair the open between pin 3 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 74 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, go to step 10.
Measure the resistance between pin 4 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 75 of the MCM 120–pin connector.
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, repair the open between pin 4 of the turbo actuator connector and pin 75 of the MCM 120–pin connector. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, replace the turbo actuator. Refer to "94.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis for SPN 3588/FMI 5 is typically an open circuit.‪
causes: This diagnosis for SPN 3588/FMI 5 is typically an open circuit.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Disconnect the Ether Start connector at the Ether Injection Relay.
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Measure the voltage between pin A of the Ether Injection Relay connector and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 11.5 volts, go to step 4.
If the voltage is less than 1.5 volts, repair the open between pin A of the Ether Injection Relay connector and pin 91 of the 120–pin connector. Refer to "113.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Check the resistance across the Ether Injection Relay connector.
If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the open between the Ether Injection Relay connector and pin 70 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "113.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 15 Ω or open, replace the Ether Injection Relay. Refer to "113.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 113.3 SPN 3588/FMI 5 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically proportional valve bank 2 circuit failed low.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically proportional valve bank 2 circuit failed low.‪
steps: Circuit Check
Turn the ignition ON (key ON, engine OFF).
Monitor the active codes.
Disconnect the front valve cover injector harness.
Does SPN 3798/FMI 4 become inactive?
If yes, go to step 5.
If no, go to step 9.
Reconnect the front valve cover injector harness.
Remove the upper valve cover
Disconnect the front Jake Brake® solenoid.
Does SPN 3798/FMI 4 become inactive?
If yes, replace the front Jake Brake solenoid. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no, replace the injector wiring harness. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Disconnect the EGR valve.
Does SPN 3798/FMI 4 become inactive?
If yes, replace the EGR valve. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no, go to step 11.
Disconnect the Electronic Dosing Valve.
Does SPN 3798/FMI 4 become inactive?
If yes, replace the Electronic Dosing Valve. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no, go to step 13.
Disconnect the Fuel Cutoff Valve.
Does SPN 3798/FMI 4 become inactive?
If yes, replace the Fuel Cutoff Valve. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no, go to step 15.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the MCM 120–pin connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 62 of the MCM 120–pin connector and ground.

If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 62 of the MCM 120–pin connector and the front injector valve cover connector, EGR Valve, Fuel Cutoff Valve and or Electronic Dosing Valve. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, go to step 18.
Measure the resistance between pin 64 of the MCM 120–pin connector and ground.

If the resistance is less than 5 Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 64 of the MCM 120–pin connector and the front injector valve cover connector, EGR Valve, Fuel Cutoff Valve and or Electronic Dosing Valve. Refer to "126.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is greater than 5 Ω, contact the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800 for MCM replacement.
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: Series 60 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 126.1 SPN 3798/FMI 4 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

causes: Common problems contributing to this code include failures of the boost controller switch and exhaust back pressure switches.
steps: Kılavuz Canlı Verileri Okuma: Rölantide ve ani gaz testinde egzoz freni basıncını izleyerek düzensiz okumaları tespit edin. Egzoz Fren Valfini İnceleme: Valfi bir vakum pompasıyla manuel olarak kumanda edin
Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Sensör konnektörünü ve kablo demetini erimiş yalıtım, korozyon veya pim hasarı açısından kontrol edin. Gerilim Ölçümü: Sensördeki sinyal pimi gerilimini ölçün
Kılavuz Gerilim Ölçümü: Konnektördeki sensör besleme gerilimini ölçün
Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Turboşarj aktüatör mekanizmasını sıkışma, çatlak veya kurum birikintileri açısından kontrol edin

Kılavuz Sensör Gücünü Doğrulama: Kontak açık, motor kapalıyken sensör Pin A ile Pin B arasında 5 V ±0,2 V olduğunu ölçün. J1939 Kablolarını İnceleme: Sensör konnektöründe CAN High/Low direncini kontrol edin
Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Manifold contalarında ve spiral bağlantılarda egzoz kaçağı olup olmadığını kontrol edin
SPN_5541.pgn_description: Contains information about the engine exhaust brake system control.
steps_en_archive: Guide Read Live Data: Monitor exhaust brake pressure at idle and during a snap throttle test to identify erratic readings. Inspect Exhaust Brake Valve: Manually actuate the valve with a vacuum pump
Guide Visual Inspection: Check sensor connector and harness for melted insulation, corrosion, or pin damage. Voltage Measurement: Measure signal pin voltage at sensor
Guide Voltage Measurement: Measure sensor supply voltage at connector
Guide Visual Inspection: Check turbocharger actuator linkage for binding, cracks, or carbon deposits
Guide Verify Sensor Power: Measure 5V ±0.2V between sensor pin A and pin B with key-on, engine-off. Inspect J1939 Wiring: Check CAN High/Low resistance at sensor connector
Guide Visual Inspection: Check for exhaust leaks at manifold gaskets and flex joints

[FMI 6 katalog] Düğüm güç hattında kısa devre/şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_19.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_19.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

SPN_380.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_380.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).
causes: Damaged sensor wiring: Chafed or broken wires in the harness between the articulation sensor and the chassis controller
Faulty sensor connector: Corroded or loose pins at the 3-pin DEUTSCH connector cause intermittent signal loss
Defective angle sensor: Internal Hall-effect element failure prevents the sensor from outputting a valid PWM signal
ECM software glitch: Firmware bug in the steering control module occasionally skips the message transmission slot
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM monitors the articulation angle message ID on the CAN bus at a 10 Hz rate
If no valid message is received for 1.2 seconds (12 consecutive missed updates), the FMI 9 is set
Technicians frequently encounter this fault on articulated dump trucks and wheel loaders during post-repair validation
steps: Kılavuz CAN Veri Yolu Trafiğini Kontrol Etme: J1939 breakout kutusu bağlayın ve açı mesaj kimliğinin her 100 ms ±10 ms'de bir geldiğini doğrulayın. Sensör Konnektörünü İnceleme: 3 pinli DEUTSCH konnektörünü ayırın

Kılavuz Görsel Tesisat Muayenesi: Sensörden ECM'ye giden kabloları mafsal noktasında kesik, sürtünme veya gevşek konnektörler açısından inceleyin. Sensör Direnç Testi: Sinyal ve şasi pimleri arasındaki direnci ölçün

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Mafsal esneme bölgesinde konnektörü eğilmiş pimler, korozyon veya kopuk kablolar açısından kontrol edin. Gerilim Ölçümü: Kontak açıkken sensör konnektöründe 5 V referansını ve şasiyi ölçün. Sinyal Tarama Testi: Mafsalı tam soldan tam sağa yavaşça döndürürken sinyal gerilimini izleyin
steps_en_archive: Guide Check CAN bus traffic: Connect a J1939 breakout box and verify the angle message ID appears every 100 ms ±10 ms. Inspect sensor connector: Unplug the 3-pin DEUTSCH connector
Guide Visual harness inspection: Examine wiring from sensor to ECM for cuts, chafing, or loose connectors at the pivot. Sensor resistance test: Measure between signal and ground pins

Guide Visual inspection: Check connector for bent pins, corrosion, or broken wire at articulation joint flex zone. Voltage measurement: Measure 5V reference and ground at sensor connector with ignition on. Signal sweep test: Monitor signal voltage while slowly articulating full left to right

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 74 - Engine Speed Response Fault
dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates the transmission is unable to use system controls to synchronize during a shift.
causes: Engine control system
steps: A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Contact vehicle OEM for further direction. Key on. Retrieve fault codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 74 is Active, contact the OEM because the engine is failing to respond to the transmissions command during a shift. If fault code is not Active, test complete.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 74: Engine Speed / Torque Response
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) communicates with the engine ECU over the J1939 Data Link. During every shift, the TECU receives speed and torque information from the engine and requests changes in speed or torque from the engine to synchronize shifts. If the engine does not respond to speed or torque commands and no J1939 communication fault codes are present, the fault is set.
causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. Notice Fault Code 74 sets due to the engine failing to respond to torque or speed requests sent by the TECU. Possible causes for this fault are due to OEM issues and cannot be caused by the transmission wiring or TECU. If an engine software update was recently performed and Fault Code 74 is Inactive, Go to Step D If Fault Code 74 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step B

dd_procedures.title: Hybrid Performance Test
dd_procedures.overview: The hybrid system uses a combination of diesel engine and electric power to provide varying levels of torque during vehicle operation. If the hybrid system has a fault, or if a hybrid component is above the optimum operating temperature, the vehicle will reduce the amount of available Motor/Generator torque. Note: This symptom-based test should only be performed when directed by the Symptom-Driven Diagnostics Index and there are no Active fault codes.

Note: No schematic for this test. Hybrid Performance

SPN_518.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_518.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 74: Engine Speed / Torque Response
procedures_full.overview: The Fuller Advantage Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) communicates with the engine ECU over the J1939 Data Link. During every shift, the TECU receives speed and torque information from the engine and requests changes in speed or torque from the engine to synchronize shifts. If the engine does not respond to speed or torque commands and no J1939 communication fault codes are present, the fault is set. This fault can also be set if the TECU or engine ECU configuration settings are not correctly matched.
procedures_full.detection: TECU monitors the net torque output and calculates the synchronization speed required to shift efficiently. If the request is sent to increase or decrease engine torque or speed and the engine does not respond or does not respond fully, the fault is set. Incorrect engine or transmission configuration settings can also set this fault code.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: TECU detects no speed/torque response from the engine for more than 2 consecutive seconds after the request is sent. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: TECU is configured for a transmission model that requires an engine specific message that was not received for 15 seconds. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: TECU receives the required engine message but is not configured for the correct transmission model.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 7: This fault is set inactive 4 seconds after the engine responds to TECU speed/torque requests. FMI 12 & 13: This fault is set inactive when the engine configurations are correctly matched to transmission configurations.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 7 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Transmission may not attempt a shift. Transmission may engage a start or reverse gear from neutral, but will not shift out of that gear. FMI 12 Engine may not be optimized for shift quality or fuel economy FMI 13 Transmission may not be able to complete a shift Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 7: This fault is set inactive 4 seconds after the engine responds to TECU speed/torque requests. FMI 12 & 13: This fault is set inactive when the engine configurations are correctly matched to transmission configurations.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 7 Engine Incorrect engine software settings Low engine power or mechanical engine issues Engine ECU FMI 12 Engine Incorrect engine software settings FMI 13 TECU Incorrect Transmission Model configuration Component Identification 1. SPN_931.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_931.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).
causes: This fault often surfaces after ECM replacements or following fuel system maintenance
Technicians might notice this fault code when the vehicle experiences erratic fuel delivery, potentially leading to power loss
In practice, such issues are observed after forced DPF regenerations, which impact actuator functions
Identifying the precise cause is critical due to the absence of a known root cause, requiring comprehensive
Actuator Microprocessor Failure: Internal control chip malfunction preventing proper CAN bus communication and position feedback signals
CAN Communication Error: Corrupted data transmission between fuel pump actuator and ECM causing
Circuit Testing: Perform resistance and continuity testing on actuator wiring harness to identify potential electrical circuit defects
Pressure Analysis: Conduct complete fuel system pressure testing to verify pump performance and identify restriction sources
steps: Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Egzoz yakınında aktüatör konnektörünü korozyon, eğilmiş pimler veya erimiş yalıtım açısından kontrol edin. Direnç Kontrolü: Aktüatör bobin direncini ölçün; 0,5-2,0 Ω arasında olmalıdır

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Motor bloğu ve egzoz yakınındaki aktüatör kablo demetini sürtünme, yanık veya ezilmiş kablolar açısından kontrol edin. Direnç Ölçümü: Aktüatörü ayırın, pimler arasındaki direnci ölçün; 2-5 Ω olmalıdır

Kılavuz Görsel Muayene: Motor kulakları yakınındaki aktüatör konnektörünü ve tesisatını hasar, korozyon veya sürtünme açısından kontrol edin. Direnç Kontrolü: Pimler arasındaki aktüatör bobin direncini ölçün
Kılavuz CAN Trafiğini Doğrulama: J1939 breakout kutusu bağlayın ve aktüatör PGN 65132 mesajını izleyin

Kılavuz Aktif Durumu Doğrulama: SPN 931 FMI 13'ün geçmiş arıza olmayıp aktif olduğunu doğrulamak için J1939 teşhis cihazı kullanın. Aktüatör Kablolarını Kontrol Etme: Konnektör pimlerini korozyon veya eğilmiş terminaller açısından inceleyin

steps_en_archive: Guide Visual Inspection: Check actuator connector for corrosion, bent pins, or melted insulation near exhaust. Resistance Check: Measure actuator coil resistance between 0.5-2.0 ohms

Guide Visual inspection: Check the actuator harness for chafing, burns, or pinched wires near the engine block and exhaust. Measure resistance: Disconnect actuator, measure resistance across pins. Should be 2-5 ohms
Guide Visual Inspection: Check actuator connector and harness for damage, corrosion, or chafing near engine mounts. Resistance Check: Measure actuator coil resistance between pins
Guide Verify CAN Traffic: Connect a J1939 breakout box and monitor actuator PGN 65132

procedures_full.overview: FMI 5 on the cylinder 7 injector circuit indicates the ECM detected missing or below-threshold current rise during commanded injection. The ECM monitors injector driver current during each injection event and sets FMI 5 when current rise is absent or insufficient. Open connector, broken harness branch, failed injector winding or piezo path, pass-through terminal backout, and oil intrusion bridging then opening intermittently are the primary causes. Service-induced opens after injector replacement when the connector is not fully latched and vibration fatigue at flex loops are documented patterns. Replacing the injector without circuit proof wastes the injector cost when the fault is a disconnected connector or broken harness branch.
causes: Open connector — connector not fully latched at cylinder 7 injector
Broken harness branch — wire break in cylinder 7 injector circuit
Failed injector winding or piezo path — internal injector open
Pass-through terminal backout — terminal backed out at valve cover pass-through
Oil intrusion — oil intrusion bridging then opening circuit intermittently
steps: Single Action Gate — Visual Connector Seat Inspection

Inspect the cylinder 7 injector connector lock and seating. Service-induced opens after injector replacement when the connector is not fully latched are a documented cause. Confirm the connector is fully latched and the lock tab is engaged before any electrical measurements.
Binary Decision Gate — Resistance Check

Measure injector resistance at the cylinder 7 connector. An OL or high resistance reading confirms an open circuit. Compare to OEM injector specification for the specific injector type. A resistance within specification with a confirmed open circuit code confirms a harness fault between the connector and the ECM.
Override Manager — Continuity to Controller

Verify continuity from the cylinder 7 injector connector to the ECM injector driver connector. A continuity failure confirms a harness break between the injector and the ECM. Inspect harness near valve cover edges, brackets, and pass-through terminals for the break location.
Safety Interceptor — Verify No Short Before Re-Actuation

Verify no short-to-ground or short-to-power exists before re-actuating the injector driver. A short in the circuit can damage the ECM injector driver. Confirm circuit integrity before any injector actuation tests.
Resume Point — Harness vs Injector Isolation

Isolate harness versus injector as the fault source. A harness with confirmed continuity and a connector with confirmed seating that still shows OL resistance at the injector pins confirms an internal injector open. An internal injector open requires injector replacement with coding or trim where required.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Contribution Confirmation

procedures_full.overview: SPN 657 FMI 5 means the Mercedes-Benz ECM sees an open circuit in the cylinder #7 injector driver and cannot fire that injector. It's a High severity fault causing a rough idle and power loss, but it does not shut the engine down. Mercedes-Benz OM460 and OM470 engines, commonly found in European-spec Actros and Axor platforms as well as some North American applications, use the same J1939 injector cylinder numbering convention as other heavy-duty engines, with SPN 657 covering cylinder #7. FMI 5 points to current below normal, the classic electrical signature of an open circuit rather than a short. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com covers this fault often because harness chafing at the valve cover is such a consistent root cause across virtually every OEM platform using individual cylinder injector codes.
causes: Chafed valve cover harness wire
Vibration wears through insulation where the harness routes near rocker arm hardware, eventually breaking the conductor completely.
Corroded or loose injector connector
Moisture intrusion or an improperly seated locking tab creates a high-resistance or open contact the ECM reads as a dead circuit.
Failed injector solenoid winding
Internal solenoid coil failure from heat and vibration fatigue can open the circuit after extended service life.
ECM injector driver stage failure
An internal ECM fault on that specific driver channel would show the same code, but only after the injector and harness both test clean.
steps: Connect a Mercedes-Benz compatible diagnostic tool and confirm SPN 657 FMI 5, then run a cylinder cutout test to verify cylinder #7 contributes nothing.
Shut down and unplug the cylinder #7 injector connector, checking for corrosion, bent pins, or a loose locking tab.
Measure resistance across the injector solenoid terminals with a multimeter and compare to the OM engine family spec.
If the injector reads good, trace the harness back toward the ECM for chafing near the valve cover or rocker assembly.
Repair or replace the faulty component, clear the code, and re-run the cutout test to confirm cylinder #7 is firing correctly before road testing.
symptoms: Rough idle with a miss traceable to cylinder #7
MIL illuminated
Reduced power and fuel economy
Possible white smoke from unburned fuel at the affected cylinder

procedures_full.overview: SPN 658 FMI 5 on Caterpillar C15/C16 engines means cylinder #8's injector circuit is reading current below normal, consistent with an open circuit. It's a high-severity fault causing a real misfire on that cylinder, most often traced to a harness connector issue rather than a failed injector. A dead or open injector circuit on any single cylinder produces an unmistakable rough-running complaint, and SPN 658 pinpoints it directly to cylinder #8 on Caterpillar's numbering. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com works this fault methodically - pin-testing the harness connector at the valve cover before ever pulling the injector itself, since a corroded or backed-out pin produces the exact same open-circuit reading as a genuinely failed injector solenoid, at a fraction of the repair cost.
causes: Corroded or damaged injector harness connector
The connector at the valve cover is exposed to heat, oil, and vibration, making it a frequent point of failure that mimics an internal injector fault.
Broken wire within the injector harness
Repeated flexing where the harness routes near the valve cover grommet can eventually fracture a wire internally, producing an open circuit.
Failed injector solenoid winding
The injector's internal solenoid coil can fail open after sufficient heat cycling and electrical stress over its service life.
ECM driver circuit fault for that specific cylinder
An internal ECM issue affecting just one injector driver circuit is uncommon but should be considered if the harness and injector both test normal.
steps: Pull the fault with Cat ET and confirm SPN 658 FMI 5 is active; check for any other injector-related codes that might indicate a broader harness issue rather than a single-cylinder problem.
Locate the injector wiring harness connector for cylinder #8 at the valve cover and inspect it closely for corrosion, a bent pin, or a connector that isn't fully latched.

Disconnect the connector and use a multimeter to check resistance across the injector solenoid winding, comparing the reading to the manufacturer's specification and to a known-good cylinder on the same engine.
If resistance reads infinite (open), trace the harness back toward the ECM looking for a break, often at a point where the harness flexes near the valve cover grommet.
If the injector itself tests open internally, replace that injector following the proper torque and calibration procedure required after Cat injector service.
Clear the code and run the engine, using Cat ET's cylinder cutout test to confirm cylinder #8 is now contributing power evenly with the others before returning it to service.
symptoms: Rough idle with a distinct miss you can feel and hear
Reduced power and possible black or white smoke depending on the failure mode
Check Engine lamp illuminated
Increased fuel consumption as the ECM compensates on remaining cylinders
