procedures_full.overview: FMI 6 on cylinder 10 injector indicates the ECM detected above-normal current on the cylinder 10 injector driver circuit. Internal injector short, harness short to power or ground, oil-bridged terminals, and pinched loom after service are the primary causes. Oil-filled connectors creating intermittent high-current faults and harness damage after in-frame service are documented patterns. Avoid repeated actuation into a shorted circuit — repeated actuation can damage ECM drivers. Disconnect the injector and isolate the harness from the component before any further testing.
causes: Internal injector short — internal injector short circuit producing above-normal current
Harness short to power or ground — harness insulation damage producing short
Oil-bridged terminals — oil intrusion bridging terminals in connector
Pinched loom after service — harness pinched during service producing insulation damage
steps: Single Action Gate — Inspect for Insulation Rub-Through

Inspect for insulation rub-through on bracket edges and valve-cover corners. A harness that rubs against a sharp bracket edge or valve-cover corner produces insulation damage that creates a short circuit. Inspect the harness routing from the ECM to the cylinder 10 injector for rub-through points.
Binary Decision Gate — Disconnect Injector and Isolate Harness

Disconnect the cylinder 10 injector and isolate the harness from the component. Avoid repeated actuation into a shorted circuit — repeated actuation can damage ECM drivers. Test harness short-to-power and short-to-ground with the injector disconnected to isolate the harness from the component.
Override Manager — Resistance and Short Tests

Perform resistance and short tests on the cylinder 10 injector and harness. A resistance below the OEM minimum specification supports an internal injector short. A short-to-power or short-to-ground confirmed with the injector disconnected confirms a harness fault. A short that clears when the harness is disconnected from the ECM confirms the fault is in the harness, not the ECM.
Safety Interceptor — Repair Circuit Before Installing New Injector

Repair the circuit before installing a new injector if the harness is at fault. Installing a new injector into a shorted harness damages the new injector and the ECM driver. Confirm harness integrity before any injector replacement.
Resume Point — Oil Intrusion Inspection

Inspect for oil intrusion in the cylinder 10 injector connector and harness. Oil-filled connectors creating intermittent high-current faults are a documented pattern. Clean and seal the connector if oil intrusion is found. Identify and correct the oil leak source before returning to service.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Current Confirmation

After repair, verify cylinder 10 injector circuit current returns to normal. Confirm SPN 660 FMI 6 does not return. Monitor for return of high-current events or driver protection events over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Harness, Connector, or Injector Decision

Repair harness or connector if short circuit is confirmed in the harness path. Replace injector only if internal short is proven after harness integrity is confirmed. Perform injector coding or trim where required by the OEM after replacement. Do not replace the injector for a harness short circuit.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 661 FMI 5 is a cylinder 11 injector circuit open/low-current class fault. The ECM driver monitors current during commanded injection and sets FMI 5 when expected current rise is absent — the driver commanded the injector but saw no current response. Unseated connectors, open harness branches, failed injector winding or piezo paths, pass-through pin backouts, and oil or corrosion intrusion are the primary causes. Service-induced opens after injector R&R and vibration fatigue at flex loops are documented patterns. Cylinder-local circuit gates prevent multi-injector shotgun repairs.
causes: Unseated connector — cylinder 11 connector not fully seated producing open circuit
Open harness branch — open in harness branch to cylinder 11 injector
Failed injector winding or piezo path — internal injector open producing no current response
Pass-through pin backout — pin backed out at valve cover or ECM pass-through
Oil or corrosion intrusion — oil or corrosion in connector producing open circuit
steps: Step 1 — Visual Connector Seat Inspection

Inspect the cylinder 11 injector connector lock and seating. A connector that is not fully seated produces an open circuit that reads identical to a failed injector. Inspect the connector lock, under-cover pass-throughs, and chafe points near brackets and valve-cover edges. Service-induced opens after injector R&R are a documented pattern — always inspect the connector first after any recent injector service.
Step 2 — Resistance Measurement

Measure injector resistance at the connector. Compare to OEM injector specification. An OL or high resistance reading versus OEM spec supports an open circuit. Resistance within spec with a confirmed open circuit at the ECM driver indicates a harness fault between the connector and the ECM.
Step 3 — Continuity to Controller

Verify continuity from the driver connector to the injector connector. A continuity loss confirms an open in the harness path. Inspect the harness for chafe, vibration fatigue at flex loops, and pin backouts at pass-throughs.
Step 4 — Isolate Harness vs Injector

Isolate the fault to the harness or the injector. Disconnect the injector and measure resistance at the injector terminals directly. An OL reading at the injector terminals with a good harness confirms an internal injector open. A good injector resistance with a confirmed harness open confirms a harness fault.
Step 5 — Confirm No Short Before Re-Actuation
Confirm no short-to-power or short-to-ground before re-actuation. Do not repeatedly actuate a circuit with an unresolved fault. Confirm the circuit is clean before any injector actuation test.
Step 6 — Replace Injector Only If Internal Open Proven
Replace the injector only if an internal open is proven at the injector terminals. Injector replacement with coding or trim where required. Do not replace the injector for a harness fault.
Step 7 — Verify After Repair
Verify cylinder 11 contribution after repair. Confirm SPN 661 FMI 5 does not return. Monitor for return of cylinder 11 open circuit faults over extended operation.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 662 FMI 6 is a cylinder 12 injector circuit current above normal (short class) fault. The ECM driver monitors current during commanded injection and sets FMI 6 when current exceeds the expected range — the driver commanded the injector and saw excessive current. Internal injector shorts, harness shorts, oil-bridged terminals, and pinched looms after service are the primary causes. Oil intrusion creating intermittent high-current faults and harness damage after in-frame work are documented patterns. Protecting ECM drivers from repeated short events is a critical diagnostic priority.
causes: Internal injector short — internal injector short producing excessive current
Harness short — harness short to power or ground producing excessive current
Oil-bridged terminals — oil bridging connector terminals producing short circuit
Pinched loom after service — loom pinched during in-frame or valve cover service producing short
steps: Step 1 — Disconnect Injector and Isolate

Disconnect the cylinder 12 injector and isolate the harness from the injector. Do not repeatedly actuate a shorted driver. Disconnecting the injector allows the harness to be tested independently from the injector.
Step 2 — Resistance Test at Injector Terminals

Measure resistance at the injector terminals directly. Resistance below OEM minimum supports an internal injector short. Compare to OEM injector specification. An internal short confirmed at the injector terminals justifies injector replacement after circuit proof.
Step 3 — Short-to-Power and Short-to-Ground Check

Check for short-to-power and short-to-ground with the injector disconnected. A short that remains with the injector disconnected confirms a harness fault. A short that clears with the injector disconnected confirms an internal injector fault. Repair the harness before any injector replacement if a harness short is confirmed.
Step 4 — Inspect for Oil Intrusion and Harness Damage

Inspect the connector for oil intrusion and the harness for damage. Oil-bridged terminals produce intermittent high-current faults. Harness damage after in-frame work produces short circuits. Inspect the loom for pinch points near valve cover edges and brackets.
Step 5 — Repair Circuit Before New Injector If Harness Is at Fault

Repair the circuit before any injector replacement if a harness fault is confirmed. A new injector installed into a harness short will fail the new injector and may damage the ECM driver. Confirm circuit integrity before any injector replacement.
Step 6 — Replace Injector with Coding Where Required
Replace the injector with coding or trim where required if an internal short is confirmed. Confirm circuit integrity before the first actuation of the new injector.
Step 7 — Verify After Repair
Verify cylinder 12 operation after repair. Confirm SPN 662 FMI 6 does not return. Monitor for return of high-current events over extended operation.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 663 FMI 5 is a cylinder 13 injector circuit open or low-current class fault. The ECM monitors injector driver current during commanded injection and sets FMI 5 when expected current rise is absent. Unseated connector, open harness branch, failed injector winding or piezo path, pass-through pin backout, and oil or corrosion intrusion are the primary causes. Service-induced opens after injector R&R and vibration fatigue at flex loops are documented patterns. Replacing the injector before proving the circuit is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Unseated connector — unseated cylinder 13 connector producing open circuit
Open harness branch — open harness branch producing no current path to injector
Failed injector winding or piezo path — failed injector internal path producing open circuit
Pass-through pin backout — pass-through pin backed out producing open circuit
Oil or corrosion intrusion — oil or corrosion intrusion producing open circuit
steps: Step 1 — Visual Connector Seat

Inspect the cylinder 13 connector lock, under-cover pass-through pins, and chafe points near valve-cover edges and brackets. Service-induced opens after injector R&R are a documented pattern — always inspect the connector after any recent injector service. Confirm the connector is fully seated and locked.
Step 2 — Resistance Test

Measure injector resistance against OEM specification. OL or high resistance versus OEM injector specification supports an open injector winding. Compare to adjacent cylinder injectors as a reference, but use OEM specification as the standard.
Step 3 — Continuity to Controller

Check continuity from the driver connector to the injector. A continuity loss from the driver connector to the injector confirms a harness or connector fault. Confirm insulation integrity before re-commanding injection.
Step 4 — Isolate Harness vs Injector

Isolate the harness from the injector. A resistance fault that clears with the injector disconnected confirms a harness fault. A resistance fault that remains with the injector disconnected confirms an injector internal fault.
Step 5 — Replace Injector Only After Internal Open Is Proven

Replace the injector only after an internal open is proven. Confirm the harness and connector are clean before injector replacement. An injector replaced into a harness open will not resolve the fault.

1 . Repair harness or connector if open circuit is confirmed in the harness.
2 . Replace injector with coding or trim where required if internal open is confirmed ($300–$900+).
3 . Inspect and repair pass-through pins if backout is confirmed.
Verification Steps

procedures_full.overview: SPN 664 FMI 6 is a cylinder 14 injector circuit current above normal or short class fault. Internal injector short, harness short to power or ground, oil-bridged terminals, and pinched loom after service are the primary causes. Oil intrusion creating intermittent high-current faults and harness damage after in-frame service are documented patterns. Replacing the injector before isolating the short source is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern — a new injector installed into a harness short will fail the new injector and may damage the ECM driver.
causes: Internal injector short — internal injector short producing above-normal current
Harness short to power or ground — harness short producing above-normal current
Oil-bridged terminals — oil bridging connector terminals producing short circuit
Pinched loom after service — loom pinched after service producing short circuit
steps: Step 1 — Disconnect Injector

Disconnect the cylinder 14 injector. Avoid repeated actuation into a shorted driver. A short that clears with the injector disconnected confirms an internal injector short. A short that remains with the injector disconnected confirms a harness fault.
Step 2 — Isolate Harness vs Component

Isolate the harness from the component. Inspect insulation rub-through on bracket edges, valve-cover corner damage, and oil-filled connectors. Oil intrusion creating intermittent high-current faults is a documented pattern — inspect the connector for oil intrusion.
Step 3 — Resistance and Short Tests

Perform resistance and short tests. Resistance below OEM minimum supports an internal short. Check short-to-power and short-to-ground with the injector disconnected. A short that remains with the injector disconnected confirms a harness fault.
Step 4 — Repair Circuit Before Installing New Injector If Harness Is at Fault

Repair the circuit before installing a new injector if the harness is at fault. A new injector installed into a harness short will fail the new injector and may damage the ECM driver. Confirm the harness is clean before any injector replacement.
Step 5 — Replace Injector With Coding After Circuit Proof
Replace the injector with coding or trim where required after circuit proof. Confirm the harness is clean and the short is resolved before injector replacement.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 666 FMI 5 is a cylinder 16 injector circuit open class fault. Connector open, harness open, injector internal open, and pass-through terminal exit failure are the primary causes. Overlooked connector not fully locked after major service is a documented pattern — harder-access connectors are often disturbed during major engine dress service. Broad injector service for a single-circuit fault is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.

Injector internal open — injector internal open producing open circuit

steps: Step 1 — Access and Inspect Connector

Access and inspect the cylinder 16 connector. Harder-access connectors are often disturbed during major engine dress service. Overlooked connector not fully locked after major service is a documented pattern. Confirm the connector is fully seated and locked.
Step 2 — Electrical Measurements

Perform electrical measurements. Measure injector resistance against OEM specification. Check continuity from the driver to the injector. The resistance and continuity process is identical to other cylinder open faults — use OEM specifications as the standard.
Step 3 — Safe Comparison to Adjacent Cylinders

Compare to adjacent cylinders as a reference only. Use OEM specifications as the standard. A resistance or continuity fault on cylinder 16 that is not present on adjacent cylinders confirms a cylinder 16 specific fault.
Step 4 — Single-Circuit Isolation Before Broad Service

Isolate the single circuit before any broad injector service. A single-circuit fault does not require broad injector service. Repair the harness or connector if a harness fault is confirmed. Replace the injector only if an internal open is confirmed after circuit proof.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Can worn synchronizers on the ZF AS-Tronic be replaced without a full transmission overhaul?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF AS-Tronic and TraXon transmissions can be repaired by qualified ZF-authorized service centers. Synchronizer ring replacement is possible as part of a targeted repair, though accessing the synchronizers requires significant disassembly. ZF Testman can identify the specific affected gear to guide the repair scope.

troubleshooting_faq.question: How does ZF Testman identify which gear is causing SPN 731 FMI 2 on the AS-Tronic?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: ZF Testman logs the gear number and shift event associated with each ratio mismatch fault occurrence. The fault history shows which specific gear consistently fails to achieve the correct ratio. This narrows the mechanical investigation to the actuator, synchronizer, and gear set associated with that particular position.

troubleshooting_faq.question: Will the ZF AS-Tronic or TraXon continue to drive if one gear has a ratio mismatch fault?
troubleshooting_faq.answer: Yes, in most cases. The ZF TCU is designed to recognize a failed gear and adjust its shift strategy to avoid that gear if possible. The transmission will continue to operate with a reduced gear selection until the fault is repaired. Extended operation avoiding a gear does add load to adjacent gears and may accelerate wear.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 13 - J1939 Shift Control Device
dd_procedures.overview: This fault indicates communication has been lost, or does not correspond with the neutral request input from the J1939 Shift Device. When troubleshooting an Inactive code, See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
causes: OEM J1939 Shift Control Device Vehicle Harness
steps: A. Verify continuity of Neutral Request Signal wire Key off. Disconnect negative battery cable. Disconnect Vehicle Harness 38-way connector. Measure resistance between 38-way connector Pin 16 and corresponding OEM pin at J1939 Shift Device and Pin 16 and ground (see OEM wiring for correct pin location) If resistance is 0 to 0.3 ohms between Pin 16 and the corresponding OEM pin and resistance to ground is 10K ohms or greater , Go to Step B If resistance is out of range , replace the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V

B. Verify continuity of Neutral Request Return wire Measure resistance between 38-way connector Pin 17 and corresponding OEM pin at J1939 Shift Device and Pin 17 and ground (see OEM wiring for correct pin location). If resistance is 0 to 0.3 ohms between Pin 17 and the corresponding OEM pin and resistance to ground is 10K ohms or greater, problem exists with the J1939 Shift Device, or J1939 Shift Device power, ground or data link wiring. Contact your OEM for repair strategy. Go to Step V If resistance is out of range, replace the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Key on. Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code. Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no fault codes, test complete. If Fault Code 13 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 13 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 14 - Invalid Shift Lever Voltage (without Park Pawl)
dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates an electrical failure of the Eaton Cobra Lever or OEM Shift Lever. When troubleshooting an Inactive code See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
causes: Eaton Cobra Lever or OEM Shift Lever Vehicle Harness
steps: A. Visually identify the lever type: Eaton or OEM manufactured. Is vehicle equipped with an Eaton supplied Shift Lever or an OEM supplied Shift Lever? If Eaton Cobra Lever, Go to Step B If OEM Shift Lever, contact OEM for troubleshooting procedures.

B. Install the Shift Lever tester and monitor Transmission Range in ServiceRanger. Utilize the Shift Lever Tester to verify transmission-lever interface. Key off. Disconnect Shift Lever 8-way connector. Connect Shift Lever tester to the 8-way Shift Lever harness. Connect ServiceRanger, a PC-based Service Tool, to diagnostic port. Key on. Select Monitor Data. Observe transmission range selected. If transmission range selected equals neutral, replace Cobra Lever (only if fault code is Active). Go to Step V If transmission range selected does not equal neutral, Go to Step C

C. Verify continuity of auto mode input wire. Key off. Disconnect negative battery cable. Disconnect TECU 38-way connector. Remove tester from Shift Lever 8-way connector. Measure resistance between: ECU 38-way Pin 15 and Shift Lever 8-way connector Pin 1 ECU 38-way connector Pin 15 and ground If resistance between Pin 15 and Pin 1 is 0 to 0.3 ohms and resistance between Pin 15 and ground is 10K ohm or greater, Go to Step D If any of the above conditions are not met, repair the OEM Vehicle Harness between the TECU and the Eaton Cobra Lever. Go to Step V

D. Verify continuity of manual mode input wire. Key off. Measure resistance between: TECU 38-way Pin 16 and Shift Lever 8-way connector Pin 8 TECU 38-way connector Pin 16 and ground If resistance between Pin 16 and Pin 8 is 0 to 0.3 ohms and resistance between Pin 16 and ground is 10K ohm or greater, Go to Step E If any of the above conditions are not met, repair the Vehicle Harness between the Eaton Cobra Lever and TECU. Go to Step V

E. Verify continuity of common ground wire. Key off. Measure resistance between: TECU 38-way Pin 17 and Shift Lever 8-way connector Pin 2 TECU 38-way connector Pin 17 and ground If resistance between Pin 17 and Pin 2 is 0 to 0.3 ohms and resistance between Pin 17 and ground is 10K ohm or greater, Go to Step F If any of the above conditions are not met, repair the Vehicle Harness between the Eaton Cobra Lever and TECU. Go to Step V

F. Check for short circuits in the shift lever wiring. Key off. Measure resistance between: Pin 15 and Pin 16 on the TECU 38-way connector. Pin 15 and Pin 17 on the TECU 38-way connector. Pin 16 and Pin 17 on the TECU 38-way connector. If resistance on all three is 10K ohm or greater, replace Shift Lever and Go to Step V If any of the three readings is less than 10K ohm, repair the Vehicle Harness between the Eaton Cobra Lever and TECU. Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Key on. Clear codes, See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code. Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no codes, test complete. If code 14 appears, Go to Step A to find error in testing. If code other than 14 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 15 - HIL Shift Device Configuration
dd_procedures.overview: Controller Area Network (CAN) is a high-speed twisted pair 500K proprietary data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) is connected to the CAN data link at the 38-way connector. This link is used to transmit information to the TECU as well as communicate or receive data from the other modules on the network like the HIL Shift Device. See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
causes: CAN data link HIL Shift Device
steps: A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Perform electrical pretest. Key on. Retrieve active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-way diagnostic connector. Perform electrical pretest, see "Electrical Pretest" If no issues are found during the electrical pretest and the fault is still active, Go to Step B If issue was repaired during electrical pretest, Go to Step V

B. Confirm the presence of terminating resistors in the HIL. Key off. Locate and remove the terminating resistor that is wired into the ECA 8-way connector Pin C and Pin E. Measure resistance between the transmission harness connector Pin 1 and Pin 2. Note: Make sure the volt/ohm meter is on the proper scale (around 200 ohm scale). If resistance between Pin 1 and Pin 2 is between 50-70 ohms, replace Cobra Lever or Shift Control and Go to Step V If resistance is outside of range, replace the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Key on. Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Driving Vehicle and attempt to reset the code. Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no Fault Codes, test complete. If Fault Code 15 appears, Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 15 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 83 - Shift Lever Missing

steps: A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Key on. Retrieve codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 83 is Active, replace Eaton Cobra Lever or OEM Shift Lever. If Fault Code 83 is Inactive, test complete.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 84 - Shift Control Device Not Configured
dd_procedures.overview: This fault indicates a new Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) has not detected a Shift Control device.
causes: Damaged OEM Wiring Harness between
steps: A. Confirm Shift Control device is properly installed. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Verify Shift Control device is connected to the OEM wiring. Key on. Retrieve fault codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 84 is Active, repair OEM wiring between TECU and Shift Control device.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 85 - Shift Control Device Incompatible

The system includes redundant neutral request and neutral confirmation signals hard-wired between the Shift Control Device and TECU. These redundant signals allow the transmission to achieve neutral if the J1939 Data Link fails. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 14: Invalid Shift Lever Voltage
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be equipped with an analog Shift Control Device. The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) supplies the analog Shift Control Device with a 5-volt reference through OEM wiring. This voltage is reduced by resistive ladder circuitry in the shift device, based on the position the driver selects. The return voltage to the TECU indicates the position of the Shift Lever. Fault Code 14 indicates the TECU has detected an electrical fault in either the OEM-supplied wiring or Shift Control Device.
causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. Note: Vehicles can be equipped with either an Eaton-supplied analog Shift Lever or an OEM analog Shift Lever. This troubleshooting guide is intended for use only with Eaton-supplied analog Shift Levers. If your vehicle has Fault Code 14 and is equipped with an OEM analog Shift Lever, consult the OEM for proper troubleshooting procedures. If Fault Code 14 is Active, Go to Step D If Fault Code 14 is Inactive, Go to Step B

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 13: J1939 Shift Control Device
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be equipped with a J1939 Shift Control Device. This version of the Shift Control Device uses the J1939 Data Link to broadcast the driver’s shift request to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The system includes redundant neutral request and neutral confirmation signals hard-wired between the Shift Control Device and TECU. These redundant signals allow the transmission to achieve neutral if the J1939 Data Link fails. Fault Code 13 indicates that either the TECU lost J1939 Data Link communications with the Shift Control Device or that the neutral request status received over J1939 and the neutral request status received through the hard-wired signal do not match.
procedures_full.detection: The ignition key is on and the TECU has not detected any low battery system faults.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 8 – Abnormal Frequency: TECU compares the J1939 Data Link message from the Shift Control Device to the hard-wired neutral signal request. When 10 consecutive messages do not match, the fault code sets Active. FMI 11 – FMI Unknown: TECU has lost communication with the J1939 Shift Control Device but can communicate with other devices on the J1939 Data Link. When no J1939 messages have been received for 5 seconds, the fault code sets Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: TECU receives a valid message over the J1939 Data Link.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 8 “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Engine may not crank. Transmission may not engage a gear from neutral. FMI 11 “F” does not flash in gear display. Service light does not flash (if equipped). Transmission may not attempt to shift. Until the fault becomes Inactive, driver may have to shut off engine with transmission in gear. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: TECU receives a valid message over the J1939 Data Link.

Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. OEM J1939 Shift Control Connector (in cab) 1. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Vehicle Harness Connector 3. OEM J1939 Shift Control Connector

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 14: Invalid Shift Lever Voltage
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be equipped with an analog Shift Control Device. The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) supplies the analog Shift Control Device with a 5-volt reference through OEM wiring. This voltage is reduced by resistive ladder circuitry in the shift device, based on the position the driver selects. The return voltage to the TECU indicates the position of the Shift Lever. Fault Code 14 indicates the TECU has detected an electrical fault in either the OEM-supplied wiring or Shift Control Device.
procedures_full.detection: TECU monitors the voltage from the analog Shift Control Device. Fault Code 14 sets when the reported voltage for a selected mode does not match the actual value for that lever position.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: TECU receives erratic gear position information from the Shift Lever. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: Short to ground is detected, or the voltage value is not defined. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: An open circuit is present on the circuit, or the circuit is shorted high. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: The TECU has detected an abnormally long up or down button request.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: Signal voltage enters a valid range for 0.2 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Engine may not crank. Transmission is limited to down shifts only. Transmission may not engage a gear from neutral. If a fault occurs with the manual mode up or down buttons, manual mode can not be used. The transmission will shift as normal in auto mode. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: Signal voltage enters a valid range for 0.2 seconds.

Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. 8-Way Vehicle Harness Shift Lever Connector 4. 8-Way Cobra Shift Lever Connector 1. procedures_full.fallback: This fault may cause a downshift only fallback mode. The transmission will re-engage the start gear when returned to a stop, but will not upshift as long as the code is active.

steps.E:

steps.F:

 Key off.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 15 - HIL Shift Device Configuration
procedures_full.overview: Controller Area Network (CAN) is a high-speed twisted pair 500K proprietary data link with one 120 ohm resistor at each end of the link. The Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) is connected to the CAN data link at the 38-way connector. This link is used to transmit information to the TECU as well as communicate or receive data from the other modules on the network like the HIL Shift Device. See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
procedures_full.detection: Fault Code 15 is set when the TECU fails to receive Shift Device data for 5 continuous seconds, and it is still communicating with other modules on CAN.
procedures_full.fallback: This fault causes a downshift only fallback while moving. Once the transmission re-engages the start gear, there will be no upshifts as long as the code is active. If the code is active during power-up a flashing F will appear on the gear display and the TECU will not engage a gear. Note: If Fault Code 16 is active, follow the Fault Code 16 diagnostic procedure.

steps.A:
A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Perform electrical pretest. 
 Key on. 
 Retrieve active fault codes and FMIs with ServiceRanger using the 9-way diagnostic connector. 
 Perform electrical pretest, see "Electrical Pretest" 
 If no issues are found during the electrical pretest and the fault is still active, Go to Step B 
 If issue was repaired during electrical pretest, Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Confirm the presence of terminating resistors in the HIL. 
 Key off. 
 Locate and remove the terminating resistor that is wired into the ECA 8-way connector Pin C and Pin E. 
 Measure resistance between the transmission harness connector Pin 1 and Pin 2. 
 Note: Make sure the volt/ohm meter is on the proper scale (around 200 ohm scale). 
 If resistance between Pin 1 and Pin 2 is between 50-70 ohms, replace Cobra Lever or Shift Control and Go to Step V 
 If resistance is outside of range, replace the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Key on. 
 Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. 
 Driving Vehicle and attempt to reset the code. 
 Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no Fault Codes, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 15 appears, Go to Step A to find error in testing. 
 If fault code other than 15 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 13 - J1939 Shift Control Device
procedures_full.overview: This fault indicates communication has been lost, or does not correspond with the neutral request input from the J1939 Shift Device. When troubleshooting an Inactive code, See "Product Diagnostic (PD) Mode"
procedures_full.detection: Starting at key on and throughout operation, the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) constantly monitors communication with the J1939 Shift Device. If a neutral request from the J1939 Shift Device does not match the neutral signal or is not received from the J1939 Shift Device, Fault Code 13 is set.
procedures_full.fallback: This fault causes a downshift-only fallback. Once the transmission re-engages the start gear, there will be no upshifts as long as the code is active.

steps.A:
A. Verify continuity of Neutral Request Signal wire 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect negative battery cable. 
 Disconnect Vehicle Harness 38-way connector. 
 Measure resistance between 38-way connector Pin 16 and corresponding OEM pin at J1939 Shift Device and Pin 16 and ground (see OEM wiring for correct pin location) 
 If resistance is 0 to 0.3 ohms between Pin 16 and the corresponding OEM pin and resistance to ground is 10K ohms or greater , Go to Step B 
 If resistance is out of range , replace the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Verify continuity of Neutral Request Return wire 
 Measure resistance between 38-way connector Pin 17 and corresponding OEM pin at J1939 Shift Device and Pin 17 and ground (see OEM wiring for correct pin location). 
 If resistance is 0 to 0.3 ohms between Pin 17 and the corresponding OEM pin and resistance to ground is 10K ohms or greater, problem exists with the J1939 Shift Device, or J1939 Shift Device power, ground or data link wiring. Contact your OEM for repair strategy. Go to Step V 
 If resistance is out of range, replace the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. 
 Key on. 
 Clear codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Drive vehicle and attempt to reset the code. 
 Check for codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no fault codes, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 13 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. 
 If fault code other than 13 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 84 - Shift Control Device Not Configured
procedures_full.overview: This fault indicates a new Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) has not detected a Shift Control device.
procedures_full.detection: The fault is detected the first time the system is powered up. The TECU looks for a shift control device if none are detected the system will set this code. Note: The fault will only be set active.
procedures_full.fallback: No crank at power-up.

steps.A:
A. Confirm Shift Control device is properly installed. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. 
 Verify Shift Control device is connected to the OEM wiring. 
 Key on. 
 Retrieve fault codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If Fault Code 84 is Active, repair OEM wiring between TECU and Shift Control device.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 73 - Failed to Engage Gear
dd_procedures.overview: This fault indicates the system cannot engage the desired gear. The system will continue attempting to engaged the desired gear after the fault is set. Vehicle must be moving and attempting to engage a gear and no electrical faults can be active.
causes: FMI 7: Mechanical issue with the shift bar housing Damaged shift bar housing interlock parts Electric Shifter New Electric Shifter installed and not recalibrated per the L-Letter (L-2003-30) Mechanical issue with the Electric Shifter Badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leak Worn center shaft bushing (TAIB-0814) Base Transmission Main box mechanical failure Sliding clutch / shift yoke wear Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) New
steps: A. Determine if an Electric Shifter was installed without recalibrating the transmission. Key off. Was a new Electric Shifter or TECU just installed without recalibrating the transmission? Yes , Perform transmission calibration. Turn key on and allow the transmission to power up. Turn key off and wait 2 minutes. Go to Step V . No , Go to Step B

B. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect the batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. Key off. Inspect starter / battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. Measure voltage across batteries. If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required. Go to Step C If voltage is outside of range , repair or replace batteries and charge system as required. Repeat test.

C. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port Locate the diagnostic port on the Transmission Harness - located at the left rear corner of the transmission. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. If voltage is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step D If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.

D. Measure battery voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. Key on. Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E If voltage is outside of range, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.

E. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port Key on. Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step F If voltage is outside of range, repair ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown Repeat test.

F. Visually inspect the Shift Bar housing, Electric Shifter and base transmission for signs of mechanical damage. Key off. Remove electric shifter from Shift Bar housing. Inspect the Shift Bar housing Visually inspect shift rails and blocks. Verify Shift Bar housing operation by confirming shift rails can physically engage each gear individually. Confirm the Shift Bar housing can not engage 2 gears at the same time. Inspect Electric Shifter Check for mechanical issues with the Electric Shifter. Visually inspect for badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leaks. Check for a worn center shaft bushing (see TAIB-0814). Inspect base transmission Drain and inspect oil for debris. Remove I-brake or PTO cover and inspect for main box mechanical failure. Inspect sliding clutches and shift yokes for wear. If no problem found, replace Electric Shifter and the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V If problem found, repair as required. Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Key on. Clear fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code. Check for fault codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no fault codes, test complete. If Fault Code 73 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If fault code other than 73 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

steps: A. Check for active or Inactive fault codes. Contact Eaton technical support for further direction. Key on. Retrieve fault codes. See "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If Fault Code 99 is Active or Inactive, Customer - Call Eaton at 1-800-826-HELP (4357). CSC - Call Technician Service.

causes: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Set parking brake and chock wheels. procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 73: Failed to Engage Gear
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the X-Y Shifter to engage and disengage a gear based on the driver’s selected mode of operation. Gear engagement is achieved by activating the X-Y Shifter Gear Motor, which controls the fore-and-aft movement of the Shift Finger. Pushing the Shift Finger against one of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks guides the Shift Yoke to engage the Sliding Clutch into a gear. The position of the X-Y Shift Finger is monitored by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) by way of the X-Y Gear Position and Rail Position Sensors. Fault Code 73 is set when the X-Y Shift Finger attempts to engage a gear, but the X-Y Gear Position Sensor indicates that the transmission was unable to engage that gear. The TECU detected a system failure, but was unable to detect the specific root cause.
procedures_full.detection: This fault can only be detected when there are no failures of the TECU, X-Y Gear or Rail Motors, X-Y Position Sensors or Battery Supply voltage. This fault code is set when the system is unable to engage a gear.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: If the X-Y Gear Position Sensor does not meet the minimum gear engagement value after five consecutive attempts to engage the desired gear, this fault code sets Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 7: The system successfully engages the desired gear.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 7 Transmission may not be able to complete a shift into gear. Transmission will attempt to move the Shift Finger to the destination gear. Engine may not crank. Gear display may flash current or destination gear. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 7: The system successfully engages the desired gear.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 73: Failed to Engage Gear
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission uses the X-Y Shifter to engage and disengage a gear based on the driver’s selected mode of operation. Gear engagement is achieved by activating the X-Y Shifter Gear Motor, which controls the fore-and-aft movement of the Shift Finger. Pushing the Shift Finger against one of the Shift Bar Housing Shift Blocks guides the Shift Yoke to engage the Sliding Clutch into a gear. The position of the X-Y Shift Finger is monitored by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) by way of the X-Y Gear Position and Rail Position Sensors. Fault Code 73 is set when the X-Y Shift Finger attempts to engage a gear, but the X-Y Gear Position Sensor indicates that the transmission was unable to engage that gear. The TECU detected a system failure, but was unable to detect the specific root cause.
procedures_full.detection: This fault can only be detected when there are no failures of the TECU, X-Y Gear or Rail Motors, X-Y Position Sensors or Battery Supply voltage. This fault code is set when the system is unable to engage a gear.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: If the X-Y Gear Position Sensor does not meet the minimum gear engagement value after five consecutive attempts to engage the desired gear, this fault code sets Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 7: The system successfully engages the desired gear.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 7 Transmission may not be able to complete a shift into gear. Transmission will attempt to move the Shift Finger to the destination gear. Engine may not crank. Gear display may flash current or destination gear. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 7: The system successfully engages the desired gear.

Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 2. 38-Way Transmission Harness Connector 3. Gear Position Sensor 4. 3-Way Gear Position Sensor Connector 5. 2-Way Gear Motor Connector (blue) 6. 2-Way Gear Motor Connector Body (blue) 1. procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 73 - Failed to Engage Gear
procedures_full.overview: This fault indicates the system cannot engage the desired gear. The system will continue attempting to engaged the desired gear after the fault is set. Vehicle must be moving and attempting to engage a gear and no electrical faults can be active.
procedures_full.detection: The system unsuccessfully attempts to engage a gear 5 times with no battery voltage faults.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: Conditions to Set Fault Code Active FMI 7 - The system is unable to engage a gear 5 times with no battery voltage faults.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Conditions to Set Fault Code Active FMI 7 - The fault becomes Inactive when neutral is achieved.
procedures_full.fallback: Fallback mode During Power-Up None. This fault can not be set at power-up. Fallback Mode During Operation When this fault is active, the transmission will continue to attempt to engage the gear. The system will alternate the engine speed up and down in an attempt to achieve engagement. The gear display may blink the destination gear. The service light will not flash, nor will an F be displayed on the dash. The diagnostic code will not be transmitted on the J1587 bus until fault codes have been requested by a service tool. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive Conditions to Set Fault Code Active FMI 7 - The fault becomes Inactive when neutral is achieved.

steps.A:
A. Determine if an Electric Shifter was installed without recalibrating the transmission. 
 Key off. 
 Was a new Electric Shifter or TECU just installed without recalibrating the transmission? 
 Yes , Perform transmission calibration. Turn key on and allow the transmission to power up. Turn key off and wait 2 minutes. Go to Step V . 
 No , Go to Step B
steps.B:
B. Measure battery voltage. Visually inspect the batteries, inline fuse, power and ground supplies to the TECU. 
 Key off. 
 Inspect starter / battery and in-line fuse holder connections for integrity. 
 Measure voltage across batteries. 
 If voltage is 11 to 13 volts on a 12-volt system or 22 to 26 on a 24-volt system, proceed with battery load test. Repair or replace batteries as required. Go to Step C 
 If voltage is outside of range , repair or replace batteries and charge system as required. Repeat test.
steps.C:
C. Verify proper ground path at 4-way diagnostic port 
 Locate the diagnostic port on the Transmission Harness - located at the left rear corner of the transmission. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin C and the battery negative post. 
 If voltage is 0.70 volts or less, Go to Step D 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair battery ground supply to TECU. Repeat test.
steps.D:
D. Measure battery voltage at 4-way diagnostic port. 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin B and Pin C. 
 If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step E 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair battery power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown. Repeat test.
steps.E:
E. Measure ignition voltage at 4-way diagnostic port 
 Key on. 
 Measure voltage between Pin A and Pin C. 
 If voltage is within 0.6 volts of battery voltage, Go to Step F 
 If voltage is outside of range, repair ignition power supply to TECU. Fuse may be blown Repeat test.

 Key off. 
 Remove electric shifter from Shift Bar housing. 
 Inspect the Shift Bar housing 
 Visually inspect shift rails and blocks.

 Confirm the Shift Bar housing can not engage 2 gears at the same time.

 Visually inspect for badly contaminated / gummed up / soiled Electric Shifter ball screw due to oil cooler leaks.

 Inspect base transmission 
 Drain and inspect oil for debris. 
 Remove I-brake or PTO cover and inspect for main box mechanical failure. 
 Inspect sliding clutches and shift yokes for wear. 
 If no problem found, replace Electric Shifter and the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V 
 If problem found, repair as required. Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. 
 Key on.

procedures_full.overview: The Medium Duty 4-Speed EV Transmission uses the X-Y Shifter to select the proper rail and engage or disengage a gear based on the driver’s selected mode of operation. The position of the X-Y Shift Finger is controlled and monitored by the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) by way of the X-Y Gear Position and Rail Position Sensors. Fault Code 99 is set when the TECU commands the X-Y Shifter to move to a specific position and the reported Shift Finger position achieved does not match the desired position.
procedures_full.detection: This fault can only be detected when there are no failures of the TECU or X-Y Position Sensors. This fault code is set when the X-Y Gear Position and Rail Position values are valid, but do not match the requested positions requested by the TECU.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: The XY Shift Actuator Gear Position reports the Gear Motor is moving in the opposite direction of the selected mode. FMI 13 – Out of Calibration: The XY Shift Actuator Gear Position reports Reverse Gear is engaged when not selected.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: Neutral mode is selected and the system confirms Neutral.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 14: “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). Transmission remains in current gear. May not engage a start gear from neutral. Motor may have to be shut down with the transmission still in gear. Audible warning tone sounds. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: Neutral mode is selected and the system confirms Neutral.

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 27 - Clutch Disengagement
dd_procedures.overview: The fault code indicates that the clutch has not disengaged as expected.
causes: Failed clutch Clutch thermal abuse Drive Disc Assembly over-speed Pilot Bearing failure Input shaft wear Additional Tools Clutch jack
steps: A. Monitor and compare engine speed to transmission input shaft speed in ServiceRanger. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To “Data Monitor”. From the “Default Parameter Files” tab, select “J1939 Transmission Speeds”. Key on with engine running. Raise engine RPM above 1500 RPM and allow engine to return to idle. Note: Engine idle must be 700 RPM or less. After engine RPM returns to idle, monitor and record engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. Key on with engine off. Compare engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. If engine RPM and transmission input shaft RPM match at idle and Fault Code 27 is Active, clutch is not releasing, replace clutch. Go to Step V If they do not match, clutch is releasing, test complete. Go to Step V

V. Verify Repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 27 sets Active during test drive, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 27 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 28 - Clutch System
dd_procedures.overview: This fault code indicates either an electrical or mechanical failure in the WetClutch system.
steps: A. Check WetClutch fluid level. Key on. Place the transmission in neutral. Allow engine to idle at 700-800 RPM for a minimum of 2 minutes. Note: Ensure transmission fluid temperature is 60 to 120 degrees F (16 to 49 degrees C). Check WetClutch fluid level. If fluid level is at or above the COLD-FULL mark, Go to Step B If fluid level is below the COLD-ADD mark, Correct fluid level, Go to Step V .

B. Verify continuity of the Clutch Lube Solenoid circuit. Key off. Disconnect the negative battery cable. Disconnect the TECU 30-way connector. Measure resistance between the Transmission Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and Pin 3 and between Pin 2 and ground. If the resistance between 2 and 3 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms and is resistance from Pin 2 to ground is OL, Go to Step C If resistance is outside of range, Go to Step D

C. Verify continuity of Clutch Solenoid circuit. Measure resistance between the Transmission Harness 38-way connector Pin 13 and Pin 14 and between Pin 13 and ground. If resistance between Pin 13 and Pin 14 is 8.5 to 12 ohms and resistance from Pin 13 to ground is [OL], Replace Transmission (Only if fault code is Active). Go to Step V If resistance is less than 10K ohm, Go to Step D

D. Verify continuity of hydraulic manifold circuits. Disconnect Transmission Harness located on left side of WetClutch housing. Measure resistance between WetClutch housing connector pins: 3 and 4 1 and 2 If the resistance between Pin 1 and Pin 2 is 8.5 to 12 ohms and the resistance between Pin 3 and Pin 4 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms, Go to Step E If resistance is outside of range, replace transmission, Go to Step V

E. Test the hydraulic manifold wiring for short circuits. Measure resistance between WetClutch housing connector pins: 3 and ground 1 and ground If resistance from Pin 3 to ground and Pin 1 to ground is 10K ohm or greater, replace the: Medium-Duty Transmission Harness Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness Go to Step V If resistance is less than 10K ohm, Replace Transmission. Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors. Key on. Clear codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the code. Check for codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" If no codes, test complete. If code 28 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. If code other than 28 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

steps: C. Perform a Load Test on each vehicle battery. Key off. Set parking brake and chock wheels. Load test each vehicle battery per OEM specifications. Record reading(s). E. Verify condition of 3-Way Gen1 ECA Connector. Key off. Disconnect 3-Way Gen1 ECA Connector. F. Verify battery voltage at ECA. Key off. Measure voltage between 3-Way Gen1 ECA Connector Pin C (Battery positive) and Pin B (Battery negative). Record reading(s) in table. Go to Step V If readings are in range, Go to Step G Pins Range Reading(s) C to B Within 1.2 V of Battery Positive (+)

Go to Step V If

I. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Determine which FMI set for Fault Code 64, as noted in Step B. If FMI 2 or 12 set and no fault was found with the ECA Power Supply Harness or battery/charging system, replace the Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) . Go to Step V If FMI 7 set, Go to Step J

Ensure Release Bearing and Cross Shaft are adequately greased per the Heavy-Duty Clutch Service Manual (CLSM0200). Go to Step V If no issues are found with the Clutch Release Yoke and Cross Shaft rotates freely without binding, and no fault was found with the ECA Power Supply Harness or battery/charging system, replace the El
L. Determine Vehicle Manufacturer. Determine if vehicle manufacturer is PACCAR. If vehicle is not manufactured by PACCAR, Go to Step M If vehicle is manufactured by PACCAR, Go to Step N

M. Verify TECU Software Version - All other OEMs. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To Programming. Under "Software Information", record TECU software version. If TECU software is less than 5570065, update TECU software to 5570065 or greater. Go to Step V If TECU software is 5570065 or greater, Go to Step C

steps: A. Monitor and compare engine speed to transmission input shaft speed in ServiceRanger. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To "Data Monitor". From the "Default Parameter Files" tab, select "J1939 Transmission Speeds". Key on with engine running. Raise engine RPM above 1500 RPM and allow engine to return to idle. Note: Engine idle must be 700 RPM or less. After engine RPM returns to idle, monitor and record engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. Key on with engine off. Compare engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. If engine RPM and transmission input shaft RPM match at idle and Fault Code 27 is Active, clutch is not releasing, replace clutch. Go to Step V If they do not match, clutch is releasing, test complete. Go to Step V

V. Verify Repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to "Fault Codes". Select "Clear All Faults". Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 27 sets Active during test drive, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 27 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

A. Check WetClutch fluid level. Key on. Place the transmission in neutral. Allow engine to idle at 700-800 RPM for a minimum of 2 minutes. Note: Ensure transmission fluid temperature is 60 to 120 degrees F (16 to 49 degrees C). Check WetClutch fluid level. If fluid level is at or above the COLD-FULL mark, Go to Step B If fluid level is below the COLD-ADD mark, Correct fluid level, Go to Step V .

B. Verify continuity of the Clutch Lube Solenoid circuit. Key off. Disconnect the negative battery cable. Disconnect the TECU 30-way connector. Measure resistance between the Transmission Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and Pin 3 and between Pin 2 and ground. If the resistance between 2 and 3 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms and is resistance from Pin 2 to ground is OL, Go to Step C If resistance is outside of range, Go to Step D

Pin 13 ile Pin 14 arasındaki direnç 8,5 ila 12 Ω ve Pin 13'ten şasiye direnç sonsuz (OL) ise, Şanzımanı Değiştirin (Yalnızca arıza kodu aktifse). Adım V'ye gidin. Direnç 10 kΩ'dan düşükse Adım D'ye gidin.

D. Verify continuity of hydraulic manifold circuits. Disconnect Transmission Harness located on left side of WetClutch housing. Measure resistance between WetClutch housing connector pins: 3 and 4 1 and 2 If the resistance between Pin 1 and Pin 2 is 8.5 to 12 ohms and the resistance between Pin 3 and Pin 4 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms, Go to Step E If resistance is outside of range, replace transmission, Go to Step V

Pin 3'ten şasiye ve Pin 1'den şasiye direnç 10 kΩ veya daha yüksekse Şanzıman Kablo Demetini (Orta veya Ağır Hizmet) değiştirin. Adım V'ye gidin. Direnç 10 kΩ'dan düşükse Şanzımanı Değiştirin. Adım V'ye gidin.

V. Onarımı doğrulayın. Kontağı kapatın. Tüm konnektörleri yeniden bağlayın. Kontağı açın. Kodları silin ("Arıza Kodu Okuma/Silme" bölümüne bakın). Aracı sürün ve arıza kodunu oluşturmayı deneyin. Kodları kontrol edin. Kod yoksa test tamamlanmıştır. Kod 28 görünürse testteki hatayı bulmak için Adım A'ya gidin. 28 dışında bir kod görünürse "Arıza Kodu Ayırma Prosedürü İndeksi"ne bakın.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 64: Gen2 Electronic Clutch Actuator
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission equipped with an Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) that controls the position of the clutch assembly. Power and ground to the ECA are OEM-supplied through a 2-Way Gen2 ECA Connector directly connected to the vehicle batteries. The ECA is connected to the TECU by an 8-Way Gen2 ECA Connector that is part of the transmission harness. The ECA communicates with the TECU over the High Integrity Link (HIL) to change position, show faults or include other operation information. Fault Code 94 indicates that a failure has been detected by the ECA, but is specific to systems that use a Gen2 ECA. Troubleshooting for this procedure is specific to the Gen2 ECA and associated harnesses. Note: The troubleshooting procedure for Fault Code 64 may direct users to use this troubleshooting procedure if the vehicle is equipped with a Gen2 ECA, even if Fault Code 94 was not set by the transmission. This is because some transmission software versions do not set Fault Code 94.
procedures_full.detection: The TECU monitors the ECA for excessive motor current, excessive motor temperature, incorrect motor position, improper battery or ignition voltage to the ECA, or various internal ECA malfunctions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: ECA detects a loss of battery and/or ground for 1 second or longer. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: ECA detects excessive motor current or ECA detects incorrect clutch position during a clutch position change for 1 second or longer. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: ECA detects an internal failure for 1 second or longer.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: No loss of battery and ground is detected for 2 seconds. FMI 7: Normal motor current is detected and ECA position is correct for 2 seconds. FMI 12: No internal ECA failures are detected for 2 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). If the fault occurs at power up, engine cranks and starts, but TECU will not engage a gear. If the fault occurs while driving, ECA maintains current clutch position or moves to the last position commanded by the TECU. Transmission may continue to shift until vehicle is stopped. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 2: No loss of battery and ground is detected for 2 seconds. FMI 7: Normal motor current is detected and ECA position is correct for 2 seconds. FMI 12: No internal ECA failures are detected for 2 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 2, 12 ECA Power Harness Bent, spread, corroded or loose terminals Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open ECA Internal failure FMI 7 ECA Power Harness Bent, spread corroded or loose terminals Wiring shorted to ground, shorted to power or open Mechanical Clutch System Lack of lubrication of clutch release shaft/bushings Lack of lubrication of clutch Damage to clutch release yoke or cross shaft Internal failure ECA Internal failure TECU Software issue Vehicle Harness Wiring shorted to ground or shorted to power Component Identification 1. 38-Way Transmission Harness Connector 2. Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) 3. Gen2 ECA Shield 4. Gen2 Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) 5. 8-Way Gen2 ECA Connector 6. 2-Way Gen2 ECA Connector Eaton ECA Clutch 1. Clutch Wear Tab 2. procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 64: Gen1 Electronic Clutch Actuator
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with an Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) that controls the position of the clutch assembly. Power and ground to the ECA are OEM-supplied through a 3-Way Gen1 ECA Connector directly connected to the vehicle batteries. The ECA is connected to the TECU by an 8-Way Gen1 ECA Connector that is part of the transmission harness. The ECA communicates with the TECU over the High Integrity Link (HIL) to change position, show faults or include other operation information.
procedures_full.detection: The TECU monitors the ECA for excessive motor current, excessive motor temperature, incorrect motor position, improper battery or ignition voltage to the ECA, or various internal ECA malfunctions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: ECA detects a loss of battery and/or ground for 1 second or longer. FMI 7 – Mechanical System Not Responding: ECA detects excessive motor current or ECA detects incorrect clutch position during a clutch position change for 1 second or longer. FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: ECA detects an internal failure for 1 second or longer.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: No loss of battery and ground is detected for 2 seconds. FMI 7: Normal motor current is detected and ECA position is correct for 2 seconds. FMI 12: No internal ECA failures are detected for 2 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). If the fault occurs at power up, engine cranks and starts, but TECU will not engage a gear. If the fault occurs while driving, ECA maintains current clutch position or moves to the last position commanded by the TECU. Transmission may continue to shift until vehicle is stopped. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 2: No loss of battery and ground is detected for 2 seconds. FMI 7: Normal motor current is detected and ECA position is correct for 2 seconds. FMI 12: No internal ECA failures are detected for 2 seconds.

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant HD transmission is equipped with solenoids to direct pneumatic flow to actuate the clutch and a sensor to monitor clutch position. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) compares vehicle inputs, clutch command, clutch position and input shaft speed to ensure proper clutch operation. The Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) is mounted to the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM). The solenoids and sensors are located in the MTM and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Transmission Clutch Actuator. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: TCM did not prohibit Creep Mode when expected based on the operating conditions. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: TCM did not release/open the clutch when expected based on the operating conditions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 12, 14: Key cycle
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 12, 14: Amber warning lamp on Non neutral modes prohibited Clutch engagement prohibited PTO Mode prohibited Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited If vehicle is moving Red stop lamp on Transmission shifts to neutral, vehicle may coast to a stop Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 12, 14: Key cycle
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 12, 14: TCM Software issue Internal failure

steps.A:
A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. 
 Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. 
 Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. 
 If Fault Code 705 FMI 14 is Active or Inactive, and the vehicle is equipped with a International Motors A26 engine, Go to Step B 
 If Fault Code 705 FMI 12 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step C 
 If Fault Code 705 FMI 14 is Active or Inactive and the vehicle is not equipped with a International Motors A26 engine, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Contact Information . Go to Step V
steps.B:
B. Verify TCM software. 
 Key off. 
 Allow TCM to perform a complete power down. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Programming”. 
 Under "Software Information", record TCM software in table. 
 If the TCM software is less than 5516014, update the TCM software to latest available version. Go to Step V 
 If the TCM software is equal to or greater than 5516014, Contact Eaton Cummins Automated Transmission Technologies for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Contact Information . Go to Step V

steps.C:

 If the TCM software is less than 5516018, update the TCM software to latest available version. Go to Step V

steps.V:

 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Fault Codes”.

 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger.

 If Fault Code 705 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A

procedures_full.overview: This fault code indicates either an electrical or mechanical failure in the WetClutch system.
procedures_full.detection: Starting at key-on and throughout operation, the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) constantly monitors this circuit. A failure mode of short to battery, short to ground or open circuit is detected. When the WetClutch is locked after urge to move, engine speed and input shaft speeds are compared. If the engine speed is significantly higher than the input shaft speed for a period of five seconds, the WetClutch is slipping.
procedures_full.fallback: There is no fallback mode; however, if the failure mode is open circuit, the engine will be disengaged from the input shaft.

steps.A:
A. Check WetClutch fluid level. 
 Key on. 
 Place the transmission in neutral. 
 Allow engine to idle at 700-800 RPM for a minimum of 2 minutes. 
 Note: Ensure transmission fluid temperature is 60 to 120 degrees F (16 to 49 degrees C). 
 Check WetClutch fluid level. 
 If fluid level is at or above the COLD-FULL mark, Go to Step B 
 If fluid level is below the COLD-ADD mark, Correct fluid level, Go to Step V .
steps.B:
B. Verify continuity of the Clutch Lube Solenoid circuit. 
 Key off. 
 Disconnect the negative battery cable. 
 Disconnect the TECU 30-way connector. 
 Measure resistance between the Transmission Harness 38-way connector Pin 2 and Pin 3 and between Pin 2 and ground. 
 If the resistance between 2 and 3 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms and is resistance from Pin 2 to ground is OL, Go to Step C 
 If resistance is outside of range, Go to Step D
steps.C:
C. Verify continuity of Clutch Solenoid circuit. 
 Measure resistance between the Transmission Harness 38-way connector Pin 13 and Pin 14 and between Pin 13 and ground. 
 If resistance between Pin 13 and Pin 14 is 8.5 to 12 ohms and resistance from Pin 13 to ground is [OL], Replace Transmission (Only if fault code is Active). Go to Step V 
 If resistance is less than 10K ohm, Go to Step D
steps.D:
D. Verify continuity of hydraulic manifold circuits. 
 Disconnect Transmission Harness located on left side of WetClutch housing. 
 Measure resistance between WetClutch housing connector pins: 
 3 and 4 
 1 and 2 
 If the resistance between Pin 1 and Pin 2 is 8.5 to 12 ohms and the resistance between Pin 3 and Pin 4 is 6.5 to 9.5 ohms, Go to Step E 
 If resistance is outside of range, replace transmission, Go to Step V
steps.E:
E. Test the hydraulic manifold wiring for short circuits. 
 Measure resistance between WetClutch housing connector pins: 
 3 and ground 
 1 and ground 
 If resistance from Pin 3 to ground and Pin 1 to ground is 10K ohm or greater, replace the: 
 Medium-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Heavy-Duty Transmission Harness 
 Go to Step V 
 If resistance is less than 10K ohm, Replace Transmission. Go to Step V
steps.V:
V. Verify repair. 
 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors. 
 Key on. 
 Clear codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the code. 
 Check for codes, see "Fault Code Retrieval/Clearing" 
 If no codes, test complete. 
 If code 28 appears Go to Step A to find error in testing. 
 If code other than 28 appears, See "Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index"

procedures_full.overview: The fault code indicates that the clutch has not disengaged as expected.
procedures_full.detection: DM Clutch Fault Detection Starting at key on and throughout operation, the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) constantly measures engine RPM and idle torque from the engine. If the engine speed falls significantly below idle or engine torque rises significantly above idle torque upon engaging a start gear, the fault is set. If the vehicle is brought to a stop when in gear and engine speed falls significantly below idle, the fault is set. Clutch Disengagement Test Note: It is recommended that the pilot bearing and LCIB be replaced whenever the clutch is replaced. Note: Refer to Installation Guide TRIG1110 for a list of recommended pilot bearings. Note: Secondary clutch failures resulting from conditions such as pilot bearing failures, excessive torsional vibration or clutch abuse are not covered under warranty. Note: Record Vehicle Performance Analysis every time a clutch is replaced
procedures_full.fallback: No gear engagement from neutral if the truck is stationary; however, if the TECU determines the vehicle is moving, it will allow a gear engagement from neutral.
procedures_full.possible_causes: This fault code can be caused by any of the following: Failed clutch Clutch thermal abuse Drive Disc Assembly over-speed Pilot Bearing failure Input shaft wear

steps.A:
A. Monitor and compare engine speed to transmission input shaft speed in ServiceRanger. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go To “Data Monitor”. 
 From the “Default Parameter Files” tab, select “J1939 Transmission Speeds”. 
 Key on with engine running. 
 Raise engine RPM above 1500 RPM and allow engine to return to idle. 
 Note: Engine idle must be 700 RPM or less. 
 After engine RPM returns to idle, monitor and record engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Compare engine RPM and transmission input shaft speed RPM. 
 If engine RPM and transmission input shaft RPM match at idle and Fault Code 27 is Active, clutch is not releasing, replace clutch. Go to Step V 
 If they do not match, clutch is releasing, test complete. Go to Step V
steps.V:

 Key off. 
 Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. 
 Key on with engine off. 
 Connect ServiceRanger. 
 Go to “Fault Codes”. 
 Select “Clear All Faults”. 
 Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. 
 Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. 
 If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. 
 If Fault Code 27 sets Active during test drive, Go to Step A 
 If a fault code other than 27 sets Active, troubleshoot per the Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

procedures_full.overview: The Endurant XD Series transmissions are equipped with solenoid valves that direct vehicle Supply Air to and from the Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) to control clutch position. A position sensor monitors clutch position and provides the information to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of making clutch engagement or disengagement decisions. The TCM compares the clutch command, clutch position and input shaft speed to ensure the transmission is operating properly. The LCA is mounted to the Mechatronic Transmission Module (MTM). The solenoids and position sensor are located in the MTM and connected to the TCM at the 74-Way Transmission Harness Connector.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors clutch operation. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 12 – Bad Intelligent Device: TCM did not prohibit Creep Mode as expected based on operating conditions. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: TCM did not disengage clutch as expected based on operating conditions.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 12, 14: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.
procedures_full.fallback: FMI 12, 14: Amber warning lamp on Urge to Move and Creep Mode prohibited Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO Mode prohibited If vehicle is moving: Red stop lamp on Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 12, 14: Key cycle and fault condition no longer exist.
procedures_full.possible_causes: FMI 12, 14: TCM Software issue Internal failure Note: If FMI 14 and vehicle is equipped with a SSPTO, ensure the SSPTO was properly shut down prior to selecting Neutral. Refer to Endurant XD Driver Instructions TRDR0960 - Split Shaft PTO Operation.

causes: Common problems include failures of the rear axle ABS sensors and challenges in ensuring the correct sensor placement.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_789.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_789.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).
