SPN_791.description_en: ABS wheel speed sensor axle 2 left - fault mode not identifiable / cause unknown. If the fault is not sporadic and occurs several times, then the following workshop activity is appropriate:
causes: Always inspect the tone ring for magnetic debris buildup before replacing components
Long-term prevention requires verifying the tone ring runout with a dial indicator (max 0.2 mm per Deutz spec) and using only OEM-specified sensor shims

In one workshop case, a technician found that after replacing a wheel hub, the tone ring had been pressed on backwards, causing a 0.5 mm air gap variation that triggered SPN 791 FMI 10 every left turn
Commonly, this fault appears after replacing wheel speed sensors or following aggressive driving conditions leading to sensor misalignment
Technicians often face this issue when wheel hubs are replaced without aligning the sensors correctly
This code may trigger the ABS warning light, prompting further
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_791.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_791.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

It uses logic algorithms to differentiate between genuine faults and transient noise
The indeterminate nature requires systematic

causes: Sensor Wire Short: Signal wire chafed against a 12V or 24V power source in the trailer harness
ECU Internal Fault: ABS ECU input stage failed short to VCC due to moisture ingress or overvoltage
Connector Corrosion: Pin-to-pin leakage in the sensor connector bridging signal to supply voltage
Aftermarket Harness: Non-OEM trailer wiring with incorrect gauge or missing shielding causing voltage pickup

Advanced Technical Analysis The ABS ECU continuously monitors the sensor signal line voltage through a comparator circuit with a threshold typically set at 4.75V for a 5V supply or 23V for a 24V system
When the raw voltage exceeds this threshold for more than 50 ms, the
Once the fault is active, the ABS ECU disables traction control and retarder intervention for axle 3 left
The system enters a safe mode where brake pressure modulation is inhibited on that channel

Installation Error: Incorrect wiring during service connects relay coil circuit directly to unswitched battery voltage

Technicians should implement preventive measures including sealed relay enclosures, vibration dampening, and regular contact cleaning protocols
Fleet maintenance data shows 40% reduction in relay failures when implementing proactive replacement intervals combined with electrical load analysis

causes: Vehicle ECU Front Axle Right Wheel Speed Message Not available Not valid
steps: A. Check for active or inactive fault codes. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 191 is Inactive and there are other Active vehicle or transmission fault codes, troubleshoot all Active fault codes. Go to Step V If Fault Code 191 FMI 13 is Active, refer to OEM and enable vehicle Front Axle Right Wheel Speed SPN 906. Go to Step V If Fault Code 191 FMI 13 is Inactive, Go to Step V If Fault Code 191 FMI 19 is Active or Inactive, there is a fault with the Front Axle Right Wheel Speed message sent from a vehicle module. Contact OEM for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V

V. Verify repair. Key off. Reconnect all connectors and verify that all components are properly installed. Key on with engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go to “Fault Codes”. Select “Clear All Faults”. Operate vehicle and attempt to reset the fault code or duplicate the previous complaint. Check for fault codes using ServiceRanger. If no fault codes set and the vehicle operates properly, test complete. If Fault Code 191 sets Active during operation, Go to Step A If a fault code other than 191 sets Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index .

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 0 means the fuel filter's pressure drop has reached a severely high level on your Scania engine. This is a high-severity code with real stalling risk - replace the filter and check fuel quality immediately. By the time this most-severe FMI level sets, the filter is genuinely choking the engine's fuel supply. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as a same-day repair, not something to schedule for later, since continued operation risks stalling under load.
causes: Severely plugged fuel filter element
Extended service intervals or heavily contaminated fuel restrict flow enough to cause a severe pressure drop across the filter.
Contaminated fuel supply
Water, algae, or sediment in the fuel can plug a filter far ahead of its normal service interval, especially after refueling from an unreliable source.
Blocked sensor port
One of the differential pressure sensor's ports can become individually blocked, though this is uncommon compared to genuine filter plugging at this severity.
steps: Pull the fault and freeze-frame differential pressure on Scania SDP3 and compare against the specification.
Replace the primary fuel filter and water separator immediately given the severity of this reading.
Pull a fuel sample from the water separator bowl to check for algae, water, or sediment contamination that caused rapid plugging.
Check the fuel tank vent and pickup screen for a severe blockage compounding the filter restriction.
Prime and bleed the fuel system fully after the filter change, since a severely restricted system often draws air during the plugging process.
Retest differential pressure under load after repairs to confirm the fault is fully resolved before returning to service.
symptoms: Amber or red warning lamp with noticeable power loss under load
Hard starting or stalling, especially at higher fuel demand
Rough idle or surging
Fuel filter housing showing severe visible contamination
procedures_full.source_title: Scania SPN 1382 FMI 0: Severe Fuel Filter Differential Pressure

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 1 on a Kenworth means the fuel filter suction-side DP sensor is reading below normal range — almost always a sensor or wiring fault, not an actual restriction. When a Kenworth T680 or T880 logs SPN 1382 FMI 1, many technicians assume the filter is performing unusually well — but FMI 1 means the sensor output is below the normal operating floor, pointing to a failed sensor, a shorted signal wire, or an open 5 V reference circuit. At ProfessionalDieselRepair.com we trace this code to the wiring harness far more often than to the filter itself. The 3-wire suction-side DP sensor circuit should show 0.5 to 1.2 V on the signal wire at idle with a clean filter. Anything below 0.3 V with a confirmed 5 V reference is a failed sensor or shorted harness.
causes: Failed differential pressure sensor stuck at minimum output
Very Common
Internal sensor failure causes output voltage to fall below 0.3 V, triggering FMI 1. The sensor membrane degrades from prolonged fuel exposure, especially with biodiesel blends above B20.
Short to ground on the signal wire
Chafed insulation on the signal wire between the sensor and ECM creates a low-resistance path to chassis ground, pulling the signal below the FMI 1 threshold even if the sensor itself is functional.
Open 5 V reference circuit on Pin A
A blown fused jumper, broken pin, or corroded splice interrupts the 5 V reference, causing the sensor output to float or drop to zero and set FMI 1.
Filter element bypass due to failed O-ring
A failed filter seal allows fuel to bypass the media with minimal restriction, producing a genuinely low DP reading. Check the housing O-ring before closing the job.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 or Diesel Laptops to the J1939 diagnostic port on the Kenworth T680 or T880. Read active faults, confirm SPN 1382 FMI 1, then monitor the live data channel for the fuel filter DP sensor voltage and computed differential pressure reading.

With the engine off, locate the 3-wire fuel filter differential pressure sensor on the primary filter housing. Pin A is the 5 V reference from the ECM, Pin B is the signal output (0.5 to 4.5 V), and Pin C is sensor ground. Measure Pin A to Pin C with a DVOM: expect 4.95 to 5.05 V. An absent 5 V reference must be traced back to the ECM connector.

With the connector attached and key on engine off, back-probe Pin B to Pin C. A functional sensor at idle reads 0.5 to 0.8 V. If Pin B reads below 0.2 V, measure Pin B to chassis ground: above 1 MOhm expected. A reading below 1 kOhm confirms a short-to-ground on the signal wire.

Disconnect the sensor connector and measure Pin B to chassis ground at the harness side. If voltage remains above 0.5 V with the sensor disconnected, the harness has a short from the signal wire to the 5 V reference circuit. If it drops to 0 V, the sensor internal circuit is the fault source.
If the harness is clean, replace the differential pressure sensor with an OEM part. Reconnect, clear codes with PACCAR Davie4, and confirm live data returns to 0.5 to 1.2 V at idle.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp illuminated with no immediate loss of power in early stages.
ECM logs an inactive filter restriction history flag alongside the active FMI 1 fault.
Fuel filter service reminder may appear prematurely on the Kenworth instrument cluster.
procedures_full.source_title: Kenworth SPN 1382 FMI 1: Below-Normal Fuel Filter DP Reading

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 16 means fuel filter differential pressure is above the moderately severe limit. Change filters, prime correctly, and verify suction-side plumbing before blaming the sensor. Detroit-powered Freightliner and Western Star trucks set SPN 1382 FMI 16 when the fuel filter is doing its job too well—or when it is completely plugged. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as a maintenance-first code, but the derate timer is real if the differential stays high on the next pull.
causes: Overdue or incorrect fuel filter element
Restricted media raises differential pressure across the filter head exactly as the sensor reports.
Contaminated fuel tank with algae or gel
Tank debris loads the filter quickly after replacement, returning high differential within hours.
Faulty differential pressure sensor
A sensor stuck high after new filters and clean fuel points to sensor drift rather than restriction.
steps: Read SPN 1382 live differential pressure in Detroit DDDL8 at idle and 1500 RPM under load.
Replace the primary and secondary fuel filters using Detroit-spec elements and torque the bowl to 25-35 N·m per service guide.
Prime the fuel system with the hand primer until DDDL8 shows positive inlet pressure and no air bubbles at the clear bowl.
Inspect the suction line from tank to pump for collapsed hose, tight bends, or a blocked pickup sock.
If differential pressure remains above 10 psi with new filters, test the differential pressure sensor against a manual gauge tee and replace only if readings diverge by more than 2 psi.
symptoms: Check engine lamp with fuel filter restriction message on Detroit dash
Gradual power loss especially under high fuel demand at highway cruise
Hard start hot or long crank after idle periods
SPN 1382 reading above OEM limit—often 8-12 psi differential on DD15—in Detroit DDDL8
May accompany SPN 94 low delivery pressure if restriction worsens
procedures_full.source_title: Detroit Diesel SPN 1382 FMI 16: Fuel Filter Differential Pressure High

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 16 means the ECM detected the suction-side fuel filter is restricting flow more than expected. It's a medium-severity code that's easy to fix now with a filter change - or expensive to fix later if it's ignored and progresses to a low fuel pressure fault. Cummins gives fleets a genuine early-warning system with SPN 1382 - it flags a restricted fuel filter well before the driver notices any power loss. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as the fault you actually want to catch, because the fix is a routine filter change instead of a roadside breakdown. FMI 16 specifically means the differential pressure across the filter is moderately elevated, not yet critical, giving the shop a window to service it proactively rather than reactively.
causes: Fuel filter element reaching end of service life
As the filter media loads up with debris and gum deposits, the pressure drop across it climbs steadily until it trips this threshold.
Fuel contamination (water, algae, or debris)
Contaminated fuel plugs even a fresh filter far faster than normal, so a recently changed filter tripping this code again points to a tank or fuel-quality issue.
Restricted suction line or plugged tank pickup screen
A mechanical restriction ahead of the filter itself will read as high differential pressure across the filter housing even with a good filter element installed.
Faulty differential pressure sensor
A sensor reading incorrectly high without a real restriction is uncommon but possible, usually identified when a fresh filter doesn't change the reading at all.
steps: Pull the code with Cummins INSITE and confirm whether SPN 1382 FMI 16 is active; check the differential pressure value against the engine's specific threshold (commonly flagged in the 15-20 psi range depending on calibration).
Inspect the fuel filter housing for the date/mileage of the last filter change - if it's near or past interval, that's the most likely culprit.
Replace the primary (suction side) fuel filter and re-prime the system per the service manual procedure to purge air.
Clear the code and use INSITE to monitor live differential pressure across an RPM sweep - it should drop noticeably lower than the pre-change reading.
If differential pressure stays elevated after a fresh filter, check for a restricted or kinked suction line, a clogged pickup tube screen in the tank, or contaminated fuel causing rapid re-plugging.
Road test under load and recheck the code status before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Gradual loss of power that worsens at higher RPM or under load
Amber dash lamp with a 'check fuel filter' style message on some displays
Slightly harder starts as filter restriction increases over time
Fuel economy that trends down over weeks or months
No symptoms at all in early stages - the code can precede any noticeable drivability change
procedures_full.source_title: Cummins SPN 1382 FMI 16: Diagnosing High Fuel Filter Differential Pressure

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 16 means the fuel filter's pressure drop is above normal, a direct sign it's restricting flow. It's a medium-severity early-warning code with no derate - replace the filter and check fuel quality before it develops into a bigger fuel starvation issue. This code measures the filter's restriction directly rather than inferring it from downstream pressure, which makes it one of the more precise early warnings in the fuel system. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats a quick filter change and fuel sample check as a routine, low-cost fix at this stage.
causes: Plugging fuel filter element
Normal accumulation of contaminants in the filter media gradually increases the pressure drop across it over time.
Contaminated fuel supply
Water, algae, or sediment in the fuel accelerates filter plugging well ahead of the normal service interval.
Blocked sensor port
One of the two differential pressure sensor ports can become individually blocked, producing a falsely elevated differential reading.
steps: Pull the fault on Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link (DDDL) and check the freeze-frame differential pressure value against the OEM specification.
Inspect the primary fuel filter for visible contamination, and replace it if it shows heavy debris or discoloration.
Check fuel quality by draining a sample from the water separator bowl - look for algae, water, or sediment contamination.
Verify the differential pressure sensor's two ports aren't individually blocked, which can produce a false differential reading.
Replace the filter and clear the code, then monitor differential pressure over the next several hundred miles to confirm the trend stays flat.
If the reading climbs again quickly after a fresh filter, investigate the fuel source or tank contamination rather than repeating filter changes alone.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp, typically no derate at this stage
Possible slight power dip that may not yet be obvious
No major drivability complaint in most cases
procedures_full.source_title: Freightliner SPN 1382 FMI 16: Fuel Filter Differential Pressure Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1382 FMI 16 on Mack means the fuel filter differential pressure is above the moderately severe high threshold — the filter is restricting fuel flow. Change the primary and secondary fuel filters first. If the fault returns with fresh filters, then check the sensor circuit. SPN 1382 is one of the best early-warning fault codes Mack's system provides. It flags a restricting fuel filter before the truck goes into serious derate from SPN 94 low delivery pressure or before the HP pump gets starved. The fix in most cases is a filter replacement you were due for anyway. If the filter change does not clear it, ProfessionalDieselRepair.com works through the sensor circuit — but that order matters. Filter first, sensor second.
causes: Plugged primary or secondary fuel filter (mechanical)

Normal service life ends with the filter media reaching its dirt-holding capacity. Differential pressure rises as flow restriction increases. This is the expected and by-design operation of SPN 1382 as an early-warning indicator.
Water or biological contamination in fuel (mechanical)
Moderate

Water contamination causes diesel bug (microbial growth) in the fuel tank, producing slime that plugs filter media rapidly — often well before the normal change interval. Severely contaminated fuel can plug a fresh filter within hours.
Wax or gel in cold-weather conditions (mechanical)
Moderate

Underpoured diesel or off-spec blends in cold weather gel and plug filter media more quickly than normal. FMI 16 may set at normal temperatures after the fuel warms, but the plugged filter does not recover once the wax has compressed into the media.
Differential pressure sensor drift or failure (electrical)
Less Common

The fuel filter differential pressure sensor can develop a positive calibration offset, reading higher differential pressure than actual. This produces an FMI 16 fault with a fresh filter installed and under-restriction actual conditions.
steps: 1. Connect Mack Premium Tech Tool (PTT) and read live SPN 1382 differential pressure. Normal differential pressure at operating temperature should be under 15-20 kPa (4-6 in-Hg). FMI 16 thresholds on Mack MP8 are typically triggered above 25-35 kPa (7-10 in-Hg). Note whether the fault is active at idle, under load, or both.

2. Check fuel temperature (SPN 174) — very hot summer fuel is thinner and lowers the differential pressure reading compared to cold, thick winter fuel. A borderline reading in summer on a nearly-new filter may not actually indicate replacement is needed yet.

3. Replace both primary and secondary fuel filters with OEM-spec or equivalent elements. Clear the fault and retest under load. If the fault does not return after a 20-minute highway drive, the filter was the cause — diagnosis complete.

4. If the fault returns immediately after fresh filters, pin-test the differential pressure sensor circuit with a multimeter. Measure 5 V reference on the supply pin, verify clean chassis ground, and measure signal voltage — normal signal should be approximately 0.5-1.0 V at zero differential pressure rising proportionally with restriction. A stuck high signal (above 4 V with no restriction) indicates a failed sensor.

5. If sensor voltage checks out and fresh filters do not resolve the fault, use Texa or Jaltest to read raw sensor data and compare against a known-good calibration value. Inspect the filter housing O-rings and bypass valve — a bypassing filter housing can mimic normal differential pressure while restriction accumulates.
symptoms: Moderate derate or fuel system warning lamp
Mack PTT showing SPN 1382 differential pressure above normal
Possible rough running or hesitation under load if restriction is severe
Fuel filter service indicator tripped (if equipped)
No external fuel leaks or visible fuel system damage
procedures_full.source_title: Mack SPN 1382 FMI 16: Fuel Filter Suction-Side Differential Pressure Above Normal

This fault commonly appears after a forced DPF regeneration or ECM software update, where the valve position feedback does not match the commanded duty cycle within the expected tolerance window

0.diagnostic_action: SPN 4012 FMI 0: Meaning, Symptoms and Troubleshooting Skip to content J1939 Hub Menu J1939 Categories SPN FMI Lookup PGN Lookup FMI Decoder CAN Frame Decoder J1939 CAN Bus Traffic Simulator DBC Generator J1939 CAN Log Analyzer SPN 4012 FMI 0: Meaning, Symptoms and Troubleshooting June 28, 2026 May 31, 2026 by 55yhaymas Home - General & Network - SPN 4012 FMI 0: Meaning, Symptoms and Troubleshooting Diagnostic Code SPN 4012 FMI 0: Meaning and Fix SPN 4012 FMI 0 indicates the ECM detected voltage on the right high beam circuit (Headlamp 2) exceeding the normal operational range, typically above 16.0 V for 12 V systems. This fault commonly appears after a technician replaces a bulb with an incorrect higher-wattage unit or after a voltage spike from a failing alternator.

causes: Shorted Wiring Harness: Insulation breakdown causing a direct short to battery positive voltage
Failed High Beam Bulb: Internal filament short or incorrect bulb with higher current draw
ECM Output Driver Fault: Internal MOSFET shorted to battery, feeding constant overvoltage

Alternator Overvoltage: Regulator failure causing system voltage spikes above 16 V. Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM monitors the headlamp 2 high beam output pin using a voltage divider and an ADC. The nominal operating range is 10.0–14.5 V. When the sampled voltage exceeds 15.5 V for more than 200 ms, the diagnostic sets FMI 0. This threshold prevents false triggers from transient load dumps while ensuring early detection of sustained overvoltage. Electrical analysis reveals that a short to battery positive (B+) on the high beam output line causes the ECM to read near system voltage even when the driver is off. The ECM uses a debouncing timer to confirm the fault before logging. Common real-world scenarios include chafed wiring against the engine block or a crushed harness under the headlamp assembly. When SPN 4012 FMI 0 becomes active, the ECM typically disables the high beam output driver to prevent further damage. Some manufacturers, like Mercedes-Benz, also impose a 30% torque derate on the engine to encourage immediate repair. The fault remains active until the voltage returns to normal and a key cycle is performed. Long-term prevention involves inspecting the headlamp harness for chafing during every major service. Technicians frequently encounter this fault after replacing the ECM without verifying the wiring condition. Using factory-specified bulbs and checking alternator output (max 14.7 V) are essential. A real-world example: a MAN TGS with a failed voltage regulator caused repeated SPN 4012 FMI 0 until the alternator was replaced.
Short to battery: Wire harness chafed against chassis or other circuit, feeding 12V/24V to the ECM driver output
Failed headlamp bulb: Internal filament short to the reflector or base, creating a direct path to ground
Corroded connector: Moisture in the headlamp plug causes high resistance and voltage drop misinterpretation
ECM driver fault: Internal short within the ECM output stage, often after a previous overcurrent event

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 345 Engine (Over) Speed
dd_procedures.overview: The Transmission Control Module (TCM) receives the vehicle’s Engine Speed message over the Primary Data Link (J1939 A). The TCM uses the Engine Speed as the primary engine speed message during normal transmission operation. The Primary Data Link is connected to the TCM at the 20-Way TCM Vehicle Harness Connector.
causes: Descending an overly steep grade Excessive vehicle weight Additional Tools None

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 345 Engine Speed
dd_procedures.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with speed sensors to monitor Engine, Primary Input, Secondary Input, and Output speeds. The speed sensors provide rotational speed inputs to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of verifying Primary and Secondary Clutch engagement, making shift decisions, and confirming gear engagement. The Engine Speed Sensor is located on the Pump assembly and captures rotational speed from a pump mounted tone wheel. The Engine Speed Sensor is connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 65: Gen2 ECA Speed Sensor
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with an Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) Speed Sensor that provides a secondary engine speed signal to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The ECA Speed Sensor is installed in the clutch housing. The ECA broadcasts the ECA Speed Sensor signal to the TECU through the High Integrity Link (HIL) contained within the Transmission Harness. The TECU uses the ECA Speed Sensor signal to determine engine speed when the J1939 engine speed signal is not available. Early models have a thread-in ECA Speed Sensor installed in the flywheel housing. Fault Code 95 indicates either a loss of the signal or an electrical issue with the ECA Speed Sensor, but is specific to systems that use a Gen2 ECA. Troubleshooting for this procedure is specific to the Gen2 ECA and associated harnesses. Note: The troubleshooting procedure for Fault Code 65 may direct users to use this troubleshooting procedure if the vehicle is equipped with a Gen2 ECA, even if Fault Code 95 was not set by the transmission. This is because some transmission software versions do not set Fault Code 95.
procedures_full.detection: The TECU monitors the ECA Speed Sensor signal and compares the sensor reading with the J1939 Engine Speed signal to determine sensor validity. The TECU also monitors the ECA Speed Sensor electrical circuit for any short or open circuits.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The system can detect ECA Speed Sensor faults when one of the following conditions is present for 1 second or longer: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: TECU detects Engine speed over J1939 at idle, but does not detect Transmission clutch input speed or the TECU detects Transmission clutch input speed at idle, but does not detect Engine speed over J1939. FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: ECA detects a short to power in the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit. FMI 4– Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: ECA detects a short to ground in the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit. FMI 5– Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: ECA detects an open on the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: TECU detects the ECA Speed Sensor signal for 2 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). No fallback mode is associated with this fault. TECU uses the vehicle engine speed signal, broadcast over J1939, to operate the transmission. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: TECU detects the ECA Speed Sensor signal for 2 seconds.

procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 65: Gen2 ECA Speed Sensor
procedures_full.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission is equipped with an Electronic Clutch Actuator (ECA) Speed Sensor that provides a secondary engine speed signal to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU). The ECA Speed Sensor is installed in the clutch housing. The ECA broadcasts the ECA Speed Sensor signal to the TECU through the High Integrity Link (HIL) contained within the Transmission Harness. The TECU uses the ECA Speed Sensor signal to determine engine speed when the J1939 engine speed signal is not available. Early models have a thread-in ECA Speed Sensor installed in the flywheel housing. Fault Code 95 indicates either a loss of the signal or an electrical issue with the ECA Speed Sensor, but is specific to systems that use a Gen2 ECA. Troubleshooting for this procedure is specific to the Gen2 ECA and associated harnesses. Note: The troubleshooting procedure for Fault Code 65 may direct users to use this troubleshooting procedure if the vehicle is equipped with a Gen2 ECA, even if Fault Code 95 was not set by the transmission. This is because some transmission software versions do not set Fault Code 95.
procedures_full.detection: The TECU monitors the ECA Speed Sensor signal and compares the sensor reading with the J1939 Engine Speed signal to determine sensor validity. The TECU also monitors the ECA Speed Sensor electrical circuit for any short or open circuits.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The system can detect ECA Speed Sensor faults when one of the following conditions is present for 1 second or longer: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: TECU detects Engine speed over J1939 at idle, but does not detect Transmission clutch input speed or the TECU detects Transmission clutch input speed at idle, but does not detect Engine speed over J1939. FMI 3 – Voltage Above Normal or Shorted High: ECA detects a short to power in the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit. FMI 4– Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: ECA detects a short to ground in the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit. FMI 5– Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: ECA detects an open on the ECA Speed Sensor signal circuit.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: All FMIs: TECU detects the ECA Speed Sensor signal for 2 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs “F” flashes in gear display. Service light flashes (if equipped). No fallback mode is associated with this fault. TECU uses the vehicle engine speed signal, broadcast over J1939, to operate the transmission. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive All FMIs: TECU detects the ECA Speed Sensor signal for 2 seconds.

procedures_full.overview: The Procision transmission is equipped with speed sensors to monitor Engine, Primary Input, Secondary Input, and Output speeds. The speed sensors provide rotational speed inputs to the Transmission Control Module (TCM) for the purpose of verifying Primary and Secondary Clutch engagement, making shift decisions, and confirming gear engagement. The Engine Speed Sensor is located on the Pump assembly and captures rotational speed from a pump mounted tone wheel. The Engine Speed Sensor is connected to the TCM through the Transmission Harness.
procedures_full.detection: The TCM monitors the Engine Speed Sensor signal. If a system failure is detected, the fault is set Active.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: FMI 2 – Data Erratic: Engine Speed signal out of range for 2 seconds. FMI 4 – Voltage Below Normal or Shorted Low: Engine Speed Sensor circuit shorted to ground for 2 seconds. FMI 5 – Current Below Normal or Open Circuit: Engine Speed Sensor circuit open or shorted to power for 2 seconds. FMI 6 - Current Above Normal or Shorted Circuit: Engine Speed Sensor power supply out of normal operating voltage (4.25 to 6.25 volts) for 2 seconds. FMI 8 – Abnormal Frequency: Engine Speed signal abnormal pulse width for 2 seconds. FMI 14 – Special Instructions: Engine Speed signal loss when compared to J1939 Engine Speed message with valid Line Pressure value present for 2 seconds. FMI 20 – Data Drifted High: Engine Speed signal greater than J1939 Engine Speed message with clutch engaged for 1 second. FMI 21 – Data Drifted Low: Engine Speed signal less than J1939 Engine Speed message with clutch engaged for 1 second.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: FMI 2: Engine Speed signal in range for 10 seconds. FMI 4: Engine Speed Sensor circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: Engine Speed Sensor circuit not open or shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 6: Engine Speed Sensor power supply voltage between 4.25 and 6.25 volts for 10 seconds. FMI 8: Engine Speed signal pulse width correct for 10 seconds. FMI 14, 20, 21: Engine Speed signal matches J1939 Engine Speed message for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.fallback: All FMIs: Amber warning lamp on Clutch micro-slipping prohibited Note: If speed substitution is not available: Primary and Secondary Clutches disengaged Non-Neutral modes prohibited PTO Mode prohibited Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive FMI 2: Engine Speed signal in range for 10 seconds. FMI 4: Engine Speed Sensor circuit not shorted to ground for 10 seconds. FMI 5: Engine Speed Sensor circuit not open or shorted to power for 10 seconds. FMI 6: Engine Speed Sensor power supply voltage between 4.25 and 6.25 volts for 10 seconds. FMI 8: Engine Speed signal pulse width correct for 10 seconds. FMI 14, 20, 21: Engine Speed signal matches J1939 Engine Speed message for 10 seconds.
procedures_full.possible_causes: All FMIs: Engine Speed Sensor Internal failure Damaged Transmission Harness Wiring shorted to power, shorted to ground or open Mechanical failure J1939 Engine Speed reporting error TCM Internal failure

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 23: Urge to Move Brake Switch Signal
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be configured with the Urge to Move (UTM) feature. If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).
causes: Brake or Vehicle Controller (OEM determined) Component and/or system fault J1939 Data Link J1939 Data Link damage between
steps: A. Check for Active or Inactive fault codes. Record the transmission fault codes, FMIs, occurrences, and timestamps from the Service Activity Report created during the Diagnostic Procedure. If Fault Code 22, 35 or 36 is Active, troubleshoot per Fault Code Isolation Procedure Index . If Fault Code 23, SPN 521, FMI 9 or 13 is Active, Go to Step B If Fault Code 23, SPN 520216, FMI 31 is Active, Go to Step C If Fault Code 23, SPN 520216, FMI 31 is Inactive, Brake Input Signals are configured correctly, Go to Step V If Fault Code 23, SPN 520215, FMI 14 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step D If Fault Code 23, SPN 597, FMI 9 or 13 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step E If Fault Code 23, SPN 116, FMI 9 or 13 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step F If Fault Code 23, SPN 1121, FMI 9 or 13 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step G If Fault Code 23, SPN 8484, FMI 9 or 13 is Active or Inactive, Go to Step H

B. Monitor Brake Pedal Position. Key off. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Key on with engine running. Allow air pressure to build to governor cut off. Key off. Key on, engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Select “Data Monitor”. Select “Position”. Select “Brake pedal position”. Select all of the SPN 521 sources. Service brake released, monitor ServiceRanger and record “Brake pedal position” value in table. Depress and hold service brake, monitor ServiceRanger, and record “Brake pedal position” value (reading) in table. Notice The “Brake pedal position” value may not be indicated in all the sources selected. Only one valid “Brake pedal position” value is required to support UTM. Compare reading(s) in table. If reading(s) are in range, no problem was found. The intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is in the Brake Pedal Position signal. Contact the OEM for further help troubleshooting the issue. If reading(s) is out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the Brake Pedal Position signal. Go to Step V Service Brake State Range Reading(s) Released 0% Depressed 1% - 100%

C. Compare Primary and Secondary Brake Input Signal Values. Key on, engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Go To “Configuration”. Select “Vehicle”. Locate “Primary Brake Input Signal” and record value in table. Locate “Secondary Brake Input Signal” and record value in table. Compare reading(s) in table. If Primary and Secondary Brake Input Signals are configured to the same value: From the Primary Brake Input Signal New Value drop down select “Default”. From the Secondary Brake Input Signal New Value drop down select “Default”. Select “Apply” and follow the on-screen prompts. Go to Step V If Primary and Secondary Brake Input Signals are not configured to the same value, contact Eaton at 1-800-826-HELP (4357) for further diagnostic instructions. Go to Step V Brake Input Signal Reading(s) Primary Brake Input Signal Secondary Brake Input Signal

D. Contact OEM regarding brake signal messages availability. Contact OEM regarding availability of “Brake Pedal Position” – SPN 521, “Brake Switch” – SPN 597 or “Brake Application Pressure” – SPN 116 signals on the vehicle. Notice If UTM was just enabled the vehicle may not be equipped with the required secondary brake signal messages to support the feature. If one or both brake signals are available, configure vehicle per OEM guidelines and perform a TECU power down. Go to Step V If both secondary brake signal messages are not available, the vehicle does not support UTM. Disable UTM, Go to Step V

E. Monitor Brake Switch Status. Key off. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Key on with engine running. Allow air pressure to build to governor cut off. Key off. Key on, engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Select “Data Monitor”. Select “Status”. Select “Brake switch”. Select all of the SPN 597 sources. Service brake released, monitor ServiceRanger and record “Brake switch” value (reading) in table. Depress and hold service brake, monitor ServiceRanger, and record “Brake switch” value (reading) in table. Notice The “Brake switch” value may not be indicated in all the sources selected. Only one valid “Brake switch” value is required to support UTM. Compare reading(s) in table. If reading(s) are in range, no problem was found. The intermittent nature of the fault makes it likely that the problem is in the Brake switch signal. Contact the OEM for further help troubleshooting the issue. If reading(s) is out of range, refer to OEM guidelines for repair or replacement of the Brake switch signal. Go to Step V Service Brake State Range Reading(s) Released Released Depressed Depressed

F. Monitor Brake Application Pressure. Key off. Set vehicle parking brake and chock wheels. Key on with engine running. Allow air pressure to build to governor cut off. Key off. Key on, engine off. Connect ServiceRanger. Select “Data Monitor”. Select “Pressure”. Select “Brake application pressure”. Select all of the SPN 116 sources. dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 23: Urge to Move Brake Switch Signal
dd_procedures.overview: The UltraShift PLUS transmission may be configured with the Urge to Move (UTM) feature. If enabled and the transmission is in gear, UTM allows the vehicle to start moving after the vehicle service brake is released without having to depress the accelerator pedal. The UTM feature requires a primary on/off brake switch signal and one of two secondary brake signal messages to function. The brake signal messages are broadcast via J1939 to the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU).

In practice, this code activates after a failed forced DPF regeneration where the ECM detects an unexpected voltage on a proprietary sensor input, such as an exhaust backpressure transducer.

SPN_520216.pgn_rate: To engine or positive torque producing devices: Control Purpose dependent or 10 ms To retarder or negative torque producing devices: 50 ms
SPN_520216.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

dd_procedures.title: Fault Code 54 - DC/DC Converter Output Voltage
dd_procedures.overview: The DC/DC Converter is connected to the Power Electronics Carrier (PEC), which provides 340 volts DC. The voltage is reduced to 12-volts DC and maintains the 12-volt system during engine off PTO operation. The DC/DC maintains a steady 14.2 (±0.2) volts output and increases the amperage with vehicle demand up to 1.5 kw or 120 amps. The DC/DC Converter also produces a feedback voltage from the 4-Way Connector. The voltage output is a 0–5 volt signal, which shows 5 volts when the Converter is at 14.2 (±0.2) volts on the output. If the Converter output drops, the feedback signal drops accordingly.
causes: FMI 2 Voltage Feedback wire from DC/DC Converter to HCM FMI 4 12-volt power cables from the 12-volt battery to the DC/DC Converter Power supply to HCM Additional Tools Basic hand tools ASTM Class 0 electrical insulating rubber gloves with leather protectors J48603 Lockout bracket J48506 Lockout tags Eaton® Test Adapter Kit J43318 Digital Volt/Ohm Meter J46708 ServiceRanger
steps: B. Verify voltage from DC/DC Converter to HCM. Key on. Select ePTO Mode on the Pushbutton. Measure voltage at the DC/DC Converter 12-Volt Output Terminals: If voltage is greater than 10 volts, repair the open or shorted harness from Pin 1 of the DC/DC Converter to Pin 19 of the HCM, then Go to Step V If voltage is less than 10 volts, replace the DC/DC Converter , then Go to Step V Connection Measurement DC/DC Converter Output Terminals

C. Verify DC/DC Converter output voltage. Key on. Connect ServiceRanger to the 9-Way Diagnostic Connector in cab. View the following Data Monitor parameters in neutral: PID 121 “DC/DC Converter Output Voltage.” PID 165 “Battery Potential Voltage.” If voltage at the DC/DC Converter is 12–14 volts, Go to Step D If voltage is outside of range, repair the open harness or fuse in the Main Power Supply from the DC/DC Converter to the 12-Volt Battery. Go to Step V Connection Measurement DC/DC Converter Output Voltage Battery Potential Voltage

D. Verify voltage of DC/DC Converter. Key on. View the following Data Monitor parameters: PID 121 “DC/DC Converter Output Voltage.” PID 165 “Battery Potential Voltage.” If PID 165 is 0.5 volts less than PID 121, repair or replace the DC/DC Converter Power Supply Harness that powers the 12-Volt Battery System, then Go to Step V If PID 121 is 0.5 volts less than PID 165, repair the voltage feedback wire that goes from Pin 1 of the DC/DC Converter to Pin 19 of the HCM. Go to Step V Connection Measurement DC/DC Converter Output Voltage Battery Potential Voltage

V. Verify repair. Key off. Key on. Clear codes, See "Clear Inactive Faults" Reconnect all connectors and the negative battery cable. Drive the vehicle and attempt to reset the code. procedures_full.eaton_fault_code: Fault Code 54 - DC/DC Converter Output Voltage
procedures_full.overview: The DC/DC Converter is connected to the Power Electronics Carrier (PEC), which provides 340 volts DC. The voltage is reduced to 12-volts DC and maintains the 12-volt system during engine off PTO operation. The DC/DC maintains a steady 14.2 (±0.2) volts output and increases the amperage with vehicle demand up to 1.5 kw or 120 amps. The DC/DC Converter also produces a feedback voltage from the 4-Way Connector. The voltage output is a 0–5 volt signal, which shows 5 volts when the Converter is at 14.2 (±0.2) volts on the output. If the Converter output drops, the feedback signal drops accordingly.
procedures_full.detection: The following preconditions must be met before the system detects the fault: Hybrid Control Module (HCM) ignition voltage is greater than 7 volts and less than 16 volts.
procedures_full.conditions_set_active: The following conditions must be met to set the fault code Active: FMI 2 is set whenever DC/DC voltage feedback signal reads greater than 15 volts or less than 10 volts and ePTO mode is engaged. FMI 4 is set if the voltage feedback is less than 15 volts and greater than 10 volts and the difference between the voltage feedback and the vehicle battery voltage is greater than 0.5 volts for 1 second or more.
procedures_full.conditions_set_inactive: Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.fallback: When Fault Code 54 is set the following conditions occur: Amber “Check Hybrid” light illuminates. Fault is stored in HCM memory. Depending on the voltage of the vehicle battery, the engine may operate to maintain the 12-volt system in ePTO mode. Conditions to Set Fault Code Inactive Only Inactive faults can be cleared from the Transmission Electronic Control Unit (TECU) or HCM history using ServiceRanger. The TECU automatically clears faults from history after 200 hours. The HCM automatically clears a fault from history after that fault has been Inactive for 200 hours.
procedures_full.possible_causes: This fault code can be caused by any of the following: FMI 2 Voltage Feedback wire from DC/DC Converter to HCM FMI 4 12-volt power cables from the 12-volt battery to the DC/DC Converter Power supply to HCM

The voltage is stepped down to 12-volts DC by the DC/DC Converter. The converter maintains the vehicle 12-volt system during engine off PTO operation. SPN_520256.description_en: VCD1 output stage (clutch actuator - slow air intake) short circuit to ground
causes: Sensor Supply Drift: Reference voltage from ECM (5.0 V) drops to 4.75 V due to corroded pins or harness resistance
Shorted Signal Wire: Signal line partially shorted to sensor ground through chafed insulation
ECM Internal Fault: Internal ADC channel offset error after ECM replacement without factory calibration download
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM microcontroller monitors the sensor signal via a 10-bit ADC with a 0-5 V range
When the raw count falls below the lower calibration limit (e.g., 10% of full scale) for more than 50 ms, the
Harness chafing: Wire insulation wears through against a metal bracket or frame, creating a direct short to ground
Connector corrosion: Moisture ingress at the sensor or ECM connector causes pin-to-pin shorting to ground

Sensor internal failure: A shorted semiconductor junction inside the proprietary sensor pulls the signal line below 0.5 V. ECM pin damage: Bent or pushed-back terminal in the ECM 120-pin connector results in intermittent or permanent short to ground

SPN_520296.description_en: Engine power supply control (E-engine #1) - abnormal frequency, pulse width or cycle
causes: Re-routing the harness with abrasion-resistant loom eliminated the fault permanently
Technicians often see this code when a sensor signal is lost momentarily but not long enough to set a specific FMI, leaving the ECM unable to classify the failure
It requires systematic wiring and connector inspection to isolate the intermittent event
Incomplete Programming: ECM software flash or parameter file did not finalize, leaving a pending special instruction
Security Access Denied: OEM-specific security login not performed, blocking the special instruction routine
Component Replacement: New ECM, injector, or turbocharger installed without executing the teach-in procedure
Corrupted Calibration: Faulty calibration file from a third-party tool causing an unresolved special instruction flag
Advanced Technical Analysis The ECM microcontroller monitors a dedicated status bit in the manufacturer-assignable SPN 520296 memory location

procedures_full.overview: SPN 520372 FMI 16 indicates the DEF dosing unit temperature is above normal. This can lead to inefficient DEF injection and increased NOx emissions, potentially causing engine derate. The Cummins SPN 520372 FMI 16 fault code is a significant indicator of potential issues within your vehicle's Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) dosing system. This code specifically points to a scenario where the DEF dosing unit is experiencing temperatures that exceed its normal operational range. Such a condition is not just a simple inconvenience but a critical problem that can lead to a cascade of further issues if not addressed promptly. When the DEF dosing unit overheats, it disrupts the efficient injection of DEF into the exhaust stream, which is crucial for reducing harmful NOx emissions. This inefficiency can result in increased emissions, potentially causing your vehicle to fail emissions tests and even leading to legal and environmental compliance issues. Moreover, if this fault is ignored, the engine's control system may respond by entering a derate mode. This mode is designed to limit engine power to prevent further damage, but it can severely impact your vehicle's performance, making it less responsive and potentially unsafe in certain driving conditions. Understanding and addressing the root cause of this fault code is essential not only for maintaining your vehicle’s performance and reliability but also for ensuring that it remains compliant with environmental regulations. Prompt diagnosis and repair can prevent more severe damage and avoid costly repairs down the line, keeping your vehicle on the road and operating efficiently.
causes: DEF dosing unit overheating

Overheating can result from prolonged engine operation in high ambient temperatures or insufficient cooling. Regular maintenance and monitoring can prevent this issue. Ensure cooling systems are functioning properly and consider additional ventilation if necessary.
Contaminated DEF fluid

Contaminated DEF can lead to improper dosing and overheating. Always use high-quality DEF from reputable sources to avoid contamination. Implement a regular DEF quality testing routine to catch any issues early.
Obstructed DEF lines

Obstructions in the DEF lines can restrict fluid flow, causing the dosing unit to overheat. Regularly inspect and clean lines to ensure they are clear. Use compressed air to clear any potential blockages and maintain optimal flow.
steps: Use an infrared thermometer to measure the DEF dosing unit temperature, comparing it against manufacturer specifications. Ensure the thermometer is calibrated for accurate readings. This step is crucial to confirm the actual temperature and rule out sensor errors that might mislead diagnostics.

Inspect DEF lines for kinks or obstructions that might cause overheating, ensuring proper fluid flow. Pay attention to bends and connection points, as these are common areas where blockages can occur. Clear any obstructions to restore normal flow and prevent overheating.

Check DEF fluid level and quality using a DEF refractometer to ensure it meets standards. Look for signs of crystallization or discoloration, which can indicate contamination. Maintaining proper DEF quality is essential for the system's efficient operation.

Examine the DEF dosing unit for signs of physical damage or wear that could affect performance. Inspect seals and connectors for leaks, as these can lead to dosing inefficiencies and overheating. Replace any damaged components to ensure the system's integrity.

Utilize an OBD-II scanner to clear the fault code after repairs, ensuring no further issues persist. Re-scan to confirm the code does not return. This step verifies that the repairs were successful and that the system is functioning correctly.
symptoms: Check engine light illuminated, indicating a potential emissions issue.
Reduced engine power due to derate mode activation.
Noticeable increase in NOx emissions, potentially failing emissions tests.
Unusual DEF consumption patterns, indicating dosing inefficiencies.
Possible engine overheating if the issue is not addressed.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 31 on a manufacturer-specific SPN indicates the ECM or body controller detected an event condition that is defined by the OEM. Body module configuration issues, low voltage events, related switch inputs, network timeouts, and true module faults are the primary causes. Generic scan tools showing a code without OEM text leading to guesswork is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern. Always decode with OEM information when possible — the event definition determines the correct diagnostic path.
causes: Body module configuration issues — configuration fault producing event condition
Low voltage events — low voltage producing module event
Related switch inputs — switch input fault producing event condition
Network timeouts — J1939 network timeout producing event condition
True module faults — module hardware failure producing event condition
steps: Single Action Gate — Decode OEM-Specific Definition

Decode the OEM-specific event definition using OEM software or service information. Generic scan tools show a code without OEM text, leading to guesswork. Always decode with OEM information when possible. The event definition determines the correct diagnostic path — a body module configuration event requires a different path than a switch input fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Check Related Module Voltage and Network

Check the related module voltage and network integrity. Low voltage events and network timeouts are common causes of manufacturer-specific event conditions. Verify module power and ground integrity. Verify J1939 network backbone resistance and termination.
Override Manager — Inspect Associated Inputs

Inspect the associated inputs identified by the OEM event definition. A switch input fault producing an event condition requires switch diagnosis. A sensor input fault requires sensor diagnosis. Follow the OEM event definition to identify the associated inputs.
Safety Interceptor — Follow OEM Flowchart

Follow the OEM diagnostic flowchart for the specific event definition. Manufacturer-specific events have OEM-specific diagnostic paths that are not generic. The OEM flowchart identifies the correct test sequence for the specific event condition.
Resume Point — Verify Voltage Stability During Event Window

Verify voltage stability during the event window. Low voltage events producing module faults are a documented pattern. Monitor module voltage during the conditions that produce the event. A voltage dropout during the event window confirms a power supply fault.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Event Confirmation
After repair, verify the event condition does not return. Confirm SPN 521049 FMI 31 does not return. Monitor for return of body controller events over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Power, Network, Configuration, or Module Decision

Repair power or ground if voltage fault is confirmed. Repair network if backbone fault is confirmed. Correct configuration if configuration fault is confirmed. Replace module only with OEM proof of module hardware failure.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair power or ground if voltage fault is confirmed.
2 . Repair network if backbone fault is confirmed.
3 . Correct configuration if configuration fault is confirmed.
4 . Replace module only with OEM proof of module hardware failure.
Verification Steps
Confirm event condition does not return after repair.
Verify SPN 521049 FMI 31 does not return after repair.
Confirm module voltage is stable after repair.
Monitor for return of body controller events over extended operation.

✓ Inspect J1939 network backbone connections at every major service.
✓ Use OEM software for manufacturer-specific SPN diagnosis.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 524287 FMI 14 indicates a critical DPF system issue in Mercedes Benz vehicles, often requiring immediate attention to prevent engine damage.
causes: Failed DPF Regeneration

Regular short trips or low-speed driving can prevent the DPF from reaching the necessary temperature to burn off soot, leading to clogging. This is a common issue in urban driving conditions where the vehicle does not operate at optimal speeds for sufficient durations.
Sensor Malfunction

Faulty pressure or temperature sensors can provide incorrect data to the ECU, resulting in improper DPF management. These sensors are critical for monitoring the DPF's status and ensuring it operates within the correct parameters.
Excessive Soot Accumulation
High levels of soot can accumulate due to poor fuel quality or engine inefficiencies, overwhelming the DPF's capacity. This can be exacerbated by infrequent maintenance or using low-grade fuel.
Exhaust Leaks

Leaks in the exhaust system can lead to incorrect pressure readings, affecting the DPF's operation and triggering fault codes. These leaks can alter the pressure differential across the DPF, leading to misdiagnosis of the system's health.
steps: Use a diagnostic tool to attempt a manual regeneration of the DPF. This can sometimes clear minor soot blockages and restore partial functionality.
Visually inspect the DPF for any signs of physical damage or excessive soot buildup that might indicate a deeper issue requiring professional intervention.
Check for exhaust leaks that could affect the DPF's performance and efficiency, leading to false readings and improper operation.
Examine the pressure sensors and temperature sensors associated with the DPF for any signs of malfunction, as these can lead to incorrect ECU readings and improper DPF management.
If manual regeneration fails, consult a professional for potential DPF cleaning or replacement to prevent further engine damage.
symptoms: DPF warning light illuminated on the dashboard.
Noticeable loss of engine power and performance.
Excessive smoke, often black, emitted from the exhaust.
Frequent engine derating or limp mode activation.
Increased fuel consumption due to engine strain.

procedures_full.overview: Caterpillar PID 91 FMI 8 indicates an abnormal signal from the throttle position sensor, often leading to a dead throttle pedal and high-idle mode. Inspect wiring and connections. Overview: Caterpillar PID 91 FMI 8 Caterpillar engines are renowned for their reliability, but even these robust machines can encounter issues. One such problem is the PID 91 FMI 8 fault code, which relates to the throttle position sensor. This code signifies an abnormal frequency, pulse width, or period signal being sent from the throttle position sensor to the ECM, leading to potential performance issues. Understanding and resolving this fault code is crucial for maintaining optimal engine performance. The throttle position sensor plays a vital role in ensuring the engine responds accurately to driver inputs. A malfunction can result in a dead throttle pedal and cause the engine to enter a high-idle failsafe mode, impacting vehicle operation. This condition not only affects the drivability of the vehicle but can also lead to safety concerns if not addressed promptly. The sensor's role is to provide the ECM with precise data about the throttle position, which is critical for fuel injection and ignition timing. Anomalies in this data can disrupt engine efficiency and performance.
causes: Wiring Harness Damage

The wiring harness connecting the throttle position sensor to the ECM can become damaged due to chafing against other components. This can result in intermittent or erratic signals. In many cases, the harness may rub against the firewall or other sharp edges, leading to insulation wear and eventual wire exposure.
Faulty Throttle Position Sensor

The sensor itself may fail due to internal wear or electronic issues, leading to incorrect signal transmission to the ECM. Over time, exposure to engine heat and vibrations can degrade sensor components, affecting its accuracy and reliability.
Connector Corrosion

Corrosion at the sensor connector can disrupt the electrical signal, causing communication errors with the ECM. This is particularly common in environments with high humidity or where road salt is used, as these conditions accelerate corrosion processes.
steps: Visually inspect the throttle pedal and sensor assembly for physical damage or obstruction. Check for any signs of wear or interference that might hinder sensor function.
Check the wiring harness for signs of wear, such as stretching, rubbing, or cuts. Pay special attention to areas where the harness might contact other components.
Disconnect the sensor connector, inspect for corrosion or damage, and reconnect securely. Ensure that the connector is free from moisture and debris.
Use a multimeter to measure the voltage at the sensor to ensure it matches specifications. Compare readings against manufacturer specifications to verify sensor performance.
Clear any debris around the pedal assembly that might interfere with its operation. Ensure that the pedal moves freely without obstruction.
symptoms: Dead throttle pedal, where pressing it produces no response.
Engine defaults to a steady high-idle failsafe mode.
Amber diagnostic light flashes to indicate a fault.
Reduced engine power and responsiveness.
Potential loss of vehicle control due to throttle issues.
procedures_full.source_title: Caterpillar PID 91 FMI 8: Diagnose and Fix Throttle Position Sensor Issues

causes: FMI 3: Voltaj normalin üzerinde veya yüksek kaynağa (+5V / +24V) kısa devre. → Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
FMI 4: Voltaj normalin altında veya şasiye (GND) kısa devre. → Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
FMI 2: Veri tutarsız, kesintili veya yanlış (Sinyal Sıçraması). → Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
FMI 0: Veri geçerli fakat normal çalışma aralığının üzerinde (Kritik Yüksek). → Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 0 on cruise or PTO input status indicates the ECM received an implausible or above-expected status from a cruise or PTO input. Failed PTO switch, miswired aftermarket PTO, stuck cruise switch, and incorrect status broadcast over J1939 are the primary causes. Aftermarket PTO installs causing status conflicts and unexpected throttle requests are a documented pattern on vocational trucks. Switch status PIDs should match actual switch positions — toggling each input and confirming clean state changes is the most efficient first step.
causes: Failed PTO switch — PTO switch failure producing incorrect status
Miswired aftermarket PTO — aftermarket PTO wiring producing status conflict
Stuck cruise switch — cruise switch stuck in active position
Incorrect status broadcast — incorrect PTO or cruise status broadcast over J1939
steps: Single Action Gate — Verify Each Switch PID

Verify each switch PID matches the actual switch position. Toggle each cruise and PTO input and confirm clean state changes in the PID. A PID that does not change when the switch is toggled confirms a stuck or failed switch. A PID that changes correctly confirms the switch is functional.
Binary Decision Gate — Inspect Aftermarket PTO Wiring

Inspect aftermarket PTO wiring for status conflicts. Aftermarket PTO installs causing status conflicts and unexpected throttle requests are a documented pattern. Inspect aftermarket PTO wiring for incorrect connections, missing pull-ups or pull-downs, and incorrect signal levels.
Override Manager — Check for Stuck Inputs

Check for stuck inputs on cruise and PTO switches. A stuck cruise switch produces a continuous active status that conflicts with vehicle speed or other conditions. Inspect switch contacts for sticking or welding. Confirm each switch returns to the inactive state when released.
Safety Interceptor — Network Source Conflict Check

Check for network source conflicts if the status is broadcast over J1939. A multi-module status conflict produces an implausible status that cannot be resolved by switch replacement. Identify the source address broadcasting the incorrect status and diagnose that module.
Resume Point — Configuration Parameter Correction

Check configuration parameters if switch and wiring integrity are confirmed. Incorrect configuration parameters can produce status conflicts on some platforms. Configuration parameter correction requires authorization — follow OEM procedures for parameter changes.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Status Confirmation

After repair, verify all switch PIDs match actual switch positions under all operating conditions. Confirm SPN 443 FMI 0 does not return. Monitor for return of unexpected throttle requests or PTO engagement behavior.
Repair Ledger Output — Switch, Wiring, or Configuration Decision

Replace failed switch if stuck or failed input is confirmed. Correct aftermarket PTO wiring if status conflict is confirmed. Correct configuration parameters with authorization if parameter fault is confirmed. Do not replace engine or transmission components for a switch or wiring status fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace failed cruise or PTO switch if stuck or failed input is confirmed.
2 . Correct aftermarket PTO wiring if status conflict is confirmed.
3 . Correct configuration parameters with authorization if parameter fault is confirmed.
Verification Steps
Confirm all switch PIDs match actual switch positions after repair.
Verify SPN 443 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm no unexpected throttle requests or PTO engagement behavior after repair.
Monitor for return of status conflicts over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify aftermarket PTO wiring against OEM specifications before installation.
✓ Inspect cruise and PTO switch contacts for sticking at every major service.
✓ Verify switch PID accuracy at every major service on vocational trucks.
✓ Document aftermarket PTO wiring for future service reference.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium Severity
Medium. Can create unexpected engagement behavior — correct before vocational operation. Input-status mapping prevents transmission and engine misdiagnosis on vocational setups.
symptoms: SPN 443 FMI 0 PTO input fault
Cruise control switch fault
PTO status conflict
Idle bump PTO code
Unexpected throttle request from PTO status fault

FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.
FMI 7: Mechanical system not responding properly.
FMI 13: Out of calibration.
steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.

SPN_1066.description: Brake signal transmitter (foot brake valve) - internal device or component failure

[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.

causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.

steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.

[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.

[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 1485 FMI 2 indicates ECM main power relay status or data erratic or implausible. Failing main relay, socket fretting, intermittent control side, and voltage drop on feed circuits are the primary causes. Random ECM resets traced to main relay contacts rather than internal ECM failure is a documented pattern. Replacing the ECM for intermittent resets without proving the main relay power path is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Failing main relay — failing main relay contacts producing intermittent ECM power
Socket fretting — socket fretting producing intermittent contact resistance
Intermittent control side — intermittent control-side ignition feed producing intermittent relay engagement
Voltage drop on feed circuits — voltage drop on ECM feed circuits producing intermittent power
steps: Step 1 — Verify Control and Load Voltage

Verify control and load voltage at the relay. Monitor ECM supply during the fault. Confirm control-side ignition feed voltage and load-side power to the ECM are both present and stable. A voltage drop on ECM feed circuits producing intermittent power requires circuit repair.
Step 2 — Wiggle Relay and Base

Wiggle the relay and base. Relay tap testing and voltage at the load side under vibration can expose intermittents. Socket fretting producing intermittent contact resistance is a documented cause. Inspect the relay socket for heat damage and pin fretting.
Step 3 — Substitute Known-Good Relay After Circuit Proof

Substitute a known-good relay after circuit proof. Confirm the relay socket and feed circuits are clean before substituting a known-good relay. A relay substituted into a socket with heat damage or fretting will not resolve the fault.
Step 4 — Inspect Socket Heat Damage

Inspect the relay socket for heat damage. Socket fretting and heat damage producing intermittent contact resistance are documented causes. Inspect the relay base and surrounding area for heat damage, corrosion, and pin fretting.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair relay socket if fretting or heat damage is confirmed.
2 . Repair feed wiring if voltage drop is confirmed.
3 . Replace relay if relay failure is confirmed after circuit proof.
4 . Address ECM path only if supplies are perfect and fault persists.
Verification Steps
Confirm ECM power is stable after repair.
Verify SPN 1485 FMI 2 does not return after repair.
Confirm no intermittent ECM resets after repair.
Monitor for return of main relay intermittent events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect relay socket for heat damage and fretting at every major service.
✓ Inspect ECM feed wiring for voltage drop at every major service.
✓ Inspect control-side ignition feed at every major service.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High. Intermittent controller power can stall or prevent start. Severity
High. Intermittent controller power can stall or prevent start. Erratic ECM main relay data is a power-distribution intermittent until proven otherwise.
symptoms: ECM main relay intermittent
Power relay dropout
Intermittent hard no-comm
Key on module reboot
Random ECM resets from relay contacts
procedures_full.source_title: SPN 1485 FMI 2 — ECM Main Relay Data Erratic

SPN_2348.description: Halogen and combined lamp and left high beam headlight short circuit to ground
SPN_2348.description_en: Halogen and combined lamp and left high beam headlight short circuit to ground
causes: Halogen and combined lamp and left high beam headlight short circuit to ground.
steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
SPN_2348.pgn_description: This lighting message is a response to the request for lighting data in the corresponding lighting command message. Each lighting controller on the tractor and attached implements must transmit this message when requested. The requestor may use this information to determine which lighting systems are functioning. Lighting controllers that have lamp sensing capability will also report failed light bulbs. This is a legal requirement in many areas. See PGN 65089 for the lighting command message.

SPN_3230.description: Downstream NOx sensor AT1OGC1 CAN receive frame length error
SPN_3230.description_en: Downstream NOx sensor AT1OGC1 CAN receive frame length error
causes: Failing or degraded NOx sensor
NOx sensor contaminated by DEF crystallization
Exhaust leaks affecting sensor readings
Wiring or connector damage at the NOx sensor
Failed SCR catalyst causing abnormal NOx readings
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
steps: Sensör arızası en yaygın neden olduğundan öncelikle NOx sensörünü ve kablo tesisatını kontrol ettirin.
Sensör konumu yakınında egzoz sızıntısı olup olmadığını kontrol edin.
Sensör ve kablolar sağlamsa SCR katalizörünü kontrol ettirin; verimi düşmüş bir katalizör bu mantıksal uygunluk (rationality) arızasını tetikleyen anormal NOx değerleri üretebilir.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
SPN_3230.pgn_description: The purpose of this PG is to group the aftertreatment outlet sensor data for bank 1. These values include the NOx, %O2, status of the sensors with respect to the power being supplied and the heating element, errors and stability of the readings.

steps_en_archive: Have the NOx sensor and its wiring inspected first as sensor failure is the most common cause.
Check for exhaust leaks near the sensor location.
If the sensor and wiring check out, have the SCR catalyst evaluated as a degraded catalyst can produce abnormal NOx readings that trigger this rationality fault.

SPN_3349.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. steps: [FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).

[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

causes: Regen inhibit switch activated during regeneration
Vehicle moved or driven during a parked regeneration attempt
Exhaust temperatures insufficient to complete soot combustion
Faulty HC dosing injector not delivering enough fuel during regen
DPF too heavily loaded to complete regen in one cycle
Failed DPF temperature sensor affecting regen control Low fuel level preventing regen from completing
Faulty regen control system interrupting the cycle
steps: Aracın güvenli bir şekilde park edildiğinden, rejenerasyon engelleme anahtarının kapalı olduğundan, yakıt seviyesinin yeterli olduğundan ve döngü sırasında aracın hareket ettirilmediğinden emin olarak yeniden bir park halinde rejenerasyon başlatmayı deneyin.
Rejenerasyon yine tamamlanamazsa, HC dozaj enjektörünü, DPF sıcaklık sensörlerini ve rejenerasyon kontrol sistemini yetkili bir dizel teknisyenine kontrol ettirin.
[FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
SPN_3826.pgn_description: This message contains SCR service information for aftertreatment system 1 (or bank 1).
steps_en_archive: Attempt another parked regeneration ensuring the vehicle is parked safely, the regen inhibit switch is off, fuel level is adequate, and the vehicle is not moved during the cycle.
If the regen fails to complete again have the HC dosing injector, DPF temperature sensors, and regen control system inspected by a qualified diesel technician.

SPN_4105.name: 4105 This is usually the transmission. The TCU detected occasional TC1 packet loss. Usually occurs when connecting diagnostic tools. Caused by CAN line instability. Turning the D/R selector knob back or switching the key off may clear the fault. Note!: When using diagnostic tools to diagnose the engine, instruments, EBS modules, it is easy to trigger. Check each module for faults with a diagnostic tool. If the yellow lamp is on, return the lever to idle or switch the key on again to clear.
SPN_4105.title_tr: Bu genellikle şanzımandır. TCU ara sıra TC1 paket kaybı algıladı. Genellikle teşhis araçları bağlanırken oluşur. CAN hattı kararsızlığından kaynaklanır. D/R seçici düğmesini geri çevirmek veya kontağı kapatmak arızayı temizleyebilir. Not!: Teşhis araçlarıyla motor, gösterge, EBS modüllerini teşhis ederken tetiklenmesi kolaydır. Her modülü teşhis aracıyla arıza yönünden kontrol edin. Sarı lamba açıksa, kolu rölantiye getirin veya kontağı tekrar açarak temizleyin.

3.description: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source

D/R çevirme düğmesiyle rölantiye dönmek veya kontak kapatıp açmak hatayı giderebilir. Dikkat: tanı cihazıyla motor, göstergeler, EBS modülü kontrol edilirken her modül ayrıca tanı cihazıyla kontrol edilmelidir; sarı ışık yanıyorsa kolla rölantiye dönün veya kontaktı tekrar açın
3.source: SITRAK/OEM fault-code DB RU (CC BY 4.0, (c) МегаДата / megadata.pro)
