SPN_4142.description: Due to a fault on the clutch disengagement valve 2 (Y16) output or on ADP3 or ADM14, the valve does not work.
SPN_4142.description_en: Due to a fault on the clutch disengagement valve 2 (Y16) output or on ADP3 or ADM14, the valve does not work.
causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.
FMI 6: Current above normal or grounded circuit.
FMI 10: Abnormal rate of change.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Aktüatörün komut aldığı halde hareket etmediğini doğrulayın; mekanik sıkışma arayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Aktüatör besleme hattında aşırı gerilim/kısa devre olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 5 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid bobin direncini ölçün ve soket kilit tırnaklarını kontrol edin.
[FMI 6 katalog] Aktüatör/solenoid hattında şasi teması (kısa devre) olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör içindeki elemanın gevşediğini veya soket pini korozyonunu inceleyin.

causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.

steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

SPN_4191.pgn_description: NOTE - Retarder can be disabled by commanding a torque limit of 0%. Use of the limit mode allows the use of the retarder only up to the limit specified in the request. This can be used to permit retarding of up to 50%, for example, if that limit is required by some device such as an EBS, or it can disable the use of the retarder by others, as when an ABS controller detects wheel slip. Note that the 10 ms transmission repetition rate is intended for temporary powertrain control (P32 of SPN 3350).

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically turbocharger compressor inlet differential pressure too high (Low Box).‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically turbocharger compressor inlet differential pressure too high (Low Box).‪
steps: High Differential Pressure Check
Check entire air intake system for leaks, restrictions or damage.
If leaks or damage are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no leaks or damage is found, go to the next step.
Disconnect the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor.
Inspect the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor harness connector for bent, corroded or spread pins.
If connector pin damage is found, repair as necessary. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no pin damage is found, go to the next step.
Inspect the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor pressure tubes for leaks, kinks or restrictions.
If damaged tubes are found, repair as necessary. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If no tube damage is found, replace the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor. Refer to "131.1.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: MBE 4000 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 131.1 SPN 4226/FMI 0 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.

Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically a circuit failed high.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically a circuit failed high.‪
steps: Open Circuit Check
Check for multiple codes.
If 3563/3, 51/4 and 4226/3 are present, repair the short to battery power between pin 117 of the 120–pin MCM connector, the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and the Inlet Throttle Valve. See Figure
"Inlet Air Delta P Sensor"
. Refer to "131.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 1. Inlet Air Delta P Sensor

If 51/3 and 4226/3 are present, repair the short to battery power between pin 103 of the 120–pin MCM connector, the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and the Inlet Throttle Valve. Refer to "131.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If only 4226/3 is present, go to step 2.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor.
Measure the voltage between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and ground.
If the voltage is greater than 5 volts, repair the short to battery between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and pin 109 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "131.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the voltage is less than five volts, replace the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor. Refer to "131.3.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.
procedures_full.source_title: MBE 4000 DDEC VI Troubleshooting - Section 131.3 SPN 4226/FMI 3 - Detroit Diesel Engine Troubleshooting

procedures_full.overview: This diagnosis is typically Inlet Air Delta P Sensor circuit failed low.‪
causes: This diagnosis is typically Inlet Air Delta P Sensor circuit failed low.‪
steps: Short to Ground Check
Check for multiple codes.

If 3563/4, 51/4 and 4226/4 are present, repair the short to ground between pin 117 of the MCM 120–pin connector, the intake throttle valve and the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor. Refer to "131.4.1.1 Verify Repairs".

If 51/4 and 4226/4 are present, repair the short to ground between pin 117 of the MCM 120–pin connector, the intake throttle valve and the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor. Refer to "131.4.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If only 4226/4 is present, go to the next step.
Turn the ignition OFF.
Disconnect the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor.
Disconnect the 120–pin MCM connector.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and ground. See Figure
"Inlet Air Delta P Sensor".
Figure 1. Inlet Air Delta P Sensor
If the resistance is less than 3Ω, repair the short to ground between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and 109 of the 120–pin MCM connector. See Figure
"120–pin MCM Connector"
. Refer to "131.4.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Figure 2. 120–pin MCM Connector
If the resistance is greater than 3Ω, go to step 4.
Measure the resistance between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and 109 of the 120–pin MCM connector.
If the resistance is greater than 3Ω, repair the open between pin 3 of the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor and pin 109 of the 120–pin MCM connector. Refer to "131.4.1.1 Verify Repairs".
If the resistance is less than 3Ω, replace the Inlet Air Delta P Sensor. Refer to "131.4.1.1 Verify Repairs".
Verify repairs as follows:‪
Turn ignition OFF.
Reconnect any electrical connections that were disconnected to perform the diagnosis.
Clear codes with DDDL 7.0 or latest version.
Start and bring engine up to operating temperature (over 140°F/60°C).

Verify operation is satisfactory and no warning lamps illuminate. If warning lamps illuminate, troubleshoot the codes. If assistance is required, call the Detroit Diesel Customer Support Center at 313–592–5800.

steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.

causes: Smart booster fault.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 8 katalog] Sensör sinyal frekansını/nabız genişliğini referans değerle karşılaştırın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.

SPN_519717.description: TSC1ACCR message (torque from active cruise control unit to gear - speed control information) checksum failure
SPN_519717.description_en: TSC1ACCR message (torque from active cruise control unit to gear - speed control information) checksum failure
causes: TSC1ACCR message (torque from active cruise control unit to gear - speed control information) checksum failure.
steps: [FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
[FMI 31 katalog] İlgili anahtar veya sensör kontak pozisyonunu doğrulayın.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 520209 FMI 31 is an OEM-specific aftertreatment event flag. The exact text depends on the manufacturer — treat it as a pointer into AT service logic, not a generic parts list. The OEM definition may indicate an inducement stage, sensor rationality fault, dosing event, or protection flag. Contaminated DEF, dosing path restriction, NOx sensor faults, ignored efficiency codes, and cold-climate heater issues are possible causes depending on OEM definition. Generic scan tools without OEM text leading to guesswork and wrong parts is the most documented pattern.
causes: OEM-defined inducement stage — OEM-defined inducement stage producing aftertreatment event flag
Sensor rationality fault — sensor rationality fault producing OEM-specific AT event
Dosing event — dosing event producing OEM-specific AT flag
Protection flag — protection flag producing OEM-specific AT event
steps: Step 1 — Decode OEM Definition

Decode the OEM definition. Use OEM software to expand the code and retrieve the full OEM text. Generic scan tools without OEM text lead to guesswork and wrong parts. The OEM definition identifies the specific AT family involved — inducement, sensor rationality, dosing, or protection.
Step 2 — Pull Companion AT Code Timeline

Pull the companion AT code timeline. Identify which companion AT codes appeared first and in what order. A code timeline that shows DEF quality or dosing codes appearing before efficiency codes suggests a fluid or dosing root cause.
Step 3 — Branch to DEF/DPF/NOx/Electrical Family

Branch to the appropriate AT family based on OEM definition and code timeline. Apply standard chemistry, delta-P, NOx, or electrical gates as indicated by the OEM definition. The OEM definition identifies the specific family — do not guess the family from the SPN alone.
Step 4 — Verify Repair With OEM Status

Verify repair with OEM status. Confirm the OEM-specific AT event flag clears after repair. Use OEM software to verify AT system status after repair. A flag that does not clear after repair confirms an incomplete repair or additional fault.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair based on OEM definition and confirmed evidence.
2 . Address DEF chemistry if quality fault is confirmed.
3 . Repair dosing path if dosing fault is confirmed.
4 . Repair NOx sensor circuit if sensor fault is confirmed.
5 . Verify repair with OEM software status after repair.
Verification Steps
Confirm OEM-specific AT event flag clears after repair.
Verify SPN 520209 FMI 31 does not return after repair.
Confirm AT system status is normal after repair using OEM software.
Monitor for return of OEM-specific AT events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Use OEM software for all AT code diagnosis on proprietary SPN ranges.
✓ Maintain OEM-specification DEF quality at all times.
✓ Inspect AT system at OEM-specified intervals.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Variable by OEM text. Assume Medium to High until decoded. Severity
Variable by OEM text. Assume Medium to High until decoded. Manufacturer-specific AT events require OEM definition first, then standard evidence gates.

SPN_520215.description: Right trailing axle 1 pressure sensor - power short circuit or pressure sensor open to ground
SPN_520215.description_en: Right trailing axle 1 pressure sensor - power short circuit or pressure sensor open to ground

steps: [FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.

[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
[FMI 31 katalog] İlgili anahtar veya sensör kontak pozisyonunu doğrulayın.

SPN_520226.description: Electronic control unit (ECU) low-level software and hardware monitoring message (MoF)
SPN_520226.description_en: Electronic control unit (ECU) low-level software and hardware monitoring message (MoF)
causes: FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 9: Abnormal update rate.
FMI 10: Abnormal rate of change.
FMI 11: Root cause not known.
FMI 12: Bad intelligent device or component.
steps: [FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
SPN_520226.causes_source: SAE J1939-73 FMI fault matrix (DB fault_matrix, Tur-30 türetme)
SPN_520226.steps_class_fixed_tur30: SPN sınıfına göre jenerik adım düzeltildi

SPN_520243.description: VG1 solenoid valve (gear position drive) short to supply voltage 3 = VG1 output stage (shift drive) voltage exceeds normal value or short to high voltage source
SPN_520243.description_en: VG1 solenoid valve (gear position drive) short to supply voltage 3 = VG1 output stage (shift drive) voltage exceeds normal value or short to high voltage source
causes: VG1 solenoid valve (gear position drive) short to supply voltage 3 = VG1 output stage (shift drive) voltage exceeds normal value or short to high voltage source.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

SPN_520260.description: CFV actual gas pressure below target value
SPN_520260.description_en: CFV actual gas pressure below target value
causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.
FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
FMI 12: Bad intelligent device or component.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.

SPN_520302.description: Speed sensor signal normal, engine timeout detected, crawling mode activated
SPN_520302.description_en: Speed sensor signal normal, engine timeout detected, crawling mode activated
causes: Speed sensor signal normal, engine timeout detected, crawling mode activated.
steps: [FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 8 katalog] Sensör sinyal frekansını/nabız genişliğini referans değerle karşılaştırın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

causes: FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
FMI 5: Current below normal or open circuit.
steps: [FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 8 katalog] Sensör sinyal frekansını/nabız genişliğini referans değerle karşılaştırın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 9 katalog] Sensör/modülün CAN-Bus hattına bağlı olduğunu ve adres aldığını (Address Claiming) doğrulayın. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 10 katalog] Sensör sinyalinin değişim hızını izleyin; aşırı dalgalanma/gecikme olup olmadığını kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.

SPN_522012.description: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated
SPN_522012.description_en: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated
causes: OBD-related fault for torque limitation of the urea injection control unit (DCU) activated.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 11 katalog] Öncelikli olarak Freeze Frame (DM4) verilerini ve motor çalışma koşullarını okuyun.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.
[FMI 31 katalog] İlgili anahtar veya sensör kontak pozisyonunu doğrulayın.

SPN_522027.description: Downstream NOx sensor - NOxNO2CorCat2Ds CAN information outside SAE defined rational limits
SPN_522027.description_en: Downstream NOx sensor - NOxNO2CorCat2Ds CAN information outside SAE defined rational limits
causes: FMI 0: Data valid but above normal operational range.
FMI 1: Data valid but below normal operational range.
FMI 2: Data erratic, intermittent or incorrect.
FMI 3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to high source.
FMI 4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to low source.
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 4 katalog] Sinyal pini ile şasi arasındaki direnci ölçün (<1.0 Ω ise tesisatta şasi teması vardır).
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 6 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında şasi teması olup olmadığını ölçün. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 7 katalog] Aktüatör itici kollarını, kurum birikmesini ve hava/yağ tahrik hatlarını mekanik olarak inceleyin.
[FMI 14 katalog] Motor üreticisinin (Cummins/CAT/Volvo) yetkili servis kılavuzuna başvurun.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.
[FMI 19 katalog] Veri yolunda 120Ω hat sonlandırma direncini ve CAN-H/CAN-L sinyal gürültüsünü test edin.

SPN_523101.description_en: DFC_NSCDsDynChkDIUMPR - calculated NOx sensor dynamic response failure for DIUMPR (when the engine transitions from load state to overrun state, the sensor responds too slowly)
causes: DFC_NSCDsDynChkDIUMPR - calculated NOx sensor dynamic response failure for DIUMPR (when the engine transitions from load state to overrun state, the sensor responds too slowly).
steps: [FMI 0 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel aşırı basınç/sıcaklık durumunu mekanik test portundan doğrulayın.
[FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 2 katalog] Kablo demetinde titreşim temassızlığı, gevşek klemens veya manyetik relüktör çark diş hasarı arayın.
[FMI 3 katalog] Sensör soketini ayırın; voltaj şasiye göre düşmüyorsa kablo demeti akü besleme hattına ezilmiştir.
[FMI 5 katalog] Sensör sinyal hattında açık devre olup olmadığını ölçün; konektörü kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.
[FMI 12 katalog] Modülün besleme voltajını teyit edin; düzelmiyorsa dahili ECU/Sensör arızasıdır.
[FMI 15 katalog] Filtre ve soğutma temizliği yapın; sistem henüz arıza lambası yakmamış olabilir.
[FMI 16 katalog] Motor tork sınırlandırması (Derate) başlamadan önce ilgili devreyi temizleyin.
[FMI 17 katalog] Sistem basınç regülatörünü ve filtre tıkanıklığını kontrol edin.
[FMI 18 katalog] Dozaj pompası, hava tahrik valfi veya debi kısıtlamalarını giderin.

steps: [FMI 1 katalog] Sensör besleme hattını ve fiziksel düşük basınç/seviye durumunu kontrol edin. Sorun sürerse ağ ve düğüm tanılaması için yetkili servise başvurun.

SPN_112.name: SPN 112 FMI 1 — Coolant Level Critically Low
SPN_112.description_en: SPN 112 FMI 1 indicates coolant level at the critical low threshold. The ECM protection strategy may limit power or warn aggressively. Major external leaks, hose failures, radiator leaks, internal leaks, continued operation after earlier low-level warnings, and rare false sensor critical events are the primary causes. Drivers continuing after low-coolant warnings until critical protection sets is a documented pattern. Continuing loaded operation with confirmed critical low coolant risks catastrophic engine damage.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 112 FMI 1 indicates coolant level at the critical low threshold. The ECM protection strategy may limit power or warn aggressively. Major external leaks, hose failures, radiator leaks, internal leaks, continued operation after earlier low-level warnings, and rare false sensor critical events are the primary causes. Drivers continuing after low-coolant warnings until critical protection sets is a documented pattern. Continuing loaded operation with confirmed critical low coolant risks catastrophic engine damage.
causes: Major external leak — major external leak producing rapid coolant loss
Hose failure — hose failure producing rapid coolant loss
Radiator leak — radiator leak producing coolant loss
Internal leak — internal leak producing coolant loss without external evidence
Continued operation after earlier warnings — continued operation after low-level warnings until critical protection sets
Rare false sensor critical — rare false sensor critical event with full tank
steps: Step 1 — Safe Cooldown
Allow safe cooldown before any inspection. Do not open the cooling system on a hot engine. Allow the engine to cool to a safe temperature before any coolant system inspection.
Step 2 — Physical Level Verification
Verify physical coolant level. Visual and physical proof dominates. Inspect the surge tank and radiator for actual coolant level. A confirmed critical low coolant level requires leak diagnosis.
Step 3 — Pressure Test If Low
Perform a pressure test if coolant is confirmed low. A pressure test identifies external leaks. Pressurize the cooling system and inspect for leaks at hoses, radiator, clamps, and fittings.
Step 4 — Identify Leak Source

Identify the leak source. Major external leaks, hose failures, and radiator leaks are the most common causes. An internal leak with no external evidence requires further diagnosis including combustion gas testing.
Step 5 — Sensor Path Only for False-Critical Cases

Evaluate the sensor path only for false-critical cases where the tank is visibly full. A rare false sensor critical event with a full tank requires sensor circuit diagnosis. Do not evaluate the sensor path before physical level proof.
Step 6 — Repair and Refill
Repair the identified leak source and refill with OEM-specification coolant. Do not return to service until the leak is repaired and the coolant level is restored.
Step 7 — Verify After Repair
Verify cooling system integrity after repair. Confirm SPN 112 FMI 1 does not return. Monitor for return of low coolant events over extended operation.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair hose, radiator, or clamp if external leak is confirmed.
2 . Address internal leak if no external leak is found.
3 . Repair sensor circuit if false-critical event with full tank is confirmed.
4 . Refill with OEM-specification coolant after repair.
Verification Steps
Confirm cooling system integrity after repair.
Verify SPN 112 FMI 1 does not return after repair.
Confirm no coolant loss after repair.
Monitor for return of low coolant events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Respond to low-coolant warnings immediately — do not continue operation.
✓ Inspect cooling system for leaks at every major service.
✓ Verify coolant level at every pre-trip inspection.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High Severity
High. Do not continue loaded operation with confirmed critical low coolant. Critical low coolant is an immediate engine-protection issue first.
symptoms: Critical low coolant
Coolant empty warning
Engine protection low coolant
Overheat risk from low coolant
Power derate from critical low coolant

SPN_113.name: SPN 113 FMI 0 — Coolant System Pressure Above Normal
SPN_113.description_en: SPN 113 FMI 0 indicates cooling system pressure above the calibrated maximum where pressure is monitored. Combustion gas entry into the cooling system, incorrect pressure cap, restriction in the system, sensor bias high, and localized boiling events are the primary causes. Head gasket or combustion entry causing rapid overpressure and wrong-cap installs are documented patterns. Replacing the head gasket without gauge proof and combustion gas testing is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 113 FMI 0 indicates cooling system pressure above the calibrated maximum where pressure is monitored. Combustion gas entry into the cooling system, incorrect pressure cap, restriction in the system, sensor bias high, and localized boiling events are the primary causes. Head gasket or combustion entry causing rapid overpressure and wrong-cap installs are documented patterns. Replacing the head gasket without gauge proof and combustion gas testing is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Combustion gas entry — head gasket or combustion leak allowing combustion gas into cooling system
Incorrect pressure cap — wrong cap rating allowing overpressure
Restriction in system — restriction in cooling system producing pressure buildup
Sensor bias high — pressure sensor bias producing false high reading
Localized boiling events — localized boiling producing pressure spikes
steps: Step 1 — Cap Rating Confirmation

Confirm the pressure cap rating. A wrong-cap install is a documented cause of coolant overpressure. Verify the cap rating matches OEM specification. A cap with a lower rating than specified allows the system to overpressurize before the cap releases. Replace the cap if the rating is incorrect.
Step 2 — Mechanical Pressure Monitoring

Monitor cooling system pressure with a mechanical pressure gauge. Verify the pressure reading against the sensor reading. A sensor bias producing a false high reading confirms a sensing fault. A mechanical gauge confirming overpressure confirms a real system pressure fault.
Step 3 — Combustion Gas Test

Perform a combustion gas test if overpressure is confirmed. Head gasket or combustion entry causing rapid overpressure is a documented pattern. Use a combustion gas test kit to check for combustion gases in the coolant. A positive combustion gas test confirms combustion entry into the cooling system.
Step 4 — Sensor Correlation

Correlate the pressure sensor reading with the mechanical gauge. A sensor reading that does not match the mechanical gauge confirms a sensor fault. Inspect the pressure sensor circuit for reference voltage, ground, and signal integrity.
Step 5 — Inspect for External Restrictions

Inspect for external restrictions in the cooling system. A restriction in the cooling system produces pressure buildup. Inspect the radiator, hoses, and thermostat for restriction. A restriction that is removed and resolves the overpressure confirms a restriction fault.
Step 6 — Repair Based on Evidence

Repair based on confirmed evidence. Replace the cap if the rating is incorrect. Repair the sensor circuit if sensor bias is confirmed. Address combustion entry if combustion gas test is positive. Address restrictions if found.
Step 7 — Verify After Repair
Verify cooling system pressure is within specification after repair. Confirm SPN 113 FMI 0 does not return. Monitor for return of overpressure events over extended operation.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Replace pressure cap if rating is incorrect.
2 . Repair sensor circuit if sensor bias is confirmed.
3 . Address combustion entry if combustion gas test is positive.
4 . Remove restrictions if found in cooling system.
Verification Steps
Confirm cooling system pressure is within specification after repair.
Verify SPN 113 FMI 0 does not return after repair.
Confirm no repeated coolant loss after repair.
Monitor for return of overpressure events over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Verify pressure cap rating at every major service.
✓ Inspect cooling system for restrictions at every major service.
✓ Monitor coolant pressure trend over time on high-mileage engines.
✓ Perform combustion gas test at every major service on high-mileage engines.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
High if combustion entry is suspected Severity
High if combustion entry is suspected. Limit operation and diagnose. The FSM enforces gauge-and-cap proof before major engine conclusions.
symptoms: Coolant system overpressure
High radiator pressure
Combustion leak into cooling system
Cap cannot hold or system overpressurizes
Repeated coolant loss with no external leak

SPN_123.name: International SPN 123 FMI 2: Diagnose and Repair Intake Pressure Sensor Issues
SPN_123.description_en: International SPN 123 FMI 2 indicates erratic or incorrect data from the intake manifold pressure sensor, affecting engine performance. Address promptly to prevent derate. The International SPN 123 FMI 2 fault code is a critical alert for diesel engine operators, indicating that the intake manifold pressure sensor is delivering data that is erratic, intermittent, or incorrect. This sensor plays a vital role in regulating the air-fuel mixture, crucial for efficient engine performance. Ignoring this fault can lead to suboptimal engine function and potential derate, where the engine reduces output to prevent damage. Understanding the symptoms, root causes, and repair strategies for this code is essential for maintaining your vehicle's performance and longevity. The intake manifold pressure sensor is integral to ensuring that the engine receives the correct amount of air to mix with fuel, optimizing combustion. When this sensor fails or provides inaccurate data, it can lead to a range of issues, from poor acceleration and increased emissions to engine stalling and reduced fuel efficiency. By addressing the SPN 123 FMI 2 fault code promptly, you can prevent these problems, ensuring your engine runs smoothly and efficiently. Regular maintenance and timely diagnostics are key to avoiding long-term damage and maintaining optimal performance.

procedures_full.overview: International SPN 123 FMI 2 indicates erratic or incorrect data from the intake manifold pressure sensor, affecting engine performance. Address promptly to prevent derate. The International SPN 123 FMI 2 fault code is a critical alert for diesel engine operators, indicating that the intake manifold pressure sensor is delivering data that is erratic, intermittent, or incorrect. This sensor plays a vital role in regulating the air-fuel mixture, crucial for efficient engine performance. Ignoring this fault can lead to suboptimal engine function and potential derate, where the engine reduces output to prevent damage. Understanding the symptoms, root causes, and repair strategies for this code is essential for maintaining your vehicle's performance and longevity. The intake manifold pressure sensor is integral to ensuring that the engine receives the correct amount of air to mix with fuel, optimizing combustion. When this sensor fails or provides inaccurate data, it can lead to a range of issues, from poor acceleration and increased emissions to engine stalling and reduced fuel efficiency. By addressing the SPN 123 FMI 2 fault code promptly, you can prevent these problems, ensuring your engine runs smoothly and efficiently. Regular maintenance and timely diagnostics are key to avoiding long-term damage and maintaining optimal performance.
causes: Sensor contamination

Dust, oil, and other contaminants can accumulate on the sensor, leading to erratic data transmission. Regular cleaning and maintenance can prevent this issue. Contaminants interfere with the sensor's ability to accurately measure pressure, causing the engine control module to receive incorrect data and potentially misadjust the air-fuel mixture.
Electrical connection issues

Loose or corroded electrical connections can disrupt the signal from the sensor to the ECM, causing incorrect readings. Inspecting and securing connections can resolve this. Electrical issues are often overlooked but can significantly impact sensor performance, leading to diagnostic confusion and potential misdiagnosis.
Intake manifold leaks

Leaks in the intake manifold can lead to incorrect pressure readings, as the sensor may detect lower pressure than actual. Sealing leaks promptly can prevent sensor errors. These leaks can cause the engine to run lean or rich, affecting performance and potentially causing damage over time.
Sensor failure

While less common, the sensor itself may fail due to age or manufacturing defects. Replacing the sensor is necessary if it is determined to be faulty. Sensor failure can lead to persistent issues that are not resolved by addressing other potential causes, necessitating replacement to restore proper engine function.
steps: Inspect the intake manifold pressure sensor and its connectors for signs of dirt, moisture, or physical damage that could affect sensor readings. Ensure that the sensor is securely mounted and free from obstructions. This step is crucial as even minor contamination can lead to significant reading errors.

Use a multimeter to measure the sensor's voltage and resistance, comparing these values to manufacturer specifications to ensure accuracy. Variations from the expected range can indicate sensor or wiring issues. This diagnostic step helps pinpoint whether the sensor itself or the wiring is at fault.

Check the intake system for any air leaks, as these can lead to incorrect pressure readings and subsequent sensor errors. Use a smoke machine to identify small leaks that may not be visible. Leaks can significantly alter pressure readings, leading to inaccurate sensor data.

Clear any debris or obstructions from the sensor area to ensure accurate data transmission. Regular cleaning can prevent future issues. This preventive measure is essential to maintain sensor accuracy and prolong its lifespan.

Reset the fault code using an OBD-II scanner after performing repairs to verify the issue is resolved. Monitor the vehicle's performance to ensure the fix is effective. This final step ensures that the repair has addressed the root cause and the engine operates efficiently.
symptoms: Fluctuating engine idle, indicating inconsistent air-fuel mixture.
Noticeable loss of power during acceleration, especially under load.
Illuminated check engine light, signaling a detected fault.
Increased fuel consumption due to inefficient combustion.
Occasional engine stalling or hesitation, particularly at low speeds.
procedures_full.source_title: International SPN 123 FMI 2: Diagnose and Repair Intake Pressure Sensor Issues

SPN_176.name: PACCAR SPN 176 FMI 3: Turbocharger Oil Temperature Voltage High
SPN_176.description_en: SPN 176 FMI 3 means the PACCAR ECM sees turbo oil temperature sensor voltage above the normal range. Boost limiting or a mild derate can follow if the ECM distrusts the reading, even when actual turbo oil temperature is normal. Turbo oil temp faults on MX engines are frequently wiring or sensor issues rather than catastrophic turbo failures, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com advises logging voltage and physical oil supply before authorizing turbo replacement.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 176 FMI 3 means the PACCAR ECM sees turbo oil temperature sensor voltage above the normal range. Boost limiting or a mild derate can follow if the ECM distrusts the reading, even when actual turbo oil temperature is normal. Turbo oil temp faults on MX engines are frequently wiring or sensor issues rather than catastrophic turbo failures, and ProfessionalDieselRepair.com advises logging voltage and physical oil supply before authorizing turbo replacement.
causes: Shorted turbo oil temp sensor
Heat cycles crack sensor elements and pull signal voltage high toward the 5V reference.
Harness chafe near turbo housing
Vibration and heat expose copper, allowing signal-to-supply shorts that peg voltage.
Connector moisture or pin spread
Poor pin fit after turbo R&R lets water bridge circuits and skew readings high.
steps: Read live turbo oil temp voltage in Davie4; expect roughly 0.5-4.5V scaled to temp, not pegged above 4.8V key-on.
Backprobe sensor supply at Pin 3 for 5.0V ±0.25V and signal Pin 2; compare to ECM expected range at cold soak.
Measure sensor resistance to ground unplugged; many PACCAR sensors read 1.5-3 kΩ cold — near 0 ohms indicates internal short.
Inspect the harness from turbo center housing to main engine harness for heat damage within 6 inches of the turbine housing.
After sensor or wiring repair, idle until oil temp stabilizes and confirm SPN 176 tracks within 20°F of engine oil temp at cruise.
symptoms: Amber MIL with SPN 176 FMI 3 in PACCAR Davie4
Reduced boost or slower turbo response under load
Fan may run harder if ECM substitutes default oil temp strategy
Fault may set after turbo service or oil leak repair
No actual overheating smell despite the temperature fault
procedures_full.source_title: PACCAR SPN 176 FMI 3: Turbocharger Oil Temperature Voltage High

procedures_full.overview: SPN 176 FMI 4 on Caterpillar engines means the turbocharger oil temperature sensor circuit is reading below normal, consistent with a short to ground. It's a medium-severity fault that mainly affects turbo thermal monitoring rather than causing a direct power loss. The turbocharger oil temperature sensor gives Caterpillar's ECM a way to watch for thermal stress on the turbo bearings, and SPN 176 FMI 4 means that data feed has gone dark with a shorted-low reading. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com treats this as a fault worth fixing promptly even without a derate attached, since it removes a safeguard that would otherwise catch a genuine turbo overheating event. The repair almost always comes down to harness damage in a hot, cramped location rather than a failed sensor element.
causes: Heat-damaged wiring shorting the signal to ground
The sensor's location near the turbo oil drain subjects the harness to extreme heat cycling, which degrades insulation and eventually shorts the circuit.
Corroded sensor connector
Oil residue and heat at the connector can accelerate corrosion, creating a low-resistance path that mimics a sensor fault.
Failed sensor element
Internal sensor failure can independently produce a shorted-low reading, though it's less common than external wiring damage in this location.
steps: Pull the fault with Cat ET and confirm SPN 176 FMI 4 is active; check the reported turbo oil temperature value, which will likely be pegged low regardless of actual conditions.
Locate the turbocharger oil temperature sensor, typically near the turbo oil drain line, and inspect the connector for corrosion or a pinched wire against the exhaust manifold.
Disconnect the sensor and check the signal wire for continuity to ground with the harness isolated from the ECM - any unexpected continuity confirms a short.
Test the sensor's resistance and compare against the manufacturer's resistance-versus-temperature chart to rule the sensor element in or out.
Repair any chafed wiring found in the high-heat area near the turbo, using heat-resistant loom rated for that environment.
Clear the code and verify the reported temperature climbs realistically during a warm-up and cool-down cycle before returning the equipment to service.
symptoms: No obvious drivability symptom in most cases
Amber Check Engine lamp on the dash
Turbo oil temperature reading pegged at an unrealistic low value on the scan tool
Possible missed warning if a genuine turbo overheat condition develops while this sensor is faulted
procedures_full.source_title: Caterpillar SPN 176 FMI 4: Diagnosing a Turbocharger Oil Temperature Circuit Fault

SPN_646.name: Caterpillar SPN 646 FMI 3: Wastegate Drive Voltage Above Normal
SPN_646.description_en: SPN 646 FMI 3 on Caterpillar means the wastegate drive circuit voltage is above the ECM maximum. Test the wastegate solenoid and harness for short to power before replacing the turbocharger. SPN 646 controls the electrical drive signal to the turbocharger wastegate actuator on Caterpillar engines. FMI 3 flags voltage above normal in that drive circuit — an electrical fault distinct from wastegate position feedback monitored by SPN 1188. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees Cat operators replace entire turbos when a shorted wastegate solenoid is the actual failure.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 646 FMI 3 on Caterpillar means the wastegate drive circuit voltage is above the ECM maximum. Test the wastegate solenoid and harness for short to power before replacing the turbocharger. SPN 646 controls the electrical drive signal to the turbocharger wastegate actuator on Caterpillar engines. FMI 3 flags voltage above normal in that drive circuit — an electrical fault distinct from wastegate position feedback monitored by SPN 1188. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees Cat operators replace entire turbos when a shorted wastegate solenoid is the actual failure.
causes: Wastegate solenoid internal short to power
Very Common
Heat-cycled solenoid windings short internally, drawing continuous 12V and reporting maximum drive voltage to the ECM.
Drive wire short to battery positive in engine harness
Chafed harness near the turbo pedestal shorts the PWM drive conductor to 12V, pegging the circuit high regardless of ECM command.
ECM wastegate driver output stuck high
Internal ECM driver failure holds the wastegate drive circuit at maximum voltage — confirm only after solenoid and harness test good on a known-good ECM.
steps: Connect Cat ET or Texa and confirm SPN 646 FMI 3. Log wastegate drive commanded duty cycle vs boost pressure target during a loaded acceleration from 1200-1800 RPM.

Key on, engine off: measure wastegate solenoid drive voltage at the connector. Cat wastegate solenoids typically receive PWM drive on a 12V circuit — steady 12V with 0% commanded duty cycle indicates a short to power.

Disconnect the wastegate solenoid and measure harness-side voltage. Above 11V with solenoid unplugged and 0% command confirms harness short; 0V with solenoid connected but high command reading points to solenoid internal short.

Inspect wastegate actuator linkage for carbon binding — mechanical sticking does not cause FMI 3, but a bound wastegate combined with full drive command can overheat the solenoid and short internally.

After repair, verify wastegate response in Cat ET: commanded duty cycle should modulate 10%-90% with boost error, and boost pressure should reach 25-35 psi at 1800 RPM under load on C15 ACERT applications.
symptoms: Yellow or red warning lamp on Cat dash display
Wastegate drive duty cycle pegged at 100% on Cat ET live data
Reduced boost and sluggish response under load
Possible overboost protection derate if ECM cannot verify wastegate control
Companion SPN 1127 boost pressure codes may appear with wastegate control loss
procedures_full.source_title: Caterpillar SPN 646 FMI 3: Wastegate Drive Voltage Above Normal

procedures_full.overview: SPN 646 FMI 5 on Mack engines means the turbocharger wastegate drive circuit is reading current below normal, consistent with an open circuit. It's a medium-severity fault that pushes boost control to a fallback strategy until the open circuit - usually in the harness - is repaired. The wastegate drive circuit gives the ECM precise control over boost by actively positioning the wastegate rather than relying on a purely mechanical spring-loaded system. When SPN 646 FMI 5 shows this circuit open, ProfessionalDieselRepair.com starts at the harness first - this connector and its wiring sit close to the turbocharger's extreme heat, making it one of the more failure-prone circuits on the engine purely from thermal stress.
causes: Heat-damaged wiring near the turbocharger
Extended exposure to high underhood temperatures near the turbo degrades wire insulation over time, eventually producing an open circuit at a chafe or crack point.
Corroded or improperly seated connector
Moisture or heat-related connector degradation can create a poor or fully open connection independent of the wire itself.
Failed wastegate actuator drive circuit internally
The actuator's internal drive coil can fail open after sufficient heat cycling and electrical stress.
ECM driver circuit fault
An internal ECM issue affecting this specific actuator's driver circuit is uncommon but should be considered if harness and actuator both test normal.
steps: Pull the fault with PACCAR Davie4 or Jaltest and confirm SPN 646 FMI 5 is active; check for any accompanying boost pressure fault codes.
Locate the wastegate drive actuator connector near the turbocharger and inspect it for heat damage, corrosion, or a pin that isn't making solid contact.
Disconnect the connector and check resistance across the actuator's drive circuit, comparing to the manufacturer's specification.
If resistance reads open, trace the harness back toward the ECM checking for a break, particularly near areas exposed to high heat from the turbocharger and exhaust manifold.
If the actuator itself tests open internally, replace the wastegate actuator assembly following the correct calibration procedure.
Clear the code and use the scan tool's actuator command test to confirm the wastegate drive responds correctly through its full range before returning the truck to service.
symptoms: Inconsistent boost behavior or a slight power reduction
Amber Check Engine lamp
Possible increase in exhaust temperature if the wastegate defaults toward a closed position
No dramatic drivability complaint in many cases

procedures_full.overview: SPN 646 FMI 5 on a Detroit Diesel means the wastegate actuator drive circuit has an open-circuit condition. Measure solenoid coil resistance and inspect the connector pigtail for heat damage before ordering parts. Detroit Diesel SPN 646 FMI 5 flags an open circuit in the wastegate actuator drive — the electrical path that commands the turbocharger wastegate solenoid to regulate boost pressure. SPN 646 specifically covers the drive (command) side of the wastegate circuit, which must not be confused with SPN 1188, the position feedback sensor. FMI 5 (current below normal / open) means the ECM is sending a drive signal but receiving back insufficient current, indicating a wire break, failed solenoid coil, or corroded connector. Without wastegate control, Detroit's GHG14 and GHG17 calibrations typically activate overboost protection or limit fueling, resulting in a derate. Fast identification and repair at ProfessionalDieselRepair.com-trained shops prevents turbocharger damage from uncontrolled boost excursions.
causes: Heat-damaged wastegate solenoid connector pigtail
The solenoid connector is mounted near the turbocharger outlet and is subjected to repeated heat cycling that cracks insulation and corrodes terminal pins, creating an open-circuit path.
Failed wastegate solenoid coil
The solenoid coil wire can break internally due to vibration fatigue or heat, creating an open circuit that triggers FMI 5.
Broken ECM driver wire
A wire break between the ECM harness and the wastegate solenoid connector prevents drive current from reaching the solenoid, producing an open-circuit fault.
steps: Connect DDDL (Detroit Diesel Diagnostic Link) to read all active faults. Confirm SPN 646 FMI 5 is present. Check whether SPN 1188 (wastegate position) is also active — a combined drive and position fault suggests both solenoid and sensor circuits are compromised in the same harness run.

Locate the wastegate control solenoid on the turbocharger and measure resistance across its coil terminals using a digital multimeter. A typical solenoid coil reads 10–30 Ω. An open-circuit reading (OL) confirms internal coil failure requiring solenoid replacement.

If coil resistance is normal, unplug the solenoid connector and measure harness resistance from the ECM driver pin to the solenoid connector. Any reading above 1–2 Ω indicates a broken or corroded wire requiring harness repair.

Inspect the wastegate solenoid connector for heat damage, backed-out terminals, or corrosion — the solenoid is mounted close to the turbocharger and is exposed to extreme heat cycling that degrades connector integrity.

After repair, use a Snap-on NEXIQ USB Link or DDDL to command the wastegate through its full duty cycle range in live data and confirm boost pressure responds correctly before returning the vehicle to service.
symptoms: Engine derate with restricted boost pressure or overboost protection active.
Black smoke and poor throttle response under load.
SPN 646 FMI 5 logged as active in ECM, possibly alongside boost pressure fault codes.
Turbocharger operating at maximum wastegate-closed boost during highway driving.
Inability to complete active regeneration due to abnormal exhaust flow conditions.
procedures_full.source_title: Detroit Diesel SPN 646 FMI 5: Wastegate Drive Circuit Open Fault

procedures_full.overview: SPN 646 FMI 7 means the turbocharger wastegate actuator on a Kenworth isn't mechanically responding to the commanded position, usually from a binding linkage. It's a High severity fault causing inconsistent boost and power delivery, but it does not shut the engine down. The wastegate actuator on a turbocharged Kenworth controls how much exhaust gas bypasses the turbine to regulate boost pressure, and SPN 646 FMI 7 flags that this actuator isn't physically moving the way the ECM expects, despite the control signal itself looking normal. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this fault most often from carbon and soot buildup binding the linkage rather than an actual failed actuator motor, which is why a careful mechanical inspection before parts replacement pays off on this repair.
causes: Soot or carbon buildup binding the wastegate linkage
Exhaust soot accumulates on the linkage pivot points over time, restricting free movement even when the actuator itself is functioning correctly.
Corroded or seized linkage pivot points
Road salt and moisture exposure can corrode the linkage hardware, causing binding independent of any soot contamination.
Failed actuator motor or internal gear mechanism
The actuator's internal motor or gear train can fail from wear, preventing it from moving the wastegate arm even with a free linkage.
Damaged unison ring inside the turbo housing
On variable geometry turbos, a soot-packed or damaged unison ring can bind internally, producing symptoms similar to an actuator failure.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and confirm SPN 646 FMI 7, then command the wastegate actuator through its range using the diagnostic tool's actuator test if available.
Visually inspect the wastegate actuator linkage for binding, corrosion, or soot buildup preventing free movement.
With the engine off, manually attempt to move the wastegate arm by hand (if accessible) to check for mechanical resistance beyond normal spring tension.
Apply penetrating oil to a stuck linkage pivot point and retest movement, since carbon and soot buildup is a common cause of binding.
If the actuator itself doesn't respond correctly during a bench or commanded test despite a free linkage, replace the actuator, clear codes, and verify normal boost behavior on a road test.
symptoms: Inconsistent power delivery or boost surging under acceleration
MIL illuminated
Possible whistling or unusual turbo noise
Reduced fuel economy from inefficient boost control
procedures_full.source_title: Kenworth SPN 646 FMI 7: Turbo Wastegate Not Responding

procedures_full.overview: SPN 646 FMI 14 on Freightliner requires OEM special instructions for wastegate drive diagnosis — calibrate the actuator and verify linkage before replacing parts. The wastegate regulates turbo boost on many Freightliner configurations. When SPN 646 sets with FMI 14, the ECM is directing technicians to a specific calibration and verification sequence rather than a generic electrical diagnosis. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com completes that workflow in DDDL8 first — most failures are procedural, not hardware.
causes: Wastegate calibration required after ECM or turbo service
Position reference is lost until the OEM calibration routine completes successfully.
Bent or disconnected wastegate linkage
Physical damage from heat shields or prior repairs prevents the drive from moving the valve.
Carbon binding at wastegate valve seat
Soot buildup keeps the valve from seating, causing boost control errors.
Failed wastegate actuator diaphragm or electronic driver
Genuine actuator failure after high heat exposure or mileage.
steps: Connect Detroit DDDL8 or Noregon JPRO and retrieve SPN 646 special instruction details and freeze frame.
Perform wastegate actuator calibration per Detroit or Cummins service procedure for the installed engine.
Inspect wastegate linkage for bent rods, missing clips, or carbon binding at the turbo housing.
Command wastegate open and closed while watching boost pressure response on live data.
Check vacuum supply or electronic driver circuit depending on actuator type before replacing the drive unit.
symptoms: Check-engine lamp with SPN 646 FMI 14 active
Boost pressure overshoot or undershoot during load
Wastegate fails commanded position test on scan tool
Audible flutter or hunting boost on acceleration
Possible derate if boost control remains out of range

SPN_3701.name: SPN 3701 FMI 15 — DPF Active Regen Frequency Above Expected
SPN_3701.description_en: FMI 15 on DPF regen frequency indicates the regen is occurring more frequently than the OEM model predicts for the duty cycle. Underboost, EGR abnormalities, injector imbalance, short-trip duty cycle, failing DOC light-off, and sensor bias affecting strategy are the primary causes. Chronic frequent regen after turbo or boost leaks left unresolved is a documented pattern. Cleaning or replacing the DPF without correcting the upstream soot source produces repeat frequent regen — the DPF reloads at the same accelerated rate after service.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 15 on DPF regen frequency indicates the regen is occurring more frequently than the OEM model predicts for the duty cycle. Underboost, EGR abnormalities, injector imbalance, short-trip duty cycle, failing DOC light-off, and sensor bias affecting strategy are the primary causes. Chronic frequent regen after turbo or boost leaks left unresolved is a documented pattern. Cleaning or replacing the DPF without correcting the upstream soot source produces repeat frequent regen — the DPF reloads at the same accelerated rate after service.
causes: Underboost — charge air leak or turbo fault increasing soot production
EGR abnormalities — EGR fault increasing soot production
Injector imbalance — injector imbalance increasing soot production
Short-trip duty cycle — short trips preventing regen completion
Failing DOC light-off — DOC not reaching light-off temperature for passive regen
Sensor bias affecting strategy — sensor bias causing incorrect soot model
steps: Single Action Gate — Review Regen Count and History

Review regen count and history from the OEM scan tool. Confirm the regen frequency is genuinely above the expected model for the duty cycle. A high regen count with a short-trip duty cycle may be normal for the application — confirm the duty cycle before diagnosing upstream causes.
Binary Decision Gate — Inspect Upstream Soot Producers

Inspect upstream soot producers. Underboost from a charge air leak or turbo fault and EGR faults that increase soot production are the most common upstream causes of high regen frequency. Inspect charge air path for leaks and EGR system for faults before any DPF evaluation.
Override Manager — Verify Sensor Integrity

Verify sensor integrity for sensors feeding the soot and regen strategy. Correlate soot rate with boost, EGR, and fueling data. A sensor bias affecting the soot model produces false high regen frequency without any actual over-soot condition. Confirm sensor integrity before any hardware diagnosis.
Safety Interceptor — Correct Root Cause Before DPF Evaluation

Correct the upstream root cause before any DPF evaluation. Cleaning or replacing the DPF without correcting the upstream soot source produces repeat frequent regen. The DPF reloads at the same accelerated rate after service if the upstream cause remains.
Resume Point — DOC Light-Off Assessment

Assess DOC light-off performance. A failing DOC that does not reach light-off temperature prevents passive regen and forces more active regens. Evaluate DOC inlet and outlet EGT during normal operation to confirm DOC is reaching light-off temperature.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Regen Frequency Confirmation
After repair, verify regen frequency returns to normal model range. Confirm SPN 3701 FMI 15 does not return. Monitor for return of high regen frequency over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Upstream Cause and DPF Service Decision

Repair upstream soot contributors — boost leaks, EGR faults, injector imbalance. Correct sensor bias if confirmed. Service DPF only after upstream causes are corrected and DPF condition is evaluated with confirmed normal soot production.

Repair Steps
1 . Repair charge air leak or turbo fault if underboost is confirmed.
2 . Repair EGR fault if confirmed.
3 . Address injector imbalance if confirmed.
4 . Correct sensor bias if confirmed.
5 . Service DPF only after upstream causes are corrected.
Verification Steps
Confirm regen frequency returns to normal model range after repair.
Verify SPN 3701 FMI 15 does not return after repair.
Confirm no upstream soot contributors remain after repair.
Monitor for return of high regen frequency over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Inspect charge air path for leaks at every major service.
✓ Monitor EGR system performance at every major service.
✓ Address injector imbalance promptly to prevent accelerated DPF loading.

Medium Severity
Medium. Frequent regen is a warning of upstream problems. Upstream production analysis before brick replacement prevents cleaning a DPF that will reload immediately.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 3702 FMI 15 indicates active regen occurs more often than the expected model allows. Underboost, EGR abnormalities, injector imbalance, short-trip cycles, DOC light-off problems, and sensor bias are the primary causes. Frequent regen after unresolved charge-air leaks is a documented pattern. Cleaning the DPF without correcting the upstream soot source is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern.
causes: Underboost — underboost producing excessive soot overloading the DPF
EGR abnormalities — EGR abnormalities producing excessive soot
Injector imbalance — injector imbalance producing excessive soot
Short-trip cycles — short-trip cycles preventing regen completion and increasing frequency

steps: Step 1 — History Review

Review regen history. Review soot rate against boost, EGR, and fueling data. Frequent regen after unresolved charge-air leaks is a documented pattern. Identify whether regen frequency increased after a specific event or service.
Step 2 — Upstream Soot Producers

Evaluate upstream soot producers. Underboost producing excessive soot overloading the DPF is a documented cause. Evaluate boost system operation, EGR system operation, and injector balance. Address upstream soot contributors before any DPF service.
Step 3 — Sensor Integrity

Check sensor integrity. Sensor bias producing incorrect soot model inputs is a documented cause. Verify DP sensor and EGT sensor integrity. A sensor bias producing incorrect regen frequency requires sensor repair.
Step 4 — Duty-Cycle Assessment

Assess duty cycle. Short-trip cycles preventing regen completion and increasing frequency are a documented cause. Evaluate the vehicle duty cycle. A short-trip duty cycle may require operational changes to allow regen completion.
Step 5 — DPF Service Only After Root-Cause Correction

Perform DPF service only after root-cause correction. Cleaning the DPF without correcting the upstream soot source is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern. Confirm upstream soot producers and sensor integrity are addressed before any DPF service.

SPN_5020.name: SPN 5020 FMI 1 — Aftertreatment SCR Outlet Temperature Below Normal
SPN_5020.description_en: FMI 1 on SCR outlet temperature indicates the sensor reports below the minimum expected temperature for conditions. Failed outlet EGT, exhaust leak before sensor, low load duty cycle, and upstream thermal management failure are the primary causes. Open EGT after AT service and unplugged connectors are documented patterns. A stuck-low outlet EGT with a rising inlet EGT confirms sensor or circuit fault or an exhaust leak near the outlet sensor boss.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 1 on SCR outlet temperature indicates the sensor reports below the minimum expected temperature for conditions. Failed outlet EGT, exhaust leak before sensor, low load duty cycle, and upstream thermal management failure are the primary causes. Open EGT after AT service and unplugged connectors are documented patterns. A stuck-low outlet EGT with a rising inlet EGT confirms sensor or circuit fault or an exhaust leak near the outlet sensor boss.
causes: Failed outlet EGT — outlet EGT sensor failure producing stuck-low reading
Exhaust leak before sensor — exhaust leak reducing measured temperature
Low load duty cycle — insufficient exhaust temperature from low load operation
Upstream thermal management failure — upstream thermal management not producing adequate SCR inlet temperature
Open EGT after AT service — connector unplugged after AT service
steps: Single Action Gate — PID Correlation SCR Inlet vs Outlet

Compare SCR inlet versus outlet EGT PIDs. A stuck-low outlet EGT with a rising inlet EGT confirms outlet sensor or circuit fault or an exhaust leak near the outlet sensor boss. Both sensors reading low simultaneously confirms a true low-temperature condition from duty cycle or upstream thermal management.
Binary Decision Gate — Circuit Continuity Check

Perform circuit continuity check on the SCR outlet EGT sensor. An open circuit confirms a harness break or disconnected connector. Open EGT after AT service and unplugged connectors are documented patterns — confirm connector engagement before any sensor replacement.
Override Manager — Inspect Sensor Boss and Exhaust Leak

Inspect the SCR outlet EGT sensor boss and surrounding exhaust connections for leaks. An exhaust leak near the outlet sensor boss reduces the measured temperature below the actual SCR outlet temperature. Inspect exhaust connections and gaskets near the outlet sensor.
Safety Interceptor — Thermal Strategy Evaluation

Evaluate upstream thermal management strategy if sensing and leak checks are normal. Low load duty cycle and upstream thermal management failure are causes of true low SCR outlet temperature. Confirm the duty cycle is producing adequate exhaust temperatures for SCR operation.
Resume Point — Sensor Replacement After Circuit Proof

Replace the SCR outlet EGT sensor only after circuit integrity is confirmed and sensor failure is proven by PID correlation. A sensor that reads stuck-low while the circuit is confirmed intact confirms sensor failure.
Verification Loop — Post-Repair Temperature Confirmation

After repair, verify SCR outlet temperature tracks inlet temperature appropriately. Confirm SCR efficiency monitoring returns to normal. Monitor for return of low outlet temperature faults over extended operation.
Repair Ledger Output — Sensor, Harness, or Thermal Management Decision

Reconnect or replace EGT sensor if disconnected or failed. Repair exhaust leak near outlet sensor if confirmed. Address upstream thermal management fault if confirmed. Do not replace SCR hardware for a sensor or circuit fault.

SPN_5697.name: SPN 5697 FMI 31 — DPF Regeneration Inhibit Condition Exists
SPN_5697.description_en: FMI 31 on DPF regen inhibit indicates the regen system is blocked from initiating or completing by one or more active conditions. Active inhibiting faults, coolant or EGT not in range, PTO mode, low fuel, vehicle speed conditions, and sensor faults blocking enable are the primary causes. Technicians forcing regen repeatedly without reading the inhibit reason is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern on this fault — repeated forced regens that never complete because the inhibit condition remains active waste time and can damage the DPF. Read the inhibit reason first, resolve it, then run regen.

procedures_full.overview: FMI 31 on DPF regen inhibit indicates the regen system is blocked from initiating or completing by one or more active conditions. Active inhibiting faults, coolant or EGT not in range, PTO mode, low fuel, vehicle speed conditions, and sensor faults blocking enable are the primary causes. Technicians forcing regen repeatedly without reading the inhibit reason is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern on this fault — repeated forced regens that never complete because the inhibit condition remains active waste time and can damage the DPF. Read the inhibit reason first, resolve it, then run regen.
causes: Active inhibiting faults — active fault codes blocking regen enable
Coolant or EGT not in range — temperature conditions not met for regen enable
PTO mode — PTO engagement blocking regen enable
Low fuel — fuel level below regen enable threshold
Vehicle speed conditions — speed conditions not met for regen enable
Sensor faults blocking enable — sensor faults preventing regen enable conditions from being met
steps: Single Action Gate — Read Inhibit Reasons

Read the regen inhibit reason list from the OEM scan tool. Do not force regen without reading the inhibit reason first. The inhibit reason list identifies the specific condition blocking regen enable. Technicians forcing regen repeatedly without reading the inhibit reason is the most documented misdiagnosis pattern on this fault.
Binary Decision Gate — Resolve Active Inhibiting Codes

Resolve all active fault codes that are listed as regen inhibitors. Active fault codes blocking regen enable must be resolved before regen can proceed. Diagnose and repair each inhibiting fault code before attempting regen.
Override Manager — Verify Enable Conditions

Verify all regen enable conditions are met. Confirm coolant temperature, EGT, fuel level, vehicle speed, and PTO status all meet regen enable requirements. A single unmet enable condition prevents regen from initiating.
Safety Interceptor — Do Not Force Endless Regens While Inhibit Is True

Do not force endless regens while the inhibit condition is still active. Repeated forced regens that never complete because the inhibit condition remains active waste time and can damage the DPF. Confirm the inhibit condition is resolved before each regen attempt.
Resume Point — Run Regen After Inhibit Is Cleared

Run regen after all inhibit conditions are cleared and all enable conditions are met. Monitor regen progress to completion. A regen that initiates and completes confirms the inhibit condition was successfully resolved.
Verification Loop — Soot and Delta-P Response Confirmation

After successful regen, confirm soot load and delta-P return to normal. A successful regen with normal soot and delta-P response confirms the DPF is functioning. A regen that completes but soot or delta-P does not return to normal suggests DPF restriction requiring further evaluation.
Repair Ledger Output — Inhibit Cause and DPF Service Decision

Repair the inhibitor cause — the specific fault code or condition that was blocking regen enable. DPF service is only required if regen completes but soot or delta-P does not return to normal after true restriction is confirmed.

AI Diesel Tech FSM Advantage: The patented Finite State Machine forces technicians through evidence gates in order — blocking parts-cannon jumps and reducing misdiagnosis. Each gate must be satisfied before the next branch opens.
Repair Steps
1 . Repair the specific fault code or condition blocking regen enable.
2 . Correct any unmet regen enable conditions.
3 . Run regen after all inhibit conditions are cleared.
4 . Service DPF only if regen completes but restriction remains confirmed.
Verification Steps
Confirm regen initiates and completes after inhibit is cleared.
Verify soot load and delta-P return to normal after successful regen.
Confirm SPN 5697 FMI 31 does not return after repair.
Monitor for return of regen inhibit conditions over extended operation.
Preventative Measures
✓ Address active fault codes promptly to prevent regen inhibit accumulation.
✓ Maintain fuel level above regen enable threshold during vocational operation.
✓ Disengage PTO before initiating parked regen.
✓ Monitor regen completion rates to identify inhibit patterns early.
Severity & Driveability Guidance
Medium to High Severity
Medium to High as soot climbs. Address quickly to avoid severe restriction. Inhibit-first logic stops wasted regen loops.

Cannot start parked regen
DPF regen will not run
Inhibit active aftertreatment
