SPN_8064.name: International SPN 8064 FMI 12: Crankshaft Position Signal Inactive
SPN_8064.description_en: SPN 8064 FMI 12 means the ECM has completely lost the crankshaft position signal, causing a genuine no-start condition. It's a Critical fault - check the sensor connector and mounting before assuming a full sensor failure.

procedures_full.overview: SPN 8064 FMI 12 means the ECM has completely lost the crankshaft position signal, causing a genuine no-start condition. It's a Critical fault - check the sensor connector and mounting before assuming a full sensor failure.
causes: Corroded or damaged CKP sensor connector
An electrical/wiring fault, not a sensor failure - a pushed-out pin or corrosion can completely interrupt the signal path even with a healthy sensor.
Sensor worked loose from its mounting bore
A mechanical installation issue where vibration or improper reinstallation after service increased the air gap beyond the sensor's detection range.
Internally failed (open) CKP sensor
A genuine sensor hardware failure confirmed by an out-of-spec resistance reading.
Damaged crankshaft target wheel
A mechanical engine component failure where the toothed wheel the sensor reads has physical damage, which is a more involved repair than the sensor itself.
steps: Confirm the no-start by watching for an RPM signal on the dash cluster while cranking - zero RPM confirms the ECM isn't seeing crank position at all.
Connect a scan tool and check for SPN 8064 as an active fault along with a related camshaft position (SPN 8021) sync fault, since these two often appear together.
Inspect the CKP sensor connector for corrosion, a broken locking tab, or a pushed-out pin, which are common causes of a totally lost signal versus a degraded one.
Check the sensor's air gap to the crankshaft target wheel, since a sensor that's worked loose or been improperly reinstalled after service can lose signal entirely.
If the connector and air gap check out, test the sensor's resistance value against OEM specification, since an internally open sensor produces this exact fault.
symptoms: Engine cranks normally but will not start
No RPM reading on the dash during cranking
Check engine light illuminated with the ignition on before cranking
Possible history of intermittent stalling before the sensor failed completely
procedures_full.source_title: International SPN 8064 FMI 12: Crankshaft Position Signal Inactive

procedures_full.overview: SPN 8064 FMI 12 means the SCR catalyst temperature sensor or its module is flagged as a bad intelligent device. Expect unreliable aftertreatment control and a possible torque derate until wiring or the sensor is verified. When an MX-powered Kenworth or Peterbilt throws SPN 8064 FMI 12, the truck loses trustworthy SCR temperature feedback exactly when the aftertreatment system needs it most. ProfessionalDieselRepair.com sees this code after heat-soaked harness failures at the SCR flange and after moisture intrusion in the sensor connector.
causes: Heat-damaged harness at the SCR catalyst flange
Repeated thermal cycles crack insulation and open the signal circuit, which the ECM interprets as a bad intelligent device rather than a simple voltage fault.
Failed SCR catalyst temperature sensor element
Internal sensor failure sends implausible or missing temperature data even when supply voltage and grounds are correct.
Corroded Deutsch connector or poor ground
Road salt and DEF mist corrode pins, raising circuit resistance until the aftertreatment module stops trusting the sensor entirely.
steps: Connect PACCAR Davie4 and read active/inactive faults plus freeze-frame SCR catalyst temperature at the time of failure.
Inspect the SCR temperature sensor harness near the DOC/SCR brick for heat damage, melted insulation, or loose Deutsch connectors.
Back-probe the sensor supply at the connector with key on: verify 5.0 V ±0.5 V reference and less than 0.5 V on signal ground.
Compare upstream and downstream SCR temperature sensors in live data during idle and loaded snap throttle; a stuck reading more than 50 °F from expected range points to a failed sensor.
Repair wiring or replace the SCR catalyst temperature sensor per PACCAR MX spec, clear faults, and confirm temperature tracks within ±30 °F of DOC outlet during a stationary regen.
symptoms: Amber check engine lamp with SCR or aftertreatment warning text on the dash
DEF dosing may suspend and SCR efficiency warnings appear in PACCAR Davie4
Reduced engine torque or an active emissions derate after repeated drive cycles
Erratic or frozen SCR catalyst temperature readings in live data
Possible MIL flash during regen attempts when temperature feedback drops out
procedures_full.source_title: PACCAR SPN 8064 FMI 12: SCR Catalyst Temperature Device Fault
